a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: And we have a roll program.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: You have good thrust on all five engines.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: And we have a pitch program.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Stand by for Mode One Bravo.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. Everything looks perfect down here.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay. Looks cleared up here, Gordo. [Long pause.]

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, the altimeter is six zero.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Going through maximum dynamic pressure at this time.

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: Okay. 1:32. Program looks good, Dave. Out at 11 miles.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay. Good shot. Two and a half g.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: 9 [nautical] miles [16.6 km] downrange, 13 - 14.5 [nautical] miles [24 - 26.8 km] height.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Stand by for Mode One Charlie.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, we're at 3g's. Stand by for inboard.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Each of the five S-IC engines [are] gulping 3 tons of fuel [means propellant] per second.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, 10 seconds to staging. Hang on.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Flight Dynamics reports Go for staging.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. You have good thrust on the S-II. All five are good.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Good show. We'll go on time.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Roger. We confirm the Skirt Sep. You're Mode II.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Coming up on 10,000 feet per second [3,000 m/s] mark. Down range 131 [nautical miles, 243 km], altitude 66 [nautical miles, 122 km].

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: Just - looks just about a hundred feet per second [30 m/s] down on the H-dot, but everything else looks fine.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, I got the big fireball going by at staging. I don't know whether you saw it or not. That beauty really goes.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. At 4 [minutes], the guidance has converged. The CMC is Go and everything looks good.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, Gordo. Looks good up here. [Long pause.]

a15_0000013.speaker: Irwin
a15_0000013.text: Man, I got the Moon in my window.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Thrusters are stable; the ball's stable.

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: We're at a V I of 11,000 and right on the money.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Good show. Let me check here at 4:30 just to make sure.

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: That sucker's right on - right on.

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: Little high on altitude. I bet you they're going to give you the [garble] here in a minute.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. Five minutes. Everything looks nominal. You're Go.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, Gordo; thank you. Looks good up here. Got a smooth ride so far.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: 40 percent of velocity needed [to achieve orbit].

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Downrange 271 [nautical miles, 501 km] altitude 88 [nautical miles, 163 km].

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: See, we're getting just a little teeny bounce. You feel it now?

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, be watching for the S-IVB for COI.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. Times are nominal. The level sense arm will be 8 plus 34, and S-II cut-off at 9 plus 09. Over.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: And stand by for S-IVB to COI.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Mark. You have S-IVB to COI now.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Roger. S-IVB to COI. [Long pause.] [To Irwin:] Jim?

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, we're right - right down the line.

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: Coming up on 15,000 V I , 260 H-dot. That's right where we ought to be, and that gives us an SCS COI.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay. Keep your eye up for S-IVB to orbit.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: 380 [nautical] miles [704 km] downrange, altitude 94.5 [nautical miles, 175.0 km], velocity 15,000 feet per second [4,572 m/s].

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Stand by for S-IVB to orbit capability.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Downrange 479 [nautical] miles, [887 km], altitude 96 [nautical] miles, [178 km], now approaching 65 per cent of velocity needed for orbit. The velocity now, 16,700 feet per second [5,090 metres per second]. Official time of lift-off [9 hours] 34 minutes, 00 seconds .79. [Eastern Daylight Time]

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: Feels like we get a little vibration out of that thing.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Well, it seems to be pretty steady though.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: We're about 1.7g, somewhere around there. Okay, 10 seconds to inboard.

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: V I 's 18,000 [fps, 5,486 m/s]. [Garble] We're at 96 [nautical] miles [178 km].

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Downrange 660 [nautical] miles [1,222 km], altitude 95 [nautical] miles [176 km], velocity 78 per cent velocity required for orbit.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, about 10 seconds to PU shift.

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: Didn't even feel it. There it goes, 8:03.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. 15, Houston. Go ahead. Say again, 15?

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Houston, 15. We didn't call. You got something?

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: You've had PU shift, and the thrust looks good.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: You've had level sense arm now?

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Stand by for Mode IV capability.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Mark. You have Mode IV now.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. You've had - you have good thrust on the S-IVB.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: 960 [nautical] miles [1,778 km] downrange, 94.7 [nautical miles, 175.4 km] altitude. Velocity 23,230 [feet per second, 7,081 m/s].

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. Everything's looking perfect. Predicted [S-IVB engine] cut-off time [is] 11 plus 37. Over.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Booster confirms the S-IVB has shutdown.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, Houston. [SPS engine] Gimbal Motors are Off, and the S-IVB oxidizer is 40 [psi, 276 kPa], and the fuel's about 31 [psi, 214 kPa].

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: Okay, Gordo. We got ourselves in a 93.7 [nautical miles, 173.5 km] by 88.9 [nautical miles, 164.6 km, orbit]; [engine] shutdown [was] on a V I [inertial velocity] of plus 25595 [fps, 7,801 m/s]; H dot, plus 00008 [fps, 2.4 m/s], altitude plus 00932 [93.2 nautical miles, 172.6 km].

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. IU shows you in a 92.5 by 91.5 [nautical mile orbit, 171.3 by 169.5 km]. Radar confirms that. And the booster is safed.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, Gordo; good job. That was a very smooth ride all the way.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. The booster is configured for orbit. Over.

a15_0001610.speaker: Scott
a15_0001610.text: Okay. Have you got the torquing angle?

a15_0001610.speaker: Worden
a15_0001610.text: Mm-hum. Okay, we could do the SM RCS monitoring check and the CM...

a15_0001610.speaker: Scott
a15_0001610.text: Okay. The S-IVB tank pressures are - about 41 [psi] on the oxidizer and about 21 [psi] on the fuel.

a15_0001610.speaker: Irwin
a15_0001610.text: I know we're over the [garble] but [garble] Indian Ocean should be.

a15_0001610.speaker: Scott
a15_0001610.text: And it looks like the S-IVB is tracking very nicely.

a15_0001610.speaker: Worden
a15_0001610.text: I - I guess I hadn't really - hadn't - myself thought we wouldn't be - it wouldn't be visibly this fast.

a15_0001610.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0001610.text: Apollo 15 [is] in a 92.5 by 91.5 nautical mile [171.3 by 169.5 km] Earth orbit. 1 [nautical] mile [1.85 km] out of perfectly circular. Communications through the Canary Island tracking station for about 4 minutes and 11 seconds total pass time.

a15_0002113.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0002113.text: 15, Houston. About 35 seconds to LOS [Loss Of Signal], and we have nothing further for you. We'll see you at Carnarvon, as shown on the checklist, at 52 [minutes GET]. Over.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay. I'm going to do a fuel cell purge check here, Dave.

a15_0002113.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0002113.text: Flight Dynamics Officer reports that the data coming from the Canary Islands tracking station confirms the initial measurements of the Earth parking orbit, and we're expecting to acquire Apollo 15 again over the Carnarvon, Australia, tracking station at 52 minutes Ground Elapsed Time, about 30 minutes from now. And at 22 minutes, 13 seconds Ground Elapsed Time; this is Apollo Control.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Do you want to get - get going down there?

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Try and clean some of this stuff off, too.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: You can take mine and stick it in there, too.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: With that indicator out, I can't confirm an H 2 purge on fuel cell 2.

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: Oh, I'm sorry. Okay. It's - it's good.

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: Okay. You can probably look out my window.

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: Saw a flash? You did? Couldn't hear it - I didn't hear it. Huh, I'll be darned!

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: Yes. Saw a flash, but I didn't hear it. Gosh, I used to hear them all the time. Huh!

a15_0005034.speaker: Worden
a15_0005034.text: You know, it's amazing what [garble] outside that window [garble].

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: That's because you got your [garble] lights on in here.

a15_0005034.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005034.text: Okay, the secondary glycol loop check's complete.

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: Rog. Houston, 15. You're loud and clear.

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: Okay the insertion [and system] checks are coming along very nicely. We're down through [item] 21 in the checklist. And the cameras are out, and Al's completed his alignment.

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: And I only got one comment [that] Jim's got for you.

a15_0005034.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005034.text: Houston - Houston, 15. On the H 2 purge, fuel cell 2, I cannot confirm [the H 2 flow rate] since I had no - no read-out of a flow indication, or a caution and warning associated with that flow.

a15_0005034.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005034.text: And, if you'd like, I could do it any time, and perhaps you could confirm it.

a15_0005034.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0005034.text: This is Houston. We're unable to help you on confirming that purge down here, Jim.

a15_0005034.speaker: Worden
a15_0005034.text: Gordo, this is Al. I've got the numbers on the P52 for you.

a15_0005034.speaker: Worden
a15_0005034.text: Okay. [I] used stars 33 and 41. Noun 05 was plus 000.01 and the torquing angles were minus 00.019, plus 00.021, minus 00.061, and they were torqued out at 50 minutes.

a15_0005034.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0005034.text: Roger. Copied. And the torquing angles are minus 00.019, plus 00.021, and a minus 00.061. Over.

a15_0005034.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0005034.text: This is Apollo Control. Cabin pressure aboard Apollo 15 [is] holding at 5.7 pounds per square inch [39.3 kPa]. Heart rates for Scott, Worden, and Irwin, respectively, are 70, 83 and 88.

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: And, Houston, one other comment. Apparently sometime during launch, the RCS-B secondary propellant isolation valve closed, and we recycled it and got a gray talkback.

a15_0005755.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0005755.text: Apollo 15, Houston. About 15 seconds to LOS. Estimating [contact with the] United States at 1:30 [GET].

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Al, my doggone checklist says Mag M ought to be on here for the UV.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Yes ... better get two of these...

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: You want to put that on there?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Yes. I don't know what we're going to do with this thing. I guess Jim has to hold this during TLI. Or something like that.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Why - why can't I put it on the bracket?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Man, that was some fantastic ride! Gaa!

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Something you're not likely to forget for a while.

a15_0005755.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0005755.text: And we've had Loss Of Signal through the Carnarvon, Australia tracking station. We're standing by now for the post-launch press conference at press site 39 at Kennedy Space Center. And at 59 hours, 22 minutes [means 59 minutes, 22 seconds] Ground Elapsed Time; this is Apollo Control."

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Okay; will do. And we're down through 27 on the checklist. The docking probe is out. Looks good. And standing by for a sequence arm and a logic check when you're ready.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Roger. We can do that now. [Pause.] Go ahead.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Okay. Logic one, On, now. Logic two, On, now. [Long pause.]

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Logics are good. You're Go for pyro arm.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Okay; and we had one other little one [an anomaly]. At about an hour [GET], we noticed that the primary and secondary propellant isolation valves on Quad Delta were barber pole. We cycled the switch, and they are now gray. And the RCS checks okay.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Roger. [Pause.] I have a TLI plus 90 and lift-off plus 8 abort PADs, when you're ready.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Can you stand by one, please, Gordo?

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Getting a little UV here. [Pause.]

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Okay, Gordo. I'm ready for the TLI [means TLI plus 90] PAD.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay. This is the TLI plus 90 abort PAD, Jim.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Okay.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: TLI plus 90, SPS/G&N; Noun 47 is 66938; minus 0.52, plus 1.90; GET for ignition is 004:19:56.99; Noun 81, minus 0425.4, plus 0000.1, plus 4921.7; attitude, 180, 166, 002; H A is N/A [not applicable], H P , plus 0021.0; 4940.1, 6:34, 4920.8. Sextant star is 40, 079.5, 35.9; boresight star, N/A; Noun 61, plus 16.04, minus 030.00; 1099.0, 34492; GET for 05g, 017:43:58; GDC Align stars are Deneb and Vega; 112, 128, 356; no ullage. Go ahead. [Long pause.]

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: 15, Houston. [No answer.]

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Apollo 15, Houston. We're not reading you. Over.

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: Okay, Houston; there is a breakup - breakup in the VHF, and Jim lost some of the first part of the transmission. Could you go through it again?

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay, just what do you need?

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: We have Noun 47 through roll, pitch and yaw.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay, Jim. Noun 47 is 66938; minus 0.52, plus 1.90; Noun 33, 004:19:56.99; Noun 81, minus 0425.4, plus 0000.1, minus 4921.7 - correction on Delta-V Z is a plus 4921.7; roll, pitch, and yaw are 180, 166, 002. Go ahead.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay, Jim, your readback's correct. Lift-off plus 8 PAD is 008:00, 6076, minus 175, 027:06. Go ahead.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Roger. And I'll have the TLI PAD when you're ready for that one. [Pause.]

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: All right. Go ahead. I'm ready for the TLI PAD.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay. Time base 6 predict 2:40:23; attitude for TLI, 180, 045, 001; burn time 5:55; 10401.1, 35599; Sep attitude, 359, 077, 320; extraction attitude, 301, 257, 040. R2 align, 045.0, 038.0; ORDEAL start, 56:45; Yaw 001; ejection time 4:16:00. Go ahead.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay. A little static on two readbacks. Read back Yaw for extraction and R2 align, please?

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Roger. 040 and 045.0.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay. Readback's correct, Jim. [Long pause.]

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: 15, Houston. We have a question regarding the primary and secondary isolation valve. Over.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Go ahead.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: We're wondering if you happened to just notice them [as] barber pole at one hour [GET], or did you notice them close at one hour? Over.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Ah, no. We just noticed that they were closed at an hour, But apparently in the shuffle here, somebody probably bumped the one switch which would do it.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Roger. You don't - you can't tie them to any other action or event there then? Is that right?

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Negative.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay; thank you.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Okay.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: 15, Houston. [Could you put] IU Uptel to Block? We have put in a second IU Nav[igation] vector, based on Stateside data.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Uptel to Block. [Long pause.]

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: 15, Houston. We'd like P00 and Accept.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: P00 and Accept. You've got it.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: 15, Houston. IU Uptel [means CM Uptel] to Block. You have a new state vector now.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Roger. CM Uptel going to Block.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Roger. My mistake. Also have a short update for your TLI checklist ORDEAL angles because of the slight performance difference in the S-IVB. Over.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Okay; go ahead, Gordo.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay. On the launch checklist, page L2-30, bottom of the page. Tell me when you have it. [Pause.]

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Go ahead, Gordo.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: At 56 minutes, slew FDAI number 1 to pitch equals 17 degrees rather than 16; and, at the top of the next page, ensure FDAI number 1 pitch equal 14 degrees rather than 13. Over.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Roger. Copied. 17 degrees instead of 16, and 14 instead of the 13.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay; then on the next page, 2-32 at 59:55, change 7 degrees to 8 degrees, ensure FDAI number 1 pitch equal 8 degrees.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Copy, 8 degrees.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: One more on the cue card for TLI down slightly below the middle, the long cue card that the CDR uses at 54 minutes. The 24 degrees should be changed to 25 degrees. "Ordeal 300/Lunar, 25 degrees.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Okay, we've got that; 25 degrees.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: And then there will be a 1 degree difference on the rest of the ORDEAL numbers.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Okay; looks like they all fit.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: That's it.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Apollo 15, Houston. We're about to LOS. Nothing further. We'll see you at Carnarvon at 2:25 GET.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Ah, Roger. 2:25...

a15_0012929.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0012929.text: This is Apollo Control. Apparently, we have had Loss Of Signal through the Vanguard tracking ship in mid-Atlantic. During that pass over the United States, the numbers for the upcoming Translunar Injection maneuver was passed up - were passed up to the crew. This maneuver, slightly over an hour from now, [is] planned at 2 hours, 50 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. The burn, lasting 5 minutes, 55 seconds with the S-IVB third stage, will place the spacecraft into a trajectory toward the Moon. It will increase the velocity by some 10,414 feet per second (actually 10,401.1 fps [3,170.3 m/s]). The meas

a15_0022400.speaker: Worden
a15_0022400.text: Well, the seat's kind of tight right underneath there.

a15_0022400.speaker: Worden
a15_0022400.text: Just passed through the ...; we're in good shape.

a15_0022400.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0022400.text: This is Apollo Control; 2 hours, 24 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We've just had acquisition [of signal] through the Carnarvon station and Gordon Fullerton [is] giving them a call at this time.

a15_0022400.speaker: Scott
a15_0022400.text: All right, Houston; [Apollo] 15 here. [You are reading] 5 by [5].

a15_0022400.speaker: Scott
a15_0022400.text: Houston, 15. We're down to the middle of the TLI Prep [on page L2-29] , and everything's in order.

a15_0022400.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0022400.text: We're showing the Manual Attitude switches in Rate... [correcting himself] in Min Impulse, and we recommend Rate Command.

a15_0022400.speaker: Scott
a15_0022400.text: Roger. Rate Command. And the pyros are armed.

a15_0022400.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0022400.text: Flight Director Gerry Griffin [is] preparing to poll his flight controllers, here in the Mission Control room, for Go/No-Go, which shows in the Flight Plan, to be passed up through one of the [ARIA] aircraft in the mid-Pacific. However, it looks like the Go/No-Go signal will be voiced up to the crew just prior to the Loss Of Signal here at Carnarvon. 22 minutes - Mark, 22 minutes to ignition for Translunar Injection.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Burn time - 5:55. And, when you get the shutdown, you got a 2-second thruster V I . Right?

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: ... degrees per second rate. The first one is at 59. Make sure you got that. 45 degrees pitch and yaw.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: ... degrees per second roll. The S-IVB guidance function ... Okay.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Do we have Hawaii all the way through the burn?

a15_0023212.speaker: Worden
a15_0023212.text: No, we haven't .... No, we have...

a15_0023212.speaker: Worden
a15_0023212.text: No. We have LOS at 49:52 for ... minutes.

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: No, we get them back at 2:55.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Yes, well, we tried it the other day.

a15_0023212.speaker: Worden
a15_0023212.text: If you did, you can change your Delta-V ... 20 feet per second.

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: I bet you it's from the S-IVB.

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: We're down to 5 on the cabin.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: When we get ready to dock, and the cabin's up to 5 pounds.

a15_0023212.speaker: Worden
a15_0023212.text: I thought we were supposed to leave some pressure for that.

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: Right after Waste Stowage Vent, Closed.

a15_0023212.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0023212.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston through ARIA. Over. [No answer.]

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: You don't have the S-band squelch on, do you?

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: Yes, yes, I thought it was...

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: ... we ought to be able to get that ...

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Oh, that's pretty - that is loud. Isn't it?

a15_0023212.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0023212.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston through ARIA. Over.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Rog, Houston, 15. You're about 1 by 1 through ARIA. [i.e. very poor.]

a15_0023212.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0023212.text: Roger. You're about 3 by [3]; clear enough to understand.

a15_0023212.speaker: Worden
a15_0023212.text: He said we're clear enough ..., I think.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Roger. We have somebody else on the loop with us, too.

a15_0023212.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0023212.text: Coming up on 10 minutes to TLI ignition. Mark, 10 minutes.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: It's a familiar sound, and I can't remember what I - what it is.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: You can't change the frequency there. You might hook up...

a15_0023212.speaker: Worden
a15_0023212.text: Why don't we hook up the speakers, and let's do some checking...

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: We have the S-II Sep light?

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: The Uplink Activity light went out.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Very well. It should come on now. Come on, baby.

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: Okay. ORDEAL FDAI 1 to Orb-rate; 2 to Inertial.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Okay, Houston. It looks like we have a slow repress start. We're up to about 22 to 23 on the fuel pressure.

a15_0023212.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0023212.text: Roger, Dave. You're just barely readable. Understand you're getting a normal Repress. We're - It looks good down here.

a15_0024404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0024404.text: Okay; at 56, slew FDAI 1 to Pitch at 17.

a15_0024404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0024404.text: Okay; at 56:45, it should be 14 degrees.

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: Plot boards here in Mission Control Center on the center screen are being set up now to monitor the Translunar Injection burn. Some 5 minutes, 43 seconds away from ignition. Should be in about a minute and a half acquired by the second ARIA spacecraft - [correcting himself] aircraft in mid-Pacific. BOOSTER reports that the tanks in S-IVB stage have been pressurized.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: Apollo 15, Houston through ARIA number 2. Over.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: 15, Houston. You're way down in the static, but I can hear you transmit. Over.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay. We'll pick you up at the keyhole.

a15_0024404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0024404.text: Why don't they have a picture like that in the simulator?

a15_0024404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0024404.text: TVC Servo - SCS TVC Servo Power 1 to AC 1/Main A.

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: This is Apollo Control. There was some doubt in the BOOSTER Engineer's mind that the engine bell of the S-IVB J-2 engine had been properly chilled down from the data that he got through the ARIA 1 aircraft. However, his new data coming in through ARIA 2 has confirmed that the chilldown procedure prior to start has been accomplished as scheduled. Some 2 minutes, 15 seconds away from TLI ignition. Continuing to standby as we approach acquisition at Hawaii in some 2 minutes from now. Still standing by through the ARIA 2 aircraft. Communications through ARIA 2 have been somewhat scratchy - almost

a15_0024404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0024404.text: Tape Recorder's going High Bit Rate.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Put it in between the camera, Al. No, don't force it.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Can you get it up there?

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: Looking at ignition time of 2 hours, 50 minutes, 1 second Ground Elapsed Time. Cut-off at 2 hours, 55 minutes, 54 seconds. Total spacecraft velocity at cut-off should be 35,608.7 feet per second [10,853.5 m/s]. Coming up on 20 seconds. Mark, 20 seconds to TLI ignition.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: 15, Houston; we're showing good thrust. [Long pause.]

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Load's about a half a g. ORDEAL ... should be tracking with it.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Well, it had a little surge right at this ...

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay. S-IVB pressure is 40 [psi for the LOX tank] and 30 [psi for the fuel tank] and we had a little surge at about one minute.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: Roger. That was PU shift and that looks - the thrust looks good.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: You feel a very slight amount of bumping ...

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: Coming up on 30 thousand... [PAO is interrupted by Dave Scott]

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay, Houston, 15. And we're about halfway through. Pressures are steady at 40 [psi] and 30 [psi] and ORDEAL is tracking right on through.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: Roger, 15. At 3 minutes, it looks completely nominal to us.

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: Coming up on 30,000 feet per second - Mark. 30,000 feet per second [9,144 m/s]. Resulting apogee, 4,685 nautical miles [8,677 km].

a15_0024404.speaker: Worden
a15_0024404.text: My countdown's going to be off probably 2 seconds here. Let's start my watch and ... it again. I want to be sure the engines ... start.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: You can feel it, can't you?

a15_0024404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0024404.text: I get the little surge before the bang.

a15_0024404.speaker: Worden
a15_0024404.text: Pressure's looking good. ORDEAL's tracking. A quarter g - a half g ...

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay, Houston. We have about a minute to go. We're tracking 39 and 30 on the pressures and ORDEAL's about zero.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: That should be on for cut-off.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: 15, Houston. We're estimating cut-off about 4 seconds earlier than the PAD time.

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: Velocity rapidly approaching TLI cut-off speed.

a15_0024404.speaker: Worden
a15_0024404.text: I'll give you a countdown to 55.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay. Al, get the data there.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: S-IVB [fuel] tank pressure is about 32 [psi], coming down. The oxidizer at about 28 [psi], coming down on the fuel.

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: Cut-off. Velocity; 35,522 feet per second [10,827 m/s]. Resulting apogee from that maneuver; 290,682 nautical miles [538,342 km].

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: SCS TVC Servo Power went Off - went Off. PCM Bit Rate going Low.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Inertial and locked. Okay, when Al gets through with ...

a15_0024404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0024404.text: Okay, it's time to switch around.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay, Gordo. Got some data for you, if you're ready to copy.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: 15, Houston. We're getting a lot of static for some reason. Say again, please.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Roger, Gordo. I've got the cut-off residuals when you're ready to copy.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: [Initially faint.] Okay. We cut-off on a V I of 35,614 [fps]. TFC was plus 02; V G was plus 145; Delta-V C was minus 14.9. And I've got the H-dot now if you want it. H-dot was 4,353 [fps] and altitude is 167.4 [nautical miles].

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: 15, Houston. Most of your readback is blocked by static. Let's wait a little while and try it again.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay, you got all your data, Al?

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay. Let's switch over. Okay. Switchy, switchy.

a15_0024404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0024404.text: Okay, when the Comp Activity light's out, you're just supposed to ..., Al.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Then when you all get down in the LEB, get that waste storage vent valve closed.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: And, Houston, we have the S-IVB in Orb-rate.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: Roger. You're loud and clear now.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay, Houston. I've got the data if you want to copy.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: Okay. Sounds good now. Go ahead again.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay. DSKY was 35599; V G plus 145; and the Delta V C , minus 14.9; TFC, plus .02. [Pause.] And, for your information, the H-dot was 4353 and the H was 167.4 at cut-off.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: Roger. Say again what that figure 'plus 02' was?

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: Roger. Okay. Copied all that. And, for your information, the maneuver to the TD&E [Transposition, Docking and Extraction] attitude should start about one second earlier than the Flight Plan. 3:10:53.

a15_0031610.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0031610.text: Everything looks good here. You're Go for Transposition and Docking.

a15_0031610.speaker: Scott
a15_0031610.text: Roger. Go for Transposition and Docking.

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: Okay, EMS Function, Delta-V. That's a verify.

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: Okay, got the DET set at 59:30.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Okay, Houston, 15; 30 seconds [to go before separation].

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: Okay. At 50, we'll go to BMAGs, Att 1/Rate 2; CMC, Auto; and come off in CMC. There is Att 1/Rate 2; CMC, Auto, at 58, we'll get plus-X.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Now get your valves, D. They look good.

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: Okay. Engine valves going to SCS.

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: Okay. I'm going to pitch over.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Okay, Houston; we got a good Sep.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: And Prime Propellant B, Secondary, and Delta Prime and Secondary with barber pole, and they're both gray, now - reset.

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: Yes. There goes the panels, right out to the side. Right outside.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: It's spinning out there. You see the...

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: What a view! You see the S-IVB?

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: [Garble]. We're at 270, now. Oh, ooops. Where is it? [Garble].

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: You look good, good, good, good. Good job. Right in there, babe. Yes, that's good. Oh, look at that.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: No, forget the TV. The TV looks okay. Get the camera over here and take some pictures.

a15_0032023.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0032023.text: 15, Houston. Would you give us Omni Bravo?

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: Okay, I'm going to give it a little plus-X.

a15_0032023.speaker: Irwin
a15_0032023.text: Got a T - good TV picture, Dave?

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Yes. ... just a little off to the side, Al?

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Don't want to get too far away, now.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Okay, Houston. Looks like you've got a good LM in there [in the SLA], and we're rolling now, and the opening rates are stopped, and you should have a TV [picture].

a15_0032023.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0032023.text: Roger. We haven't got the [TV] picture up here yet. Stand by, and I'll give you a check on that.

a15_0032023.speaker: Irwin
a15_0032023.text: I can shift that camera if you want, Dave.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: No. It would just be ... the orientation the LM has for the attitude.

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: Yes, that is a big bang when you come off of there, isn't it?

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: All I've got to look at it is the TV picture.

a15_0032023.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0032023.text: Goldstone's receiving the carrier, but we're not getting any signal on the carrier for the TV. Over.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Okay; we've got a good picture on the monitor up here.

a15_0032023.speaker: Irwin
a15_0032023.text: This switch here should probably go to Transmit.

a15_0032023.speaker: Irwin
a15_0032023.text: Do what? How about S-Band Aux TV to TV?

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Hey, we need High Gain, don't we?

a15_0032023.speaker: Irwin
a15_0032023.text: You have. I've got ... use High Gain ...

a15_0032023.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0032023.text: 15, Houston; we're getting a picture now, and the LM is coming in, in the lower right-hand corner of our field of view.

a15_0032023.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0032023.text: Starting to get a black and white picture here, in Mission Control. [It will] take a little while to get it through the converter.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Of course, ... your pictures. Take your pictures.

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: It was a lot slower than I thought it would be.

a15_0032023.speaker: Irwin
a15_0032023.text: As long as they're getting the picture on the Omni, I guess there's no hurry to - that we get the High Gain up.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Okay, Houston. It looks like we've got a good High Gain Antenna. Do you want us to give you the High Gain or stay on the Omni [antenna]?

a15_0032023.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0032023.text: We'll take the High Gain, Dave.

a15_0032023.speaker: Irwin
a15_0032023.text: There's sure a lot of crap flying out...

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Okay, Houston. We're in Auto and Medium. Looks like we got a good lock.

a15_0032023.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0032023.text: Roger; and we're getting a very good picture here. It's - it[the LM]'s over on the right-hand side of the field of view.

a15_0032023.speaker: Irwin
a15_0032023.text: Shall I put the TV ... long, Dave.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Huh! I think it looks good, Jim.

a15_0032023.speaker: Irwin
a15_0032023.text: I can adjust it and get it in center.

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: I find I'm working the stick a lot more than I thought I would.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Just play it cool. We've got plenty of time.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Six on your camera would be right where you'd want it.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Okay. I would say we were - what, Jim? 20 feet? 15? 10?

a15_0032023.speaker: Irwin
a15_0032023.text: I have 15 feet on the camera.

a15_0032023.speaker: Irwin
a15_0032023.text: Did we forget anything on that checklist, Dave?

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: Okay. We're sliding in there, David.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Okay. I think we're about a couple feet away.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: What do you want to do?

a15_0032023.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0032023.text: 15, Houston. The centering on the picture is good now, and we're getting an excellent quality picture.

a15_0032023.speaker: Irwin
a15_0032023.text: Put it at 12 frames per second.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Okay; let's go down the checklist. You get ... Okay, On capture, changing Free, to damp, align pitch and yaw...

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: Still got a little pitch rate going.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: You're fine. Just align pitch and yaw.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: They're all aligned and damped out?

a15_0032023.speaker: Worden
a15_0032023.text: We're off at a little bit of an angle.

a15_0032023.speaker: Irwin
a15_0032023.text: Here. I can hold this a minute. ...

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: Your rate's going? Don't mess around.

a15_0032023.speaker: Scott
a15_0032023.text: I should have told you about that. I forgot about it.

a15_0033607.speaker: Scott
a15_0033607.text: Okay; that all [the Transposition and Docking] went fairly nominally, and the only different thing we've noticed is the SPS Thrust light on the EMS is now on. And we don't know when it came on; somewhere in the process here.

a15_0033607.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0033607.text: Roger. I understand the SPS Thrust light is on.

a15_0033607.speaker: Scott
a15_0033607.text: And all the switches are off.

a15_0035506.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0035506.text: At 3:55:54 - about 40 seconds [from now] - [the] non-propulsive vent will be opened on the booster.

a15_0041130.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0041130.text: Apollo 15, Houston. The [non-propulsive] vent should be complete now.

a15_0041130.speaker: Irwin
a15_0041130.text: Okay; I'll cycle the cryo fans.

a15_0041130.speaker: Scott
a15_0041130.text: That's right, we got a change for that.

a15_0041130.speaker: Worden
a15_0041130.text: You don't need the checklist. You got that silly bunch of junk. Garbage, rather.

a15_0041130.speaker: Scott
a15_0041130.text: Okay; load RCS DAP. Al, you want to load your DAP?

a15_0041130.speaker: Irwin
a15_0041130.text: Oh, let's see. We need to load...

a15_0041130.speaker: Scott
a15_0041130.text: Load Noun 22 attitude. Monitor APS maneuver, [garble].

a15_0041130.speaker: Irwin
a15_0041130.text: Okay. Cue MSFN, because we'll be getting the Logics on the Arm pretty soon.

a15_0041130.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0041130.text: This is Apollo Control; [we're] some 4 minutes away from ejection of the Command Service Module docked to the Lunar Module, from the spent S-IVB stage, which has now completed its non-propulsive vent. Spacecraft now 12,036 nautical miles [22,291 km] out from Earth; velocity dropped off to 16,839 feet per second [5,133 m/s]. The only anomaly encounted - encountered thus far after Translunar Injection, is a couple of Service Module Propulsion System valves were noted, both on board and on telemetry, as being in the Open position when they should be in Closed position. The crew was instructed to

a15_0041130.speaker: Worden
a15_0041130.text: Rog, Gordo. We're ready to get the Pyro Arm and Logics on now.

a15_0041130.speaker: Worden
a15_0041130.text: Okay, logics coming on; Logic 1; Logic 2. [Pause]

a15_0041130.speaker: Irwin
a15_0041130.text: Sequence Pyro Arm, two, go to Arm.

a15_0041130.speaker: Worden
a15_0041130.text: Pyro Arm coming on. They're on.

a15_0041742.speaker: Scott
a15_0041742.text: Okay, Houston. We got a good sep.

a15_0041742.speaker: Irwin
a15_0041742.text: Okay; you can Pro on that display.

a15_0041742.speaker: Irwin
a15_0041742.text: You have to go into P00. Then when the activity light's out, you can key Verb 66. Okay, Al, you ready to clean it up?

a15_0042941.speaker: Scott
a15_0042941.text: Okay, Houston; 15. We have the S-IVB in sight, and it looks like it's probably about - oh 7 or 8 hundred feet away.

a15_0042941.speaker: Scott
a15_0042941.text: Roger. We have the S-IVB in sight, and it looks like it's 500 feet [150 metres] or so away.

a15_0042941.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0042941.text: Roger. We copied the first time. If it's okay with you and looks clear, we'll command the yaw maneuver.

a15_0042941.speaker: Scott
a15_0042941.text: Ah Roger, and it looks like a clean bird out there.

a15_0042941.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0042941.text: Roger. [Pause.] We'll be sending the yaw command at 4:31.

a15_0042941.speaker: Scott
a15_0042941.text: Okay. We can see the thruster activity on the S-IVB.

a15_0042941.speaker: Scott
a15_0042941.text: It looks like a light mist and a sort of conical shape, maybe - oh, a hundred feet long or so.

a15_0042941.speaker: Scott
a15_0042941.text: And, Houston, as a sidelight, we can verify that the Falcon has his Rover aboard.

a15_0042941.speaker: Scott
a15_0042941.text: As we watch the S-IVB drift away here, how about passing along to Jim Harrington at the Cape, congratulations from the crew to the launch team for a superior job.

a15_0042941.speaker: Scott
a15_0042941.text: Smooth all the way, and right on time.

a15_0042941.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0042941.text: Gerry Griffin reports that he's already done that.

a15_0042941.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0042941.text: But we'll second it from the crew.

a15_0042941.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0042941.text: I was thinking about your "SPS Thrust On" light problem, and we'd like you to verify the positions of the EMS Function and Mode switches.

a15_0042941.speaker: Irwin
a15_0042941.text: Houston, this is 15. We're starting to configure for charging battery B.

a15_0042941.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0042941.text: I think you may have missed a Verb 66 - right there [in the Flight Plan] just after LM ejection. We need one now.

a15_0042941.speaker: Scott
a15_0042941.text: Roger. In works [meaning we are carrying out the instruction]. [Long pause.]

a15_0042941.speaker: Scott
a15_0042941.text: And, Houston, 15. The S-IVB looks nice and stable out there. You're Go for your basic maneuver as far as we're concerned.

a15_0042941.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0042941.text: Okay, fine. We're just about to ask you on that.

a15_0042941.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0042941.text: It[the evasive burn]'ll be started at 4:40 [GET].

a15_0042941.speaker: Scott
a15_0042941.text: Roger; 4:40. [Pause.] And we're just about 90 degrees abeam.

a15_0044045.speaker: Scott
a15_0044045.text: Okay, Houston. We see the S-IVB moving very slowly.

a15_0044517.speaker: Irwin
a15_0044517.text: Do you want us to terminate the charge when - when I'm reading 39.5 [volts]?

a15_0044517.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0044517.text: Stand by. [Pause.] Ah, Jim, we'll call you, based on integrated amp-hours that we figure out down here.

a15_0044807.speaker: Scott
a15_0044807.text: Okay; we have a LM/CM Delta-P of plus .2 at the present time.

a15_0045130.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0045130.text: We need to have you re - reinitialize the High Gain [antenna]. We'd like you to set Pitch, [to] minus 30 [degrees]; Yaw, plus 98 [degrees]; and go to Reacq. Over.

a15_0045130.speaker: Worden
a15_0045130.text: Roger. We copied minus 30 and plus 98.

a15_0050031.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0050031.text: At 5:01:20, we'll be starting a LOX dump through the S-IVB engine. And we have the REFSMMAT when you're ready for it - for the P52.

a15_0050031.speaker: Worden
a15_0050031.text: Okay. [Do] you want P00 and Accept?

a15_0050437.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0050437.text: 15, Houston, the computer is yours. You have a new REFSMMAT and the trunnion bias has been zeroed.

a15_0052553.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0052553.text: When you get a free moment, we have a reasonably short procedure in align with checking out the SPS Thrust light. Over.

a15_0052553.speaker: Irwin
a15_0052553.text: Go ahead, Gordo. Ready to copy.

a15_0052553.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0052553.text: Okay. We see you're starting the P52 [platform realignment program]. This shouldn't interfere, but it - We can wait if you wish.

a15_0052553.speaker: Irwin
a15_0052553.text: I was just going to copy the procedure, and we'll do it later.

a15_0052553.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0052553.text: Okay. It's - it's the kind of thing we have to watch on the ground as you do it, so it's probably not even worth writing down.

a15_0052553.speaker: Irwin
a15_0052553.text: Okay. Let's wait then until after [the] P52 [is finished].

a15_0052913.speaker: Worden
a15_0052913.text: Okay, Gordo. If you're reading, I've got the gyro torquing angles up [on the DSKY display] and I'll torque them out at 5:30.

a15_0052913.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0052913.text: Okay; we're reading the DSKY [via telemetry]. Understand [you will torque the platform around to the correct alignment at] 5:30.

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Standing by with a lift-off plus 15 abort PAD.

a15_0055159.speaker: Irwin
a15_0055159.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_0055159.speaker: Irwin
a15_0055159.text: Okay, Gordo. I'm standing by for the PAD.

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: Okay. It's GET of ignition [is a time] of 015:00. Delta-V T , 4926; minus 175; 051:20. Go ahead.

a15_0055159.speaker: Irwin
a15_0055159.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_0055159.speaker: Irwin
a15_0055159.text: All right, Gordo, give me that - it's a P37 PAD that you have there?

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: That's right, Jim. I should have used that terminology.

a15_0055159.speaker: Irwin
a15_0055159.text: Go ahead.

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: Okay; 015:00, time of ignition; 4926; longitude is minus 175, and GET for 400K is 051:20. Over.

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: That's correct, Jim. [Long pause.]

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: Go ahead. [Long pause.]

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: 15, Houston. When you - when ya'll get a chance, we'd like to go with this SPS Thrust light check.

a15_0055159.speaker: Worden
a15_0055159.text: Okay, Gordo. I'm over in the left couch now; let's go ahead and try it.

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: Okay. Stand by; I'll get everybody watching [their consoles, in Mission Control]. Okay. First of all, I'd like to be sure that both the Pilot Valve circuit breakers on panel 8 [to the far left of the Main Display Console] and both Delta-V Thrust switches are Off - both circuit breakers.

a15_0055159.speaker: Worden
a15_0055159.text: Okay, Houston. Both Pilot Valves [circuit breakers] are Open, and the Delta-V Thrust switches are Off.

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: Okay. Now when we do the following steps, we'd like you to watch the SPS Thrust light, and watch it for changes either going out or changes in intensity. We're trying to determine if it's a high resistance or a low resistance short; and if it gets brighter, that'll tell us something about this short with any one of these actions.

a15_0055159.speaker: Worden
a15_0055159.text: Okay.

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: Okay. First item is: put the thrust hand controller clockwise, and watch the light.

a15_0055159.speaker: Worden
a15_0055159.text: Ah, Gordo. Do you mean the THC, the translation hand controller?

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: Rog. That's what I meant. THC, clockwise.

a15_0055159.speaker: Worden
a15_0055159.text: Okay. We'll go clockwise with it. We're clockwise, and no change.

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: Okay. Put the THC back to neutral.

a15_0055159.speaker: Worden
a15_0055159.text: Rog. [Pause.]

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: Okay. SPS Thrust switch, Direct On.

a15_0055159.speaker: Worden
a15_0055159.text: Okay. SPS Thrust, Direct On.

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: And any change in the light?

a15_0055159.speaker: Worden
a15_0055159.text: I didn't see any change. And it's Off.

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: Okay. Back to Normal.

a15_0055159.speaker: Worden
a15_0055159.text: Rog. Back to Normal.

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: Okay. We'd like you to do the first part of an EMS Delta-V check - from page G2-5 and just the first steps - down to the - you don't have to do the bias check, but the first six steps there.

a15_0055159.speaker: Worden
a15_0055159.text: Right. [Pause.]

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: [The] idea here is to check for a possible short in the Delta-V test circuits. It might be causing the light [to come] on. [Long pause.]

a15_0055159.speaker: Worden
a15_0055159.text: Okay, Gordo. That part of the check's been run and it's shut off at a minus 21.4 in ten seconds, and the SPS light - the SPS Thrust light got distinctly brighter during the decelerat... or during the acceleration period.

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: Roger, Al, copy. And I'll see if there is anything else they [the engineers in Mission Control] want to do here.

a15_0055159.speaker: Worden
a15_0055159.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_0055159.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0055159.text: Okay, Al. I guess no more questions right now. We'll mull that over a little bit.

a15_0055159.speaker: Worden
a15_0055159.text: Okay, Gordo.

a15_0061600.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0061600.text: I've got a short update for your erasable load update as contained in the back of the G&C Checklist. Three num - three addresses to update. Over.

a15_0061600.speaker: Worden
a15_0061600.text: Okay, Gordo; go ahead. I've got the G&C Checklist out now.

a15_0061600.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0061600.text: Okay; on that 9-4, the first one is changing NBD-X, the static drift compensation for the X-gyro. Under load Alpha, the octal ID number 11, which now reads 77332, change that to 00377. Over.

a15_0061600.speaker: Worden
a15_0061600.text: Understand. That's Alpha octal ID 11, where it now says 77332, change that to read 00377.

a15_0061600.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0061600.text: That's affirmative. And on load Bravo, IDs four and five are changed. This changes T ephem[erides] to correspond with actual lift-off. And load 4, which is now 30560, change that to 32251. And while you're still writing, change the next one, load - or ID number 5, from 10000 to 26157.

a15_0061600.speaker: Worden
a15_0061600.text: Roger; understand. That's column Bravo, IDs 4 and 5, change 4 to 32251, and 5 to 26157.

a15_0061600.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0061600.text: That's correct. That's - that takes care of it, Al.

a15_0061600.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0061600.text: This is Apollo Control. Apollo 15 now 27,621 nautical miles [51,154 km] out from Earth. Velocity now 11,498 feet per second [3,506 m/s]. Spacecraft communicator Gordon Fullerton passed up some troubleshooting procedures on the apparent short circuits that are causing some spurious indications not only in the spacecraft cockpit, but also here in the Control Center through telemetry. The pilot valves were opened, the Delta-V lights turned off on the EMS, or the Entry Monitor System, thrust controller was rotated clockwise and back to neutral, The SPS Thrust switch was turned to Direct On and the

a15_0064349.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0064349.text: If you're not using the optics, we suggest you zero them; they're - we noticed them drifting.

a15_0064349.speaker: Scott
a15_0064349.text: We've been taking turns looking at the Earth through the telescope. It's a fantastic sight.

a15_0064349.speaker: Scott
a15_0064349.text: As a matter of fact, this sure would be a neat place for a space station out here.

a15_0073459.speaker: Henize
a15_0073459.text: Hey, the results that we got out of that last test procedure - didn't solve many problems for us. I guess the best we found out was that we don't have a simple problem like a stuck EMS relay. And there's a lot of thinking going on down here, and at the present time, we line up three - three possibilities, depending on where the [electrical] ground is in the system. And the first one is that it's still a ground that simply turns on the light and affects nothing else. Second possibility, that it's a ground that's going to light the engine early when you put on the Delta-V Thrust switches. And th

a15_0074051.speaker: Scott
a15_0074051.text: You have down [in the Flight Plan] a null bias check [of the EMS]. Delta-V with .9.

a15_0075226.speaker: Henize
a15_0075226.text: We're seeing a low O 2 repress package pressure down here. Okay; we'll take that back. We have a suspicion that we have a low O 2 repress package, and I would like to have an onboard readout of your pressure there.

a15_0075226.speaker: Scott
a15_0075226.text: Houston, it is a little low. We just never finished filling it after we pressurized the tunnel.

a15_0090959.speaker: Henize
a15_0090959.text: Hey, would you ask Al to give us about 3 seconds on the Noun 49, so we can read them out down here.

a15_0091943.speaker: Henize
a15_0091943.text: 15, this is Houston with an update for your procedures for UV photos.

a15_0091943.speaker: Irwin
a15_0091943.text: And, Houston, that last Noun 49 looked like 60 and 16.

a15_0092236.speaker: Worden
a15_0092236.text: Houston, this is 15. Ready on that update concerning the UV photos.

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: Roger. On page 3-15 in the Flight Plan, in the left column, about the 17th line down, we have 2 frames with filter number 2.

a15_0092236.speaker: Worden
a15_0092236.text: I found that line.

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: Roger. And instead of 2 frames at 20 seconds, we would like one frame at 20 seconds; and we would like a second frame at 2 seconds. [Pause.]

a15_0092236.speaker: Worden
a15_0092236.text: Roger. I copy one at 20 seconds and one at 2 seconds.

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: Roger. The reason for that is that they have recently measured a secondary light leak in that filter, and they need a - two different exposures like this to really separate the two peaks in the filter transmissitivity. [Pause.] Incidentally, this is going to pertain to all the UV photography of the Earth on down the line, but we'll - we'll update it as we come to them. [Long pause.]

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: And, 15. We have a preliminary procedure about to come up to you to see if we can isolate whether this ground in the SPS system is in bank A or bank B. And that'll be coming up in just a few minutes. We...

a15_0092236.speaker: Worden
a15_0092236.text: Okay. I understand.

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: And we would like to do that before we start the UV photography.

a15_0092236.speaker: Worden
a15_0092236.text: Very well.

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: 15, this is Houston. I have the preliminary procedure I spoke about and we're hoping you might be able to do it while Al works with the P23.

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: Okay; go ahead.

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: You might refer, if you want to see what's going on, to Drawing 8.9 down in area E-3. We're playing with the - Delta-V Thrust switch, and the idea is this: First of all, let's open the - the Group 5 circuit breakers on panel 229, both Main A and Main B. That's a back-up to the SPS Pilot Valves on Panel 8, which we also want open. Verify that.

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: Okay. Group 5, Main A and Main B on 229. Stand by.

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: Okay, both those are open.

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: Roger. We've verified Group 5, both open; and the SPS Pilot Valves both open. Then, we'd like to take the Delta-V Thrust A switch and try to balance it right in a center position. Tease it back and forth a little bit to see if you can get any flickering in the SPS Thrust - Thrust On light.

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: Okay. Stand by.

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: Ah, Jim, let's - let's hold up a little bit before we do that. We don't - We're not all set up down here to watch that also. So let's - let me read on through the procedure.

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: Okeydoke.

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: If the light does flicker, of course, that's going to isolate, in this case, if we were playing with - with the Delta-V Thrust A switch, that'll isolate the problem into the - to the A bank of valves. If we don't see any flicker, then we'll go ahead and try it with the B - well, with the B bank. Actually, we would like to go ahead and do it with the B bank also. So, stand by a moment.

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: Okay, understand. Standing by. [Pause.]

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: Eight - 8.9-E3.

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: We'd like to have a [setting of the] High Gain [antenna], [to] Medium [beamwidth].

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: High Gain, Medium.

a15_0092236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0092236.text: [Garble].

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: No. No. It's not under EMS.

a15_0092236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0092236.text: [Garble].

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: What?

a15_0092236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0092236.text: [Garble].

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: No, we're not. We're talking about Group 5, on 229.

a15_0092236.speaker: Worden
a15_0092236.text: [Garble].

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: No, he's also - he's talking about pilot valves.

a15_0092236.speaker: Worden
a15_0092236.text: Oh, he is? [Garble] circuit breakers [garble]. That light.

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: Huh! EPS Group 3. He said Group 5.

a15_0092236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0092236.text: He said Group 5?

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: Group 5. It's Group 3 here. That's not what he's working on. He's working on the Delta-V thrust. 8.9-E3.

a15_0092236.speaker: Worden
a15_0092236.text: 229, GROUP 3.

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: Huh!

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: 15, this is Houston. We're ready to go ahead. Verify again the Group 5 breakers and the SPS Pilot Valve breakers, and then let's tease that Delta-V Thrust A switch. Try to balance it in a central position.

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: Okay. Will do. We - we note that drawing 8.9 Echo 3 doesn't seem to fit what you're doing. [Long pause.]

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: Actually, it's area Echo 3 and 4, and it simply shows you the Delta-V Thrust switches there.

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: Oh, okay. Okay.

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: Shoot!

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: The light has a contact, whether that switch is On or Off and we would like to balance it half way between so that we don't have a contact.

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: Okay. Here goes Delta-V [switch] A now. [Pause.] Okay, A is up and on, and the SPS Thrust light is off. [Long pause.]

a15_0092236.speaker: Worden
a15_0092236.text: It is? Gee! Good grief!

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: Would you confirm that the Delta-V Thrust A switch is up and the light went out. Is that correct?

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: That's correct. It's still in the up and On position, and when I went to the On position, the light went out.

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: Thank you.

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: I'll just leave it there while you think about it.

a15_0092236.speaker: Henize
a15_0092236.text: Thank you. That's - stand by.

a15_0092236.speaker: Worden
a15_0092236.text: Wonder why it'll do that?

a15_0092236.speaker: Scott
a15_0092236.text: [Snicker.] I can only think of one reason - that it's really in backwards. Did you cycle those switches [garble], Jim?

a15_0093448.speaker: Henize
a15_0093448.text: 15, this is Houston. We'd like to feel our way ahead here, and we'd like to have you put Delta-V Thrust A back to Off.

a15_0093448.speaker: Scott
a15_0093448.text: A is Off, and the light remains off.

a15_0093448.speaker: Worden
a15_0093448.text: Huh! Is the light still off?

a15_0093448.speaker: Scott
a15_0093448.text: It's a switch problem. Yes, the light's still off. I bet it was a - when we did that Sep, bet we got a little solder ball in that switch or something.

a15_0093448.speaker: Henize
a15_0093448.text: 15, this is Houston. Our telemetry confirms both of your observations, and we would now like to have you cycle [switch] Bravo.

a15_0093448.speaker: Scott
a15_0093448.text: Roger. [Pause.] Bravo is up and On; the light is off. [Pause.] Now Bravo is Off and the light remains off.

a15_0093448.speaker: Scott
a15_0093448.text: All we got to do is change out that switch.

a15_0093448.speaker: Worden
a15_0093448.text: Yes. All we got to do is bring that bank on late, and turn it off early.

a15_0093448.speaker: Scott
a15_0093448.text: Yes, unless you get a contact in there, we wouldn't have the ignition signal, though.

a15_0093448.speaker: Henize
a15_0093448.text: 15, we'll sit tight and think about that for a while, thank you.

a15_0094421.speaker: Henize
a15_0094421.text: 15, this is Houston. As a final check as to what's happening in that switch, we'd like to have you tap around the Delta-V Thrust switches a bit. See if any light flickering comes on.

a15_0094421.speaker: Scott
a15_0094421.text: Would you believe? It came on.

a15_0094421.speaker: Henize
a15_0094421.text: We copy, and we saw it down here. [Pause.] Okay. With the light on now, let's cycle Bravo on and try to tease it in the middle if it stays on.

a15_0094421.speaker: Scott
a15_0094421.text: Okay. No change at all with the Bravo on, cycling several times through the middle.

a15_0094421.speaker: Henize
a15_0094421.text: We copy. [Pause.] Okay. Leave Bravo Off, and let's cycle A again.

a15_0094421.speaker: Scott
a15_0094421.text: Okay. Right in the center of - the contacts with A, right between the two, I can get the light to go out. But now, when I go on up - up and On, the light comes on again. And now, I've come back to the Off position, and the light's off. So, I think you've isolated your problem.

a15_0094421.speaker: Worden
a15_0094421.text: Think so, too. That just says we're going to have to use - ban - bank B this time.

a15_0094847.speaker: Henize
a15_0094847.text: 15, this is Houston. We're willing to stop playing with the - with the light problem at the present time. We'd like to verify that both Delta-V Thrust switches are Off. And we'd like to have the Group 5 circuit breakers both Closed, but please keep the Pilot Valve circuit breakers Open.

a15_0094847.speaker: Scott
a15_0094847.text: Okay. Delta-V Thrust verified Off. Pilot Valves verified Open, and we'll Close the Group 5s.

a15_0095717.speaker: Henize
a15_0095717.text: Let's - summarize our situation with that - with that Thrust - Thrust On light. The telemetry we got down here - we actually have two lights which show up in that area, E-4 and 5 on diagram 8.9 - gave us some rather confusing data that we don't understand yet, but we'll be working on it. But we - we do feel confident enough that there's no need to fire the engine at the present time, and since the midcourse [correction number] 1 is a correction of 2.8 feet per second we don't think that we'll be having a midcourse 1. For your information, at the present time, midcourse 2 looks about like 5.0 f

a15_0095717.speaker: Scott
a15_0095717.text: Okay; understand. We'll just hold tight; skip midcourse 1; stand by for [midcourse correction] 2.

a15_0095717.speaker: Henize
a15_0095717.text: Roger. [Pause.] And, 15, be advised we'll have a Flight Plan update in the near future.

a15_0095717.speaker: Scott
a15_0095717.text: Roger. [Pause.] That was a pretty good S-IVB, wasn't it?

a15_0095717.speaker: Henize
a15_0095717.text: Hey, and you can tell Al up there that those look like real good P23 markings.

a15_0095717.speaker: Scott
a15_0095717.text: Okay. He's glad to hear that.

a15_0100550.speaker: Henize
a15_0100550.text: 15, if you'll give us Accept, we'll send up a new state vector.

a15_0100550.speaker: Worden
a15_0100550.text: Okay. You have P00 and Accept.

a15_0100957.speaker: Henize
a15_0100957.text: 15, you can have your computer back. [Pause.]

a15_0103010.speaker: Irwin
a15_0103010.text: Rog, Karl. Would you go back and recheck the attitude - the attitude for the UV pictures of the Moon?

a15_0103010.speaker: Henize
a15_0103010.text: Stand by. We'll check that. The numbers you have in the DSKY are what we have in the Flight Plan. [Pause.]

a15_0103010.speaker: Irwin
a15_0103010.text: Houston, 15. As you were on that. Looks like we are all set up.

a15_0103535.speaker: Henize
a15_0103535.text: 15, this is Houston. Could we bring up the High Gain [Antenna] with the angles in the Flight Plan?

a15_0103535.speaker: Worden
a15_0103535.text: What are the angles in the Flight Plan? Isn't that where we're supposed to do this?

a15_0103931.speaker: Henize
a15_0103931.text: 15, This is Houston. I have a Flight Plan update whenever you can copy it - to be followed by a P27 update and P37 block data.

a15_0103931.speaker: Irwin
a15_0103931.text: Okay, Karl. I'm [garble] you a Flight Plan.

a15_0103931.speaker: Henize
a15_0103931.text: Okay. As is obvious [because of the cancelled midcourse correction maneuver], you can delete all of the midcourse activities, beginning there at 11:21, running through the burn status report. And the other activities this evening can be moved up so that you can go to bed as early as 12 hours GET, if you wish. A couple of notes here is that we do want you to stay up to 12 hours in order that we can finish a battery charge that's in progress. And, also, that waste water dump; be sure to - to do the water dump before you start PTC [Passive Thermal Control].

a15_0103931.speaker: Henize
a15_0103931.text: And, I'm - I've got a P37 for you - plus 25 hours, if you're ready.

a15_0103931.speaker: Irwin
a15_0103931.text: I'm ready for the P37 for 25 hours.

a15_0103931.speaker: Henize
a15_0103931.text: That's all correct. The next one I have is a P27 update.

a15_0103931.speaker: Irwin
a15_0103931.text: Okay; I'm ready on the P27.

a15_0103931.speaker: Henize
a15_0103931.text: That's all correct. Thank you, Jim.

a15_0111400.speaker: Worden
a15_0111400.text: Roger, Karl. We've got the gyro torquing angles up for the P52. And we'll torque them out on the minute.

a15_0111400.speaker: Irwin
a15_0111400.text: And, Houston, this is 15 now. Looking at the Oxidizer Pressure on the SPS, looks like it's a little low; I just wondered what you all are reading down there? [Long pause.]

a15_0111400.speaker: Henize
a15_0111400.text: 15, this is Houston. We're reading a pressure of 168 [psi] down here on the SPS Oxidizer and that's normal at this time. We expect it to be a bit low because of absorption in the helium.

a15_0111400.speaker: Henize
a15_0111400.text: And, 15, this is Houston. When you doff your biomed harnesses, we'd very much like to have you double check those sensors. We've been getting poor readings in respiration from all three of you, and we'd like to have you report any anomalies in - in how they're rigged on you.

a15_0111400.speaker: Henize
a15_0111400.text: You can send that down with the evening report.

a15_0113523.speaker: MCC
a15_0113523.text: Right on. CapCom's hearing it. Just a little fainter than it was.

a15_0113811.speaker: Henize
a15_0113811.text: 15, this is Houston. Anytime you have the time to copy down about six lines of information, I could give you a general update on the UV filter photography. [Pause.]

a15_0113811.speaker: Scott
a15_0113811.text: Okay; stand by one, Karl. [Long pause.]

a15_0113811.speaker: Henize
a15_0113811.text: And, 15, we'd like to have you verify that the waste water dump has been terminated.

a15_0113811.speaker: Irwin
a15_0113811.text: Okay, Karl; I'm ready to copy [the] Flight Plan change relative to the UV [photography].

a15_0113811.speaker: Henize
a15_0113811.text: Roger. The change is the same as I gave you before. When you're shooting the Earth, two frames with filter 2, at - what was formerly 2 frames with filter 2, exposure time 20 seconds, in the future, it will be one frame, filter 2 with an exposure time of 20 seconds. And one frame, filter 2, exposure time 2 seconds. And the following is the places that this occurs in the Flight Plan in the future. First is page 3-38, line 17. I believe we've probably passed that one already. The next one is - Negative, we haven't passed that one yet. The next one is page 3-57, line 16. The third is page 3-167 -

a15_0113811.speaker: Irwin
a15_0113811.text: Roger. I copied all that, Karl.

a15_0114404.speaker: Worden
a15_0114404.text: Okay, Karl. Would you check the page for PTC, and let me know what that Verb 49 attitude is? It says, Verb 49 maneuver to PTC, Noun 20, 090 and 000. [Long pause.]

a15_0114404.speaker: Henize
a15_0114404.text: 15, this is Houston. I understand that you used the present roll [angle]. The one you have now, I believe, is 169.6 [degrees] and, then, the other two numbers give you pitch and yaw.

a15_0114404.speaker: Worden
a15_0114404.text: Affirm. Roger, Karl; thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_0114404.speaker: Worden
a15_0114404.text: And, Houston, 15; we're maneuvering to PTC attitude now.

a15_0114404.speaker: Henize
a15_0114404.text: 15, this is Houston. We'd like to have a LM/CM Delta-P whenever you can check that number for us?

a15_0114404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0114404.text: Okay, Houston; the Delta-P is point - plus .4 and we're going to secure the High Gain and give you Omni Bravo. [Pause.]

a15_0114404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0114404.text: And, Houston, we're doing an O 2 purge on the fuel cell. Presently purging fuel cell 3, and I'm getting a Fuel Cell 3 caution light.

a15_0114404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0114404.text: This is Apollo Control at 11 hours, 50 minutes. Apollo 15 is 56,527 nautical miles [104,688 km] from Earth. Velocity; 7,844 feet per second [2,391 m/s].

a15_0114404.speaker: Henize
a15_0114404.text: 15, this is Houston; we'd like to have Omni Charlie. [Long pause.]

a15_0114404.speaker: Henize
a15_0114404.text: Roger. That last comment was to give us Omni Charlie [instead of Omni Bravo].

a15_0120454.speaker: Henize
a15_0120454.text: Your spacecraft [rotation] rates are low enough now to spin up for PTC, but we'd like for you to verify first that all of your dumping has been finished. [Pause.]

a15_0120454.speaker: Worden
a15_0120454.text: Karl, we'll hold off for a little bit here and finish up the dumping before we go into PTC.

a15_0120454.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0120454.text: This is Apollo Control at 12 hours, 6 minutes. The spacecraft rate of revolution that we've set up for this Passive Thermal Control throughout the rest period is 3 tenths of a degree per second. This will provide thermal balance for the spacecraft and its systems during the rest period. Apollo 15 now 57,742 nautical miles [106,938 km] from Earth, travelling at a velocity of 7,745 feet per second [2,361 m/s].

a15_0121839.speaker: Henize
a15_0121839.text: 15, this is Houston. In connection with the respiration sensor problem, we'd like for you to - go through a special procedure for us before you - you doff your biomed harnesses.

a15_0121839.speaker: Scott
a15_0121839.text: Okay. Stand by one, Karl. [Long pause.]

a15_0121839.speaker: Scott
a15_0121839.text: Okay, Houston; ready to copy special procedure.

a15_0121839.speaker: Henize
a15_0121839.text: I'm sorry. I didn't - I don't think it needs copying, but we'd like all three of you - when you go into the doffing phase here, we'd like all three of you to pull off the impedance pneumograms. Those are the two respiration sensors back on your kidneys there. Pull them off, and let any - let any trapped air get out, and then reseal them and give us a couple minutes of read-out down here to see if that improves the situation.

a15_0121839.speaker: Henize
a15_0121839.text: 15, this is Houston. We can terminate the battery Bravo charging.

a15_0122914.speaker: Worden
a15_0122914.text: Houston, this is 15. We've terminated the charge on battery B.

a15_0122914.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0122914.text: This is Apollo Control at 12 hours, 40 minutes. Apollo 15 has just passed the 60,000 [nautical] mile [111,120 km] mark outbound to the Moon. Distance now 60,188 nautical miles [111,468 km]. Velocity; 7,555 feet per second [2,303 m/s].

a15_0130309.speaker: Worden
a15_0130309.text: Okay, Karlos. Looks like we're getting organized, and we'll go ahead with the PTC now. Do you have any preference on which [RCS] jets to use?

a15_0130309.speaker: Henize
a15_0130309.text: Roger. We'd like to use the B/D jets.

a15_0130309.speaker: Worden
a15_0130309.text: Understand. B/Ds. I guess that would be B-2, D-2, huh?

a15_0130309.speaker: Worden
a15_0130309.text: Guess that means you want us to use B-2 and D-2, huh?

a15_0130309.speaker: Henize
a15_0130309.text: That's affirmative. And we'd like you to - to hold the spin-up until we - Okay; we're able to give you a Go for spin-up now.

a15_0130309.speaker: Worden
a15_0130309.text: Okay; understand the rates are favorable for a spin-up DAP.

a15_0130819.speaker: Worden
a15_0130819.text: Okay, Karl, this is Apollo 15. If the rates still look good down there, we're ready to go to PTC.

a15_0130819.speaker: Henize
a15_0130819.text: That's affirmative, Al. Go ahead and spin her up. [Pause.]

a15_0130819.speaker: Henize
a15_0130819.text: We'd like to select Omni Bravo now. [Pause.]

a15_0132540.speaker: Henize
a15_0132540.text: 15, this is Houston. How's the view up there?

a15_0132540.speaker: Worden
a15_0132540.text: Houston, 15. It is fantastic, Karl. You ought to be here, man.

a15_0132540.speaker: Henize
a15_0132540.text: I'm eating my heart out. [Long pause.]

a15_0132540.speaker: Scott
a15_0132540.text: Karl, I think you said that just to be mean. [Long pause.]

a15_0132540.speaker: Henize
a15_0132540.text: And how does 13 hours of continuous zero-g feel? [Pause.]

a15_0132540.speaker: Scott
a15_0132540.text: Well, I think everybody is pretty well adjusted, Karl; no problems at all, and we've finished dinner and we're happy. [Pause.]

a15_0133748.speaker: Henize
a15_0133748.text: 15, this is Houston. On your PTC, when it started out, it looked okay; but we find that it's diverging now, and we're going to have to reinitialize it. We suggest this time around that we use a - a rate of .375 [degrees per second] in Noun 79, that might help.

a15_0135154.speaker: Worden
a15_0135154.text: Roger, Karl. When the rates look like they're down again, we'll try PTC again.

a15_0135154.speaker: Henize
a15_0135154.text: Roger. We'd like to have you verify that all the vents are secured before we spin it up again.

a15_0135154.speaker: Henize
a15_0135154.text: And, 15, in this damping process, we'd like to make sure that all of the jets on two adjacent quads are disabled.

a15_0135154.speaker: Henize
a15_0135154.text: And, 15, as a part of trying to figure out what went wrong with that first PTC, we'd like to know whether or not you went into any [gymnastic] exercise period after - after we spun it up.

a15_0135154.speaker: Scott
a15_0135154.text: And, Houston, the LMP and CDR have recycled their impedance pneumograms. You can give us a word if you see - if you see any improvement in data. [Long pause.]

a15_0135154.speaker: Henize
a15_0135154.text: Dave, we missed that last transmission. Could you say again?

a15_0135154.speaker: Scott
a15_0135154.text: Rog. The LMP and CDR have recycled the impedance pneumogram, and we just wondered if you'd seen any improvement in the data [coming from it].

a15_0135154.speaker: Henize
