a15_0135154.text: Okay; he[SURGEON]'s looking at it now, and he says, yes, it has improved. [Long pause.]

a15_0135154.speaker: Henize
a15_0135154.text: 15, the Surgeon says it's okay for the CDR and the CMP to doff their biomed harnesses now. Thank you.

a15_0135154.speaker: Scott
a15_0135154.text: Okay. Did that - did that recycling [of the biomedical sensors] do any good?

a15_0135154.speaker: Henize
a15_0135154.text: Roger. The recycling cleared up the respiration data we have down here very nicely.

a15_0140339.speaker: Henize
a15_0140339.text: 15, this is Houston. I'm sorry to tell you that that spin-up didn't work very well. We're going to have to reinitialize again. [Long pause.]

a15_0140339.speaker: Worden
a15_0140339.text: Okay, Houston. We'll try it again.

a15_0140339.speaker: Worden
a15_0140339.text: Yeah, Karl, I think if there was a problem that time, it was because I hesitated just momentarily, thinking I had it Free, and I ended up in Hold.

a15_0140339.speaker: Henize
a15_0140339.text: Ah ha, thanks; thanks for the information.

a15_0140339.speaker: Henize
a15_0140339.text: And, 15, we think that your jet configurations were all okay that time around, but we'd like to confirm that, during damping, you disable all jets on two adjacent quads, and then for the spin-up, you use only B-2 and D-2.

a15_0141534.speaker: Henize
a15_0141534.text: 15, this is Houston. Everything down here looks Go for the spinup.

a15_0141534.speaker: Worden
a15_0141534.text: Okay, Karl. We'll try it once more.

a15_0141534.speaker: Henize
a15_0141534.text: 15, that looked like a very good start.

a15_0142541.speaker: Henize
a15_0142541.text: It looks like we've got it pretty well wrapped up for your rest period. We've got three or four small items to remind you here. Crew status report is outstanding; onboard readouts, we'd like; and whenever your ready, we're ready for an E-memory dump.

a15_0142541.speaker: Scott
a15_0142541.text: Okay. We're about that point of the checklist, and we'll give you the whole page at one time. Stand by one.

a15_0142541.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0142541.text: This is Apollo Control at 14 hours, 28 minutes. As the Apollo 15 crew prepares to wind up a long day, the spacecraft is 67,080 nautical miles [124,232 km] from Earth. Velocity; 6,992 feet per second [2,131 m/s].

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: Okay, Houston, 15. We're ready for the E-memory dump for you, if you're ready.

a15_0143244.speaker: Henize
a15_0143244.text: Okay, 15. We're ready to go with it.

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: Okay, here it comes. [Long pause.]

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: And, Houston, 15. We've got the rest of the presleep checklist if you're ready to copy. [Pause.]

a15_0143244.speaker: Henize
a15_0143244.text: Roger, 15. We're ready to copy.

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: Okay. Crew status report: everybody's in good shape; no medication today. Onboard readouts: Bat[tery] C, 37.0 [volts], Pyro Bat A, 37.2; Pyro Bat B, 37.2; RCS [tank] A, 94 [percent]; B ,92; C, 94; D, 94. And the water has been chlorinated; the H 2 fans have been cycled; the valves are all verified; got your E-memory dump [done]. The cabin is at 5.7 [psi]. Direct O 2 [valve] is closed, and I guess we're ready to go to sleep communications configurations. [Long pause.]

a15_0143244.speaker: Henize
a15_0143244.text: Roger, 15. We copy all of that, and the Surgeon has a question about - was - were there any obvious anomalies in the biomed harness?

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: No, as a matter fact, we were just discussing that. Al and I both have taken them off, and the sponges are all still quite damp and have their color and they're all sticking very well. I think the system looks real good.

a15_0143244.speaker: Henize
a15_0143244.text: Very good. Thank you.

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_0143244.speaker: Henize
a15_0143244.text: 15, this is Houston. I guess we're ready to go to the presleep comm configuration.

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: Roger.

a15_0143244.speaker: Henize
a15_0143244.text: Good night.

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: Okay; good night.

a15_0143244.speaker: Henize
a15_0143244.text: Incidentally, 15, your PTC's looking very good.

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: Oh, that's good. [Long pause.]

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: By the way, Karl, it's about time for you to get some sleep too, isn't it?

a15_0143244.speaker: Henize
a15_0143244.text: Rog. It's been a long day for all of us.

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: Yeah, I think you're a couple - three hours ahead of us.

a15_0143244.speaker: Henize
a15_0143244.text: Not that much.

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: Houston, 15. One more thing here. We note on page 1-24 of the Systems book in the comm sleep configuration, you've got the S-band Norm Voice [correcting himself] Norm Mode Voice, Off. Is that correct?

a15_0143244.speaker: Henize
a15_0143244.text: 15, this is Houston. The noise was very bad then; are you reading me?

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: Okay, I'm reading you 5 by. Just had a question to verify the sleep configuration of the S-band. Is Mode Voice to Off?

a15_0143244.speaker: Henize
a15_0143244.text: That's affirmative.

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: That gives [garble] to Down Voice [Back-up].

a15_0143244.speaker: Henize
a15_0143244.text: That's affirmative.

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: Okay.

a15_0143244.speaker: Henize
a15_0143244.text: That gives us a little cleaner TM [telemetry].

a15_0143244.speaker: Scott
a15_0143244.text: Roger.

a15_0143244.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0143244.text: This is Apollo Control at 14 hours, 40 minutes, and the crew has just turned the Voice Off. The light has gone out on the INCO's [Instrumentation and Communications Officer] console indicating the crew has thrown the switch.

a15_0252756.speaker: Irwin
a15_0252756.text: Houston, Apollo 15. [Long pause.]

a15_0252756.speaker: Allen
a15_0252756.text: Hello, Endeavour, this is Houston.

a15_0252756.speaker: Irwin
a15_0252756.text: Good morning, Joe.

a15_0252756.speaker: Allen
a15_0252756.text: Good morning, Troops. Has the Sun come up, up there?

a15_0252756.speaker: Irwin
a15_0252756.text: Oh, yes; very bright all the way. Ready to give you our status here.

a15_0252756.speaker: Allen
a15_0252756.text: Roger, Dave. We're standing by.

a15_0252756.speaker: Irwin
a15_0252756.text: Okay. We all figure we had 8 hours. Dave figures he got his in about three [segments]; Alfred, two; and [garble] about five.

a15_0252756.speaker: Allen
a15_0252756.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. Stand by on your report. You're broken up at the moment, please.

a15_0252756.speaker: Allen
a15_0252756.text: Dave, this is Houston again. Go ahead. Our comm is not so noisy now. [Pause.]

a15_0252756.speaker: Irwin
a15_0252756.text: Joe, this is Jim.

a15_0252756.speaker: Allen
a15_0252756.text: Roger, Jim. Good morning.

a15_0252756.speaker: Irwin
a15_0252756.text: Good morning. Would it be okay now [to give you the crew status report and comsumables update]?

a15_0252756.speaker: Allen
a15_0252756.text: Rog. You're loud and clear now.

a15_0252756.speaker: Irwin
a15_0252756.text: Okay. We figure we all got about 8 hours of sleep. The duration of that sleep was different. Dave figures he got it in about three segments; Al, about two; and - I had about five different periods of - of deep sleep. On the consumables update at 25:20 [GET]; RCS A, 94 [per cent]; B, 94; C, 94; D, 93. On the H 2 tank 1, 95 [per cent]; 2, 93; and 3, 81. O 2 tank 1, 91 [per cent]; 2, 93; 3, 96. Standing...

a15_0252756.speaker: Allen
a15_0252756.text: Roger, Jim, copy.

a15_0252756.speaker: Irwin
a15_0252756.text: ...by to charge battery A. [Believing his words were lost] And, Joe, I'm standing by to charge battery A.

a15_0252756.speaker: Allen
a15_0252756.text: Okay, Jim. Could you stand by on that? We'd just as leave [sic] you not do it right at the moment.

a15_0252756.speaker: Irwin
a15_0252756.text: Okay. We'll stand by.

a15_0252756.speaker: Allen
a15_0252756.text: Rog. And we'll give you the word when we're ready for that.

a15_0252756.speaker: Irwin
a15_0252756.text: I'll get the radiation report here shortly, and - could you confirm the position that - H 2 Fan 3 should be in?

a15_0252756.speaker: Allen
a15_0252756.text: Rog, Jim. [Pause.] And, it - the H 2 Fan 3 should be Auto.

a15_0252756.speaker: Irwin
a15_0252756.text: Roger. I copy Auto.

a15_0252756.speaker: Allen
a15_0252756.text: Roger.

a15_0253425.speaker: Allen
a15_0253425.text: Jim, this is Houston. [Pause.]

a15_0253425.speaker: Irwin
a15_0253425.text: Go ahead, Joe. [Pause.]

a15_0253425.speaker: Irwin
a15_0253425.text: Go ahead, Joe.

a15_0253425.speaker: Allen
a15_0253425.text: Roger, Jim. Just for your own information here, let me read up to you the CSM consumables that we've generated from the ground.

a15_0253425.speaker: Irwin
a15_0253425.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a15_0253425.speaker: Allen
a15_0253425.text: Okay. At GET 25:09, we had RCS total [quantity remaining], 90 [per cent]; Quad A, 89; [B] 91, 89, 91. H 2 tank 1, 94 per cent, [tank 2] 92 per cent, [tank 3] 81 per cent. O 2 tank 1, 91 per cent, [tank 2] 92 per cent, [tank 3] 97 per cent. So it agrees pretty well with - what you guys are reading.

a15_0253425.speaker: Irwin
a15_0253425.text: Good. Except for the - the RCS quantity.

a15_0253425.speaker: Allen
a15_0253425.text: Rog.

a15_0253425.speaker: Irwin
a15_0253425.text: Okay, Joe. The LM/CM Delta-P is a plus .7.

a15_0253425.speaker: Allen
a15_0253425.text: Roger. Copy, plus .7.

a15_0253425.speaker: Allen
a15_0253425.text: Endeavour, this is Houston.

a15_0253425.speaker: Irwin
a15_0253425.text: Go ahead, Joe.

a15_0253425.speaker: Allen
a15_0253425.text: Jim. Are all three people still there? [Pause.]

a15_0253425.speaker: Irwin
a15_0253425.text: All here, busy doing little things.

a15_0253425.speaker: Allen
a15_0253425.text: Okay, good. I've got some information for you when - you reach a minute - you - you want to listen here, and it concerns our - short - little [electrical] short problem in the switch. [Pause.]

a15_0253425.speaker: Irwin
a15_0253425.text: Okay, Joe. We're all listening. Go ahead.

a15_0253425.speaker: Allen
a15_0253425.text: Roger, guys. We're going to ask you to do a - a test burn on your SPS a little later; in fact, around 28 and a half hours. And - depending upon the results of that, we'll go ahead and do the midcourse, and it'll be a normal midcourse if the burn test doesn't really come off. And it'll be a trim midcourse of some kind if - the test, in fact, does give us an SPS burn. And I'll come up to you a little later on in the day with a set of procedures. There - a long list of them, but you'll be able to use your Launch Checklist for most of them. However, the test burn will mean that we're going to chan

a15_0253425.speaker: Scott
a15_0253425.text: Yes. That's fine, Joe. Can you give us a little run down on what you think the problem is?

a15_0253425.speaker: Allen
a15_0253425.text: Dave, when we get the better Omni in a second, I'll start talking about that. We're about to lose the comm.

a15_0253425.speaker: Scott
a15_0253425.text: Okay.

a15_0254341.speaker: Allen
a15_0254341.text: Endeavour, this is Houston.

a15_0254341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0254341.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a15_0254341.speaker: Allen
a15_0254341.text: Roger, guys. First of all, Dick Gordon's over in the simulator right now running through this SPS burn procedure, and as soon as he says that's okay, we'll read that procedure up to you; I guess. It's not too complicated. Dave, in regard to your last question, very briefly - and I'm sure you guys have been thinking a bit about this yourselves - we're interested in finding out exactly where in your Delta-V Thrust A switch the short seems to be. And we're all of us down here are convinced that it's either in that switch or physically very near that switch. It's important that - that we know wher

a15_0254341.speaker: Scott
a15_0254341.text: Okay. We get the general...

a15_0254341.speaker: Allen
a15_0254341.text: Go ahead, Dave.

a15_0254341.speaker: Scott
a15_0254341.text: We get the general - yeah, we get the general gist of that, Joe. Go ahead.

a15_0254341.speaker: Allen
a15_0254341.text: Okay, Dave. What - what we're going to try to do now is to go - go ahead and do an SPS burn using bank A. And we want that short to be active when we do it. So at some point, we're going to ask you to tap on the panel and try to get the short back for us. We - we show that the light is currently out, and I'm sure that you will confirm that.

a15_0254341.speaker: Scott
a15_0254341.text: That - that's verified.

a15_0254341.speaker: Allen
a15_0254341.text: Rog. Assuming we cannot get the light on again - we think that's unlikely but, if we can't get it on again, we'll delete this particular test and just go ahead and do a - a midcourse - normal midcourse 2 burn and - while we scratch our heads on this other thing.

a15_0254341.speaker: Scott
a15_0254341.text: Okay.

a15_0254341.speaker: Allen
a15_0254341.text: Now. Dave. We've got the changes to the Flight Plan here if your recording secretary is standing by to copy it. [Pause.]

a15_0254341.speaker: Scott
a15_0254341.text: Okay, go ahead. I'm ready Joe.

a15_0254341.speaker: Allen
a15_0254341.text: Rog, Dave. Are you just going to mark up the Flight Plan as I read it to you.

a15_0254341.speaker: Scott
a15_0254341.text: I'd prefer to do it that way.

a15_0254341.speaker: Allen
a15_0254341.text: Ah, Rog. We think that'll be the easiest. And, Jim, are you copying this now.

a15_0254341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0254341.text: I'm standing by, Joe.

a15_0254341.speaker: Allen
a15_0254341.text: Rog. Okay. [Pause.] Okay. We're going to start at 25:05, and we've already deleted the charge-Bat-A line. Then moving on to 26:50, add P52 IMU realign, option 3. [Pause.] Moving to 27...

a15_0254341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0254341.text: I copy.

a15_0254341.speaker: Allen
a15_0254341.text: Okay. Moving to 27:55. [Pause.] Move Delta-V test and null bias check up to 27:00. In other words, just move that line up. And coming up to 28:00 - a little something for you Al - we're going to delete the crew exercise period. [Pause.] And at 28:00, add in midcourse column - MCC-Houston column - uplink to CSM, CSM state vector and Verb 66; update to CSM SPS test maneuver PAD. [Pause.] And at 28:05, [pause] H 2 Purge Line Heaters, On; exit G&N PTC; and maneuver to PAD burn attitude. Have you copied so far?

a15_0254341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0254341.text: Yes, I copied everything to the MCC-H column. Understand the H 2 Purge Line Heater, On; and exit PTC; and maneuver to PAD burn attitude at 28:05.

a15_0254341.speaker: Allen
a15_0254341.text: Roger, Jim. And we're going to lose comm in a minute; I'll be back with you.

a15_0254341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0254341.text: Okay.

a15_0255200.speaker: Allen
a15_0255200.text: Okay, Jim; this is Houston. The comm's back again. How do you read me?

a15_0255200.speaker: Allen
a15_0255200.text: Okay, I'm ready to continue. And we'll pick up at 28:15, with a sextant star check. [Pause.]

a15_0255200.speaker: Allen
a15_0255200.text: Okay; 28:20 I'm - going - going to read to you seven lines of instructions here, and they're all reproduced two pages over in your Flight Plan at 30:30. Your choice as to whether you want to copy them or just look two pages ahead. I'll go ahead and read the lines now.

a15_0255200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0255200.text: Why don't we just look two pages ahead?

a15_0255200.speaker: Allen
a15_0255200.text: Okay. We're going - I want you to move seven of the lines from 30:30 to 28:20. And those seven lines are: The SM Sector 1 SM/AC Power, On; Pan Camera Power, Boost; Map Camera Image Motion, Off; Map Camera, On, Standby; H 2 and O 2 fuel cell purge; waste water dump; and, at 28:35, H 2 Purge Line Heaters, Off. [Pause.]

a15_0255200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0255200.text: Okay, I'll move those - the six steps there...

a15_0255200.speaker: Allen
a15_0255200.text: Roger, Jim. That's right. And the seventh step was at 28:35; you're correct, and that brings us to 28:40, which is SPS burn test. And at 28:41, Verb 66, set CSM state vector into LM state vector. [Pause.]

a15_0255200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0255200.text: Okay. Copied SPS burn test, Verb 66.

a15_0255200.speaker: Allen
a15_0255200.text: Rog. 30:13, delete, and in fact, all the other items from here on out are deletes. And I'll go through them quickly. 30:13, delete battery charge A termination; 30:15, delete H 2 Purge Line Heaters, On; 30:18, delete exit G&N PTC; 30:23, delete 'if SPS MCC required' and the references to pan and mapping cameras - the things, in fact, that you moved ahead; 30:35 delete H 2 and O 2 fuel cell purge and waste water dump; and, finally, 30:50, delete H 2 Purge Line Heaters, Off. Over.

a15_0255200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0255200.text: Okay. I copied all that, Joe. [Long pause.]

a15_0255200.speaker: Allen
a15_0255200.text: Okay, guys. That's all we've got for you for the moment. Dick walked into the MOCR a few minutes ago. He says that the test burn procedure went okay. We're going to look it over one last time and then read the procedures to you.

a15_0260403.speaker: Scott
a15_0260403.text: Houston, this is [Apollo] 15. We're ready to cycle the film in the - the Pan[oramic] and Mapping Cameras. [Long Pause.]

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Endeavour, we're ready when we get the High Gain going here. And I guess we'll have that ready [in] about 5 minutes.

a15_0260403.speaker: Scott
a15_0260403.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Endeavour, this is Houston with your High Gain Antenna angles update.

a15_0260403.speaker: Scott
a15_0260403.text: All right; go ahead, Joe.

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Rog. For the High Gain; Pitch, minus 25 [degrees]; Yaw, 90.

a15_0260403.speaker: Irwin
a15_0260403.text: Okay, minus 25 and 90.

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Roger; and the Omni [Means HGA], Reacq, NBW. [Pause.]

a15_0260403.speaker: Irwin
a15_0260403.text: Roger.

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: And that's just for your information. [Long pause.]

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Jim, if you'll go ahead and set the angles in, we'll give you the cue when we're ready for you to select the High Gain.

a15_0260403.speaker: Irwin
a15_0260403.text: Okay.

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: And it looks like it will be about 10 minutes, I guess.

a15_0260403.speaker: Irwin
a15_0260403.text: Roger.

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Endeavour, this is Houston.

a15_0260403.speaker: Irwin
a15_0260403.text: Go ahead.

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Roger, guys. [I] wondered if you were interested in any breakfast-time news up there?

a15_0260403.speaker: Irwin
a15_0260403.text: Yes, sir; we always are.

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Is it breakfast time?

a15_0260403.speaker: Irwin
a15_0260403.text: It's just about. [Pause.]

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Okay, Troops. Let me start with a special message of Godspeed to the crew of Apollo 15 from President Richard Nixon. And I'll quote directly from him, and there are some words in here that are very well expressed, I think. "Apollo 15 is safely on its way to the Moon, and man is on his way to another step across the threshold of the heavens. Man has always viewed the heavens with humility, but he's viewed them as well with curiosity and with courage; and these defied natural law, drawing man beyond gravity, beyond his fears, and into his dreams, and on to his destiny." And we may be losing comm

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Endeavour, select the High Gain for us, please. [Pause.]

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Okay, guys; suddenly you're back loud and clear, how do you read, Houston? [Pause.]

a15_0260403.speaker: Irwin
a15_0260403.text: Okay, we're [garble]. [Long pause.]

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Hello, Endeavour, this is Houston. Over.

a15_0260403.speaker: Irwin
a15_0260403.text: Go ahead.

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Rog, Jim. Sorry for the inter - interruption there. We had severe noise on our comm momentarily, but it's cleared up now. I'll go ahead with the morning's news and a quote from President Nixon. "The flight of Apollo 15 is the most ambitious exploration yet undertaken in space. Even as it reflects man's restless quest for his future, so it also re-enacts another of the deeper rituals of his bones, not only the compulsion of the inner spirit to know where we are going, but the primal need in man's blood to know from what we have come. We hope, by this journey, to know better the origins of Earth

a15_0260403.speaker: Scott
a15_0260403.text: Rog, Joe.

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Okay. Western Union employees have announced agreement on a new contract that will end a nationwide walkout that began June 1. The 17,000 striking workers will go back on the job Wednesday morning. The Lockheed Company lost two senate vote - votes today in its attempt to avoid bankruptcy by obtaining a $250 million Government loan guarantee. In sporting news or further sporting news, the Oilers traded Jerry LeVias to the San Diego Chargers in exchange for two linemen, defensive lineman Ron Billingsley, and the 300-pound Gene Ferguson. The Oilers will use Ferguson at offensive tackle, it says.

a15_0260403.speaker: Scott
a15_0260403.text: Okay. Thank you very much, Joe, and please express our appreciation to the President and the Vice-President.

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Roger. Sure will. [Long pause.]

a15_0260403.speaker: Allen
a15_0260403.text: Endeavour, Houston. Go to Auto Track for us now, please, and we're going to wait for another rev before we start to cycle those cameras. [Pause.]

a15_0260403.speaker: Scott
a15_0260403.text: Okay, Joe. Auto Track.

a15_0262000.speaker: Allen
a15_0262000.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. We'll be coming up on your camera cycling in about 15 minutes. It's for your own planning, and we'll cue you when we're ready for that.

a15_0262844.speaker: Allen
a15_0262844.text: Endeavour, could you select your Reacq mode, now for us please.

a15_0263218.speaker: Allen
a15_0263218.text: Okay, Endeavour; this is Houston. And we're ready for the camera cycling procedure now.

a15_0263512.speaker: Allen
a15_0263512.text: 15, this is Houston. If we're going to complete the camera cycling on this rev[olution of the spacecraft], I guess we'd better get started on that.

a15_0263512.speaker: Scott
a15_0263512.text: Yeah, we're in the process, Joe.

a15_0263512.speaker: Worden
a15_0263512.text: Okay; if you're reading all the te - good telemetry down there, Joe, we'll be glad to cycle this thing.

a15_0263512.speaker: Allen
a15_0263512.text: Roger, Al. Go ahead. But stand - stand by. Sorry; stand by.

a15_0263512.speaker: Allen
a15_0263512.text: We're not getting high-bit-rate data yet.

a15_0263512.speaker: Worden
a15_0263512.text: Okay; we'll stand by for your cue then, Joe. [Long pause.]

a15_0263512.speaker: Allen
a15_0263512.text: Al, this is Houston. Is your data system switch on? [Pause.]

a15_0263512.speaker: Worden
a15_0263512.text: Rog, Joe. That's affirm; it is.

a15_0264320.speaker: Allen
a15_0264320.text: Guys, we're having trouble picking up the proper data so we can monitor the film cycling process here. So we're going to have you stand by on that until our next High Gain acquisition, and we'll be back with you. In the meantime, leave all the SIM bay in the present configuration, if you would, please.

a15_0264320.speaker: Worden
a15_0264320.text: Is there anything we can do to help, Joe?

a15_0264320.speaker: Worden
a15_0264320.text: Is there anything we can do to help? [Long pause.]

a15_0264320.speaker: Allen
a15_0264320.text: Al, this is Houston. We don't think that there's anything that - that you can do to help us at the moment. [Pause.]

a15_0264320.speaker: Allen
a15_0264320.text: Okay; and in the meantime, we'd like to talk about the upcoming SPS burn, and we're going to be reading procedures up to you in a moment, and we think it's the easiest for you to copy these into your CSM Launch Checklist. So you might be looking for that and getting that out. [Pause.]

a15_0264320.speaker: Scott
a15_0264320.text: Okay, Houston. I wonder if you could hold off for about 10 or 15 minutes and let us get through the breakfast chores here, and then we can settle down and concentrate.

a15_0264320.speaker: Allen
a15_0264320.text: That'll be fine, Dave. We'll be standing by for your call on that and there is no hurry.

a15_0265401.speaker: Allen
a15_0265401.text: Apollo 15, select High Gain for us, please. [Long pause.]

a15_0265401.speaker: Allen
a15_0265401.text: Roger. Stop PTC mode for us now, please.

a15_0265802.speaker: Allen
a15_0265802.text: Guys, could you tell us how far down in your cycle film procedure you've proceeded - down to what step.

a15_0265802.speaker: Worden
a15_0265802.text: Joe, this is Al. We've got down to the point where we want to get a cue from you to cycle the film.

a15_0265802.speaker: Allen
a15_0265802.text: Okay, Al; that's fine. We copy that, and we suspected that, but wanted to confirm it.

a15_0270102.speaker: Allen
a15_0270102.text: Roger, Alfredo. Could you verify two things for us, please, that the Map[ping] Camera is in Standby and that the Pan[oramic] Camera power switch is On; and when you turned it on, did you get the proper talkback indication?

a15_0270102.speaker: Worden
a15_0270102.text: The answer is affirmative to both of those, Joe.

a15_0270514.speaker: Allen
a15_0270514.text: Al, this is Houston with another request on this film cycle procedure.

a15_0270514.speaker: Allen
a15_0270514.text: Roger, Al. Could you cycle the SM/AC Power switch for us, Off, and then, On, please.

a15_0270514.speaker: Allen
a15_0270514.text: Okay; and the problem here, we're seeing all the carriers, but we don't get proper modulation, and so we're just not getting the right data. [Long pause.]

a15_0270514.speaker: Worden
a15_0270514.text: Okay, Joe; that[SM/AC Power switch]'s been cycled now.

a15_0271105.speaker: Allen
a15_0271105.text: Rog, guys. The attitude which you're currently holding is a good attitude for your P52, if one of you wants to get started on that. We'll have some words for you on the SIM bay problem in a few minutes, and then we'll want to be talking about the SPS burn coming up pretty shortly here. That is, we want to talk about it shortly; it won't be coming up for a while.

a15_0271105.speaker: Worden
a15_0271105.text: Okay, Joe; I'll start doing the P52 [platform realignment].

a15_0271105.speaker: Allen
a15_0271105.text: Okay, Al. This - this is Houston again.

a15_0271105.speaker: Allen
a15_0271105.text: Al, your choice here. We suddenly found the missing data [in the downlink]. It mysteriously reappeared, and we - we're ready to go ahead with your film cycling procedure. Your choice if you want to do your P52 first or the film cycle first, and we're standing by for either.

a15_0271105.speaker: Worden
a15_0271105.text: We're all set up on the - We're all set up on the film cycle, Joe. Why don't we go ahead and do that and then I'll flip down and do P52.

a15_0271105.speaker: Allen
a15_0271105.text: Okay, Al that sounds good to us and we'll be watching.

a15_0271639.speaker: Allen
a15_0271639.text: Okay, Al; film cycling's complete, and it all looked very good to us. You can proceed on with the powerdown.

a15_0271639.speaker: Worden
a15_0271639.text: Okay, Joe. Thank you, sir. [Long pause.]

a15_0271639.speaker: Irwin
a15_0271639.text: Okay; the powerdown to the SIM bay is complete, Joe.

a15_0272200.speaker: Worden
a15_0272200.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Go ahead, Al.

a15_0272200.speaker: Worden
a15_0272200.text: Okay, Joe. I've got [the] gyro torquing angles up [on the DSKY], and I'll torque them out on the minute. That'll be at 27 hours and 24 minutes.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Okay, Al.

a15_0272200.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0272200.text: At any rate, the camera tests shown on page 3-28 of the Apollo 15 Flight Plan, were completed satisfactorily and the crew is presently doing a P52 realignment - program 52 realignment of the Inertial Measurement Unit. Earlier, the midcourse 2 correction burn time was shown on displays here in the control center as being at 22 [correcting himself] or 28 hours, 30 minutes. The Flight Dynamics Officer has subsequently shifted the [burn] time to ten minutes later at 28 hours, 40 minutes. Duration of the burn is less than one second; .85 seconds to be precise. In this burn, it's hoped to determine

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: 15, Houston.

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Go ahead, Joe.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Guys, we just had indication that your Thrust light came on again for about 10 seconds. Did you notice that?

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Yeah. Roger, Joe. That was the EMS Delta-V check.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Okay, Dave. Thank you. And, guys, we - we'd like to ask that you locate your CSM Launch Checklist, because we want to start talking about this SPS burn procedure. [Pause.]

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay, we'll be ready in a couple of minutes.

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay, Houston. We've got the checklist out, and we're ready to listen.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Okay, Dave. If you would, please, turn to page L/4-14, and we're just going to ask you to copy the procedure onto that page, because it'll consist of just a few changes to what's already listed on - on those few pages there.

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay; we've got L/4-14. Go ahead.

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: We've got L/4-14. Go ahead.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Okay. Unless you'd like an explanation of what's to come, I'll go ahead and read through the steps here and pause from time to time to make sure that you're getting it all, and then we can talk about the details of why it's breaking out like this when we finish it.

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay. Go.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Rog. I'm going to start there at the line, "If time permits, go to G&N thrusting procedures," et cetera, and right underneath that short paragraph, write in: "Circuit breakers EPS Group 5, two, Close;" and that's a "Verify."

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay, circuit breakers EPS Group 5, two, Close. That's the Main A and Main B, right?

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Yes, sir. And then we'll go on down about 4 lines to the "Set Delta-V" and that should read: "Set Delta-V C minus 100.

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Rog. Set Delta-V C minus 100.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Rog. Now into the TVC check and prep section. After the first line, which is "Circuit breaker Stab[ilizaton] Control System [SCS], all Close," insert: "Circuit breakers SPS pilot valves, two, Open;" and that's a "Verify."

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay. Circuit - okay; circuit breaker SPS pilot valves, two, Open, verify. Below the line it has "CB stability control system, all, Close.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: That's correct, Dave. And the next line should read "Circuit breakers SPS, 10, Close.

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay, understand. Circuit breakers SPS, 10, Closed.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Rog. Skipping down several lines; Delta-V CG, LM/CSM.

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Roger. Delta-V CG, LM/CSM. [Pause.]

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Page 4-15.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Okay, Dave. Turn to page 4-15. And your next...

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Rog. And your next change is in the TVC check, third line from the bottom of that first group there; delete "Rate, High.

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay; secondary TVC check, third line from the bottom; delete "Rate, High." That's the line right after "Limit Cycle, Off.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: That's correct. Down into the next group, "Delta-V Thrust A to Normal." You can...

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: "Delta-V Thrust A to Normal," and delete "B.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: That's affirm, and then insert right after that - immediately after that, the following note. "Get thrust light on by pushing on panel first. [Pause.]

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay. In other words, you want us to try and get the SPS Thrust - Thrust light on by tapping on the panel some way, so that the light is on with the Delta-V Thrust A switch up to normal. Is that right?

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Dave, that's not quite right. Let me read through it. We want you to get the light on, but we want you to try to first get it on just by pushing, by flexing the panel around the switch in question. And the reason we're doing that, we think - it's - The probable short is contamination in the switch, but there's a small chance that it's some sort of problem in the wire bundle that will be flexed very slightly when you just push on the panel. So that - the note should read the following, and I'll read it clear through to the end. "Get thrust light on by pushing on panel first. If this doesn't wor

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay. Why don't we try that right now?

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Dave, stand by a second.

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Dave, let's - let's ask you to stand by on that. We'd prefer to complete reading the procedures to you, and then - we'll worry about this light business. At any rate, you should have inserted the note "Get thrust light on by pushing on panel first. If this doesn't work, rap on panel or cycle the switch and if no light, then delete the test.

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay, understand. Push, rap, cycle and if no light, delete the test.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Beautiful. Okay. Now, at about 1 minute to go, but definitely after the light is on, proceed on to the next step, which is Verb 37 Enter, 47 Enter. [Pause.]

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay. If we get the light on, then we're at 2 minutes, and we'll work for about a minute to try to get the light on. And if we don't get it on by 1 minute then we'll consider that we cannot get it on, and if we do get it on by 1 minute, we'll call up P47.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Dave, it's - I guess the 2-minute mark out to the side of your checklist there is meaningless in this case, because the test is in no way time critical. We want you to take your own time and work to get the light on, but if it does come on at about 1 minute before the burn, we'll want you to go into Program 47.

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay, I'm with you. Just to make sure we have P47 running.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Roger. That's exactly it. Okay. That brings us down to our next change, which is an insert just below the line "EMS Mode, Normal." And the change is "on MSFN cue, Circuit Breaker SPS pilot valve A, Close." And a note that goes with this line, "1 second burn desired. If no ignition, Circuit Breaker SPS pilot valve A, Open, after 3 seconds."

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay, understand. Just before EMS mode, Normal, on MSFN cue, CB SPS pilot valve, Closed. And you desire 1 second burn, which means that if we get a light, we open the circuit breaker after 1 second. If we have no light, you want to leave the circuit breaker closed for 3 seconds and then open it.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: That - that's exactly right, Dave. Now I've got some words here from Dick Gordon who's run through the procedure this morning and he tells me that - that - a good cue to monitor is the SPS P C coming off the peg, and, at the same time, Jim or Al can, or - or whoever is there, can - watch the ball valve indicators, also, for a cue that the engine is starting to burn.

a15_0272200.speaker: Scott
a15_0272200.text: Okay. Stand by one now, Joe. Let us regroup here for a minute and make sure that we have no questions up to this point.

a15_0272200.speaker: Allen
a15_0272200.text: Okay.

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Okay, Joe. I guess one question we wanted to make sure here was that the - on the MSFN cue to close the pilot valve, is prior to going to EMS mode normal. In other words, we'll never get the EMS...

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Nega - negative.

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: ...Is that correct?

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Dave, that's negative. EMS mode normal...

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Okay.

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: And then, on MSFN cue, the SPS pilot valve A, Alpha, Close, and let me repeat here, Dave, you may or may - may or may not get a light at this particular point. If you do not get a light, open the circuit breaker after about 3 seconds. If you do get a light, we're interested in - in as short a burn as you can give us, so - and Dick tells me that the reaction time - a good, reasonable reaction time would be, in pulling the circuit breaker after you see the P C come off the peg, would give you about 3 to 4 feet per second [of velocity change]. And that's a real good number for us as far as the mi

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Okay. Well, that's why we asked the question, just to make sure. It makes more sense the way you're doing it. So, - I guess we understand that. We can have Al watching the P C gauge, and Jim can watch the ball valves, and if anybody sees something move, why - Al can pull that circuit breaker.

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Okay, Dave. That sounds good. Now a word about the circuit breaker. You might want to cycle it a couple of times - but [you should do it] before we go through this, just to make sure its not a lot stiffer than what you're used to working with in the simulator. And just get some idea of how its best to - to position yourself to pull this. It's also not all that critical that it get pulled absolutely immediately, but - you know, what - whatever's comfortable to do. It might make it easier for us on trimming up with your midcourse if we do get a burn.

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Okay, we'll work that one. Over.

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: And, before you - you test that particular circuit breaker, just make sure that the Group 5 circuit breakers are Open, and we won't be risking anything by testing it. Now finally, after this note, we've got several deletions, and I'll continue on here. Delete "Ullage and thrust, On"; delete "SPS Thrust light, On"; delete "Delta-V thrust, B"; delete "Ullage and thrust, On"; delete "Monitor thrusting, P C 95 - 105, EMS counting down. [Pause.]

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Okay. We got that. Deleting the next seven lines. [Pause.]

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Yes, sir; exactly. Now the next line should read "SPS Injection Valves, two, Open.

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Roger. SPS Injection Valves, two, Open.

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Roger. Three lines down, delete "PUGS, balanced".

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Rog. Delete "PUGS, balanced."

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: And then, the next line, after ignition confirmed, circuit breaker SPS pilot valve A - Main A, Open. [Pause.]

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Okay. After ignition [is] confirmed, CB SPS pilot valve A - Main A, Open. That's - just about what you gave us in the notes.

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Rog. Exactly. And then a note - well, let's see. The note is - just a rehash of what we've already told you. The burn should not exceed 1 second if it's possible to avoid it. And then, exit P47 immediately after burn.

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Okay. Shouldn't exceed 1 second and exit P47 immediately after the burn.

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Roger. And that takes us to page 4-16. The first line...

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Page 4-16.

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Rog. First line, "Delta-V Thrust A, Off. [Pause.]

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Delta-V Thrust A, Off. [Pause.]

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Okay, Dave. And that's really the end of the procedures. We have - another note for this page, which is "After test, if SPS light goes out, attempt to get light back on by your standard procedures, pushing, rapping, cycling," I guess.

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Okay. After the tests, if the SPS light is out, attempt to get it back on.

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Roger. And that completes the procedures. Maybe a couple of - more words about it here. It's also possible that when you push the circuit breaker - to the pilot valve A, in, that the light will just go out, in which case, we'd be pretty confident that - the contamination causing the short is just a burn through. In other words, just disappeared and is no longer shorting the switch. The light would go out, and otherwise, nothing else would happen. [Pause.]

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Okay; understand. If we - if when we push the circuit breaker in, the light goes out, we've burned to [through] the short. Okay. [Pause.]

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: And, guys, you might look through those again, and - if you have any questions, please come right back to us with them.

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Okay. Let us mull it over, and we'll get back with you.

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Okay.

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Okay, Joe. We have no further questions. We think we can run through that one okay. [Pause.]

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Okay, Dave. And we'll have a PAD for you in a few minutes.

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Okay, and I guess I still have a question as why we don't take a look at that light now with the push, rap and cycle technique.

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Let me get a reading [means advice] on that.

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Okay. You know, we've tapped it, cycled it, but we've never pushed that panel just by pushing the panel to see if the light'll come on. [Long pause.]

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Dave, I guess the main reason is, before you do it, we'd like to get some recorders configured. We're setting the recorders up now so we can monitor the problem as you go through it, and then there is no reason you can't try pushing on the panel, provided the pilot valve breakers and the group 5 breakers are pulled.

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: Well, Joe, when you get a - a chance, or when you're set up down there, why - why don't we try that, and at the same time, we could run through our little check to see how the pilot valve Main A circuit breaker works, cycling it.

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Okay, Dave. That sounds good.

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: We'll stand by for your call.

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Endeavour, this is Houston requesting P00 and Accept, and we'll give you a state vector and some drift terms.

a15_0273858.speaker: Scott
a15_0273858.text: You got it. P00 and Accept.

a15_0273858.speaker: Allen
a15_0273858.text: Thank you.

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: Endeavour, this is Houston.

a15_0275235.speaker: Scott
a15_0275235.text: Houston, Endeavour. Go.

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: Rog, Dave. After you verify for us that your pilot valve circuit breakers and group 5 circuit breakers are out, you can go ahead with the push, rap, cycle test if you like.

a15_0275235.speaker: Scott
a15_0275235.text: Okay. [Pause.] Okay. Group 5 are open and the pilot valves are open, and we'll take a look at it. [Long pause.]

a15_0275235.speaker: Scott
a15_0275235.text: Okay, Houston. Nothing worked pushing an I'll try rapping.

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: Okay, Dave. We agree.

a15_0275235.speaker: Scott
a15_0275235.text: Came on with the rap - up just to the top of the switch. [Long pause.]

a15_0275235.speaker: Scott
a15_0275235.text: Okay; I'll cycle it and see if it goes off. [Long pause.]

a15_0275235.speaker: Scott
a15_0275235.text: Okay; it flickers as - as I pass through neutral.

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_0275235.speaker: Scott
a15_0275235.text: And now she doesn't want to stay on. [Long pause.]

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: Dave, as long as you keep those circuit breakers out, there's no reason we can't leave that light on. We need it on for the test anyway.

a15_0275235.speaker: Scott
a15_0275235.text: Okay, Joe. I can find a position on the switch where I can turn the light out now - in [the] neutral position on the switch, if you want to look at it. I've cycled the switch a number of times, and I think I've got the spot where the light will go off, and I'll turn it off for a couple of seconds here for you.

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: Okay, Dave. Go ahead, and we're watching the drivers at the same time.

a15_0275235.speaker: Worden
a15_0275235.text: Okay, Joe. The light's out right now; Dave's holding the switch [in the neutral position].

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: Roger. We confirm that.

a15_0275235.speaker: Worden
a15_0275235.text: Okay; it's coming back on now.

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: Rog.

a15_0275235.speaker: Worden
a15_0275235.text: [It's going] off now.

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: Rog.

a15_0275235.speaker: Worden
a15_0275235.text: And [it's] coming back on. [Long pause.]

a15_0275235.speaker: Scott
a15_0275235.text: And it seems like it goes off just at the lower portion or near the Off portion of the - force range there when you get to neutral. As you go into the neutral position, you have high forces, and right at the beginning of those high forces, it'll go off. And if you hold it in the neutral position, or the - the mid-position, where the - the force on the bottom of the switch, holding it so it won't go over center, that's when the light will go off. As soon as you let it go over center and flick up to the top, the light comes back on.

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: Roger. Dave, we copy that. [Long pause.]

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: Dave, let's go ahead and stay in this configuration. If you want to practise with the pilot valve circuit breaker, we emphasize that [the] group 5 circuit breaker definitely should be open.

a15_0275235.speaker: Scott
a15_0275235.text: Okay, we'll do that now. And the cir... [correcting himself] group 5 [circuit breakers] are open. [Long pause.]

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: And, Endeavour, this is Houston with the maneuver PAD when you're ready to copy. [Pause.]

a15_0275235.speaker: Irwin
a15_0275235.text: Okay, Joe, I'm ready to copy.

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: Okay, Jim; and it's your computer.

a15_0275235.speaker: Irwin
a15_0275235.text: Okay.

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: Maneuver PAD for the SPS test. SPS/SCS; NA; plus 1.24, minus 0.11; 028:40:00.00; NA, NA, NA; roll 061, 018, 020; NA, NA, NA, NA, NA; 11, 216.1, 18.6; NA, NA, NA. NA all the rest of the way; GDC Align, Vega, Deneb; roll align, 209, 009, 349. Other comments, set up SPS gimbal thumbwheels with pitch trim, [and] yaw trim; High Gain Antenna, Pitch, minus 25; Yaw 359. Over. [Pause.]

a15_0275235.speaker: Irwin
a15_0275235.text: Okay. Readback on the SPS test. SPS/SCS; plus 1.24, minus 0.11; 028:40:00.00; 061, 018, 020; 11, 216.1, 18.6; Vega and Deneb; 209, 009, 349. And set the SPS thumbwheels to the Pitch and Yaw trim. High Gain Antenna is Pitch minus 25 and Yaw 359.

a15_0275235.speaker: Allen
a15_0275235.text: Rog. Readback correct.

a15_0280257.speaker: Allen
a15_0280257.text: Al, just a couple more words here. We're quite interested in subtle changes that may take place in the thrust light. And we'd like for you to think about perhaps playing around with the cabin lighting control there so you can get a good view of the light, and you may or may not want to use the filter in front of the light as you watch it, and I guess the third one of you should be watching the light during the burn test.

a15_0280257.speaker: Worden
a15_0280257.text: Okay, Joe. We'll keep a close eye on the light.

a15_0280257.speaker: Allen
a15_0280257.text: Roger, Al. And you understand, it's not a question of on/off but also if the intensity changes and - and...

a15_0280257.speaker: Allen
a15_0280257.text: Rog, okay. And, guys, you can go ahead with the waste water dump if you want to now. There's nothing magic about the time we gave you on that. [Pause.]

a15_0280257.speaker: Allen
a15_0280257.text: Rog, Al. And - the provision on that is that you [should] be at [the] burn attitude before you dump the water. And [you should do it] after the sextant star check.

a15_0281350.speaker: Allen
a15_0281350.text: Apollo 15. This is Houston requesting Beam Width to Wide.

a15_0282549.speaker: Allen
a15_0282549.text: 15, you can terminate the waste dump anytime.

a15_0282549.speaker: Allen
a15_0282549.text: Okay, guys, and just want to reemphasize another point here. This burn is not at all time critical. It has very little effect on - on our midcourse corrections later on or whatever. Just want you to understand that.

a15_0283601.speaker: Allen
a15_0283601.text: Okay, Endeavour. This is Houston, and we're showing about 4 minutes to ignition.

a15_0283601.speaker: Scott
a15_0283601.text: Okay, and we've got about 5 and we're proceeding through the checklist.

a15_0283953.speaker: Worden
a15_0283953.text: Okay, Joe. We're all set up ready to go. We've got about 50 seconds to go. Sorry Joe, there we are - Yeah, we're ready to go now, any time, on your cue. [Pause.]

a15_0283953.speaker: Worden
a15_0283953.text: Okay, Joe. [To Scott and Irwin] Ready? [Long pause.]

a15_0283953.speaker: Scott
a15_0283953.text: Mark; about 5.3 [fps] on the DSKY and about 4.7 [fps] on the EMS. [Pause.]

a15_0283953.speaker: Scott
a15_0283953.text: And, Houston, the light's still on.

a15_0284339.speaker: Allen
a15_0284339.text: Roger, guys. When you're comfortably through with the procedure here, we'd like for you to turn the thrust light out for us, please, by pulling the EMS Main A and B circuit breakers, two of them, on panel 8.

a15_0284339.speaker: Scott
a15_0284339.text: Rog. They're both open; the light is out.

a15_0284339.speaker: Allen
a15_0284339.text: Okay, Dave, and that - the reason for that is just to conserve that light bulb and a little power, and - that burn was exactly what we wanted to see. We'll proceed with a normal mission.

a15_0284339.speaker: Allen
a15_0284339.text: I'm a smooth talker, aren't I?

a15_0284339.speaker: Scott
a15_0284339.text: Well, I'm glad you guys down there can figure all this out. [Long pause.]

a15_0284339.speaker: Allen
a15_0284339.text: And, guys, a further word here. As you're probably already aware, the short is in what we've been calling the downstream side of that driver solenoid, and it means only that it's a little bit annoying to have. We can still turn bank A on and off as we want. We might modify a few procedures a little bit, but we haven't lost that bank.

a15_0284339.speaker: Scott
a15_0284339.text: Okay; very good. Thank you, Joe. Let's go to Hadley. [Pause.]

a15_0285555.speaker: Allen
a15_0285555.text: Rog, Dave. We're requesting a Narrow Beam Width, and then we have an attitude we'd like you to maneuver to for - for a DSE dump which we will initiate. Specifically, roll 40, pitch 12, yaw 50. High Gain, minus 38 and 318. Over. [Pause.]

a15_0285555.speaker: Scott
a15_0285555.text: Okay, understand. High Gain is now in Narrow [beamwidth], maneuver to roll 40, pitch 12, yaw 50. High Gain [pointing angle] is [pitch] minus 38 and [yaw] 318.

a15_0285555.speaker: Allen
a15_0285555.text: Roger, Dave. And after that, we'll need only a roll maneuver to get us into the sextant photo test attitude.

a15_0285920.speaker: Allen
a15_0285920.text: Roger, Dave. I'm pleased to report that not only did you carry out a successful SPS test burn, but you did a superb midcourse 2 correction at the same time. In fact, you burned it to within a half a foot per second of being exactly what we wanted. Consequently, we're going to omit midcourse 2 and midcourse 3. We'll be looking at a midcourse 4 correction of around 6 feet per second, it looks like now. And, additionally, because of this, we'd like for you to go ahead and secure the Mapping Camera and the Pam Can - Pan Camera at you convenience per the procedure that's shown at 31 hours and 10 mi

a15_0285920.speaker: Scott
a15_0285920.text: Okay, Joe. Well, we sort of had that in mind when we ran the burn. And we'll secure the Map and Pan [cameras], and we'll be standing by for midcourse 4.

a15_0285920.speaker: Allen
a15_0285920.text: Rog, Dave. Al Worden always did have a very fine touch on the circuit breakers.

a15_0285920.speaker: Scott
a15_0285920.text: Yes, sir. He's - we call him nimble finger up here. [Pause.]

a15_0285920.speaker: Allen
a15_0285920.text: Rog. No comment to that one.

a15_0285920.speaker: Allen
a15_0285920.text: Roger. Al, for your benefit, we'd scrubbed the crew exercise period earlier. We'd like to put that back in again, any time between now and the sextant photo test.

a15_0285920.speaker: Scott
a15_0285920.text: Okay, Joe. Jim and I are doing some housekeeping now, and we're going to make sure we get all the exercise periods for you.

a15_0285920.speaker: Allen
a15_0285920.text: Roger, Dave. I'll rely on you for that.

a15_0285920.speaker: Scott
a15_0285920.text: Gee, we might even do a couple extra.

a15_0290520.speaker: Allen
a15_0290520.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. Please start your battery A charge at your convenience.

a15_0290520.speaker: Allen
a15_0290520.text: Okay, Dave. And we do have one question regarding the burn. On our data down here, we saw the thrust light go off right after the burn for about 7 seconds and wondered if you noticed the same thing up there? [Pause.]

a15_0290520.speaker: Scott
a15_0290520.text: Houston, the consensus here is that it stayed on, and I guess - we - we might have missed a short period there in getting the engine off and getting out [of] P47, but Al and I both feel like it stayed on all the way, but I guess we're not a hundred per cent sure of that.

a15_0290520.speaker: Allen
a15_0290520.text: Okay, Dave. We copy. Thank you.

a15_0294025.speaker: Scott
a15_0294025.text: Would you like the P52 at 30 hours, or do you want to bypass that one?

a15_0294025.speaker: Allen
a15_0294025.text: Say that again, Dave. I didn't copy.

a15_0294025.speaker: Scott
a15_0294025.text: Would you like the P52 at 30 hours or would you like to bypass it?

a15_0294025.speaker: Allen
a15_0294025.text: Dave, that's not required. Go ahead and bypass that please.

a15_0294025.speaker: Allen
a15_0294025.text: Dave, this is Houston again. While we're talking, could you look back in your time line for us, please, and give us the results of your EMS test. I guess that's a bias reading at around 27 hours.

a15_0294025.speaker: Worden
a15_0294025.text: And the Delta-V test was - was okay.

a15_0295405.speaker: Allen
a15_0295405.text: Roger. Al, I've got a correction to the erasable loads in your G&C Checklist. If you'd fish that out for me, I'll go ahead and read them to you.

a15_0295405.speaker: Scott
a15_0295405.text: Okay, Joe. Could you stand by about 5 minutes?

a15_0295405.speaker: Allen
a15_0295405.text: Rog, Dave. Standing by, and no hurry. Just give me the word. [Long pause.]

a15_0295405.speaker: Irwin
a15_0295405.text: Houston, 15. If you could stand by about 5 minutes, why, our trusty CMP could fin - finish up his exercise period and get with you on that.

a15_0295405.speaker: Allen
a15_0295405.text: Roger. I'll stand by 10 or 15 minutes in that case.

a15_0300152.speaker: MCC
a15_0300152.text: Dave, in all that going on with that Flight Plan activities - about 28 hours, we may have missed something. Did you change your lithium hydroxide canister about 28 hours or so?

a15_0300152.speaker: Scott
a15_0300152.text: Houston, 15. The canister was changed at about 26:10.

a15_0300152.speaker: MCC
a15_0300152.text: Okay, Dave. We're just seeing a little rise in the partial pressure CO 2 . That's the - the reason we asked the question. We'll watch it.

a15_0300900.speaker: Worden
a15_0300900.text: Rog, Joe. I'm ready with the erasable update if you want to go with that. [Pause.]

a15_0300900.speaker: Allen
a15_0300900.text: Roger, Al. Turn to page 9-4 if you would. And it's a - an update only to your column Alpha - octal ID, column Alpha. And it's octal ID...

a15_0300900.speaker: Allen
a15_0300900.text: Rog. Octal ID 11 should read 00634; 12 is 77425; and 13, 77317. Over. [Pause.]

a15_0300900.speaker: Worden
a15_0300900.text: Roger, Joe. Understand. Column Alpha, octal ID 11 should read 00634; 12 should be 77405; and 13 should be 77317.

a15_0300900.speaker: Allen
a15_0300900.text: Al, there's a mistake in your readback for 12. That should be 77425.

a15_0300900.speaker: Allen
a15_0300900.text: And that's the extent of it. Thank you.

a15_0303321.speaker: Allen
a15_0303321.text: Roger, guys. We're requesting - that, at your convenience, you roll to the sextant photo attitude, which is a roll of 270 - [you can stay in] the same pitch and yaw you're presently in - so that you'll be getting some sunlight on the SIM bay to - to start to warm it up. And during the roll, we'll call out an antenna change to you. [Pause.]

a15_0303321.speaker: Worden
a15_0303321.text: Okay, Houston; 15. Understand you want us to roll, with our present pitch and yaw, to a roll of 270.

a15_0303321.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0303321.text: This is Apollo Control; 30 hours, 44 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. To repeat, in view of the success of the Service Propulsion System test, back at 28 hours, 40 - 40 minutes, 30 seconds, the scheduled midcourse correction number 2, shown in the Flight Plan at 30 hours, 55 minutes, some 11 minutes from now, will not be done. Nor will midcourse correction number 3 be performed. Midcourse correction number 4, right now, looks like it might be in the neighborhood of some 6 feet per second [1.8 m/s]. Apollo 15 is now 120,487 nautical miles [223,141 km] out from Earth. Approaching the Moon at a veloc

a15_0304400.speaker: Allen
a15_0304400.text: Apollo 15, select Omni Charlie, and stow the High Gain [antenna], please.

a15_0304400.speaker: Worden
a15_0304400.text: Rog, Joe. Omni Charlie, and stow the High Gain.

a15_0304400.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0304400.text: This is Apollo Control at 31 hours, 13 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Shift handover under way here in the Control Center. Milton Windler's Maroon team of flight controllers taking over from Gerry Griffin. Estimating change of shift briefing right at 4 o'clock or a few minutes thereafter in the main auditorium [in the] Manned Spacecraft Center. Meanwhile Apollo 15 is 121,800 nautical miles [225,573 km] from Earth, traveling at a velocity of 4,614 feet per second [1,406 m/s]. Some 3 hours and 10 minutes ago, at 28 hours, 3 minutes and 14 seconds Ground Elapsed Time, the spacecraft was equidistant

a15_0304400.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0304400.text: This is Apollo Control again. Some numbers now on the check of the Service Propulsion System back at 28 hours, 40 minutes, 22.5 seconds actual ignition time. We got a Delta-V or a velocity change of 5.3 seconds [means feet per second] which was within a half a foot of the desired velocity for midcourse 2, which was not scheduled for another 2 hours after the SPS check. The burn time was 7/10ths of 1 second, which is fairly rapid reaction time when you consider it was a manual burn, essentially. At any rate this unscheduled midcourse correction burn number 2 brought about by this test has resul

a15_0315622.speaker: Irwin
a15_0315622.text: You asked a question on the UV procedures.

a15_0315622.speaker: Henize
a15_0315622.text: Say again, which procedures. You're coming in very weak. [Long pause.]

a15_0321409.speaker: Henize
a15_0321409.text: That's a good question. Stand by.

a15_0321409.speaker: Irwin
a15_0321409.text: Okay Al, you can verify through the sextant, if you can, that the optics are boresighted on the target.

a15_0321700.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0321700.text: This is Apollo Control at 32 hours, 17 minutes. We accumulated 1 minute, 18 seconds in air/ground tape during the news conference. We'll play that back now.

a15_0321700.speaker: Irwin
a15_0321700.text: Let's see. You want - Let's see. You want ...?

a15_0321900.speaker: Worden
a15_0321900.text: It's always been my understanding that it wouldn't. It's not long enough anyway, I don't think.

a15_0321900.speaker: Irwin
a15_0321900.text: We really can't do a thing.

a15_0322142.speaker: Henize
a15_0322142.text: I guess we have to agree with you that that cable doesn't reach all the way over to 227, and the request down here is that you voice-record shutter opening and shutter closing on the S - on the DSE.

a15_0322142.speaker: Scott
a15_0322142.text: Okay. I'll voice-record shutter opening and shutter closing. We'll do that.

a15_0322142.speaker: Scott
a15_0322142.text: What's the number of that panel down there, Al?

a15_0322142.speaker: Scott
a15_0322142.text: Okay; and be advised, we also tried to get it to panel 162 without success. It was too short for that one, too.

a15_0324547.speaker: Henize
a15_0324547.text: 15, Houston. We'd like to have Omni Delta, please. [Pause.]

a15_0324547.speaker: Scott
a15_0324547.text: Okay. I want to get my su - want to get my suit back out of the way. You got to - you got to rotate that strut.

a15_0325100.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0325100.text: This is Apollo Control at 32 hours, 51 minutes. It appears that the crew is running behind the Flight Plan [by] approximately 15 minutes at the present time. Flight Director reports that they may be able to make this up prior to the scheduled TV time at 33 hours, 45 minutes [Ground] Elapsed Time. That's 06:19 Central Daylight Time. However, we're unable to determine that at present, and the possibility that does exist that the television transmission will begin late. Apollo 15 now 126,083 nautical miles [233,505 km] from Earth. Velocity; 4,480 feet per second [1,366 m/s]. This is Mission Contr

a15_0325100.speaker: Irwin
a15_0325100.text: Okay, tell me when you're ready. The next one's 5 seconds.

a15_0325100.speaker: Irwin
a15_0325100.text: Okay. Then you change to 24 frames per second.

a15_0330525.speaker: Henize
a15_0330525.text: 15, this is Houston. We're anxious to know down here if you've checked the LM/CM Delta-P. [Pause.]

a15_0330525.speaker: Scott
a15_0330525.text: Not yet, Karl. We will though.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay, Houston, 15.

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, this is Houston.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay. The LM/CM Delta-P is now plus .8 [psi, 5.5 kPa], and I guess - there's no need to do the Tunnel Vent Valve, is there, at this stage? Looks to us like we can go ahead and bring the pressure back up - equalize the Delta-P before we get into the tunnel.

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, this is Houston. We would like to go to Vent on the Tunnel Vent Valve until the Delta-P is - is greater than 2.7.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay. We'll do that. [Long pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: Dave, we'd like for you to tell us when the Delta-P gets to 2.7 [psi], and stop there. The basic problem here is, we want to dump the residual atmosphere out of the LM in order to put in good fresh oxygen before we have you climb in. We're sort of up against the time line now...

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay. That's what we...

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: Righto.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay. That - that's what we figured, Karl, [garble].

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: Good; okay. Don't - don't go below 2.7 Delta-P there.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Rog.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay, Houston. We're at 2.7 on the Delta-P on tunnel vent.

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, this is Houston. Say again.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Roger. We're at 2.7 on the Delta-P on the tunnel vent. [Pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, this is Houston. The number that we need now [for the LM/CM Delta-P], since the [CM] cabin [pressure] went up, is; we need a Delta-P of 3.1 [psi]. We have to vent the tunnel.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay, Delta-P at 3.1. [Garble]. [Pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, we'd like Omni Bravo.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Yeah, Rog. Omni Bravo. And what was your last, after you said you wanted 3.1 on the LM tunnel vent?

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: Stand by on that one. [Long pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, this is Houston. To keep our records straight here, we're anxious for you to bring the tunnel down until we have a Delta-P of 3.1. [Pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Rog, Houston. That's in work, and we're up to 2.9 [psi].

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, this is Houston. There's a couple of read-outs we'd like to get, when you have time. First of all, we'd like to get the PRD read-outs for all three of you. And we'd also like to have the magazine numbers used for the sextant photography and for the UV photography.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay. Those are as - magazines are as per Flight Plan, and we'll get you the PRD's when we can get down into our suits. We'll get them before the day is out.

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: Okay, Dave. And, incidentally, can you give us any sort of report on that number 5 window? [Pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: [The window] looks clear.

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: We copy. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay, Houston. The Delta-P is hanging right in at about: 2.9 to 3.0. I'd suggest we pressed on, huh? [Long pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: Stand by on that, Dave.

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, This Houston. Time is not too critical. We'd like to let it vent a little longer. Try to get 3.1 [psi on the gauge]. If we don't reach it in about 5 minutes, we'll probably go ahead.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay; understand.

a15_0334126.speaker: Henize
a15_0334126.text: 15, this is Houston. Can you tell us how the pressurization is going?

a15_0334126.speaker: Scott
a15_0334126.text: Oh, we're all squared away, and the probe's coming out. [Pause.]

a15_0334126.speaker: Henize
a15_0334126.text: Roger. And - if you could give us the high-gain angles [in the Flight Plan] there, we'd like to get that going.

a15_0334126.speaker: Scott
a15_0334126.text: Okay, Houston. The probe is out, and it worked very smoothly.

a15_0334126.speaker: Worden
a15_0334126.text: Okay. Here it is. Jettison, Jim.

a15_0334126.speaker: Irwin
a15_0334126.text: I've got the drogue here, Al, if you can get the TV between my legs.

a15_0334126.speaker: Scott
a15_0334126.text: I got the probe, Jim. Let's see, you take the jettison bag. I want to put the probe over here by the hatch.

a15_0334126.speaker: Irwin
a15_0334126.text: Okay, I've got the Jett bag.

a15_0334126.speaker: Henize
a15_0334126.text: 15, Houston. We'd like to have Narrow Beam, please. [Pause.]

a15_0334622.speaker: Henize
a15_0334622.text: 15, this is Houston. Whenever you have a chance up there, we're interested in seeing some TV.

a15_0334622.speaker: Scott
a15_0334622.text: Rog, Houston. We thought we'd get the tunnel cleared out because, with all that extra gear in the Command Module, it's sort of tough to find a place to stow everything. And the TV is - right now, sort of in the way. So we'll try and get to you as soon as we can.

a15_0334622.speaker: Scott
a15_0334622.text: It's a new world in this Command Module, with all these extra box - boxes and everything.

a15_0334622.speaker: Scott
a15_0334622.text: Roger. We had an AC Bus 2 light and a Main Bus B Undervolt. Voltage looks good, and AC Bus 2 looks good. Reading 28.5 volts on Main Bus B and AC Bus 2 looks good. [At] about that time, we had a loss of S-band. I don't know whether it was coincidental or not.

a15_0334622.speaker: Henize
a15_0334622.text: 15, this is Houston. We saw some of those problems here on the ground, too. And we would like to get back on the High Gain [Antenna], if you would reacquire.

a15_0334622.speaker: Worden
a15_0334622.text: Auto's fine for what we're doing.

a15_0334622.speaker: Scott
a15_0334622.text: Okay, Houston. You should have the [signal from the] High Gain [Antenna, HGA] now.

a15_0334622.speaker: Henize
a15_0334622.text: Roger, 15. Give us Narrow Beam, please.

a15_0334622.speaker: Scott
a15_0334622.text: Okay, Houston, the LMP is in the LM.

a15_0334622.speaker: Henize
a15_0334622.text: 15, this is Houston. Could you give us a description of any actions you took when you had that electrical glitch? [Long pause.]

a15_0334622.speaker: Worden
a15_0334622.text: Karl, Jim just reset both [electrical buses] and they - everything seems to be okay now. He checked the voltages, and they were fine.

a15_0335605.speaker: Worden
a15_0335605.text: Hey, Karl, [are] you getting anything in on the TV?

a15_0335605.speaker: Henize
a15_0335605.text: Negative, we have no signal yet. [Voice in background: "It's coming, it's coming."] Pardon me; something is just now coming down.

a15_0335605.speaker: Worden
a15_0335605.text: Okay, fine. I'm over in the LM with them, and they're just going through the checklist.

a15_0335839.speaker: Henize
a15_0335839.text: 15, this is Houston. We're getting a reasonably good TV signal from you. And, we have about four procedure changes connected with the ASA [Abort Sensor Assembly] heater circuit breaker coming up at about 34:30 in your time line, and we'd like your choice as to whether I read it up to you as a block, or whether you want us to read it to you step by step when the time comes. [Long pause.]

a15_0335839.speaker: Worden
a15_0335839.text: Houston, 15. Hey, Karl, how about waiting until Jim and Dave get on comm, and then read up the procedure.

a15_0335839.speaker: Worden
a15_0335839.text: If that's satisfactory, let's do it that way.

a15_0335839.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0335839.text: This is Apollo Control at 34 hours, 1 minute. Dave Scott and Jim Irwin are going through a LM checklist to ensure that all the switch settings in the LM are the same as they were prelaunch; that they have not somehow changed position since launch.

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: 15, this is Houston.

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Go ahead, Houston; 15.

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: 15, when you had the S-band loss back there a few minutes ago, we think the problem was basically on the ground. And, when you lost uplink, it's - it's likely that your High Gain Antenna slewed against the limits; and we wonder if there was any circuit breaker resetting required to get you back up?

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Okay, Karl, stand by one, and I'll find out. [Long pause.]

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Negative, Houston. No circuit breakers are reset.

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: Very good. [Pause.] And, Al, we're getting a real good picture down here.

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Okay, Karl.

a15_0340408.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0340408.text: The conversations since the start of the TV have been between CapCom Karl Henize and Command Module Pilot Al Worden. Major Worden reporting that Dave Scott and Jim Irwin are not on the air/ground communications while they are completing the checklist.

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: 15, the TV picture is beautiful, and we're going to give that cameraman an honorary union card. [Long pause.]

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: That cameraman's got too many hands busy to answer you right now, Karl.

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: 15, this is Houston.

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Okay, give us a time hack, would you Karl, please? GET. [Pause.]

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: Roger. We're counting up to 34 hours, 11 minutes and 50 seconds. 4, 3, 2, 1...

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: Mark. [Long pause.]

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: 15, go ahead.

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Rog. If you're ready, Dave and Jim are ready to activate the comm now.

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: Roger. Did you get that time hack okay.

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Yes, sir, sure did. Thank you.

a15_0341613.speaker: Worden
a15_0341613.text: Roger, Karl. You guys ready to start a comm check now? [Long pause.]

a15_0341613.speaker: Henize
a15_0341613.text: Roger. We're ready down here for a comm check.

a15_0342237.speaker: Crewmember
a15_0342237.text: [Garble]. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Falcon, this is Endeavour reading you 5 square in Duplex B. [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. I got your message loud and clear.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Houston, Endeavour.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. Go ahead.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Rog, Karl. Jim's been calling you on S-band.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Sorry about that. They're just telling me here that we do have some problems, and we need to stand by for a few more minutes.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Okay; understand. Stand by for a few minutes before we try again.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: 15, this is Houston, and we're all set up for the voice check. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: 15, Houston is now configured to go along with you on the voice check. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Houston - Houston, this is Endeavour. It - apparently Falcon is reading you five square, but you're not reading him.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: That's correct, I've had no messages from Falcon.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Okay, he has been calling you, Karl. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: 15, this is Houston.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Okay, Karl. What are you receiving? Are you getting any low bit rate [data] from the - from the LM - from the Falcon?

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: That's affirmative.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: You are? Okay. [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Houston, this is Endeavour. Be advised Falcon's going high bit rate, we'll give you another call.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Falcon, this is Houston. How do you read? [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Houston, this is Endeavour again. Apparently Falcon's still reading you, but you're not reading him. How do you pick him up with high bit rate? [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Endeavour, Houston is getting the high bit rate data okay, and we'd like to have you hold this present configuration while we think a bit.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Okay, Karl.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Aren't those pretty?

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Say again.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Aren't those pretty little things?

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Oh boy. Navy blue, yet. Colorful. Too bad they don't work very well.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: [Garble] had them watch you configure the camera.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: You do?

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Yeah. That might be embarrassing.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Really?

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Because you might not get it con - Should be back over on the right-hand side. Oh my! You had it last, Al, when you were cleaning up the - screens. I put it in that compartment there, Al, just above the emergency medical kit - compartment above the emergency medicikinal [sic] kit.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: 15, this is Houston. We're reading you on Vox.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: [Ha, ha] Hot on Vox. ...

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Okay. Down Voice Back-up...

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah, they would - hot mike.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Good, I'm glad you're reading us, Fi - Houston, finally. [Pause.] Are we coming through loud and clear now, Karl?

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger, Falcon. You're coming through loud and clear.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Okay. I guess while we're in this position, we ought to go back to low [bit rate].

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: We've got...

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: We ought to go back to low bit rate.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger. Dave, we're reading you loud and clear.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: [Garble] you want to go back? [Pause.] Okay; back to low bit rate. Let's try that.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Yeah. [The] camera's configured, Dave.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Okay.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
