a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: And, Houston, this is Falcon. ED batteries both check at 37 volts.

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Copy; 37 volts. And I have an update to your PDI PAD. [Pause.]

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: And, Falcon, give us P00 and Data, and we'll give you an uplink. [Pause.]

a15a1040100.speaker: Scott
a15a1040100.text: P00 and Data. Go ahead with the PAD.

a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: Ed, if you're reading us, you ought to call us after the - the uplink. We cannot read you.

a15a1040100.speaker: Scott
a15a1040100.text: Here it comes; don't change it. It's coming in.

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Falcon, Houston. How do you read now?

a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: Read you loud and clear, Ed. I'm ready for that update now.

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Roger. India: 104:30:08.54; Noun 61 crossrange, plus 0003.3; DEDA 231, plus 56943. [Pause.]

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Readback is correct, and be advised that crossrange number means you're going from south to north. You'll probably see some roll during the PDI.

a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: Okay, your T - your Throttle in min? Okay. Throttle, min.

a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: Check DPS, APS, RCS, ECS, EPS. Okay?

a15a1040100.speaker: Mission Control
a15a1040100.text: We're coming up now on 20 minutes until ignition for the powered descent. The landing point for Apollo 15, in a plains area boxed in by mountains on one side, actually on two sides and a rille on the third side. We'll put Falcon down about 1 mile from the Hadley Rille. They'll be coming in about 2 miles to the south, rather to the north of the point where Hadley Delta begins to rise abruptly to an altitude of about 13,000 feet above the landing site, and approximately 6 miles behind their approach path, about 6 miles from the touch down point to the east, the Apennine Front itself begins to ri

a15a1040100.speaker: Scott
a15a1040100.text: Did you check the RCS? Okay. ECS look all right?

a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: If we should be up-linked, Dave, I'll need a - Verb 47.

a15a1040100.speaker: Mission Control
a15a1040100.text: And our Instrumentation and Communications Engineer reports that we should have lock on now with Endeavour . Al Worden in the Command Module.

a15a1040100.speaker: Scott
a15a1040100.text: Okay. Looks like I just screwed. Okay.

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Endeavour, Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Endeavour, Houston. You're on the scan limit. Go to Reacq when you're at the angles. [No answer.]

a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: Get - I think we Enable on the - S-Band?

a15a1040100.speaker: Scott
a15a1040100.text: Okay. Houston, how do you read Falcon?

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Endeavour, Houston. How do you read?

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Roger, Endeavour. I have an update for the PDI PAD, India. [Pause.]

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Endeavour, Houston. We're ready for Auto on the High Gain [Antenna] please.

a15_1041842.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1041842.text: Roger. We did not see the 231 load go in. Can you verify that, please? [Pause.]

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: There's the readout. I didn't put the 231 in. You want that also, Ed?

a15_1041842.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1041842.text: We're coming up now on 10 minutes until the beginning of this 12-minute powered burn to the lunar surface. At the initiation of this maneuver, the Command Module Endeavour will be about 350 nautical miles [650 km] behind the Lunar Module. The Command Module will pass overhead at just about the time the Lunar Module is touching down. Aboard the Lunar Module Falcon the crew has completed updating their backup guidance system with the same information that has been loaded into the Primary Guidance [and Navigation] System.

a15_1041842.speaker: Scott
a15_1041842.text: Hey, Houston, Falcon on Vox. How do you read?

a15_1041842.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1041842.text: And the crew has now switched on the guidance program - program 63 which will guide the Lunar Module during the initial portion of the power descent, the principal braking phase.

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: Okay; you ready for the DPS configuration card?

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: Okay; CBs on 11. DECA Gimbal AC, Closed.

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: Command Override logic is Closed. Att Control circuit breakers, all Closed, except AEA, Open.

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: Okay. The throttle, Yours to Min and mine to Soft Stop.

a15_1041842.speaker: Scott
a15_1041842.text: Soft stop. And you're - you're clipping a little bit on the first part, Jim.

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: We're down here where I can take a Verb 40, Noun 20.

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: Stand by for 5 minutes [to PDI ignition].

a15_1041842.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1041842.text: A last look at the Lunar Module orbit showed it to be in an orbit with a high point of 60.6 nautical miles [112.2 km] and a low point of about 8.1 nautical miles [15.0 km]. The Command Module Endeavour , that was in an orbit of 64.6 by 53.8 [nautical miles, 119.6 by 99.6 km]. And we're now coming up on about 6 minutes prior to the beginning of the powered descent. Everything continuing to progress very smoothly, and rather quietly here in Mission Control at the moment.

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: [Garble, may be landing radar] breaker is in. Altitude transmitter.

a15_1041842.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1041842.text: Flight Director Glynn Lunney, at this moment getting a final status for powered descent.

a15_1041842.speaker: Scott
a15_1041842.text: Okay. Go for the final trim.

a15_1042352.speaker: Irwin
a15_1042352.text: [Garble, may be landing radar] breaker is in. Altitude transmitter.

a15_1042352.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1042352.text: Flight Director Glynn Lunney, at this moment getting a final status for powered descent.

a15_1042352.speaker: Scott
a15_1042352.text: Okay. Go for the final trim.

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: And, Falcon, you are Go for PDI.

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: And, Falcon, you are Go for PDI (Powered Descent Initiation).

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Roger. Go for PDI.

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Roger. Go for PDI. (Long Pause) [Stephen Tellier has provided a pre-mission illustration of the planned LM ground track from PDI to landing ( 2.9 Mb or 640k ).]

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: (Garbled)

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Okay. Endeavour, how do you read the Falcon?

a15a1042610.speaker: Worden
a15a1042610.text: Falcon, Endeavour. Reading you loud and clear there, Dave. (Long Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Endeavour, Falcon. If you're reading, we're not reading you.

a15a1042610.speaker: Worden
a15a1042610.text: Falcon, Endeavour. How do you read? (Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: Falcon, Endeavour's reading you loud and clear.

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Okay; fine. Thank you. (Long Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: Stand by for 1 minute.

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: (The readings) on our oxidizer...They're low, aren't they?

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Yeah. [In Houston, the knowledgeable Flight Controller tells the Flight Director that this condition is normal prior to the ullage burn described below. The readings will rise to normal values after the PDI burn starts.]

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: (Garbled) cycle the cir(cuit breaker). [Journal Contributor Frank O'Brien notes, "Jim is probably referring to the Propellant Quantity Measurement Device (PQMD) circuit breaker. His suggestion to 'cycle the breaker' - which means turning power to the system off, and then back on - is intended to reset the PQMD, with the hope that a more 'normal' reading will result."]

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: No. That's all right. Be accurate later on. (Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: Houston, we're reading 87 and 85 on the Fuel Quantity (gauge).

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: Roger. Roger. It'll come up here in a moment. (Pause) It looks good to us, Jim.

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: Mark. One minute. (Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Okay. Master Arm's On; I have two (pyrotechnic system) lights. (Long Pause) [With the Master Arm switch On, Dave will be able to fire the small explosive charges that open the valves connecting the helium pressurization system to the tanks holding the descent stage oxidizer and propellant.] [David Woods has released an annotated version of the DAC (16-mm film) footage that includes the air-to-ground audio and transcript plus commentary. Synchronization is superb, of course. Available on YouTube 16:14 .]

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott

One reason it takes you so long up there is because it's not meaningless, because, now, you're really paying attention. This is a rehearsal we practiced in the mission simulator

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: All right. My gloves are on. Let me check yours. (Pause) Okay, locked and locked. Check mine.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay, Gordo. You got it.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1063500csm.text: Roger. I think we're getting a little better comm now. [Long pause.]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay, you're locked.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay. [In the following sequence, they will reconfigure the ECS (Environmental Control System) Suit Circuit in preparation for the cabin depressurization. Readers interested in a detailed description of the ECS and the Suit Circuit should consult the Apollo Operations Handbook.]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: Pressure integrity check. Okay, if you'll read to me. [The ECS controls are behind Jim who, undoubtedly, has turned around to reach them.]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay. Suit Gas Diverter (Valve) , Pull-Egress; verify.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: Verified. [They have verified that there is no air flow from the ECS into the cabin.]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Cabin Gas Return (Valve) , Egress; verify?

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: Verified. [Here, they are verifying that there is no flow from the cabin back into the ECS .]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Suit Circuit Relief (Valve), Close?

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: Close. [The Suit Circuit Relief valve would normally open if the pressure in the circuit exceeded 5.3 pounds per square inch (psi). Here, they are making sure that the relief valve will not open during the SEVA.]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Press Reg(ulator) A to Egress?

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: A to Egress. [In the Cabin position, one or both of the two Pressure Demand Regulators would maintain the cabin pressure in the range of 4.6 to 5.0 psi. In the Egress position, enough oxygen is added to the Suit Circuit to maintain the Suit Circuit pressure in the range 3.6 to 4.0 psi.]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Press Reg B , Direct O2?

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: Direct O2. [With Reg B in Direct O2, there will be an unregulated flow of oxygen into the suit circuit, albeit at a modest flow rate of 7 pounds per hour. This flow is enough to pressurize the heretofore unpressurized suits. Now, they will monitor the suit pressurization and, once the suits are pressurized to 3.7 psi above cabin pressure, they will shut of the oxygen flow and monitor the suits to make sure there are no leaks. Once they are satisfied with the suit integrity, then they will depressurize the cabin.]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay, (reading) monitor cuff gauge to 3.7 to 4.0 (psi).

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay, cabin pressure's coming up. (Correcting himself) Suit pressure's coming up - in the cabin.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: We might as well turn the urine-line heater off. [While performing the tasks on Surface 2-1, they emptied the urine collection bags in their suits into a transfer line which led, ultimately, to a collection tank in the descent stage. The heater prevents the line from freezing.]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Yeah. Right. For now. (Long Pause) Okay, mine's off of the peg on the cuff gauge. [The cuff-mounted pressure gauges do not go down to zero.]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1063500csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. You're T-2 now.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1063500csm.text: Roger. I have the landing site in view.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1063500csm.text: Roger. Very good.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: (Garbled) on mine (Pause) Want to take it up to 3.7?

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Yeah. (Pause)

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay, there's 3.5.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Right.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: 3.6, 3.65. Okay. I'm (setting Reg B to) Egress (thereby cutting off the oxygen flow). Reading 3.6.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay. One minute. [They will now monitor the suits for one minute.]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay. You hack (that is, note) the time?

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Yeah. (Long Pause)

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay. And, Houston; Endeavour. I've got the LM.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1063500csm.text: Roger, Al.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1063500csm.text: I'll give you the coordinates in a minute.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1063500csm.text: But he's almost directly north of Index.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1063500csm.text: Roger. Understand. [Long pause.]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1063500csm.text: Dave and Jim, while you're timing that minute out, be advised that Endeavour is passing overhead. Al's got you in sight, and I suspect there are two big cameras (the pan camera and the mapping camera, both in the SIM Bay) that'll be brought to bear on you a little later on.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay, very good. I'll bet Al can tell you where we are better than we can.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1063500csm.text: Al says you're...

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay, Joe; that's a minute, and...

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1063500csm.text: ...just north of Index.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: ...I've got...(Pause)

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: North of Index, huh? [The following is the conversation between Al Worden and Gordon Fullerton regarding Worden's observations of the landing site through the Command Module Sextant.] 106:38:10 Worden: I have the landing site in view. 106:38:13 Fullerton: Roger. Very Good. 106:38:29 Worden: Okay. And, Houston, Endeavour. I've got the LM. 106:39:34 Fullerton: Roger, Al. 106:39:39 Worden: I'll give you the coordinates in a minute. 106:39:41 Fullerton: Okay. 106:39:43 Worden: But he's almost directly north of Index. 106:39:46 Fullerton: Roger. Understand. 106:40:28 Fullerton: Endeavour, Houston.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1063500csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. You're TCA now.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay, I'm reading 3.4. [Jim's suit pressure has reduced by 0.2 psi due to breathe-down, minor leaks, and flow into nooks and crannies. Anything less than a 0.3 psi decrease in one minute is acceptable.]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay. Okay. I'm reading 3.4. That's 2/10ths in a minute. (Pause) Okay, Suit Circuit Relief (Valve) to Auto.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1063500csm.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1063500csm.text: Circuit Relief going Auto. (Pause) [With the pressure integrity check complete, they have now reset the relief valve so that it will open if the pressure in the Suit Circuit exceeds 5.3 psi.]

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1063500csm.text: Okay. He's about half way between Index and the next crater off towards the North Complex. He's sitting right by a very small crater. And, as soon as I lose them here, I'll give you the coordinates, but he's quite plain down there.

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1063500csm.text: Suit circuit pressure should go down to 4.8. (Long Pause) [They are now on Surface 2-3.] Post-landing Activities Apollo 15 Journal Stand-up EVA

a15_1063500csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1063500csm.text: Roger, Al.

a15a1064115.speaker: Allen
a15a1064115.text: And, Falcon, you are Go for depress.

a15a1064115.speaker: Scott
a15a1064115.text: Roger; understand Go for depress. [Readers should note that, according to the Apollo 15 Final Lunar Surface Procedures document, Dave and Jim had planned to start the SEVA at about 106:10. Consequently, they are about 30 minutes behind the nominal timeline.]

a15a1064115.speaker: Scott
a15a1064115.text: Okay, we're down almost to 5 on the gauge.

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: Cabin Repress coming open. (Pause) Open! [By opening this circuit breaker on the panel ( CB(16) ) at Jim's right shoulder, they are preventing any possibility that the ECS will try to repressurize the cabin once they open the dump valve .]

a15a1064115.speaker: Scott
a15a1064115.text: Okay, overhead or forward dump valve Open, then Auto, at three and a half (psi). (Pause) [Jim will open the dump valve in the hatch until the cabin pressure drops to 3.5 psi. At that point, he will close it by going to the Auto position so that they can monitor the response of the Suit Circuit to the reduced cabin pressure.]

a15a1064115.speaker: Scott
a15a1064115.text: Verify cabin pressure 3.5, LM suit circuit lockup at 4.3. Okay, the LM suit circuit about 4.5 (psi). (Pause) And it's (pause) stable. (Pause)

a15a1064115.speaker: Worden
a15a1064115.text: Okay, Gordo. If you look at the grid map, 1 to 250; that's HR25-11, he's on BR, .5, 75.5.

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: Yeah, it looks like it's locked up.

a15a1064115.speaker: Scott
a15a1064115.text: Okay, overhead...I mean, forward dump valve to Open and verify LM suit circuit 3 (garbled, but undoubtedly '3.6 to 4.3').

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: Ready to turn the card? [Rather than using the Surface Checklist Book, they are using a large cue card which they have mounted on the panel in front of them.] [Scott - "The Cue Cards were a major and formal part of the procedures and of the checklist system."]

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: I'll hold it if you'll push it on there.

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: Okay, hatch opening. [This is the overhead, docking hatch normally used in orbit for transfers between the LM and the Command Module.]

a15a1064115.speaker: Scott
a15a1064115.text: Well, I guess. (Garbled) Okay, it's partially open.

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: Okay, I'm going to go Auto on the dump valve here.

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: Okay, I'm Auto on the forward dump valve.

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: Okay. "Overhead hatch: full open and latched."

a15a1064115.speaker: Scott
a15a1064115.text: Okay, coming full open. (Pause) [Jones - "Did the hatch swing down into the cabin and, if so, was it hinged at the back?"] [Scott - "Yeah, and there's a latch at the back (of the cabin) that locks it in, as I recall. This was a very easy procedure, relatively speaking, and it's interesting, when we got into it, how straight-forward it was - almost to the extent that the LM almost might have been designed to do this."] [Jones - "I'll have to ask why the 16 and 17 crews didn't do it."] [Scott - "I don't know, but it was easy to do and I thought we got a lot of benefit out of it."]

a15a1064115.speaker: Allen
a15a1064115.text: Roger. Endeavour places you very near November Crater; very close to November Crater.

a15a1064115.speaker: Scott
a15a1064115.text: Okay. A little short (that is, east), huh? (Pause)

a15a1064115.speaker: Allen
a15a1064115.text: A little short and a little north. [A detail from Pan camera frame 9377, which will be taken in about one hour, shows the LM on the northwest rim of Last Crater. November is the sharp-rimmed crater farther east. The planned landing spot is just off the bottom of the image, about 200 meters south of the southern rim of Last. Stephen Tellier has provided a higher-resolution detail of the area immediately around the LM.]

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: Okay, Dave, you got the hatch open?

a15a1064115.speaker: Scott
a15a1064115.text: Okay. (Garbled). Forgot about the LCG (garbled) ISA. (Long Pause) [The Interim Stowage Assembly ( ISA ) is a set of cloth bags on a frame that fits over Dave's wall-mounted PLSS immediately behind his flight station. An ISA can be seen on the left at Neil Armstrong's back in Apollo 11 training photo KSC-69PC-319 . The dialog suggests that Dave has caught his LM hoses on the ISA. The LCG is a mesh garment which, during the EVAs, the astronauts wear over their long-john underwear. The LCG has a network of thin tubes woven through it. Water is circulated through these tubes and carries away exces

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: Push them (possibly Dave's hoses) out of the way? [After opening the hatch, Dave will sit on the engine cover and reach up to remove the docking drogue. Once he removes the drogue, he will hand it to Jim who, in turn, will put it on the floor on the left side of the cabin. Here, Dave may be getting himself into position on the engine cover. His hoses come across the cabin from the ECS which is behind Jim's station.]

a15a1064115.speaker: Scott
a15a1064115.text: Yeah. All right, give me a little...

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: What do you want me to do?

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay, are you sitting up there now?

a15a1064115.speaker: Scott
a15a1064115.text: Yeah, just stand by. (Long Pause) Okay. (Pause) Okay, overhead hatch is open and latched.

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: Okay. (Reading) Sit on the engine cover, facing forward, unlock the drogue, and rotate counter-clockwise to release.

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: (As per checklist) I'll block the sun from impinging on the instrument panel.

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: (I'm a) shadow device. (Long Pause) [Jones - "Why was it necessary to shade the instrument panel?"] [Scott - "So it won't get too hot. It wasn't really designed to take the heat."]

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: I just (garbled). [Dave is probably handing the drogue to Jim.]

a15a1064115.speaker: Scott
a15a1064115.text: Why don't you...Wait, wait. (Watch out for the) utility lights. That a boy. Okay, you got it?

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: I've got it. (Long Pause) [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "(Getting the drogue out) was very similar to the one-sixth-g airplane exercises we had."]

a15a1064115.speaker: Irwin
a15a1064115.text: Okay. 106:48:01 Scott: Give me the next step (in the procedure). (Pause) Go ahead, Jim; read the next step.

a15_1064802csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1064802csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. Give us Omni Bravo, please.

a15_1065022csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1065022csm.text: Houston, Endeavour. The - the Gamma-ray boom is out and took 2:30; 2 minutes and 30 seconds, fixed in.

a15_1065022csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1065022csm.text: Okay, let's get a good fix; hand me the compass there. (Long Pause) [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "(I had a) very good vantage point, primarily because we landed on a topographic high. This proved helpful; subsequently, when we were great distances from the LM, many times we could locate it."] [In Houston, the Flight Director is informed that, if the SEVA extends past 106:58, it will eat into the rest period.]

a15_1065022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1065022csm.text: Roger; 2 minutes and 30 seconds, Al. [Long pause.]

a15_1065022csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1065022csm.text: Want the map? 106:50:50 Scott: Just the Sun compass first. Let's get a pick on our position. (Pause) [Jones - "Did the Sun compass have a little gnomon/shadow device so that you could get it properly aligned?"] [Scott - "It was a card on which a circle was drawn with the highlights of the topographic features, the mountains around and the angles and a little flap that you would raise and align with the Sun so that the shadow fell within the marks on the map. And that would orient the card to where it should be and then you could look out at the mountains to see if they lined up. It was a backu

a15_1065022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1065022csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. One other thing, if you don't have it already, we'd like to have the S-Band Squelch, Off, so you'll realize the loss of signal, Over.

a15_1065622csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1065622csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. 30 seconds now to T-start for the Mapping Camera.

a15_1065622csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1065622csm.text: Rog, Gordo. I'm all set for it.

a15_1065622csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1065622csm.text: And now over to Spur and Window, I believe. [According to the Apollo 15 Photo Catalog, photo 11237 shows Contour Crater which is high up on the northern flank of Mt. Hadley Delta.]

a15_1065622csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1065622csm.text: Roger. (Pause) (Passing on a reminder from the Flight Director) And, Dave, we're coming up on 15 minutes SEVA. 106:56:54 Scott: Okay. (Long Pause) [Here, Dave is taking a 500-mm pan of Hill 305 (assembly by Dave Byrne). The frames are AS15-84- 11238 to 11241 .] [Jones - " Hill 305 has a number for a name. How come?"] [Scott - "Probably the elevation of that hill was 305 meters above something, because that's the normal way the Army designates a hill."] [In June 2003 it occurred to me that a more likely explanation is that the name refers to the azimuth of the summit as seen from the landing si

a15a1065723.speaker: Irwin
a15a1065723.text: When you finish with the 500, Dave, I have the other camera. [The third camera has a 60-mm lens and a color magazine.] 106:57:25 Scott: Okay. Try not to hit my foot there. (Long Pause) Looking back into the Sun is almost useless, Joe. Really blots everything out. [Dave has turned to the east to take a mini-pan of the base of Mt. Hadley (assembly by Dave Byrne). These are AS15-84- 11247 to 11249 . He will get much more extensive coverage of the mountain from Station 6 on the flank of Hadley Delta during the second EVA.]

a15a1065723.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1065723.text: Endeavour, Houston. When you have a minute, I have another Pan Camera PAD.

a15a1065723.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1065723.text: This one goes [in the box in the Flight Plan] at 108:10.

a15a1065723.speaker: Allen
a15a1065723.text: Rog, Dave. Any sign of the big mountain back there?

a15a1065723.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1065723.text: Okay. T-start is 108:15:27, and T-stop is 108:43:15. Over.

a15a1065723.speaker: Scott
a15a1065723.text: Yeah. You can see Big Rock Mountain back there! 106:58:07 Allen: Roger. Copy Big Rock Mountain . (Long Pause) [Big Rock Mountain is named for Rocco Petrone. Note that, at 106:57:57, Joe was not passing on a question from the Backroom but, rather, was reminding Dave to mention Petrone's mountain.] [Dave is taking 500-mm photos of Mt. Hadley Delta, starting with the striking feature known as Silver Spur , named for Caltech geologist Lee Silver. These photos are AS15-84- 11250 , 11251 , 11252 , 11253 . Mini-pan assembled by Dave Byrne. Compare the view of Silver Spur in 11250 with the one shown i

a15a1065723.speaker: Irwin
a15a1065723.text: Okay. 106:58:27 Scott: I think we'll get a chance to get a lot more of those (500-mm photos). Okay. Got it. [Comm Break. Dave now has the camera with a 60-mm lens and a color magazine. The photos in this color pan (assembly by Dave Byrne) are AS15-87- 11758 11730 to 11758 . David Harland has assembled a high-resolution version of the portion showing Hadley Delta and Silver Spur (1 Mb) . Marv Hein has created a VR version of the pan.] [Frame 11732 shows Hill 305 , which is on the west side of the Hadley Rille. ] [Frame 11747 is a good photo of Silver Spur and the Swann Range , named for U.S. Ge

a15a1065723.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1065723.text: Roger. The last seconds on the T-stop are 43:15. Is that what you've got?

a15a1065723.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1065723.text: Okay. For the information, the LM troops are in the middle of the SEVA now, and Dave is standing up in the hatch and taking the panoramic pictures.

a15a1065723.speaker: Scott
a15a1065723.text: Okay, Joe. We've got all the photos. (Handing the camera down) Here you go, Jim. 107:00:07 Irwin: Okay. I got it. [Next, Dave will describe the scene for the geologists in Houston.] [Jones - "What is the purpose of the horizon description?"] [Scott - "Just to describe the general geological setting. What's there, what's it look like, how you relate it from one place to another, are there any surprises, anything that we didn't expect?"] [Jones - "Is it a way to get you to look at it in a systematic way?"] [Scott - "Yes, in a sense. But it's a way to explore the area, to go look at it. On field

a15a1065723.speaker: Scott
a15a1065723.text: Okay. And let me start by 12 o'clock (west), Joe, and I'll go around real quick. On the far distant horizon, apparently across the rille, I can see - just about our 1 o'clock, now - a very large mountain, which I'd have to call Hill 305 .

a15a1065723.speaker: Scott
a15a1065723.text: And all of the features around here are very smooth. The tops of the mountains are rounded off. There are no sharp jagged peaks or no large boulders apparent anywhere. The whole surface of the area appears to be smooth, with the largest fragments I can see are in the walls of Pluton. There are no boulders at all on St. George, Hill 305, Bennett (Hill) , or, as far as I can tell, looking back up at Hadley. Hadley's sort of in the shadow. It's a gently rolling terrain completely around 360 degrees; hummocky, much like you saw on 14. The ridge line across the rille, from Hill 305 around to 1 o'cl

a15_1070143csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1070143csm.text: We'd like you to bring up the High Gain [Antenna]. Use Pitch of minus 38 and Yaw, 186. Over.

a15_1070143csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1070143csm.text: Okay, Houston; Endeavour. You've got the High Gain now.

a15_1070809csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1070809csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. Would you give us Auto on the High Gain.

a15_1070809csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1070809csm.text: Roger, Houston. Auto on the High Gain.

a15_1071341csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1071341csm.text: Okay. The SEVA's over; they're crawling back in to button up the LM, for your information. Also, we're contemplating another VHF comm check on the next rev. It will occur around 108:32, at the time you come over the LM horizon, and probably interfere with your photo of the Caucasus Mountains. We'll have more procedures after AOS. Over.

a15_1071341csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1071341csm.text: I can't see it as well as you can, Dave.

a15_1071814csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1071814csm.text: Endeavour, Houston, we're about to LOS, so see you next time around.

a15_1071814csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1071814csm.text: Okay, Gordo. See you on the other side.

a15a1072424.speaker: Scott
a15a1072424.text: (Unaware that they have hot mikes) I think I know where we are too. If I can just look at that map. (Long Pause)

a15a1072424.speaker: Scott
a15a1072424.text: Be sure I get that all the way up.

a15a1072424.speaker: Irwin
a15a1072424.text: Yeah.

a15a1072424.speaker: Scott
a15a1072424.text: Okay.

a15a1072424.speaker: Irwin
a15a1072424.text: Okay. Are you ready to do a little urine transfer?

a15a1072424.speaker: Scott
a15a1072424.text: Go ahead. You first. (Pause)

a15a1072424.speaker: Allen
a15a1072424.text: And, Hadley Base. Be advised, you're still on VOX.

a15a1072424.speaker: Scott
a15a1072424.text: How about that. Are you still VOX?

a15a1072424.speaker: Irwin
a15a1072424.text: No.

a15a1072424.speaker: Scott
a15a1072424.text: Down Voice Backup?

a15a1072424.speaker: Irwin
a15a1072424.text: I bet we are. I bet we're on hot miked.

a15a1072424.speaker: Scott
a15a1072424.text: Yes.

a15a1072424.speaker: Irwin
a15a1072424.text: Let's see.

Any feel for that?

a15a1072424.speaker: Irwin
a15a1072424.text: I'll have to ask Dave. (Long Pause) [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief, commenting on his observations during the SEVA - "I couldn't tell exactly why we had the tilt on the LM. a15a1072424.text: Houston, Hadley.

a15a1072424.speaker: Allen
a15a1072424.text: Go ahead.

And as you might have heard Jim and I discussing, there's a rather high crater density. And I guess my references to trafficability were really to boulders, because that's what I was really most concerned with on driving the Rover. There is a fairly high crater density around. a15a1072424.speaker: Allen

And we'll be standing by. 107:31:57 Scott: Okay, Joe. There's so much here, I could talk to you f

a15a1072424.text: Roger. We copy. And, Dave, earlier you talked about, specifically, a very bright crater, I think, fairly near by. Could you estimate for us the size, distance, and azimuth of that bright crater?

a15a1072424.speaker: Scott
a15a1072424.text: Stand by. (Pause) I can tell you're still looking for our position.

a15a1072424.text: No, that's not necessarily true. We think we're pretty well squared away on your position. This probably would cinch it down, though.

a15a1072424.speaker: Scott

They're listening to everything and it's triggering their thinking. You can see the system working in this. This is not a pre-planned question. a15a1072424.text: But, before we go, I got to tell you about a rock that's right out at 12 o'clock, almost at the radar antenna shadow, and it's going to be gone pretty soon. There's a dark, black, angular fragment which is on the order of, I'd say, 6 to 8 inches across. It's got some light-colored, apparent dust on it. It's unique on the surface. All the other fragments appear to be white. And this one really looks like a jewel. You can think about that for awhile.

a15a1073559.speaker: Scott
a15a1073559.text: Okay. Well, just tell him that I'll guarantee that it wasn't running when we touched down. a15_1080752csm.text: Roger, Dave. No hurry at all. [Long Comm Break]
