a15_1334613csm.text: Hello, Endeavour. Endeavour, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a15_1334613csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1334613csm.text: Hello, Endeavour. This is Houston in the blind. If you read, go Reacq and Narrow at angles of Pitch, plus 25; and Yaw, 185. That's Pitch, plus 25; and Yaw, 185. Over.

a15_1334613csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1334613csm.text: Hello, Houston; this is Endeavour. Go ahead.

a15_1334613csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1334613csm.text: Okay, Al, this is Houston. You're loud and clear now. I would like to suggest going to the presleep configuration before you bed down for the night there on the comm.

a15_1335202csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1335202csm.text: Okay. If you've gone through the presleep checklist, we noticed a couple of things. The optics power should go off, and also - in your DAP load, go to all ones in R-1. And, we'd like a call when you finally turn in and turn the voice mode off, just before you do that, please. Over.

a15_1335202csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1335202csm.text: Yeah. Okay, Gordo. Haven't been through the checklist yet.

a15_1340245csm.speaker: Fullerton
a15_1340245csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. No need to acknowledge, but we need the Mass Spec. Discriminator to Low as per an earlier update. Over. [Long pause.]

a15_1340245csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1340245csm.text: Gordo, was that Mass Spec, Discriminator, Low or Multiplier, Low? I got an update about 5 hours ago. It was - they said Multiplier, Low.

a15_1374500.speaker: Houston Comm Tech
a15_1374500.text: Honeysuckle Comm Tech, Houston Comm Tech. Net 1, voice check.

a15_1374500.speaker: Honeysuckle Comm Tech
a15_1374500.text: This is Honeysuckle Net 1. Loud and clear.

a15_1374500.speaker: Houston Comm Tech
a15_1374500.text: Roger. Loud and clear also, Honeysuckle.

a15_1374500.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1374500.text: This is Apollo Control at 139 hours, 11 minutes. Dave Scott and Jim Irwin will be beginning preparations soon for the second EVA at the lunar surface. Here in the Control Center, the flight controller teams which will be active during the EVA are beginning to arrive. Flight Director Gerry Griffin preparing to relieve Flight Director Milt Windler. And Flight Director Gene Kranz has reported. He - he will be handling the Command Module during the EVA period. The CapComs will be astronaut Joe Allen for the surface exploration and astronaut Karl Henize for the Command Module. We'll continue to sta

a15a1380343.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1380343.text: Good morning, Falcon. This is Houston. Over. (Pause)

a15a1380343.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1380343.text: Roger, Falcon; Houston. Loud and clear. And when you're up and ready to converse, let me know.

a15a1380343.speaker: Scott
a15a1380343.text: Okay, Gordo. Will do. [Scott - "Want to know one of the interesting coincidences? Gordon Fullerton now lives in a house I lived in in Lancaster (California). When he went to Edwards, he bought the house that I'd sold to another guy, who sold it to Gordy. Every once in a while, some mail will go to that house and I'll get a note from Gordy."] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "When we woke up the next morning, I was surprised how clean the spacecraft was. I think most of the dust had been removed. That's right. It surely had."] [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "That night (afte

a15a1380343.speaker: Scott
a15a1380343.text: Okay. There was some on the floor and the midstep , and we just never took the time to take a look in the back, but we will.

a15a1380343.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1380343.text: Okay. If you find any water back there, we have some suggested procedures to clean it up, and we'd like to do that before depressurization.

a15a1380343.speaker: Scott
a15a1380343.text: Rog. Will do. [Long Comm Break] [Scott - "If we had a problem, they should have awakened us early, to take care of the problem...if you want to stay on the timeline. Cause, if you ever get behind, you get behinder. You know, the old saying, 'Get ahead and stay ahead.'"] [Jones - "Otherwise, you might lose the North Complex or something."] [The reason for cleaning up the water prior to depressurization is to prevent sublimation in the vacuum which would not only cool the cabin but might also lead to ice formation on the hatch seal and/or various cabin systems. Indeed, the fact that there is, in

a15a1380343.speaker: Scott
a15a1380343.text: Hello, Houston; Falcon. Yes, we do have a little puddle of water back behind the engine cover. [If none of the 25 pounds of water had sublimated, the puddle would contain a bit over 11 liters. As can be inferred from the quantity of water involved - and Dave's statement during the post-flight Technical Debrief - Dave's "little puddle" is undoubtedly an understatement.] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "Sure enough, there was a great big puddle back there."] [Irwin - "I don't know if we'll ever get around to talking about that water leak that occurred. We had that slope, and the attitu

a15a1380343.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1380343.text: Okay, Dave. Our suggested procedure for collecting that will be to remove the netting and whatever is required to get down to it. [The netting is designed to keep things from falling behind the engine cover where they would be difficult to retrieve. See Figure 14-25 from the Mission Report .]

a15a1380343.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1380343.text: Use a used food bag as a scoop if it's a deep enough puddle to scoop it up and take one of the used (PLSS) LiOH containers that contains a used cartridge that's in the buddy SLSS bag now that's scheduled for the upcoming jettison. Take the LiOH cartridge out of the container, then use the container itself to hold the water as you scoop it up with the food bag. And then when you get down to the point where you can no longer get any more water, use utility towels to mop up the rest. Over.

a15a1380343.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1380343.text: And if one of you is not busy, I do have a Pad with the lift-off times for rev 32 to 37.

a15a1380343.speaker: Scott
a15a1380343.text: Stand by. (Long Pause) [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "The ground suggested using a food bag and LiOH canister to get it all up, and they wanted all the water cleaned up before we depressed. That was probably a pretty good idea because, immersed in the puddle of water, were a couple of glycol lines and some wires. Thereupon, we entered into another mopping operation. We took one of the large meal-container bags and cut it out like a scoop. And Jim passed me the canister cans. I scooped up the water, and then we took towels and dried up the rest of it. I think we got it completely dr

a15a1380343.speaker: Irwin
a15a1380343.text: Good morning, Gordo. I'm ready to copy.

a15a1380343.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1380343.text: Okay, Jim. One more tidbit on the water problem. According to our figures here, that ETB bag that has the cameras and film you are going to use on the next EVA may be back there where the water is, and we suggest you get it up out so it won't get wet. Over.

a15a1380343.speaker: Irwin
a15a1380343.text: No. That's taken care of. (Long Pause while Jim waits for Fullerton to start reading the Pad) Okay, Gordo. I'm ready for the Pad.

a15a1380343.speaker: Irwin
a15a1380343.text: Okay. 140:10:24; 142:08:33; 144:06:40; 146:05:03; 148:02:57; and 150:01:04. 138:14:31 Fullerton: Okay Jim. Your readback's correct. (Pause) And, Jim, one other question. If you can remember back to before you went to sleep; this is in reference to the problem you had with the ( RCU warning) flags at the start of the EVA-1, and we're figuring that that was probably caused by an air bubble that was in your PLSS feedwater system. We're wondering if, when you recharged the PLSS feedwater here after EVA-1, were you holding the PLSS in a vertical position? That would eliminate any possibility of a b

a15a1384952.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1384952.text: Falcon, Houston. Over.

a15a1384952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1384952.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a15a1384952.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1384952.text: We've got some conversation to come up to you regarding to some updates to the EVA prep and also about the EVA traverse plans. And if that would fit in with what you're doing, let us know and we'll go ahead and give those words to you. Over.

a15a1384952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1384952.text: Well, Dave is off comm right now, so I don't want to talk about the EVA plan or the traverse plan; but maybe EVA prep, I can talk to you about.

a15a1384952.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1384952.text: Okay, Jim. If you get a piece of scratch paper here, I'll give you the camera magazines that we figure should be in the ETB and on the cameras at the start of this. They've changed slightly from what you loaded last night. Over.

a15a1384952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1384952.text: Okay. Did Dave tell you what we had loaded last night?

a15a1384952.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1384952.text: I'm not sure; I'll have to check on that.

a15a1384952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1384952.text: I don't think we...(Pause) We have the ETB loaded, and let us tell you what we have in ETB.

a15a1384952.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1384952.text: Okay, fine. (Long Pause)

a15a1384952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1384952.text: Okay. The ETB is loaded per checklist (page 5-7) and the additional Mag is Mag Papa.

a15a1384952.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1384952.text: I understand. That's Mag Papa, is that correct?

a15a1384952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1384952.text: That's affirm. 138:51:57 Fullerton: Okay. (Pause) Let me cross-check that here and see if we can get any more words on that. Let me give you one other suggestion and that's for securing the high-gain antenna cable on the Rover (to prevent snags such as occurred at Station 2). We'd like to suggest that you get the roll of tape out, strip off about 1 foot, and fold a 1- to 2-inch tab on one end of it and wrap that piece of tape around the CDR camera so that after you get down to the Rover you can use it to secure the high-gain cable to the high-gain antenna mast and keep it from flopping around.

a15a1384952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1384952.text: Yes; we copied. [Without mentioning the need to secure the high-gain cable to the mast, at 141:44:46 Joe Allen will repeat the suggestion that the take some tape out with them. At 142:21:32 , Dave decides to stick some strips of tape to his checklist - perhaps because it's cleaner than his camera ; and does the taping job before 142:32:52 .]

a15a1384952.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1384952.text: Okay. One other thing is we suggest that you each wear your EVA-1 cuff checklist on your right arm for use at the end of EVA-2. That's for both of you. Over.

a15a1384952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1384952.text: (Very faint) Okay. (Long Pause)

a15a1384952.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1384952.text: Jim, this is Houston. Did you copy that about the tape?

a15a1384952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1384952.text: Oh, yes. We've already put that in the ETB. []

a15a1384952.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1384952.text: Okay. And can you give us a post-sleep status report there?

a15a1384952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1384952.text: Well, we both slept for the full time, and we'll get the PRD readings, if required, in a little bit.

a15a1384952.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1384952.text: Okay. Understand. [Long Comm Break]

a15a1384952.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1384952.text: Jim, this is Houston. Over.

a15a1384952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1384952.text: Go ahead.

a15a1384952.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1384952.text: On the ETB-load camera stuff, we'd like you to add Delta Delta - 16-millimeter Mag Delta-Delta - to the bag, and also, if you have your camera loaded with Kilo-Kilo, we'd like you to take it off, put Kilo-Kilo in the bag, and put Papa-Papa on your camera. Those are the only two changes that we see from what we figure you have right now. Over. [Magazine KK, or AS15-87, is a color mag that was partially used prior to descent and during the SEVA. Magazine PP, or AS15-90, is a fresh black & white magazine.]

a15a1384952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1384952.text: Let me jot down your recommendations again. Say again.

a15a1384952.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1384952.text: Okay, Jim. Add 16-millimeter Mag Delta-Delta to the bag load, first of all; and then on your 70- millimeter camera, that's the LMP 70-millimeter camera, take off...We assume that Kilo-Kilo is on it now. We'd like you to take that off and put Papa-Papa onto your camera. Over.

a15a1384952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1384952.text: You're suggesting we take 16-millimeter Delta out(side), and take Mag K off my camera and put Papa on my camera; but probably carry Kilo out with us.

a15a1384952.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1384952.text: That's affirmative, Jim. Carry Kilo-Kilo with you - and I think you said it right - but take Delta Delta along, also, in the bag. Over.

a15a1384952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1384952.text: Understand. [Long Comm Break]

a15a1392734.speaker: Fullerton
a15a1392734.text: Hadley Base, Houston. The only two items we have remaining to brief you on are the EVA plans themselves and a...(Long Pause) And Hadley, Houston. The item that slipped me there for a moment was PRD readouts when you get a chance. That and the traverse plans are all that are hanging (loose) so far.

a15a1392734.speaker: Scott
a15a1392734.text: Okay. [Scott - "I think we sort of ignored the PRD. (Joking) So, obviously, we're really concerned about radiation."] [Jones - "And the PRD was in a suit pocket, as I recall, and it wasn't until you started to get the suits on that it was handy to get at."] [Scott - "It is important to set the record straight on this, because of the Drury novel about the astronauts who got irradiated at Flamsteed Crater, and also Space by Michener, which are both incorrect. A lot of people think Michener's book is an historical account of the space program. It's not. It's really fiction. And, as time goes on,

a15a1400607.speaker: Allen
a15a1400607.text: Roger, Dave. We'd like a rough idea of where you are in your EVA Prep at this time. And we'd like an OPS (pressure) readout at your convenience. Just a reminder. Over.

a15_1403019csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1403019csm.text: Alfredo, it's looking like wake-up time. [No answer.]

a15_1403019csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1403019csm.text: Good morning, Al. They tell me you're sleeping very well right now; I'm sorry to wake you up. [No answer.]

a15_1403019csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1403019csm.text: Good morning, Al. On the planet Earth, August the first is creeping in upon us, and your bleary eyed Flight - CapCom down here is standing by at your service. [Long pause.]

a15_1403019csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1403019csm.text: Hello, Endeavour. Good morning. How are you doing?

a15_1403019csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1403019csm.text: Well, other than being rudely awakened, I'm doing fine, Karl.

a15_1403019csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1403019csm.text: Hey, I'm sorry that I have to do that, Al. Sounded like you were sleeping good. Hey, as the first step, can you give us High Gain [Antenna], Auto, and give us Accept for a state vector? [Pause.]

a15_1403019csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1403019csm.text: Okay, Karl. You've got them both.

a15_1403019csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1403019csm.text: Thank you. And we've got about ten minutes 'til LOS at the present time. When you've got a pencil and a paper, I'll give you a short Flight Plan update and a camera PAD. [Long pause.]

a15_1403019csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1403019csm.text: Okay, Karl. Go ahead. I'm ready to copy.

a15_1403019csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1403019csm.text: Okay. On the Flight Plan update at 141:03, they simply want you to add the report on the Gamma-ray and Mass Spec boom Delta-T's. [Pause.] And at 141:04 there is a "Laser Altimeter, On," which should be transferred down to 141:15. Those numbers come through okay? [Pause.]

a15a1403515.speaker: Irwin
a15a1403515.text: Houston, how do you read the LMP? (Long Pause)

a15a1403515.speaker: Worden
a15a1403515.text: Rog, Karl. I got you. At 141:03 you want me to report the Delta-T's on the retract for the booms; and move the "Laser Altimeter, On" to 141:15.

a15a1403515.speaker: Allen
a15a1403515.text: Jim, this is Houston. Were you calling?

a15a1403515.speaker: Irwin
a15a1403515.text: Yeah. Just want a comm check, Joe.

a15a1403515.speaker: Allen
a15a1403515.text: You're 5 by. [Comm Break]

a15a1403515.speaker: Henize
a15a1403515.text: Roger. And, over at 141:55, I guess we're having a look at photo target 25, and there's a friendly little note that goes with this. It says to be performed only if the CMP feels it won't interfere with his eat period. So, this is your choice. Do you want some numbers?

a15a1403515.speaker: Worden
a15a1403515.text: Roger. Let me have them.

a15a1403515.speaker: Henize
a15a1403515.text: Okay. Camera configuration. CM/EL/250/CEX, f/5.6, 1/250, infinity; 15 frames. And at 142:04, the actual [time to] execute [the photography]: photo target 25; A12, A13-P25. And, it says CM with window 3, with the same - with the same camera configuration: f/5.6, 1/250th at infinity; and 15 frames at 10 second intervals. Right, and this is magazine Q, pardon me. So much for the short Flight Plan update. Did the photo target 25 stuff come through okay? [Pause.]

a15a1403515.speaker: Worden
a15a1403515.text: I think I got most of it. But let me read it back to you just in case. Okay, at 141:55, that would be: set up cameras for photo target 25, at CM/EL/250/CEX, f/5.6, 1/250 at infinity, 15 frames; and then at 142:04 at A12, A13, photo target 25. CM, 3; and the settings going to be for 15 frames at 20 seconds from Mag Q.

a15a1403515.speaker: Allen
a15a1403515.text: Hello, Jim, this is Houston. Our biomed on you is a little noisy. We're wondering if you're all plugged up properly on that or if it's easy to get to those sensors still. Over.

a15a1403515.speaker: Irwin
a15a1403515.text: No, (they're) all plugged up, Joe.

a15a1403515.speaker: Allen
a15a1403515.text: Roger. Is it your biomed there that we're reading now?

a15a1403515.speaker: Henize
a15a1403515.text: Okay, everything's right except 15 frames at 10 second intervals - one zero.

a15a1403515.speaker: Irwin
a15a1403515.text: No. You're reading Dave's.

a15a1403515.speaker: Allen
a15a1403515.text: Okay. We're getting quite a noisy return down here. He may want to take a look at those sensors.

a15a1403515.speaker: Worden
a15a1403515.text: Ah, so. Okay, 15 frames at 10 seconds.

a15a1403515.speaker: Henize
a15a1403515.text: That's right. And the computer is yours.

a15a1403515.speaker: Worden
a15a1403515.text: Okay.

a15a1403515.speaker: Scott
a15a1403515.text: I'm all buttoned up, Joe.

a15a1403515.speaker: Henize
a15a1403515.text: Okay. The only other important thing on this front side pass is to get up the camera PAD to you. [Pause.] That's about the same page there...

a15a1403515.speaker: Allen
a15a1403515.text: Roger.

a15a1403515.speaker: Scott
a15a1403515.text: Is it usable data? 140:38:47 Allen: Stand by. And in the meantime, have you put tape over the canisters that are filled with water there (as per the discussion at 139:06:56 )? And if so, we're a little worried down here that you may have taped it so well that it's making an airtight seal now, could you comment on that?

a15a1403515.speaker: Worden
a15a1403515.text: All right, go ahead.

a15a1403515.speaker: Henize
a15a1403515.text: ...okay. The Mapping Camera Photo PAD starts 141:17:26; [and stops] 144:09:30. And right down below is the Pan Camera PAD, [starts] 141:46:11; [stops] 142:01:31. And as a part of this, just across the page there, at 141:45, we would like to move down that statement, "Mapping Camera Image Motion, Increase;" move that down to 57 - 141:57. And that's all.

a15a1403515.speaker: Irwin
a15a1403515.text: We put the locks back on, Joe.

a15a1403515.speaker: Allen
a15a1403515.text: That sounds good. [Comm Break] [Scott - "I think the top of the canister is locked on by a band - that's an overcenter-latch kind of band. And it sounds like we just put that back on, so it wouldn't be airtight but it would hold it tight."] [Jones - "You want the pressure to come out of there."] [Scott - "But you don't want it to leak."] [Jones - "You want it to be able to respond to cabin depressurization."] [Scott - "I wonder why they didn't suggest that in the first place, instead of tape. If that is, indeed the mechanical case."] [Jones - "So somebody did think about that in terms of your

a15a1403515.speaker: Worden
a15a1403515.text: Roger. Understand. The Mapping Camera photo PAD is, 141:17:26; 144:09:30. The Pan Camera photo PAD is 141:46:11; 142:01:31. And move the "Mapping Camera Image Motion Increase to talkback, barber pole" from 141:45 to 141:57.

a15a1403515.speaker: Henize
a15a1403515.text: That's excellent. I - I also have science report, which you can probably pick up on the next rev, and consumables report. And I guess we would like a status report from you. We could either do that now or early in the next rev. How do you feel about it?

a15a1403515.speaker: Irwin
a15a1403515.text: Joe; my PRD reading this morning is 8029...No, 24.

a15a1403515.speaker: Allen
a15a1403515.text: Roger, Jim. Copy 8024. Thank you.

a15a1403515.speaker: Worden
a15a1403515.text: Oh, I can give you the status report now, I think, Karl. Stand by one. [Pause.]

a15a1403515.speaker: Scott
a15a1403515.text: And, Joe, mine's 5020.

a15a1403515.speaker: Allen
a15a1403515.text: 5020, Dave; thank you. [Comm Break]

a15a1403515.speaker: Worden
a15a1403515.text: Okay, Karl, I guess - crew status report: Got 6 hours sleep all in one period, and a very good night's sleep, I might add; and my PR - no medication, and my PRD [Personal Radiation Dosimeter] is 23149.

a15a1403515.speaker: Henize
a15a1403515.text: Roger. 23149. [Pause.]

a15a1403515.speaker: Worden
a15a1403515.text: And standing by for the consumables. [Long pause.]

a15a1403515.speaker: Henize
a15a1403515.text: What was that comment on consumables? Would you like to copy them now?

a15a1403515.speaker: Worden
a15a1403515.text: Roger, Karl. Might as well get them now.

a15a1403515.speaker: Allen
a15a1403515.text: Hello, Jim. This is Houston.

a15a1403515.speaker: Henize
a15a1403515.text: Okay. The time is 140 hours; RCS total is, 61 [percent]; quad A, 61; [B] 61; [C] 59; [D] 61; H 2 tanks, 70, 70, 48; O 2 tanks, 75, 78, 60. [Pause.]

a15a1403515.speaker: Irwin
