a15_1414541csm.text: Rog, Karl. Right with you. [Long pause.]

a15_1414815csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1414815csm.text: Al, if you're not too busy now, I could send you up a science report. And I can cue you on that Gamma-ray Gain Step.

a15_1414815csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1414815csm.text: Righto. Here we go. On X-ray Spectrometer, words by Izzy Adler say the general health of the X-ray experiment is excellent and a large amount of useful data is being received.

a15_1414815csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1414815csm.text: Okay, Jim. We'll go through it (meaning the LMP comm check on 6-4) again. (Pause) Okay; you're connected. And go to A.

a15_1414815csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1414815csm.text: Okay, Karl, go ahead. It's on. [Pause.]

a15_1414815csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1414815csm.text: (Squealing) Houston, how do you read the LMP?

a15_1414815csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1414815csm.text: Okay. One more comment on the Gamma-ray Spectrometer. It says that regional differences have been observed in the quick look data, but details will require computer analysis for confirmation. So they're beginning to see some point-to-point differences there also.

a15_1414815csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1414815csm.text: Okay, you're still too loud. You got a squeal.

a15_1414815csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1414815csm.text: Yeah, I'll turn it down a little bit. How's that?

a15_1414815csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1414815csm.text: That's better. Okay. (Reading) " CB(11) Comm, CDR Audio, open, and connected to PLSS comm ." In work. (Long Pause) Okay, I'm in B, I have a Press flag and an O; O2 Momentary. Pressure gauge, and how do you read, Jim?

a15_1414815csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1414815csm.text: I read you loud and clear.

a15_1414815csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1414815csm.text: Okay, you have to check with Houston.

a15_1414815csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1414815csm.text: Dave and Jim, we read you both loud and clear. MP3 Audio Clip ( 19 min 30 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Okay, they read me loud and clear.

a15a1415133.speaker: Allen
a15a1415133.text: Roger. Go on to next step.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: PLSS mode for you to B and me to A. (Pause)

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay, how do you read, Jim?

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Loud and clear.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay, you're loud and clear to me, and Houston, how do you read the CDR?

a15a1415133.speaker: Allen
a15a1415133.text: Roger. You're both 5 by.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay. Let's both go to AR.

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: AR.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay, AR. You're loud and clear to me; how me to you?

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Same.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay, Houston. How do you read the LMP and the CDR again? And how's your TM?

a15a1415133.speaker: Allen
a15a1415133.text: Okay, Dave. We're loud and clear on both, and we're Go for the next step.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay. My PLSS O2 quantity is 90 percent. How about yours, Jim?

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Reading 92.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay. "CB(16) ECS, LCG Pump, close."

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Closed.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay. "LCG, cold as required." [Once they turn off the LM LCG pump, they won't have cooling until they have depressurized the cabin and have started PLSS cooling. Here, they are taking one last opportunity to cool down before shutting off the pump and disconnecting the LM water hoses. Pete Conrad and Al Bean added this cool-down step, on their own, during the preparations for their first Apollo 12 EVA. See the Apollo 12 Lunar Surface Journal at 114:53:38 and following.] [Scott - "An example of procedures evolution."]

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: "CB(16) ECS Cabin Repress, close; verify."

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Verified.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: "Suit Fan Delta-P, open."

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Open.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: "Suit Fan 2, open."

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Open.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay. "Verify ECS caution and H2O SEP component lights on, about a minute." (Pause) And there they come. (Pause) Oop, got a tone. Yeah; okay. (Pause) [They are now on checklist page 6-5.]

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: " Suit Gas Diverter (Valve) , Pull-Egress; verify."

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: That's verified.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: " Cabin Gas Return (Valve) , Egress; verify."

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: That's verified.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: " Suit Circuit Relief (Valve), Auto; verify."

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: That's verified.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay. "OPS connect; LMP first. Suit Isolation (Valve) to Suit Disconnect."

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Suit Disconnect.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay. Why don't you slip around here? (Pause) (I'll) get your OPS. (Pause) That water is cold, isn't it? (Pause) Okay. "OPS O2 hose to PGA blue to blue." (Long Pause)

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: I'll turn off the LCG Pump. (Dave laughs, probably because he is getting quite cold) (Pause) [Scott - "When my water started going through...I mean, it was a great system. Your whole body, all of a sudden, got cool!"]

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay. That's closed and locked. What's the next\ step? (Garbled) Look where I'm hooked again. I'm hooked the same place. The PLSS stowage handle.

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Okay. "Retrieve purge valve, verify closed; and lock pin, In and Lo. Install purge valve red to red."

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay. (Yawns; Long Pause) Okay. Purge valve is in, and locked, and locked.

a15a1415133.speaker: Worden
a15a1415133.text: Roger, Karl. We can check that out, and - if we don't see anything there, we can check it out during the EVA.

a15a1415133.speaker: Henize
a15a1415133.text: Very good. Good idea. On the...

a15a1415133.speaker: Worden
a15a1415133.text: And, the Mass Spectrometer is now fully retracted. Talkback is gray.

a15a1415133.speaker: Henize
a15a1415133.text: Wonderful. Just recycling it a couple of times, and it finally came in; is that what happened?

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Okay, (PGA) diverter valve's going vertical. (Pause) Okay, repeat on you. [As shown in Figure I-23 in the EMU Handbook , the diverter valve is part of the oxygen inflow connector and gives them the option of directing the PLSS oxygen flow entirely into the helmet (the vertical position) or partly into the suit torso (the horizontal position). Generally, the astronauts put the diverter valve to horizontal only when they were in the cabin and were trying to dry the suits out a little. In the hoizontal position, used in the cabin, all the incoming oxygen stream is divided between a duct leading t

a15a1415133.speaker: Worden
a15a1415133.text: Well, it took - I guess probably a half a dozen re - just recycles, jogging it out, then pulling it back in again and that may be - that may be the problem. Maybe that cable is kinking some way or other.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay. You're going to have to...Yeah, suit disconnect.

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Suit disconnect...

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Get...My O2 hose has just sort of drifted up there.

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay.

a15a1415133.speaker: Henize
a15a1415133.text: Okay. Real glad to hear you got that gray talkback.

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Okay, I'll disconnect your (LM O2) hoses. (Pause) And we'll connect the PLSS O2 hose. (Pause) In (and) locked.

a15a1415133.speaker: Henize
a15a1415133.text: Incidentally, the boys on the surface just about took a shower bath this morning. They had a small water leak in the gun there that let loose a couple of gallons of water. It was a major perturbation, although they've got it cleaned up pretty well. And they're running about an hour, to an hour and a half behind their time line on the second EVA. They haven't got out yet.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay.

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Okay. The purge valve. (Pause) Very low. (Pause) Okay, all locked, and the pin's in. (Long Pause) Okay. And it's locked.

a15a1415133.speaker: Worden
a15a1415133.text: Roger. Understand. [Pause.]

a15a1415133.speaker: Henize
a15a1415133.text: Okay, Al. We have about 10 seconds before we give an Image Motion Increase for the Mapping Camera.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay. "PGA diverter valve to vertical." Take a little drink. (Pause) Did you turn the Descent Water off? (Pause)

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Hose (garbled) last... (Pause)

a15a1415133.speaker: Allen
a15a1415133.text: Dave, that Descent Water was turned off on your PLSS recharge exercise.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Rog. We figured that out. It's working okay.

a15a1415133.speaker: Allen
a15a1415133.text: Roger.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay.

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Descent water closed. And stow that hose properly.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Yeah, man.

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Put it in the holster and I'll...

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay.

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: ...(get the) cable stowed (Long Pause)

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay; it's stowed. (Pause) Okay, helmet and gloves donning. (Pause) Okay. "Position mikes, both. PLSS fans on, Right. Vent flag clear." (Pause) Okay, my fan's coming on. Got a tone. Vent flag's clear. (Pause) (Looking at Jim's RCU ) Okay, your vent flag's clear. Let's get your LEVA . (Pause)

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: That's yours.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Yeah. (Pause)

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Put the flaps...

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Yeah. (Pause) Okay; let me get your water (that is, the in-suit drink bag ). And your food stick . (Pause)

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Here, I'll line it up.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Yeah, you line it up and I'll push it.

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: Okay, it's lined up.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: Okay. Wait, let me get this...(Long Pause)

a15a1415133.speaker: Irwin
a15a1415133.text: That did it.

a15a1415133.speaker: Scott
a15a1415133.text: (Chuckles) (Pause) There. Closed and locked. Let's get the back flap. (Long Pause) Okay; front flap. My turn. (Pause) [Next, they will get Dave's helmet on.]

a15_1420059csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1420059csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. You have 30 seconds until Pan Camera Mode goes to Standby.

a15_1420059csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1420059csm.text: Okay, you watch my water spigot there?

a15_1420059csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1420059csm.text: You may have to push it some.

a15_1420323csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1420323csm.text: Al, we're still waiting for a cue on the lens stow, and in the meantime, photo target 25 is roaring down on us.

a15_1420323csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1420323csm.text: Rog, got it in sight. [Long pause.]

a15_1420323csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1420323csm.text: Push them just as far back as you possibly can, Dave.

a15_1420323csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1420323csm.text: Yeah, I will. (Long Pause) Yeah, they're snapped in the ECS handhold. I think they'll hold today. (Pause) Okay. You got your hoses stowed?

a15_1420323csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1420323csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. We can go Pan Camera Power, Off.

a15_1420949csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1420949csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. When you get the camera stowed, I have one more small item, and then we'll give you some time to get out some food.

a15_1420949csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1420949csm.text: Okay, my PLSS O2 is On.

a15_1420949csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1420949csm.text: And mine's On. (Pause) Okay, and the press flag should clear at 3.1 to 3.4 (psi). (Pause) I'm coming up. (Pause)

a15_1420949csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1420949csm.text: Okay, Al - we're finding out that the - tight deadband in P20 is using a little more RCS propellant than we'd anticipated. Nothing's critical yet, but we would like to take - some preventive measures here. And we suggest that you go into the DAP - and load in a CSM weight of 30000, thirty thousand. And before you erase the current LM weight record it [corrects himself] the current CSM weight, record it for future use. We think that'll cut down the thruster firing a bit.

a15_1420949csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1420949csm.text: Mine's clear. (Pause) [Apparently, Jim's O2 flag cleared almost immediately.]

a15_1420949csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1420949csm.text: No, I'm sorry; no; I didn't clear the (tone)...

a15_1420949csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1420949csm.text: Yeah, there's your tone; yeah, mine too. (Long Pause) Okay, I'm off the peg.

a15_1420949csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1420949csm.text: Okay, understand. Rog. You want me to go back and reload the DAP with a CSM weight of 30,000 and record the current weight that's in there for future use.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1421615csm.text: Endeavour, a news bulletin from the surface says that they are now depressing the cabin; and there is no need for you to acknowledge. Keep eating.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1421615csm.text: Roger, Houston. Understand that, and - one point from here, Karl, - I'm over the spot in Imbrium, I think close to where you and Whitaker drew some, or figured out, some lava flows coming out of where the wrinkle ridge is, and at this low Sun angle, I can very clearly see some lava flows coming out of what appears to be a ridge, extending in both directions from the ridge. And I wasn't set up in time to take a picture of it, but it might be interesting on the next pass if we could get a - if we could get a PAD to take a picture of that.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1421615csm.text: Coming down [to] about 5.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1421615csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1421615csm.text: We'll breath it down. (Pause)

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1421615csm.text: And, Falcon...

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1421615csm.text: Take a while at this rate.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1421615csm.text: ...the PLSSs look right on.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1421615csm.text: (Responding to Joe) Okay! Thank you.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1421615csm.text: Jim, your PLSS water recharge cured that problem we had yesterday completely, it looks like.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1421615csm.text: Good.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1421615csm.text: Yeah, it was worth the effort then. (Pause)

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1421615csm.text: Very interesting. Which window are you looking out?

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1421615csm.text: Those tones are a little disturbing. (Pause)

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1421615csm.text: I'm looking out window 3.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1421615csm.text: Window 3; that sounds like it's down to the south of you, then.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1421615csm.text: Just slightly north of groundtrack.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1421615csm.text: Okay. Well; " partially open the forward hatch." Maybe I can get that if you'll slip over there...

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1421615csm.text: Very good.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1421615csm.text: That's right. Just down in the south, just a little.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1421615csm.text: Thank you. Sounds like an interesting observation, and I'm sure the guys down below will be sending you up more work to do as a result. Be careful there, now.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1421615csm.text: A bit tight.

a15_1421615csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1421615csm.text: ...about as far as you can go. Careful not to get hooked. (Pause) That's it. Okay. (Long Pause) Okay, got a tone. (Long Pause)

a15a1421855.speaker: Scott
a15a1421855.text: Let's see. Let me see if I can get around the hatch here and give you some more room.

a15a1421855.speaker: Irwin
a15a1421855.text: Well, maybe I can get my arm back there. (Pause) Yeah. I've got my arm back there. No sweat, Dave.

a15a1421855.speaker: Scott
a15a1421855.text: Okay. Mine's Open. (Long Pause) Get it okay?

a15a1421855.speaker: Irwin
a15a1421855.text: Just a minute. I think it's on. Yeah. It's on.

a15a1421855.speaker: Scott
a15a1421855.text: Okay. I'll tell you, my gloves feel a lot better today.

a15a1421855.speaker: Irwin
a15a1421855.text: (Laughs) Stretched them a little bit yesterday, Dave.

a15a1421855.speaker: Scott
a15a1421855.text: Yeah. I think you're right. (Pause) Okay. "Rest until cooling sufficient", after we get the water going. And "verify the CWEA status". We might do that. The ECS and PREAMPS. Okay. (Pause) And I got a tone and a clear water flag. How about that? (Long Pause)

a15a1421855.speaker: Irwin
a15a1421855.text: Mine hasn't cleared yet. (Long Pause) 142:21:32 Scott: Okay. Let me get that (piece of duct) tape up by your left elbow.

a15a1421855.speaker: Irwin
a15a1421855.text: Yeah. Why don't you take both?

a15a1421855.speaker: Scott
a15a1421855.text: Yeah, I will; in case I drop one. Stick it right on my cuff checklist. (Long Pause) [At 138:51:57 , Gordon Fullerton asked Dave to take some tape outside to secure the high-gain cable to the mast to keep it out of the way of the TV camera and suggested that he wrap a piece around his camera. Less specifically, at 141:44:46 , Joe suggested that Dave put some tape &quot"in your pocket for later". The EVA-2 cuff checklist is the only clean surface on Dave's suit and, therefore, is the only surface the tape will stick to. Dave will do the taping job before 142:32:52. ] [Jones - "You had separate c

a15a1422253.speaker: Scott
a15a1422253.text: Hey, Jim, let me get the old hatch open here. If you can...Okay...Yeah.

a15a1422253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1422253.text: Let me turn the other way, Dave.

a15a1422253.speaker: Scott
a15a1422253.text: Okay. (Pause) Make it all right? (Pause)

a15a1422253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1422253.text: Okay, I'm around.

a15a1422253.speaker: Scott
a15a1422253.text: Okay.

a15a1422253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1422253.text: Get the hatch open a little farther today.

a15a1422253.speaker: Scott
a15a1422253.text: Oh, yeah; it's much better. (Pause) Okay, I'm going to come around this way today. (Pause) Little easier.

a15a1422253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1422253.text: Just me. [Dave may have bumped into Jim as he turned; and Jim is reassuring him that he hasn't hit any of the equipment.]

a15a1422253.speaker: Scott
a15a1422253.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay. (Pause)

a15a1422253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1422253.text: Whoa, Dave, whoa.

a15a1422253.speaker: Scott
a15a1422253.text: Okay.

a15a1422253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1422253.text: Now you can get down. You were hung up on my RCU .

a15a1422253.speaker: Scott
a15a1422253.text: Okay. (Pause) How does that look to you? Okay?

a15a1422253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1422253.text: Yeah, that looks like you're pretty well cleared there. (Pause) You're well centered. I could get your (PLSS/OPS) antenna right now if you'd like.

a15a1422253.speaker: Scott
a15a1422253.text: No, let me get out.

a15a1422253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1422253.text: Okay. (Pause) Wanna hold right there?

a15a1422253.speaker: Scott
a15a1422253.text: Yeah. Why don't I hold here and you can get it.

a15a1422253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1422253.text: Okay. Your antenna is up. [Jim is on EVA-2 cuff checklist page LMP-3 and Dave is on CDR-3.]

a15a1422253.speaker: Scott
a15a1422253.text: Okay, you might check the...The water gun came out (of its stowage bracket) again.

a15a1422253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1422253.text: Sure did.

a15a1422253.speaker: Scott
a15a1422253.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1422253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1422253.text: Hold there, and I'll get the BSLSS bag ( 159k ) and all our...

a15a1422253.speaker: Scott
a15a1422253.text: Yeah, do that.

a15a1422253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1422253.text: ...gear. (Pause)

a15a1422253.speaker: Scott
a15a1422253.text: Okay, Houston. I'm out on the first rung of the ladder, and we'll take care of the jettison procedures here.

a15a1422253.speaker: Allen
a15a1422253.text: Okay, Dave. According to our calculations, here, you'll just about fill Hadley Rille with water (collected from behind the engine cover).

a15a1422253.speaker: Scott
a15a1422253.text: (Laughs) Yes, sorry to say. (Pause) Okay. That's...That a boy. Good. (Pause) Okay; one (water-filled LiOH) can's down. (Pause) [The timing in this sequence indicates that as Jim pushes the LiOH canisters and other articles out through the hatch, Dave takes them and drops them over the railing, probably on the right (south) side to avoid hitting the MESA.]

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1422537csm.text: As I look at the map, Al, it looks to me like you're going smack over Tsiolkovsky every rev now. How is it looking to you?

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1422537csm.text: That's just about right, Karl. Coming right over the middle of it.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1422537csm.text: That's all right, Jim. Just like the last one. That a...Oop. Little...Push with your foot? That's good. I got it. Okay. Canister going down. (Pause) Okay; toss it right here. That a boy. (Pause) Okay, the other can is down. Okay, a Jett bag. I mean, the BSLSS bag.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1422537csm.text: That must be a beautiful sight. Hey, I was sort of fascinated by the fact that, on your first couple of revs, you noted that you could really see the peaks sticking up - the central peak before you could see the rim. Is that really true?

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1422537csm.text: Yeah. (Long Pause)

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1422537csm.text: Okay.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1422537csm.text: Just a minute...

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1422537csm.text: You dropped it. Oh! I've got it. (Pause) Okay; it's down. And if you can hand me the ETB.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1422537csm.text: Stand by. (Long Pause) [The ETB contains the cameras and, consequently, Dave will carry it down by hand.]

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1422537csm.text: Easy does it; that's it.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1422537csm.text: Got her?

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1422537csm.text: Hey, that would be great to get pictures of that. I don't know when you were scheduled to look at that - that landslide on the northwest corner of it, but are you seeing anything of that area?

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1422537csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1422537csm.text: Good. (Pause) 142:27:19 Scott: Okay, down the ladder to the plains of Hadley. (Long Pause) By golly. Just like we left it yesterday.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1422537csm.text: Absolutely, I look at it every time I go by and there's just - there's no question in my mind at all that it is a - that it is a - rock avalanche. It - it does have some interesting qualities about it, though. And it's a little bit hard for me to decipher right now, but it seems like the density of crater impacts in that slide is - is greater than in the surrounding terrain, even though the slide had to be emplaced on top of the surrounding terrain. Maybe it's just that the craters are - are fresher in that - fresher looking in that particular material. But no question about the lineaments bei

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1422537csm.text: Jim, this is Houston with a request.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1422537csm.text: (To Dave) Good. (To Joe) Go ahead, Joe.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1422537csm.text: Roger, Jim. We're seeing some excursions in your Delta-P (pressure difference on) the Glycol Pump 1. We'd like for you to pull the Auto Transfer circuit breaker on that Glycol Pump, and select Pump number 2. Over.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1422537csm.text: Okay, stand by. Okay, I'm pulling Auto Transfer now; and I'm selecting Pump 2. Is that affirm?

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1422537csm.text: Roger. That sounds interesting. [Pause.]

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1422537csm.text: That's affirm; thank you. (Long Pause) 142:29:05 Scott: (To himself) Okay. Pick up the pallet. (Long Pause) Oh, boy; is that easy and fixed. My! (Pause) [Dave is removing pallet number 2 from the MESA. It contains PLSS LiOH canisters, PLSS batteries for EVA-3, and food for the remainder of the LM mission. They will not do a pallet transfer during EVA-3.]

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1422537csm.text: Guess I'd add one other comment to that. So far, I haven't been able to locate the other one. [Pause.]

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1422537csm.text: Say again on that, Al? [Pause.]

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1422537csm.text: So far, I haven't been able to locate Alvin.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1422537csm.text: Roger. Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1422537csm.text: Okay, "PLSS LiOH cans, check the pins are in." (Pause) Green.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1422537csm.text: Al, Alvin heard that, and he feels crushed. [Pause.]

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1422537csm.text: Pins is green, yeah.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1422537csm.text: Yeah; they're green. Okay. Transfer the old pallet.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1422537csm.text: Well, tell him not to worry. I'm sure it's there and I'll - I've just got to get a little bit further south around the edge of the crater.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1422537csm.text: Sounds good.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1422537csm.text: Okay. Hey, when you can get the Flight Plan and a pencil, I've got a - a few more updates to finish up on this rev. [Pause.]

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1422537csm.text: Don't have to put an LiOH (canister for the ECS) in it. So, I guess it makes it little easier. [Jim loaded an ECS LiOH canister in Pallet No. 1 at about 120:52:24 during the early stages of EVA-1.]

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1422537csm.text: Just so there's plenty of food in it, Dave.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1422537csm.text: Yeah, that's a good idea. (Long Pause) [At some point, possibly here, Dave carries the pallet up the ladder to Jim. The lack of discussion about the LEC clearly indicates that they are not using it at this point in the mission. The Apollo 16 and 17 crews wouldn't use the clothesline version of the LEC at all.]

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1422537csm.text: Okay, go ahead.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1422537csm.text: Okey-doke, let's go over to 143 hours. And, at 143:09, we want to add...

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1422537csm.text: Say, Houston, Endeavour. Go ahead with your up-dates, Karl.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1422537csm.text: Roger. At 143:09, we would like to add "Laser Altimeter, Off". At 143:12, in that P20 there, we would like you to do a "Verb 25" instead of a "Verb 24"; and we would like to add, in addition to your two angles there, we would like to add "Omicron plus 161.00." Did that come through?

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1422537csm.text: Joe, before I get out, do you want to close the Auto Transfer? Or, do you want to leave it...

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1422537csm.text: Stand by, Jim....

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1422537csm.text: ...in that configuration for the EVA?

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1422537csm.text: ... Stand by on that. I think we probably will. I'll give you some words shortly.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1422537csm.text: Okay. I'll call you before I get out.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1422537csm.text: Roger. [Comm Break] MP3 Audio Clip ( 11 min 31 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1422537csm.text: Rog. Understand, we're going to do - Omicron - add omicron to that load of plus 161.00.

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1422537csm.text: Roger. And we're going to do the same trick over on 144 hours and 26 minutes. We want add, again, to that load, we want to add "Omicron as plus 180.00." [Long pause.]

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1422537csm.text: Understand. At 144:26, you want to add a "Verb 25, Noun 78" - "Omicron plus 180.00."

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1422537csm.text: That's correct. Next change is over on 146:13. [Pause.] And over there we have a "Laser Altimeter, Off," which had already been put off before so you can delete "Laser Altimeter, Off."

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1422537csm.text: Rog. Delete "Laser Altimeter, Off."

a15_1422537csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1422537csm.text: And then, if we go over to 151 hours. [Pause.] At 151 hours and 10 minutes, we would like to change the Pan Camera operation there, and we would like to say "Stereo Exposure, Normal." And at 151:15, we would like to delete the "Pan Camera Exposure, Normal." [Pause.]

a15a1423239.speaker: Allen
a15a1423239.text: Okay, Dave, how're you doing?

a15a1423239.speaker: Scott
a15a1423239.text: Oh, I'm doing just fine, Joe. I'm getting the high-gain antenna squared away for you, hopefully. 142:32:52 Allen: Okay. And while you're working there, Dave, you did such a beautiful job on fixing Jim's PLSS antenna, we've got another Walter Mitty repair job we'd like for you to carry out for us, please, on the cable lead from the high gain antenna to the LCRU, and when you think you're at a good place to do that, I'll go through a description of what we need. [Mitty was the fictional hero of the James Thurber story, The Secret Life of Walter Mitty . In real-life, Mitty was an unremarkable, in

a15a1423239.speaker: Worden
a15a1423239.text: Okay, I understand. At 151:10 you want that to read "Stereo Exposure, Normal;" and at 151:15, delete that line.

a15a1423239.speaker: Henize
a15a1423239.text: That's correct, and that's the end of the update.

a15a1423239.speaker: Worden
a15a1423239.text: Okay.

a15a1423239.speaker: Scott
a15a1423239.text: Gee, I'm right there, Joe.

a15a1423239.speaker: Allen
a15a1423239.text: Roger, Dave. Basically, our camera keeps hanging...

a15a1423239.speaker: Irwin
a15a1423239.text: And, Joe, I'm going to put...

a15a1423239.speaker: Allen
a15a1423239.text: ... our camera keeps hanging up on that cable, and we'd like for you perhaps, if you think it's feasible, to tape a part of a cable below the fastening device on the staff of the high-gain antenna. If you think a piece of tape right there might help, we suggest you go ahead and do that now. 142:33:52 Scott: Joe, I just completed that little task. It's all done! [As requested by Houston , Dave brought a piece of tape out to secure the cable. In a before-and-after comparison ( 0.25 Mb or 0.5 Mb ), a detail from AS15-86- 11602 (left) shows the configuration at the end of EVA-1 of the cables conne

a15a1423239.speaker: Irwin
a15a1423239.text: Dave, if you are clear, I'm going to pitch the pallet out.

a15a1423239.speaker: Scott
a15a1423239.text: I'm clear, Jim. (Pause)

a15a1423239.speaker: Irwin
a15a1423239.text: And, Joe, I'm in a position to get out. Let me know what the final configuration is on the glycol pumps.

a15a1423239.speaker: Allen
a15a1423239.text: Jim, the best I can do for you right now is ask you to stand by one minute. We're going to make a final decision.

a15a1423239.speaker: Irwin
a15a1423239.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a15a1423239.speaker: Allen
a15a1423239.text: And, Dave, as you might guess, when Jim comes out, you can delete that step to deploy his antenna.

a15a1423239.speaker: Scott
a15a1423239.text: Yes, sir. Will do.

a15a1423239.speaker: Allen
a15a1423239.text: I have a very keen sense of the obvious.

a15a1423239.speaker: Scott
a15a1423239.text: No, that's a good reminder, Joe.

a15a1423239.speaker: Irwin
a15a1423239.text: Don't worry; I wouldn't let him do it, Joe.

a15a1423239.speaker: Allen
a15a1423239.text: Shows you're thinking.

a15a1423239.speaker: Irwin
a15a1423239.text: But I sure would...(Stops to listen to Allen) Time's a wasting, Joe. (Pause) You're going to get way ahead of me, Dave.

a15_1423529csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1423529csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. They have some data on that new DAP configuration, with the new weights. I guess we're not sure we want to stick with it, and at this time we'd like you to go back to the normal DAP load with the normal weight.

a15_1423529csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1423529csm.text: It's alright. [Scott - "He's up there waiting for them to tell him on the glycol pumps. And he knows that our tasks are sequenced. We're working in parallel. So, he's saying I'm going to get way ahead of him, 'cause I'm doing my tasks and he should be doing his. He's standing up there, knowing he's falling behind and waiting for them to tell him about the glycol pumps, and wanting to get going."] [Jones - "Not only is it putting him a couple of minutes behind but, at some point, it's going to put you a couple of minutes behind."]

a15_1423529csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1423529csm.text: Okay, Jim, requesting you go back...

a15_1423529csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1423529csm.text: You get too far ahead, you might have to go out and drill a little bit.

a15_1423529csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1423529csm.text: Okay, select Pump 1, Jim, and then close the...

a15_1423529csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1423529csm.text: Okay, Karl. Understand you want me to go back to normal DAP load and normal weight.

a15_1423529csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1423529csm.text: Auto Transfer circuit breaker. Close the circuit breaker when you're on Pump 1.

a15_1423529csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1423529csm.text: Roger. And, I was so busy talking, I forgot to cue you on [extending] the Gamma-ray boom [19 minutes ago]. I trust you have started - you got that out yet, or did I talk you out of thinking about it.

a15_1423529csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1423529csm.text: Okay, Auto Transfer, closed, and I'm egressing.

a15_1423529csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1423529csm.text: Roger. Sounds good. [Comm Break] [Once Jim is down on the surface, he will be on cuff checklist page LMP-4.] 142:37 33 Irwin: Okay, I'm down. 142:37 37 Allen: Roger, Jim! Copy. (Long Pause) Dave, this is Houston...

a15_1423529csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1423529csm.text: Did you record an extension time on that?

a15_1423529csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1423529csm.text: No. I didn't get that, Karl.

a15_1424507csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1424507csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. All your systems look Go as you go around the corner. And see you on the other side.

a15_1424507csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1424507csm.text: And Mag Delta is on the 16 millimeter, and it seems to be working okay.

a15_1424507csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1424507csm.text: Okay, Karl. See you on the other side.

a15_1424507csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1424507csm.text: Good; okay. And, Joe, I'm in a position to take another crack at that steering, if you'd like to talk me through the procedures. [Dave is ahead of Jim in his list of tasks and has a chance to check the steering while Jim completes the tasks on LMP-4.]

a15_1424507csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1424507csm.text: Okay, Dave. We want you to exercise the Forward Steering switch by cycling from Bus A to Bus C and back several times; and then stop with the switch finally at Bus Charlie.

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Okay, the blankets are open a hundred (percent); on Internal; PM1/WB.

a15a1425024.speaker: Allen
a15a1425024.text: Roger.

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: And the SESC (Special Environmental Sample Container) is going into my seat bag. (Pause) Oh, we're going to have a lot of bags under my seat, Joe.

a15a1425024.speaker: Allen
a15a1425024.text: Okay, Jimmy. I hope we can fill some of them.

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: I guess that will be all right. (Responding to Joe) Oh, we'll do our best. 142:51:19 Scott: There. Get the lens brush out. Try to take care of those lens. (Pause) Hey, that works pretty good.

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Work good?

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Man, does it ever. Bright and shiny.

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Let's see, you still have some sample bags on your camera, don't you?

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Yeah, so do you, Jim.

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Better put these under the seat then.

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Okay.

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Why don't I just put one under your seat and one under mine? 142:51:55 Scott: Yeah. That's good. I'll tell you that lens brush really does the trick.

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Yep. (Pause)

a15a1425024.speaker: Allen
a15a1425024.text: Hence the name, Dave.

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Say again.

a15a1425024.speaker: Allen
a15a1425024.text: Roger. I say hence the name. 142:52:23 Scott: Oh. Rog. Hence the name. (Pause) Well, our cameras, as you might have expected, got pretty dirty yesterday. As a matter of fact, we were having to wipe the dust off of the settings every time we took a picture so we could see them, and the lenses got pretty dusty, but they're all cleaned off now.

a15a1425024.speaker: Allen
a15a1425024.text: Yes, sir, we copied and sounds good now. (Long Pause) [This exchange suggests that Dave is taking care of some of the equipment tasks on CDR-5.]

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Give me a call when you're ready, Jim.

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Yeah. (Pause) Still sorting out the bags.

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: That's okay. Better to have them right. (Pause) Get to my tongs, here. (Pause) Okay. (Long Pause) [Because both yo-yos broke during the first EVA, Dave and Jim will stow the tongs and scoop between the seats.] [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I positioned the scoop extension handle on the left-hand side of my seat, kind of under the bracket, at the attachment of the seat to the Rover frame. It did ride fairly securely there."] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I took the tongs and stuck them under the left-hand side of my seat between the seatpost and the (seatpan) bag, and

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Okay, Dave, I guess I'm in a position here; I got bag number 2 on the right side. (I'm in) position to put your gear on you (as per LMP-5)...

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Okay.

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: ...and you on me (as per CDR-5).

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Okay, stand by one, Jim.

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Okay. In the meantime I'll look at the seatbelt. See if I can do anything with it.

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Okay. [Comm Break] [As indicated in the dialog at 142:56:47 , Dave is probably collecting the glass ball they have decided to call an Aggie.]

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Adjustments all the way out on my seatbelt.

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Okay, I think without the extension handle, it ought to work okay. (Pause) [Because both yo-yos broke during EVA-1, neither of them will be wearing tongs. They should be smaller around and the seatbelts should fit better.]

a15a1425024.speaker: Allen
a15a1425024.text: Dave and Jim, this is Houston. Are you...

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Careful how you do ...

a15a1425024.speaker: Allen
a15a1425024.text: ... putting the collection bags on now?

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Yeah. Just starting.

a15a1425024.speaker: Allen
a15a1425024.text: Okay. [They're at 0:39 in the checklists and 41 minutes into the EVA. The EVA started at 142:14:44 .]

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Ready, Jim?

a15a1425024.speaker: Allen
a15a1425024.text: We think you should wind up with collection bags 3 and 7 on your PLSSs and not collection bag 2, which still should be under the seat. (Pause) I'm sorry, not on the PLSSs, on the Hand Tool Carrier. I called that incorrectly. [Jim's prior transmissions indicated that he correctly put onto the HTC and pallet the bags called out in the checklist.]

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Two should be on the Hand Tool Carrier, right-side.

a15a1425024.speaker: Allen
a15a1425024.text: Right. 142:56:25 Scott: Yeah. On the PLSSs, Joe, we're going to put on number 2 and number 5, just like in the (checklists)...

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: No, that's wrong.

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Huh?

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: That's wrong.

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Oh, you changed it, huh?

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Somehow the wrong gear's in bag 2.

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: How did that happen?

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: We still have the core tubes in here.

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Oh, yeah! [Because EVA-1 was shortened, they did not have a chance to use the core tubes in SCB-2. See the dialog at 125:44:19 .]

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: I'll get bag 3.

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Okay.

a15a1425024.speaker: Allen
a15a1425024.text: Okay, Jim, that's right on. 142:56:47 Scott: Hey, Joe, by the way, bag...(Listens to Joe) Okay. (Pause) Joe, bag number 162 has that little glass aggie in it.

a15a1425024.speaker: Allen
a15a1425024.text: Roger, Davy. You never walked past it. Beautiful. [An aggie is a type of playing marble. A genuine aggie was made of agate stone as opposed to a glass imitation. A more complete discussion of the name can be found following 108:30:36 . Prior to collecting the aggie, Dave took 86- 11604 , a cross-Sun from the north. He had noticed this small glass sphere on the ground under the Rover stowage position prior to the first EVA at 108:30:36 . The piece of hardware on the ground is probably a so-called "pip-pin" that was pulled off the Rover during the deployment. The "aggie" is above the slightly-bu

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: No, the right one is still up!

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Yeah, the right one is still up.

a15a1425024.speaker: Allen
a15a1425024.text: Okay, Jim. Thank you. We will ask you to move that one down before you climb on.

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Okay. (Long Pause) 142:58:47 Scott: (To Jim) Yeah, they really stretch. Hold on the bag a minute, Jim. The straps really stretch. (Pause) [Dave is probably talking about the tool harness which they fit over the PLSS during the EVA Prep, as per checklist page 3-6 .]

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Now, if you could stand up straight, just for a second.

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Man, I am straight.

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Are you kidding!

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: (Chuckling) I'm (standing) in a crater. You want to move back?

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: No, I can get it. (Pause) Okay, take a step forward then. Give me the bag. (Pause) Okay, a little to the left. There. No, rotate left. Now, okay. (Long Pause) Sure glad they put so much Velcro on here. (Pause) Okay, now if you could bend over, Jim. Take a step. Well, if you can take a little step forward. Don't fall down in the hole.

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Try not to.

a15a1425024.speaker: Scott
a15a1425024.text: Okay. Get me? [Now, Jim will put SCB-5 on Dave's PLSS. While it is not absolutely certain as to which bag Dave just put on Jim's PLSS, the dialog following 142:56:25 suggests that it was SCB-3.]

a15a1425024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1425024.text: Okay. (Long Pause) Snaps came open there on your flap. . (Long Pause) Okay. Hang on; I'll...(Pause) Okay, your bag is secure.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Okay, Dave. Once again, we want you to exercise the forward steering procedure here.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Okay. You want to try it first just the way it was and then we'll try the circuit breaker, right? 143:04:15 Allen: Roger. (Pause) The Forward Steering switch should be at Bus Charlie, and the Forward Steering circuit breaker should be finally closed, and then attempt forward steering. 143:04:34 Scott: You know what I bet you did last night, Joe? You let some of those Marshall guys come up here and fix it, didn't you? [Design of the Lunar Rover was supervised by NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center, Huntsville Alabama. The vehicle was built by Boeing.]

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: They've been working. That's for sure.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: (Laughing) It works, Dave?

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Yes, sir. It's working, my friend.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Beautiful.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Lot of smiles on that one, Dave. We might as well use it today.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Boeing has a secret booster somewhere to (send engineers to the Moon to) take care of their Rover! (Pause)

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Oh, that's so much better. (Pause) See if I can find a level spot around here. (Long Pause) Okay Houston, I'm at the Nav site, and I'll reset here, and I'll give you the readings.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger, Dave. Standing by.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Okay. As a matter of fact, to make sure we're balanced, I'll hop off. (Pause) Okay, roll is one (degree) to the left; pitch is about, oh, one down; and bearing, distance, and range have recycled to zero and the heading on there now is 305; and the Sun shadow device is about, oh, a half to one (degree) to the right.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger, Dave. And when you are ready you can start torquing towards 285, and we'll modify that in a minute.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Okay. (Long Pause) Okay. Want to hop on Jim and see if you can get it...

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: I was going to get cameras all adjusted. Okay, we wanted 12 frames per second.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Jim, while you are climbing on there, we're going to want you to start out towards course 160 for a distance of 1.9 clicks towards Checkpoint Number 1. [The LM is at about map coordinate BS.4/73.3.] [The LM is clearly visible in a detail from Pan Camera frame 9377 provided by the Lunar and Planetary Institute.] [Checkpoint 1 is at BL.3/75.9 . The planned landing site is at BQ.0/74.0.] 143:07 52 Irwin: Just a minute, Joe, I didn't... 143:07 54 Scott: Wait. You got to get up, Jim. You're leaning too far back. Grab the handle low. That a boy. Okay, now you can set down. You're in good shape. 143:

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Yeah.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Oh, you wait, wait, wait, wait, wait, wait. (Pause) You've got to sort of bias it to the right. 143:08:23 Allen: And, Dave, your torquing angle, exactly, 283, over.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Okay, 283, Joe. Can you get your seatbelt, Jim?

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: I'm doing that right now.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Huh? (Pause) Get it up and over the (strap-on thigh) pocket ( 153k ); let me have it here a minute. There, now; bet you can get it. (Pause) Let me get it. 143:08 53 Allen: Rover, did you copy 283 heading, and we're standing by for total Nav readouts before you depart the station. 143:09 01 Irwin: Okay, Joe. We'll park it at 283 (meaning that they will adjust the heading to read 283). Reading about 284 now. Bearing, distance, and range, of course, are zero; amps are 100, 108; (battery temperatures are) 68 (and) 78; and motor temps, forward and rear, are off-scale low.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger, Jim. Copy. And the motor temps are normal.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay, you going to torque to 283 Dave.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Yeah, just hold on. That darn cannon plug again down there. [Having helped Jim with his seatbelt, Dave is now trying to get his own belt on and is having the same trouble he had during EVA-1 with his belt catching on the cannon plug which is alongside the seat on the outside.]

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: You want me to hold it for you.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: No. I have to get off and unhook this thing every time.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: That's bad because every time you bend over like that you put strain on that PLSS antenna.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Do I really?

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: It bumps against this low-gain (antenna which is mounted on Dave's inboard handhold).

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Oh, I have to be careful. (Pause) Okay. (Pause) Here we go. (Pause)

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Okay, my seatbelt's on. Is your seatbelt on?

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Yes, sir.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Okay. (Pause) Here we go!

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: You got to torque that 283...

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: ...It's almost on 283. (Pause)

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Okay, it's 283. Okay. 143:11:13 Irwin: Okay, we're off, Joe; we're moving.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: What's the heading, partner?

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: (To Joe) Give us that heading again.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger; and we're marking. We want you to proceed towards Checkpoint Number 1. Your general heading is 160 at 1.9 clicks and this may take you down between Salyut and Index Craters.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay. [Salyut is at BO.2/74.5 and Index is at BO.8/76.5 on the EVA-1,2 Part A map . A larger scale map shows the named features at the site and a map by Journal Contributor Ken Rattee shows an excellent approximation to the actual traverse. The latter can be compared with a traverse map from the Lunar Sourcebook , which has significant errors.] [By chance, the bearing of the planned landing site from the actual site is about 160 degrees, so Dave and Jim actually are driving toward checkpoint 1.]

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Okay 160. I'd like to go down there and see those (two craters), just for drill.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger, Dave. No one should come to Hadley Rille without seeing Index Crater, and we'll try to keep you posted on when you're coming up on that.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: (Chuckles) Okay, fine.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Joe, I'm going to start the (16-mm) camera here. Will you keep track of it? I'm on 12 frames per second.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger, Jim. We're marking it now. Thank you.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Wait a minute. Why don't you hold off for awhile, Jim?

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay. Never mind.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Hold off.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Let me get squared away here.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Hey, Joe, the steering is a new task, Joe. It's really responsive now. I guess I got pretty used to quiet steering, and this thing really turns!

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger, Dave. We don't want it to be too easy for you.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Hey, look. We can always disengage the rear steering.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: No, I'll get used to it, it's just a matter of getting used to. 143:12:48 Irwin: Okay, on our left, now, we have a very large subdued crater. I'd estimate 4- or 5-hundred meters across. It has a crater of about 25 meters (diameter) on its eastern, inner wall, about half way to the bottom. And on that smaller crater there's some rock exposed. Looks like some bedrock exposed, in that particular crater. [The 'very large subdued crater' is Last Crater, which has an actual diameter of about 200 meters. The smaller crater on the eastern wall is readily visible in a detail from Pan Camera frame 9809

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: I'm going to hold up here.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: You want to disengage rear steering, maybe?

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Yeah.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay, we're stopping, Joe.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Just a minute.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Okay, Jim. Stopping.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Okay, try it that way.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay, we're moving again.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger. And your description is remarkable, remarkably similar to Index. Perhaps you're looking at Index Crater.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: I guess it's the largest crater that I've seen, Joe, as far as (lost under Joe).

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger. We'll reserve judgment on that, but keep describing, please. Sounds great. [Based on the bearing and range they report at 143:15:30 , they are now somewhere near the southern end of Last Crater, and are about a kilometer northwest of Index Crater.]

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay, we're heading 155 and at our 1 o'clock position, there's a doublet. Gee, I think it's the doublet we drove across yesterday. I'll tell you in a moment when we see our tracks. Do you want to talk, Dave?

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: I just want to tell them I turned off the rear steering to see how she works with the front and it's really a lot better. The double Ackerman's a little too responsive when you have the lack of traction, especially on the slopes. [Double Ackerman means having both front and rear steering.] [Jones - "Does 'lack of traction' refer to the wheels being off the ground?"] [Scott - "Yeah. Moving relatively fast on an irregular surface, you don't have much grip. And then, with both front and rear wheel steering, you oversteer because, if the wheel comes off and it's being turned, it comes down at angl

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger, Dave. Copy that. Why don't we save the double Ackerman for the rougher terrain later on.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Yeah. I think that's a good idea.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay, Joe. I mentioned those...It's really a triplet arrangement here that we just passed on our right. I did not see our tracks.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: So we're definitely east of our track from yesterday.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger; copy. [The cuff checklist pages covering the traverse are CDR-6, which is blank: CDR-7, which covers the to the now-deferred Station 4; CDR-8, which is a sketch map of Station 4; CDR-9 which lists features of potential interest on the way to Checkpoint 2; and CDR-10, which covers the traverse between Checkpoints 2 and 3. Jim has identical pages in his checklist. The decision to defer Station 4 was discussed at 139:43:48 . The checkpoint locations are shown on the EVA-2 contour map .]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, range is 0.6. We're heading 160.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: And we're doing about 8 to 9 clicks.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Okay, Dave. Sounds good. Standing by for amps.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay; amp reading is...Let me get my hand down there, Dave (to shadow the gauge). I want to put my hand down there to get the amps.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Okay, go ahead. (Pause) Let me get it.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: I got it. Okay, the max looks like about 10 amps.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger, good enough. 143:16:58 Irwin: Get no reading on 2. (Pause) Okay, coming up on our right is a very subdued crater again. No blocks at all on its rim, and it is about 50 meters in diameter. [Jones - "In talking about crater sizes and the presence of blocks on rims, some people would use that as an indication of the depth of the regolith. Would that have been something you were thinking about?"] [Scott - "I think this is an observation, not a conclusion."] [Jones - "But you're providing data for that kind of analysis."] [Scott - "Sure. And subdued and old and rounded versus sharp, angular.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Okay. Let me stop and get the rear steering going.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay. We stopped, Joe.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger. (Pause)

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Now we're going again, Joe.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Okay.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: And I see a very large crater over at 1 o'clock. [This may be Salyut.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Okay, let me just get the steering squared away here, Jim.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah. Okay, we've stopped.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger, Jim; and that might very well be Earthlight at 1 o'clock. And Domingo Crater should be on your left, now. [Earthlight is at BJ.5/75.5 and Domingo is at BK.3/76.3. Houston still thinks Dave and Jim are a kilometer south of their actual location. See the EVA-2 map and the map showing feature names .]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay. We'll give you a little more report when we get a little closer to it.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: I'm going to hold off too many comments here until Dave gets the steering squared away.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger. [Scott - "There is so much to see up there, all of which is brand new - because, again, we had no photography at this resolution, whatsoever. So, old Jim is just having a ball! All this stuff to talk about, and it's all different and all new. And I'm trying to get the thing to steer. I can't wait! That was part of the excitement of the whole region, 'cause you could have just stopped there, and you could have looked around, and you could have spent several hours describing what you see, 'cause it's all so different."] [Jones - "Even at the 17 site - where they had good overhead photogra

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Joe, it feels like the rear steering, when I turn it off, doesn't center. Feels like my rear wheels are drifting. So I guess I better turn it back on. (Pause)

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger, Dave. We agree...

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: And we're gradually increasing. A very gentle slope.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: ...maybe you should turn it back on.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: (To Joe) Yeah, I guess you might think about why they don't center for us.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger. That sounds like the Rover moves like Jim's sand crabs move. (Jim laughs)

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, that's just exactly what it feels like too.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Dave, if you could swing to the right here, we could go by the rim of Earthlight - what Joe is calling Earthlight (but is probably Salyut).

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Good. Let's do that. Well, there's a big thing here in front of us, too.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, but we could swing...Can you get around to the right? Maybe not!

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: No, let's go to the left. We're not going to stop at Earthlight. Let's go left.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Because that's a big excursion there. (Pause)

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, now we're going downslope.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Well, we're going in and out of the craters.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: I get the impression, out to our left, that there is a shallow depression there.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Gee, over to the left there is a big hole. Huh? See that over there?

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: A big subtle crater. Oops, and we're coming up on a sharp one!

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Hey, you got those two ahead of us there?

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah. See if we can find a reasonable path through here. (Pause) [Scott, from a 1996 letter - "(The preceding dialog) is a pretty good indication of the irregularity of the surface. I have yet to see a photo that captures the many, local elevation changes. It would be great if somebody could do a surface model and then put the LRV on it, provide a driver's-eye view, and then 'IMAX' it!]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, we're heading 140; we're out to 1.0 (km from the LM).

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger; Jim, copy. [What seems likely is that, in order to avoid Salyut, Dave has turned to a heading of 140, as indicated on Ken Rattee's map by the bend to the east immediately north of Salyut and directly west of Index. If they are 1.0 kilometers from the LM at a bearing of 160, they are near BO.6/74.7 . The 'sharp' crater that Dave mentioned at 143:19:42 could be the raised-rim crater at about the 1:30 position just outside the rim of Salyut that is marked on a detail from Pan Camera frame 9809.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Doing 9 clicks.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Beautiful.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: I think we're going by a very large one here, over at the 9:30...9 o'clock, Jim, huh?

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yes. [On a heading of 140 passing northeast of Salyut, they would have Index would, indeed, be at a 9 o'clock with the near rim no more than 250 meters from them. Index is about 350m in diameter.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: What do you suppose that is?

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: It could be Domingo.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: No, it's too big!

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Too big for Domingo?

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Couple of hundred meters.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Let's see, 1 out...Let's see, Checkpoint 1 is...You said 1.7.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Dave and Jim, that could be, possibly, Index Crater, if you started from where we thought. The distance is right on that. And continue on towards Checkpoint 1.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Okay, I would say that probably was Index. It was about that size.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, you've got the right bearing.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah. That's nice, huh?

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah. We're going for 1.7.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Going for. Yeah, okay, we're 1.2 now.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah. [Houston suggested an average heading of 160 degrees and, as Dave indicates at 143:21:55, their average heading - corresponding to a bearing of 340 degrees - is very close to the suggested figure. At a range of 1.2 kilometers, they are near BN.9/74.9.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: There's a nice deep one there that's smooth and rounded, about 30 meters across. [The 'smooth, round' crater could be the one at about BN.4/75.1 which is also marked on the detail from Pan Camera frame 9809.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: You know, on one of these trips, we ought to stop at one of these very fresh ones and really sample it.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: On the way back we'll get that one.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah. I mean these small ones, you know, just filled with...

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Oh, yeah.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: ...rock debris and glass in the middle. Just do a systematic sampling on it.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Like this one over here at 1 o'clock.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, I know what you mean. (Pause) Okay, bearing is now 339 and the range is 1.3. Look out, oh! Note that, because the range is given by the nav system in tenths of a kilometer, the range uncertainty is at least plus or minus 50 meters, which corresponds to plus or minus 0.2 map units. That is, for this location more or less south of the LM, the indicated location is between BN.3 and BN.7.] [Rattee puts Dave and Jim a

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Ohhhh! Whoa baby!

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Okay. We're all right.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yup. (Pause) Great machine.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah; does it good. (Long Pause)

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Okay, Rover, Checkpoint 1 is 160 at 1.9 clicks, and there's no need to stop there. We can press on towards Checkpoint 2, if you're satisfied.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah; Rog. I guess we're okay, Joe. [Jones - "Would you have ever contemplated stopping at one of these checkpoints? It's just a distance/bearing point, isn't it?"] [Scott - "I don't recall. It was a feature, but it wasn't a station. But, if it was of interest, you might stop because you would think you knew where you were."]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, we've got the right bearing. We're at 1.4 now, Joe.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Okay, Jim, and we're enjoying your description.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Why don't you just give them a running comment; I'll keep my eyes on the road.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, there's a...

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Sounds like a good idea. 143:23:22 Irwin: (Lost under Joe)...a crater on our right now about 50 meters in diameter with a lot of gray fragments on its rim. And we're just passing one (rock) that's sitting right on the surface - about 2 feet, subangular. I can look out now and see the South Cluster and I get the impression of perhaps, some horizontal beds in the first mound in the South Cluster. I do see a lot of blocks over in that direction; particularly the second mound - the west side of the second mound that appears to be in the Secondary Cluster.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger, Jim. Copy.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Probably over the area of Crescent. [As indicated on the map showing feature names , Crescent Crater is the northwestern member of the South Cluster.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, we're 1.7. And, again, we have a very fresh crater on our left with several blocks. [They left the LM at 143:11:13 and, therefore, have an average, straight-line speed - or range rate - of 7.8 km/hr.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: The blocks (are) about a meter or so and the crater is probably about 15 meters, like it might have excavated or been a secondary, huh?

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, well, notice all the debris here, that the surface is covered with more debris in this particular area than what we've seen before.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, it sure is.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Just around that particular crater.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, "more" being probably 2 percent (surface coverage).

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: (Chuckles) Yeah.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: It's noticeably more.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger. We copy that. And, Jim, you may want to start your (16-mm movie) camera, if you think this is a good area, and don't hesitate to fire off shots from the hip with your 70 millimeter. [On Apollo 16 and 17, Charlie Duke and Jack Schmitt took traverse photos at regular intervals with their Hasselblad cameras during the traverses. They were wearing their cameras on their RCU brackets and had no trouble getting good horizon centering. Photo AS15-85- 11471 , which Jim took at the start of the EVA, shows Dave seated on the Rover with his camera pointed virtually level.]

a15a1431615.text: Okay, I'm going to start the...

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Point it (meaning the 16-mm camera) down, Jim; it's pointed up a little too much, here.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay. (Pause) About like that?

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, that's dandy.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, I'm starting the camera, Joe.

a15a1431615.text: Roger. We got the mark, and we'll watch it. 143:25:38 Irwin: Tracking...(Responding to Joe) Okay. In the picture, we can see that Jim's got a map mounted on the accessory staff. We can even see your OPS antenna. This was taken toward the west, so Bennett Hill is in the background. a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Reckon we can get between those two there? Yeah. (Pause) It's a bridge between two, about 20 meters in diameter, a little doublet and the one on the left has got a bunch of debris, and the one on the right has got nothing, huh, or very little.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Boy, there was a very large crater over on our 1 to 2 o'clock position.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Oh, yeah! [They have been driving for two minutes since giving their last range readout of 1.7 km and, if Dave has been driving more or less away from the LM, they are now at a range of about 2 km and are somewhat north of Earthlight Crater . As Jim indicates in a moment, they are also somewhat east of Earthlight, perhaps near BL.1/76.5 .]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: That's the largest one...Oh, I guess it would be equal (to or) maybe larger than...Well, larger than Elbow, certainly.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, it looks like it. You can't see too much of it but it does...

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: I don't see that on the map.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Dave and Jim, we think you might be looking at Earthlight now. It might be...Its long (meaning north-south) dimension is greater than the east-west dimension. On the north side, Earthlight appears to overlap a smaller, shallower crater which may have contributed to the apparent elongation shown in the pre-flight maps and may be visible from the ground.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, well that's certainly true. Certainly true. (Pause) Okay, you would have us east of Earthlight.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Hey, here's a big deep one here (lost under Joe) 143:26:57 Allen: That's exactly correct. And Arthur Clarke would be proud of you. On their return from the Moon they sent me the beautiful relief map of Falcon's landing site, which now has pride of place in my office. It shows the routes taken by the Lunar Rover during its three excursions, one of which skirted Earthligh

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: ...about 50 meters...(Stops to listen to Joe) 143:27:03 Irwin: Okay, and on the south...I can just barely see the western slope of Earthlight. But the southern slope of it, I can also see, has several blocks on it.

a15a1431615.text: ...the quantity indicator. Why don't you feel it?

a15a1431615.text: I did and...

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott

a15a1431615.text: Okay, it's stopped now.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah; why don't you try it again. (Pause) Make a little turn here.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, it's trying to run, Dave.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Okay, point it to the forward and let's see if it will...I just noticed that the film counter wasn't going.

a15a1431615.text: Yeah. I hope we don't have another...

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: ...film problem.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Dave and Jim, the film counter may not have dropped off the hard-stop yet. It's only been going a couple minutes. We need a range and bearing, if you'll give it to us, please. And continue on; we'll watch the camera.

a15a1431615.text: Okay, bearing is 358; range is 2.2.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger...

a15a1431615.text: I think bearing's 338.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: ...and let the camera run.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, isn't that what I said? What did I say?

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: You said 358.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, 338.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger; copy. 338. (Long Pause) [They are now near BK.2/76.6 . On Ken Rattee's map , they are very close to that location, which is east of Earthlight and NW of Crescent , which is the large crater immediately NE of Dune. .] MP3 Audio Clip ( 12 min 11 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15a1432900.text: Yeah, sure does. (Quietly) Oh, come on. Easy does it. (Pause) Look at that big hole there, Jim! Are we up on Dune? Yeah, there's a rampart over there.

a15a1432900.text: I was wondering whether we could possibly be at Dune.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott

a15a1432900.text: Dave, I think you're probably...

a15a1432900.text: Crescent? Boy, that's the biggest one we've seen.

a15a1432900.text: ...looking into Crescent. [As shown on the larger-scale, Apollo 15 Named Features map, Crescent Crater is the northwest member of the South Cluster.]

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: Yeah, I think it is.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Yeah, I guess you're right, Joe.

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: 'Cause this little one, just to the right of us here, I see it on the map. [The 'little one' may be a small feature east of Earthlight and northwest of the larger crater on the rim of Crescent at BJ.0/77.0 . The 'BJ.0/77.0' crater is circled in yellow on Ken Rattee's map .]

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: So, yeah, that's Crescent.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Yeah, I guess you're right. That's a big fella isn't it? [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "When we went by the big craters, Crescent and Dune, they were really subdued. They sure weren't very obvious."]

a15a1432900.text: Okay.

a15a1432900.speaker: Allen
a15a1432900.text: Exactly correct, Jim...

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: Oh, yes.

a15a1432900.text: Jim, disregard...

a15a1432900.text: You want a bearing of 334?

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: Okay. Yeah, checkpoint 2. Okay. [Checkpoint 2 is at BA.7/76.8 .]

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Hey, we're in a debris field now, Joe, with fragments on the order of 6 inches to a foot, in general, and maybe, oh, I'd say almost 5, (to) 8 percent coverage. Wouldn't you, Jim?

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: Yeah.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: And there are some (rocks) that are up to a couple of feet that require some maneuvering.

a15a1432900.speaker: Allen
a15a1432900.text: Roger. [The Rover has a 14-inch (0.36 m) clearance.]

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Let's see, I think I'll go left around this one, Jim, and then swing over to the right.

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: Okay, yeah, that'll be good.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Lots of...The smaller ones are deeper here. Man, there's one (meaning a crater) and that's got direction to it (that is, a noticeable asymmetry). (The crater is) about 4-meters across and (it has) a big block in it on one side, on the south side.

a15a1432900.speaker: Allen
a15a1432900.text: Roger. [Dave's observation strongly suggests that the crater was dug by the block and that the impacting object was coming in from the north at low speed and a relatively low angle.]

a15a1432900.speaker: Allen
a15a1432900.text: We're looking in particular for fresh craters, lots of frags, good sampling drill holes into the Front and mare. a15_1433145csm.text: Yeah, I'm afraid the rim might be (lost under Joe)

a15_1433145csm.text: Okay.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Henize

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1433145csm.text: Our world's up here right now, Karl.

a15_1433145csm.text: Oh, yeah, you called them right, I think. Secondaries. I think they just splattered right up the slope. Because they're the only craters on the side of the mountain. a15_1433145csm.text: Up on your planet, the latest word is that the Rover is still functioning - functioning brilliantly, and the fellows are well into EVA number 2 and just recently passed Crescent Crater and Dune Crater - well on their way to exploring the Front at Hadley Delta.

a15_1433145csm.text: Yes, sir. Avoid that fella. [Hate to get] stuck in there. (Pause) Okay, we're going south. (Pause)

a15_1433145csm.text: Okay, Jim, and please continue. (Pause)

a15_1434915csm.text: Okay, see this little crater up on the ridge line here at 1 o'clock? I think that's where I'll head, Jim. We'll call that something or another. And you know, I can see an inflection point (meaning a slope change) here as we go upslope. Another inflection point.

a15_1434915csm.text: There aren't any like that, Joe! Just aren't any! They're all very subtle up here.

a15_1434915csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1434915csm.text: Okay, Dave. I guess we want to continue on towards the east, and keep your eyes open.

a15_1434915csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1434915csm.text: Well, we're up on a little ridge here. And I think it would do well for us to stop here and sample the rocks we can see in this area, and then head over to that boulder, there. See how we do, okay?

a15_1434915csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1434915csm.text: Okay.

a15_1434915csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1434915csm.text: What do you think about that, Joe?
