a15_1434915csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1434915csm.text: Yeah, we have a number of fragments in our local area, none having really been excavated from a particular crater. There is no crater up here which has excavated a lot of debris. They're all very subtle and old, but there are rocks on the surface. So, I think, our best shot here is to hop off and gather up a number of these rocks in our vicinity. I bet we can get, oh, 10 (to) 12 very easy, and then think about that.

a15_1434915csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1434915csm.text: Okay, that sounds great. Let's press on.

a15_1434915csm.speaker: Irwin

a15_1434915csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1434915csm.text: Yeah, you're right.

Fendell gives us a good view into Spur before pointing the camera down at the LCRU mirror and, after a few seconds, the camera's own shadow on the ground in front of the Rover.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Jim?

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Yes.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Why don't you come over here and get your scoop and scoop me up one big rock?

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: And...

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: And get your camera on it, because I don't...I don't have any film. How about this one right here that looks like it has some layering in it? Maybe...

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Yeah, that's the one I was talking about.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Right there?

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Yeah.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Why don't you...? 146:07:51 Irwin: You want to point to it with the...

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah, I've got my foot right there. Why don't you take a couple of cross-Suns real quick?

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Seven feet, cross-Sun? (Pause) (You're) a little too far away, old buddy. (Pause)

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay. [Jim's cross-Sun stereopair is AS15-90- 12235 and 12236 , which, indeed, show Dave pointing at the proposed sample with his foot.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Okay. Now come grab your scoop and we'll take it.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: It's a pretty big one to try and get with a scoop.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah; you're right. I don't see anything else (suitable for collection).

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: This little fracture. (Pause)

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Too big.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Too big. Get another one.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Oh! Here, Dave. 146:08:28 Scott: Oh, sure. Good boy. Get that one on your side.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay. (Pause) [The sample is 15459 , a 4.8 kg breccia. It is the second largest of the Apollo 15 samples but, evidently, is not the one Dave was pointing at with his foot.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Getting it. That a boy. There.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Should have left the rake on.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yep. (Pause) Can you get it? Good show. Easy does it. Easy does it. That's it. Up a little more. Keep your balance. (Pause) Can you get it up higher?

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Whup! Don't fall backwards.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Yeah. (Pause) [There are two possibilities here. One is that Jim has gotten his scoop under the sample and is raising it, undoubtedly gingerly, into Dave's reach. The other is that Jim has actually gotten down low enough to get the rock in his hand and then against his leg as he rises. He then works it up his leg high enough that Dave can grab it. The latter scenario comes to mind because of a similar maneuver performed by Charlie Duke at the rim of Plum Crater at the Apollo 16 site.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Man! I got it.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Good. (Pause) Video Clip 2 min 20 sec ( 0.6 Mb RealVideo or 21 Mb MPG )

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Okay, fill that square. Okay, Jim. Let's get on the Rover and head back.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay, I haven't secured the rake there, yet.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Okay. You secure the rake, and I'll secure the TV, and we'll get moving. [We see the shadow of somebody working at Jim's seat. This may be Dave, looking for a place to stow rock they've just collected.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: Sounds good, Dave and Jim. And we want to leave...

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: I wonder how I'm going to do this (that is, stow the rock).

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: ...the TV camera where it is right now. It's stowed in the proper position.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Okay. (Looking under Jim's seat) Oh, shoot!

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Hardly room there, is there?

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: "Hardly room there" is right. Any place we can put your bag on it?

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Why don't you put that in one of those bags, Dave?

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah. I'm going to put it in the seat pan now. And then, why don't you put your bag in here. Here, let me have...Come over here. I'm going to put your bag in there. Your carrier is awful loose, and I don't want to lose that bag. Put this on the Hand Tool Carrier. [Dave has probably taken an empty SCB out from under Jim's seat to make room for the SCB Jim has been wearing. The TV image shakes as he works around the seat. His shadow goes out of view, probably as he joins Jim at the back of the Rover.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: What's in there? Rocks?

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Oh, I don't know what's in there. No...

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: And, troops...

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: ...(garbled)...

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: How many big rocks did you pick up? One?

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: I think that's our best...(Stops to listen to Joe)

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah, one, Joe. We're about out of time, here.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: Rog. Although we're not hurting all that bad, but...

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: (Probably getting Jim's bag off) Bend over, Jim.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Yes, sir.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: ...we think you should be climbing...

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Bend over, Jim.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: ...aboard now. Looks like you really put some weight on our suspension system when you loaded it, there.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: [Chuckles] Wait until you feel this bag! (Pause) [We see Dave's shadow as he returns, undoubtedly with Jim's SCB.] [Jones - "We're well past the three minutes that Joe was talking about at 146:06:59 , so I suspect that you're not up against a hard walkback but, rather, trade-offs."] [Scott - "Yeah. Go back and fool with the drill. That's what's probably driving it at this point."]

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: It'll weigh even more when you get it home. And we're interested in getting you to move on out now, troops.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Going as fast as we can, Joe. Right now.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: Roger.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Okay, Jim. (Pause) Okay, you want to just stay in FM/TV , Joe?

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: Negative, Dave. Go ahead and stow it (meaning the high-gain antenna). We just don't want you to move the television camera. It's in the proper position now. We want you to go ahead and stow the antenna.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Understand. Okay. Better let me get in first, Jim. Okay; doing PM1/WB . [TV off.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: Roger, Dave. And don't forget the ignition key.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yes, sir. Got it. Okay; the brush is going to be under my seat pan.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: Standing by for your heading reading.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: (With a slight scolding tone) Okay; stand by, Joe.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Are you going to give us an update, Joe?

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: What's the reading, Jim? You probably won't need it.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: Torque it to 293, please. 293.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Okay.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay; understand 293. You want me to torque it, Dave?

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yes, go ahead; and then...Oh, shoot! You better get in so I can get your...

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: No...

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: ...seatbelt.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: ...If we're going downslope, I'll just hang on.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: (Firmly) No. Seatbelt. Get in.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a15_1461301csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1461301csm.text: Endeavour, we have the Mapping Camera coming Off in just one minute.

a15_1461301csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1461301csm.text: Okay, that looks good (meaning that Jim is properly seated). Where's your seatbelt?

a15_1461301csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1461301csm.text: Shoot, I didn't put it down (between the seats). I didn't think I was going to use it.

a15_1461812csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1461812csm.text: Al, I have a couple of comments on the water dump coming up in - 10 or 15 minutes. [Pause.]

a15_1461812csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1461812csm.text: We'd like to dump down to 10 percent. Stop at 10 percent. And they say that the dump will probably take about 8 minutes, so about 6 minutes after you start dumping, keep an eye on it and stop at 10 percent. And also, they'd like for you again to - to make an observation of the particle cloud at the sunset and sunrise terminators, if you would, please.

a15_1461812csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1461812csm.text: Okay. Will do. And I understand you just want me to dump down to 10 percent.

a15_1461812csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1461812csm.text: That's correct. And over at 146:33, where you have a "Gamma-ray Gain Step Shield, On, [Center]," we'd like you to take - to make one step increase in - in gain there. That's up momentarily, once.

a15_1461812csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1461812csm.text: That's over at 146:33, where you - they want you to put Shield, On [center]. After you have it on center, take it up once momentarily for one step increase in gain, and then leave it on center. [Pause.]

a15_1461812csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1461812csm.text: Okay; Understand. Gain Step Shield, On and go one step up, and then leave it Shield, up.

a15_1462151csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1462151csm.text: Okay, Endeavour. We're coming up to Gamma-ray Gain Step, Shield, Off in - in about 5 seconds.

a15_1462956csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1462956csm.text: Al, a bulletin from Hadley Rille, says that...

a15_1462956csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1462956csm.text: Karl, I didn't call. I'm waiting on you.

a15_1462956csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1462956csm.text: Oh, Roger. A bulletin from Hadley Rille - the crew finished their exploration of the Apennine front. They got over to Spur Crater and actually into Spur Crater, found there a large block of rock, which probably is a really true sample of the Apennine Front and got some good samples there. And, now they're driving back down by the South Complex and they're digging some samples around Dune Crater.

a15_1462956csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1462956csm.text: Very good. Sounds like they're doing quite well down there.

a15_1462956csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1462956csm.text: I think we're going to give lots of people lots of things to do for a while.

a15_1463956csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1463956csm.text: Al, this is Houston. All of your systems are looking in great shape as you go around the corner.

a15_1463956csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1463956csm.text: Okay, Karl. And we're looking okay up here. Getting ready to do the gegenschein calibration.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: Beautiful, Davey. Beautiful. And some more words...

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Camera's on...

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: ...about your next assignments coming up here. Dave, we want you to drop Jim at the LM and I'll talk to him in a minute. And then you go on over park near ALSEP, headed west.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Okay, understand, Joe. (Pause) Boy, there sure are a lot of neat rocks in the Dune. Too bad we can't spend some more time.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: On your next trip.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: (Lost under Joe)

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, next trip. You're right.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: And, Jim, you might want to start the camera.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, it's running, Joe.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Let's see. Think we can get through up here? Seems to me we could.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, I think you should be able to. Maybe a little to the right?

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, I'll come right now. Past this little bump. (Pause) And we're in the little boulder field. And about a foot, at the biggest, down to about 6 inches.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, it looks like from a crater that hit on the rim of Dune.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, it sure does.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Joe. We're reading on a bearing of 350, range 3.3.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Okay, and we're on our tracks.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: Roger. And follow 'em home.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Okay. (Pause) [These readouts put them at BE.4/75.6 . The fact that they are re-tracing their outbound tracks suggests that they are close to the west rim of Dune as shown on Ken Rattee's map . The changes in LM bearing and range since leaving Station 4 - 347/3.4 to 350/3.3 - are also consistent with a location near the rim.] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I didn't notice anything particular driving back. You could see albedo changes where we'd been. Any disturbance of the soil was apparent. These Rover tracks were a little different."] [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "A

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Gee, it's nice to sit down, isn't it?

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Oh, it is.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: (Laughing) It's a good deal. You hop off and work like mad for 10 minutes and hop back on, sit down, and take a break. (Pause) [This is one of the many advantages that the Rover provides. Not only do the crews have greater range and carrying capacity, but they arrive at the geology stations rested. The difference is dramatic between this Apollo 15 experience and the experience of the Apollo 14 crew during their arduous climb to the summit of the Cone Crater ridge. I asked Dave about walking traverses they might have trained for as the Apollo 12 backup crew.] [Scott - "I don't remember. Whateve

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, I guess in a couple craters we remarked that we saw a boulder distribution that looked like it was linear, like it was a ray pattern.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: But we never did get a chance to really sample any of those. As I recall, we saw one on the, what, south side of the Dune, on the way down.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: We could probably save some time going back by not following the tracks, you know, because...

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah...

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: ...we can see the LM.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: You're right. I think we ought to head right straight ahead. We can see home.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: The only big crater over that way would probably be Earthlight. (Pause) I think that's probably Earthlight that we see at 12 o'clock.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yep.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: If we stay west of Earthlight, we ought to save a little distance.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, (but) let's get out of this little boulder field first. (Pause) [During the southbound traverse, they drove east of Earthlight. Jim is correct, a straight-line route to the LM will hit the south rim of Earthlight, as indicated on Ken Rattee's map .] 146:49:02 Scott: Okay, now we'll take a little left here, and keep...Oh well; we can look at Pluton. We'll see Pluton all the way. And the LM is silhouetted right against the base of Pluton so we can't miss that. And just to the right of it is Schaber Hill which we'll be heading for tomorrow. (Pause) [Although Schaber Hill does not appear on

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Okay, by the way, Joe, I guess we ought to tell you about what we saw at that last stop. We gathered a few quick samples that were covered with dust, which we didn't look at very carefully, just so we could get ahold of them. Then the very large boulder, which was probably about 6-feet (tall) sticking up out of the ground, with a very large 3- to 4-inch vesicles, was a very fine-grained, dark, black, basalt, with maybe, gee, I'd say 15-percent plage in it, wouldn't you, Jim?

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, a very fine lath.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, a very fine lath. And on the top, it had some smaller millimeter-size vesicles, and adjacent to it was another, lighter-gray, vesicular basalt, which was uniform in vesicularity, and which we didn't have time to sample, but the vesicles in that looked similar to that one rock that we got yesterday, Jim. The rounded one? Remember that was in the bag alone. Anyway, these vesicles were, gee, I'd say 4 millimeters to...some of them, were a centimeter all the way through it. And the two rocks seemed to be in contact with each other. Unfortunately, we didn't have time to sample the second one,

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: Roger, Dave. Beautiful description. And, Jim, you might stop the camera now. It's probably run through the film load, and we'd like clicks (speed) and amps reading please.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Okay, we're doing...Well, that can wait. Okay, the camera is empty, Joe, (grunting slightly, probably as he leans forward to shut the camera off) so we got some coverage there. (Pause) And we're going at about 10 clicks; amps reads about 10.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: Okay, sounds good. (Pause)

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: That might be Earthlight up ahead, Dave.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: I think you're right. I guess we'd better go east of it, huh?

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Yeah. (Pause)

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: (Grunts)

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: We might end up on our tracks.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: (Laughing) Yeah. Oh, I don't know. I think I'll make it up. [They may be climbing.]

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Cross-Sun (driving) is pretty good, you know?

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Yeah.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Visibility-wise. (Pause)

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Okay; coming down this morning. I guess we looked over at Earthlight, didn't we?

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Commented on the southern rim of it (at 143:27:03 ). (Pause)

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, we're in good shape now! It's a straight shot. See the old LM sitting out there? Start making out detail on it. We're (at a) range, 2.4. I think we're closer than that. [As we know from the stop at Station 4, they are about 270 meters NNE of the indicated position and, therefore, are at a range of about 2.1 or 2.2 km and have finished he drive around the east side of Earthlight. Because they haven't mentioned seeing their outbound tracks - as Jim will do at 146:57:58 when they get close to Arbeit - they have probably driven between the east rim of Earthlight and the outbound track.] [The

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: See how it checks out when we get there.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: Jim, I've got some words for your next task when you arrive at the LM, if you're ready (to listen).

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Go ahead, Joe.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: Roger. For both of you now! Dave, we want you to stop at the LM and you'll have to off-load your collection bags and get configured for the next part of the EVA. Jim, we want you to run a mal(function) procedure on your camera. If you can't get that mag to work, put on mag Kilo Kilo and then your first job will be the LM site pans and then photographs of the descent engine and photographs of the solar-wind-composition experiment - the window shade. Those three sets of photographs. Do you copy?

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Yes. I understand, Joe.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: Okay. (Pause) And, Dave and Jim. I'll talk you through the reconfiguration of the equipment when you're ready for it. I think we have a good handle on it down here.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Joe, why don't you wait till we get to the Rover (meaning the LM)? Because it'll just slip right through us right now.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: Roger, Dave...

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: So, wait until we get there.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: ...that's exactly the plan. I'll be standing by, and when it's time, I just talk you through it.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Okay. That's just fine.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: As far as Dave's bag, Joe. I forget the number on it, but I'll just take out the core tubes that we have not used, and then it will be ready to go in SRC 2. Is that correct?

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: Sounds good! (Pause)

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Do you agree with that, as far as Dave's bag?

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: That agrees, we think, Jim. We'll think it over once again here.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Okay. (To Dave) Think you can get through there, Dave?

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: No. I'm going to go around to the right. Miss this boulder here. There's a directional set of ejecta; isn't it?

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: It sure is.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Look at that! It's right straight out one side. It would be a good place to take a radial sample. That thing came in from...Let's see, we'll be...

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: West. We're going north...

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, we're going north and the ejecta pattern is spread out due west about 20 meters across; and it must go out a good 150 meters or so. [Directionality of the ejecta blanket indicates a low velocity, secondary impact]

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: To the east, right?

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah. And our bearing is 347 and our range 2.0 at that point.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: Roger. (Pause) [These readouts indicate a position of BK.6/75.1 . Using the same correction that applied at Station 4, Ken Rattee puts them at about BL.5/75.8 .]

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Ooops! (Laughing) Some of those babies sneak up on you. (Long Pause)

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: This time we ought to get the covers up in the cabin, Dave.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Get the what?

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: The covers. You know, the Bull Durham sacks.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, I know it. (Garbled) [Jones - "In trying to figure out what Jim's talking about, the thing that comes to mind is putting the legs of the suit in sacks because of the dirt."] [Scott - "Yeah, we were real dirty. I would guess that's what he's probably talking about. Bull Durham bags, you know what those look like, for Bull Durham Tobacco. These look very much like big Bull Durham bags."] [Jones - "Bull Durham bags are the big gunny sacks. Yours were made out of beta cloth?"] [Scott - "Yeah."] [David Woods points out that some readers will need help with these Americanisms. "Gunny" is a coa

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: You got to go around to the right.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yes, I guess we'd better. (Laughs) [Ken Rattee shows a change in course to NNE at about this point. "Looking at the Arbeit area close-up gave me an idea fits the dialogue and Nav readouts. On the inbound route, after rounding Earthlight to the east, they headed straight for the LM (146:52:54 'It's a straight shot. See the old LM sitting out there?'). South of Arbeit at this heading they would be confronted by a line of four craters ('c' on the Pan Camera detail ) which perhaps might of looked too imposing to snake thru and indeed in the dialogue around this point - 146:57:25 Irwin: 'You got to

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: Hello, Rover; this is Houston.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Go ahead, Houston. Rover, here.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: Roger, Dave. Be advised that the ALSEP is picking up the rumble of the Rover rolling across the plains.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Is that right!? How about that!

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: (Joking) And according to our data, you're heading right for the LM.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Jim, I think...(Responding to Joe) Aah! Yeah, you can give us a DF on the seismometer.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: Roger. [Scott - "DF, or Direction Finding, is a technique fighter planes used to get to home base during World War II. When I was flying in Europe we used what they called DFQGHGCA, which was direction finding from a ground radar. They told you which way to go, from home base...You know, home base tells you to go 360 or whatever and then they tell when to start letting down, altitude-wise, and then they Ground-Controlled Approach into a landing. So the reference here is that the seismometer is right next to the LM so, from the seismometer, they can tell us which direction to go to get home."]

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: ...Stand by for practice DF steer.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, but I still think we were straighter...

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Yeah.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: (Responding to Joe) Yeah, man! (To Jim) Hey, I think this is Index, Jim.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: The one on our left here?

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah. In fact, I'm pretty sure it's Index. It's got the nice side crater in the north.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, I thought Index had a larger crater though on the north side.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Well, I don't know how large "large" is anymore.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Yeah.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: (Chuckle) I give up on distances and sizes.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Okay, we're (at a range of) 1.7.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: It's probably Arbeit. [Jim will report a bearing of 340 at 146:59:07 and, if we use that bearing here, a range of 1.7 would put them at BM.0/75.6 . Application of the Station 4 correction then puts them near BM.9/76.2 .]

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: (Not having heard Joe yet) No. It couldn't be it then.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: I don't think so. 146:58:34 Scott: (Hearing Joe) Arbeit. Yeah, yeah. That's right, that's right. We came by that before. Yeah. We might as well just head on over those tracks, because we know we're straight...(Pause) [Scott - "Arbeit means 'work' in German. By the way, 'Ausgezeichnet' (a German phrase that Joe used at 145:23:45 ) is not necessarily 'wonderful', it's more like 'excellent'. It's a word that's probably not directly translatable; it's interpretable. I was thinking about that last night. It's 'excellent' or 'super', not 'wonderful'. 'Arbeit' means 'work' and, at some point when we

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Notice that crater at 12:30 to us now.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: Yeah. The fresh one.

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: It's fresh and has a very light albedo.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: That's November. Got to be November . Yeah. That's clearly November Crater .

a15a1464546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1464546.text: Yeah, we're heading 360; the bearing's 340; and the range 1.5.

a15a1464546.speaker: Allen
a15a1464546.text: We copy that.

a15a1464546.speaker: Scott
a15a1464546.text: And we were pointing right at November at the time. So, Index is over there on the right. (Pause) [November is at BR.5/75.3 and the LM is at BS.4/73.3. The bearing and range give an indicated Rover position of BM.8/75.4 . Ken Rattee puts them at about BN.3/75.7 . From that position, the heading to November Crater is 355 and the southern rim of Index is only about 125 meters from them.]

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Notice that crater at 12:30 to us now.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Yeah. The fresh one.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: It's fresh and has a very light albedo.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: That's November. Got to be November . Yeah. That's clearly November Crater .

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Yeah, we're heading 360; the bearing's 340; and the range 1.5.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: We copy that.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: And we were pointing right at November at the time. So, Index is over there on the right. (Pause) [November is at BR.5/75.3 and the LM is at BS.4/73.3.
