a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: (Laughing) Making me seasick (because of the bumpy, rolling ride).

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: (Laughs)

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: (Punning) What...

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: What were we...

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: ...do you expect traveling on the mare.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: (Laughing) See that one right...

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: (Hearing Joe) Yeah. (To Dave) Are we just about...

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Yeah. (Chuckling) Pretty good machine, isn't it?

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: It sure is. Couldn't ask for better. And we're going 12 clicks.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: And it's a new outdoor record. (Long Pause)

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Talk about dusty. Whew!

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: (Laughs) Yeah, Bo. [Jones - "What does 'Yeah, Bo' mean?"] [Scott - "That's an old saying, from way back. I don't remember where I picked it up. From some western movie - Gregory Peck or one of those guys - back when they made good westerns."]

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: But, you know, it sure doesn't kick up as much as I thought it would.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: No. You know, even if you had rubber tires on here, I think you'd kick up the same amount of dust.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Yeah.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: In this kind of terrain. 147:01:02 Scott: And you sure wouldn't climb that hill (referring to the climb to Station 6) like we did. (Pause)

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Notice that white-colored rock there that we just went...

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Yeah.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: ...over.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Uh huh. (Long Pause)

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Okay. We're still going at 12 clicks; heading 340. 147:01:30 Allen: Roger. Copy, Jim. And I'm wondering if you caught sight of the small crater you saw outbound, which you described as having bedrock in the bottom? [Jim made that observation at 143:12:48 . The small crater showing bedrock is a crater in the eastern wall of last Crater.]

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: I don't think we've come that far yet.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Okay.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: I don't think so, either.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: (To Joe) Why? Are you contemplating a stop there?

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Negative. Just curious.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Yeah, I see it dead a(head)...(Stops to listen to Joe)

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Where?

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: We...

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: There it is. See it...

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: ...are interested...

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: ...on the horizon...

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: ...in a Nav reading; an odometer reading. And we're going to measure how far away that is from the LM.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: You can use that Rover for everything.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Yeah, man! Sure can.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Looks like November has a lot of blocks, too, but I can't see any (brief pause) bedrock. I thought the crater that looked like it had bedrock was off to the east of our tracks.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: It is. Over here to our 11 o'clock. I mean...No, no. I'm sorry; you're right. I was thinking of a different one, Jim. (Pause) November has a raised rim which is, I think, unique around here.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Kind of a large rock to the north of November.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Yeah. 147:02:55 Irwin: That looks like it's half buried. (Long Pause) [The following is a purely academic discussion Dave and I had about the problems caused by the difficulty they are having unambiguously identifying some craters. In the particular case of November Crater, the difference is moot because they are, indeed, looking at the crater they named November before the flight.] [Scott - "As we go along and we talk about these craters, I wonder if these are really the craters we named before the flight. Should the craters be named based on what we called them during the flight, instead of

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Now, this fresh crater that we're coming up ahead. I know we talked about it but I don't know whether there was any bedrock.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Well, we'll see when we get there.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) Having a bite to eat.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Good. (Long Pause) [We can hear Jim chewing or, at least, knocking his microphone as he reaches down with his teeth to pull out a section of fruit bar and bites off a piece.]

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Yeah, I think this is the one we called. Isn't it, Jim? Looks like an excavated bedrock. There are frags on the side. It's got a light albedo; it's relatively fresh. I think this is the one, isn't it? Well, we'll give it to them anyway. 352 for 0.7.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Roger. Copy. Thank you.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Let's enter it.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Okay. (Pause) [The indicated position is BP.6/73.7 . Ken Rattee puts them at about BP.8/73.8 .]

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Dave and Jim, a comment about your equipment off load. The off-loading should go exactly as if it were at the end of EVA-1 with regards to transferring core tubes, and so forth. Only the collection bag numbers will be different. And we'll try to talk you through that.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Yeah, you'd better. (To Dave) I just didn't see that crater that I...That wasn't the one, Dave.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Don't think so?

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: No, because it was to the east of us and I looked out and saw a layer of bedrock about a quarter of the way up on the wall.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Okay, Jim. Give us another odometer reading.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: No, I haven't seen it!

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Okay. Whenever you pick it up.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: I haven't been able to see it on the way back.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Okay, no problems.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: We're almost back to the LM. (Pause) The freshest one was the one that Dave just gave you the coordinates on.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Roger.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Unless this might have been the one.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Where?

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Right here. (Pause) Call it Last.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: No. (Pause) 147:06:24 Irwin: That wasn't the one, that's too large. (Pause) [Scott - "You notice that, when we're driving along, we're always talking about the geology? That's probably a reflection of driving along with Lee Silver , going on the field trips and looking out the (car) window and talking about the geology. As I recall, when we'd go out on our field trips, we'd leave from some hotel/motel in the morning, and our conversation was usually geology. And we probably got used to doing that. So this is probably a result of that. And, perhaps, the guys back at the Control Center are sayin

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: The (high-gain?) antenna drifted. [Jones - "I would be more inclined to think that it was the high gain - rather than the low-gain - that drifted. The low-gain wasn't really in your field-of-view, was it?"] [Scott - "I could see it, I guess. (After some thought) We're looking at the LM. Why would I all of a sudden make a comment on the antenna on the Rover, when it's been sitting there in front of me, all the time. Now, I look at the LM, now I'm looking at something new. So I may be commenting on the LM antennas."] [Jones - "There was a lock on the (Rover) high-gain? You usually drive with it

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Yeah. I wonder if that's the best position for thermal. (Pause) Oh, that antenna. I'm looking at the LM antenna.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Oh, yeah! The radar antenna's pointing straight up.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Guess it is, that's the white side.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Yeah. (Pause) (Laughing) Tracks upon tracks, Jim.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Yeah, it looks like a thoroughfare. It looks like a freeway.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Yeah. Okay; we'll take this fork here. (Laughs) (Pause)

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: And, Dave, as you know, the only thing we have to worry about, especially with regard to kicking dirt, is the solar wind composition experiment and the LR-Cubed, which is pretty far away.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Okay, we'll be careful.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: And we'll mark when you stop.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Roger. We're almost there. (Pause) Home sweet home. (Pause)

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Okay, Jim, I'm going to drop you off right here.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Okay.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Okay, Joe. Run through what you want to do now.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Okay, the first thing I guess...

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: I might get a (film) mag.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: ...is to off load the gear as if you were out at the ALSEP site, with regard to transferring cores, et cetera. (Pause) And we marked...

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Oh ...

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: ... you stopped. [Joe may be referring to EVA-1 checklist page CDR-22 but, if so, Dave's question at 147:09:57 indicates that Joe's meaning isn't clear to him, either.]

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Yeah, I got to get off, too.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Okay.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: And, Jim, standing by for your LRV readouts, if you're still there.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Yeah, I am Joe. I'm reading (heading) 004, (bearing) 018; (distance driven) 12.5; (range) 00.2; (amp-hours) 91, 98; (battery temperatures) 92, 98, and motor temps are low. 147:09:22 Allen: Roger, thank you. (Long Pause) [Although they are actually at the LM , the Nav system thinks the LM is 200 meters NNE or, more specifically, 0.8 map units north and 0.2 map units east.]

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Jim, are you climbing off the Rover now?

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: (To Joe) Okay...(Stops to listen).

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: (Responding to Joe) Yeah, we're climbing off. 147:09:57 Scott: Let me ask you a question now. Joe, what did you say? You want us to configure now like we would at the ALSEP site?

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Dave, basically, you just want to unload the collection bags that you're carrying. We want to wind up with collection bag number 2 on the hand tool carrier and number 3 under Jim's seat. (Pause) In addition to that...

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Okay.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: ...we want number 5 on the hand tool carrier.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: 2 and 5 on the hand tool carrier. Okay.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Rog. And 2 is under Jim's seat right now. We want to trade that out for number 3 going under the seat.

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Okay.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: I'm wondering if we should take our tools off (the PLSSs). We might as well take our tools off, right, Dave.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Jim, Roger...

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: Yeah, I think probably so.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: ...take your tools off...

a15a1465852.speaker: Scott
a15a1465852.text: I think so. Don't you, Joe? 147:11:07 Allen: ...and we're going to ask you to deploy the flag a little later, and you probably will need the hammer for that.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: No, I won't need the hammer (because of the soft soil).

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Okay.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: Not here. I can't get that mag to operate, Joe. I manually advanced it. It just won't kick over.

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Okay, we copy that.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: I think I'm going to be forced to...

a15a1465852.speaker: Allen
a15a1465852.text: Jim. Put on mag Kilo Kilo on that camera, please.

a15a1465852.speaker: Irwin
a15a1465852.text: I was wondering: is Dave going to need his camera out there? 147:11:46 Scott: No, why don't you take mine. Mine happens to have Kilo on it.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Joe, let's see you want 2 and 5 on the hand tool carrier, and the rest under the seat, is that correct?

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: That's correct.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay, stand by.

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: And, Dave, we do want you to unload the tools. Clip 'em them back on the Hand Tool Carrier. We'll need them later at the ALSEP site, perhaps.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Rog, Joe.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Bend over a little, Dave.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: I'd like to take this little cargo here, and take it right over to the MESA.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: What bag number is it?

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Well, that's the bag that goes in...(It's) bag 5. And bag 5 goes in the SRC.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Yeah. [Jim is probably reading EVA-2 checklist page LMP-21.]

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Let me just take out the unused core tubes. Joe, speak up now if there is anything else you want to put in bag 5. (No answer) I'm going to take it over to the MESA.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Yeah, there's no sense in putting bag 5 on the hand-tool carrier, Joe, because it's just about full. Why don't we put it on the MESA or in the SRC, or something.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Dave, when you take your camera off, just leave it on my (Rover) seat.

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: Dave, the only problem is, if we're able to get the deep (core) samples using the drill stems, we'd like them in the SRC. I guess we'll leave it up to you, your choice. It may be better just to take bag 5 over there right now and forego that little nicety.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Well, Joe, you didn't...Just a minute, Jim. Just a minute. Now, Joe, you didn't say anything about getting deep cores. That's why...(To Jim) Here, let's take 3 and put it over there. Keep it there. Let me take 2 back, because now that I know that they want to try and get the deep cores, we do need bag 2.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Yeah.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: That's the first time anybody said anything about that.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: That's bag 5, Dave.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: I mean 5...

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Well, Dave, why not leave 5 there!

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: If you get the cores, bring them back, and we'll put it in there. I just won't load it in the SRC.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: We'll hold the SRC open.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Yeah, that's right.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Yeah. Okay.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: I'll hold it open.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay. 147:14:30 Allen: Sounds good, Jimmy. [Obviously, Dave and Jim are well versed in the contents of the various bags.] [Scott - "What they should probably say is, 'Here's the plan at the LM: want to get the deep core, want to move bags', and then let us go do it, 'cause we're probably more familiar with the bags and what's in 'em. For instance, one bag is almost full, and they don't know that. So, what they should have done was give us the objectives and then let us tell them what we did, 'cause then we can shuffle things around and, as long as they know what we did, they're in good shape."

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Hey, Jim, I'm going to leave you my camera...

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Yeah.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: ...right here, on the MESA, huh?

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: No, just hand it to me now. I'll take it right here.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: I'll put it on.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: There you go.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Let me read it.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Yes, let me read the numbers on it first. Of course, it's not on all the way, but it's reading 89. (Pause) Get that, Joe? My camera, 89?

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: Got it, Dave, thank you.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Dave, you're hung up on that strap. (Pause)

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay. Thanks, Jim. (Pause) Okay. Now. 147:15:21 Irwin: Listen, why don't you take my tools off.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Yeah. That's a good idea. Get cleaned up here. (Pause)

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: I think we only have two bags to go up (into the cabin) this time.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Yeah. Here's your hammer. (Pause)

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay. Here's the rammer.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Core tube caps.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Okay.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Tidy up your Velcro. (Pause)

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Let me check yours again, Dave.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: I don't recall that I tidied yours. Okay; when you get in, your right side is loose. So be careful.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay. You're tidy.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay. Right side okay?

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Yeah.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Put these core tube caps under the seat. We got more core tube caps now than we know what to do with.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Yeah.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Listen, those rocks that are under the seat. I'll put those in bag...Well, the bag that's under there, before you drive off.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: No, there isn't any bag under there now. I got it right here. It's 7.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: No, here's a bag right here. Right, or is that the sam(ple)...

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: No.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: ...sample bag? That's your sample bag.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay, here's a bag here, 6.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: You're going to use that one out there, right?

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: I don't know. Where do you want bag 7, Joe?

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: Bag 7 stays there, Dave. Leave it there.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Hey, where's "there"? Under the seat?

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: Is it under the seat? I think it's under the seat, and I think it's the bag for the next EVA. Keep it there.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay! It is. I think it is, yeah.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Yeah, that's one for the next EVA.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay. It's under the seat.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: I was going to get those rocks and put it in this bag. Bag 6.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay. (Pause) Can you get the bag?

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Yeah.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: My arms are a little longer, maybe I can reach it, Jim. That a boy. Okay.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: I don't want to leave any rocks there.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: You're right. (Pause) Okay. (Pause) Is that the only one, or do we have another one? (Pause) It's the only one. [This is probably the large sample Dave broke off the Station 4 boulder.]

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Put "A" under your seat, huh? [Neither Dave nor I could figure out what this means.]

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Oh, yeah! Thank you. I did. You're right. (Pause)

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: I'll just hold up on the SRC closing until...

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Yeah.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: ...you decide what you're going to do out there.

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: Sounds good, Jim.

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: There's a couple of samples there we probably ought to put in here.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Yep. (Pause)

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: Sounds good, and, Jim, while you're working there, once again...

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Anything else in there?

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: ...we want you to get your LM site pans...

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Okay.

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: ...pictures of the descent engine and solar wind composition pictures, and then I'll be back at you with the next job. And, Dave, standing by for when you're ready. And, I'll talk about your task coming up here.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay, Joe. Are you through with the Hand Tool Carrier, Jim?

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Yeah, I am, Dave.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay. I'm going to tidy up the Rover. (Long Pause)

a15a1471212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1471212.text: Okay, Joe, back at the...On the MESA, I have bags 3, 5, and 6.

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: Roger; copy, Jim. We'll get them later. 147:19:33 Scott: And, Joe, I'm on the Rover and ready to go.

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: Okay, Dave. We want you to park east of the ALSEP heading toward the west, and as far east as is comfortable for you. Once again with the dust problem in mind. And we want you to clean the TV camera and LCRU before you leave the Rover.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay. Park east heading west. And, I'll just get it fairly close to the Central Station and avoid the dust. How does that sound?

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: Roger. Just don't drive too far west. Keep it east, if you could, please. [Houston probably wants the TV pointing down-Sun to get good lighting but, as Joe indicates at 147:21:29 , they are primarily concerned about getting dust on the experiments.]

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Okay. Incidentally, at the Rover (meaning the LM), our bearing was 018 and range 0.2. That's pretty good for a trip like that.

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: Ain't it, though. (Pause) And, Dave, as you climb off there and get the TV set and are ready, I'll talk to you about the next drilling job.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: All righty. (Long Pause) Okay, I'm going to park right here. And if you get bored (watching the drilling), there's a big chunk of dark-gray breccia with white clasts right in front of the left wheel. Have fun looking at that, maybe. 147:21:29 Allen: Okay, Dave... 147:21:30 Scott: Brake's on, power's off.

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: ...we know you're not too close to the heat flow experiment holes now. We do want you to be particularly aware of the SIDE which has had its dust cover pulled off of it, too. So it'll be particularly sensitive to dust. And, when you are ready, once again, I've got words on how this drill should work. 147:21:51 Scott: Okay, first you want me to dust off your TV. Is that right?

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: Yes, sir, please. And the LCRU.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Alright, you broke up, Joe, I...

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: Roger, Dave... 147:22:04 Scott: Do you want your TV lens dusted off?

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: ...dust off the TV and the LCRU, please.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: Roger. TV, I understand that, but do you want the TV lens, because we have a (cooling) mirror (on the top of the TV camera) we can dust off and we also have a lens we can dust off.

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: Yes, sir, both the camera and the lens, please.

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: All righty. It takes a couple different brushes. I hate to put this big brush on that lens.

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: You read it correctly. (Long Pause)

a15a1471212.speaker: Scott
a15a1471212.text: There. Your eye is all cleaned off. (Pause)

a15a1471212.speaker: Allen
a15a1471212.text: Okay, Dave, we're standing by for TV turn on.

a15a1472442.speaker: Scott
a15a1472442.text: Are you getting any picture, Joe?

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: Say again, Dave.

a15a1472442.speaker: Scott
a15a1472442.text: Are you getting any picture, yet? 147:24:53 Allen: Beautiful picture. [ Fendell tips the camera down, giving us a view toward the northwest of Hill 305 .]

a15a1472442.speaker: Scott
a15a1472442.text: You clipped on the front. I didn't hear what you said.

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: Beautiful picture, Dave. Gorgeous picture. Thank you.

a15a1472442.speaker: Scott
a15a1472442.text: Oh, fine. Oh, good! That AGC is a great idea. (Pause) [Jones - "Your statement suggests that the AGC was added to during training. That it wasn't there in the original design."] [Scott - "No. Procedures. It was already there. But we added the idea of using it to lock up on the Earth. I think what I'm saying here is that I looked at it and it locked in, or it went to max, which says it's a good procedure."] [Jones - "Eyeball the course alignment and then look at the meter for final alignment."] 147:25:15 Scott: Okay, Joe, I'm ready to go to work.

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: Okay, Dave, we want you to try to get the heat flow drill in at least another section. We think that perhaps there might be an extra section added onto the unit you started yesterday.

a15a1472442.speaker: Scott
a15a1472442.text: All righty. [At the end of the first EVA, Dave drilled the first of two heat flow holes but achieved a depth of only 172 cm instead of the planned depth of 294 cm. He finished emplacing the probes in this first hole at 125:16:27 , and then started work on the second hole. As was the case with the first hole, the rate of penetration slowed dramatically once the joint between the first two drill-stem sections entered the ground. Drilling was abandoned before Dave could complete the hole because his oxygen supply was getting low. Drilling was terminated at 125:22:33 . Post-mission analysis indica

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: If you'll tell me what's there, I'll continue. If one or maybe two sections, however many you think you can put on and still drill. Once you get the sections on, we want you to use the drill again. And first, recycle the chuck several times, as you used to do in the simulations, and then start the drill, and put only a few pounds of force on top of the drill. And, while it's running, if you notice from the torque that it starts to seize up, we want you to try to pull it back out of the hole a bit to free it, as you drill. Over.

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: Roger, just try to free the torque that the drill is picking up from the soil. It seems to be binding around it. Soil and/or rock, that's binding around it. And we think that the secret to this...

a15a1472442.speaker: Scott
a15a1472442.text: To free the probe, huh? [Fendell shifts his aim to the left and centers the picture on the drill-stem rack. The 3-meter-pole leaning against the rack is the rammer-jammer used to emplace the heat flow probes.]

a15a1472442.speaker: Scott
a15a1472442.text: Okay.

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: ...may be not to put quite so much pressure on the top of the drill.

a15a1472442.speaker: Scott
a15a1472442.text: I see; I understand that.

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: And...

a15a1472442.speaker: Scott
a15a1472442.text: We'll give it a go.

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: ...you might want to (garbled) before you get started. [The unintelligible part of Joe's remark sounds like 'check south', which would be a repeat of the reminder that Dave and Joe discussed at the start of the heat flow drilling at 124:53:10 .]

a15a1472442.speaker: Scott
a15a1472442.text: Yes, sir. (Pause) Video Clip 3 min 03 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 27 Mb MPG ) [Dave threads a drill-stem section on the two that are already in the ground.]

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: And, Jim, how are you doing? 147:27:12 Irwin: Just about finished, Joe. [Jim is taking photographs in the vicinity of the LM, starting with four photos of the Solar Wind Collector (SWC), AS15-87- 11781 to 11784 .] [The SWC is west of the LM and, from that spot, Jim took a 12-o'clock pan (assembled by Dave Byrne). It consists of frames AS15-87- 11785 ) to 11804 .] [Frame 11785 is a down-Sun which shows Dave on the Rover near the ALSEP site. This picture was taken sometime after 147:19:33 but before 147:21:30 . In frame 11787 , readers should note the dark Rover tracks extending all the way to t

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: Okay, Jimmy. Sounds good. We want you to deploy the flag after you finish the photography. And, we're wondering at the moment where the two empty core tubes are. If they are still in bag 5. we'll want you to carry them in your hand out toward the ALSEP station later on. [The Apollo 15 U.S. flag is stowed in the MESA.] [Dave gets another drill-stem section. He starts to thread it on to the stack but, for some reason, takes it off and puts it back in the rack.] [Scott, from a 1996 letter - "It may not have started on smoothly."]

a15a1472442.speaker: Irwin
a15a1472442.text: No, they are under my seat, Joe.

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: Okay, and unless I miss my guess, your seat's out near the ALSEP now. So that is beautiful.

a15a1472442.speaker: Irwin
a15a1472442.text: Yeah. (Pause) Why do you want them out near the ALSEP, Joe?

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: Jim, I don't...

a15a1472442.speaker: Irwin
a15a1472442.text: (Garbled)

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: ...know how to break this news to you, but we're going to do Station 8 out at the ALSEP site, or nearby. Saving it especially for you.

a15a1472442.speaker: Irwin
a15a1472442.text: Ohh! (Hearty laugh) Oh, thank you, Joe!

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: I knew you'd like it.

a15a1472442.speaker: Scott
a15a1472442.text: Hey, Joe, before we got out this morning, we figured you guys had a conspiracy against us, having Jim doing Station 8 and me drilling at the same time.

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: It may work out that way. [Scott - "Jim didn't like Station 8, and I didn't like to drill. In relative terms. (Dryly) I mean, we liked everything we did, right? But they were both mechanical chores (and not nearly as much fun as collecting rocks)."] [Ken Glover prepared a short Real Video clip showing Jim practicing trench digging at the Cape.] [Fendell pulls back on the zoom and begins to pan clockwise, just as Dave picks up the drill.] 147:28:32 Allen: And, Jim, you just could get the flag out; don't necessarily deploy it. We'll get that later when the TV's back at Falcon. And keep me posted

a15a1472442.speaker: Irwin
a15a1472442.text: Okay. Well, listen...

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: ...here. When you finish pulling the flag out of its holder, but not yet deployed, we'll ask you to walk on out to the ALSEP site. [Fendell is looking up-Sun and the dark Rover tracks extending out from the LM are quite evident in the TV picture Over the back of the Rover, we can see some movement at the LM. This is probably Jim getting the flag out of the MESA. Fendell starts to pan counter-clockwise.] 147:29:02 Scott: Okay. Okay, Joe, I've got the drill on one extra section now. Run through it again, please, just so I don't (garbled).

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: Okay, Dave. We are interested in your starting to drill. We've got a lot of power left in the drill, just run it around several times; and don't bear down on it too much. Let's see how free - (correcting himself) or how freely - it moves in the surficial layer there, first of all.

a15a1472442.speaker: Scott
a15a1472442.text: Okay. (Pause) Joe, I put very little force on it, and it binds up.

a15a1472442.speaker: Allen
a15a1472442.text: Roger. Any luck by trying to pull it back a bit out of the hole to free it?

a15a1472442.speaker: Scott
a15a1472442.text: (Chuckles) No, it pulls me right on down with it.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1472954csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. How do you read?

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1472954csm.text: Okay, Dave, stand by a second. 147:30:00 Scott: Okay. Video Clip 3 min 28 sec ( 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 31 Mb MPG )

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1472954csm.text: Hello, Houston; Endeavour. Loud and clear.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1472954csm.text: Good to hear your cheery voice. How is everything up there?

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1472954csm.text: Dave, is it possible at all to clear out the flutes on it by lifting up as you turn the power on? 147:30:13 Scott: I'll try. But it seems to want to pull me with it. (Grunts) There, I got it up. [Dave comes into view just as he steps up to the drill and pulls it out of the hole perhaps six inches. Fendell stops his pan and zooms in on Dave. Dave lets go of the drill and steps back. During the following conversation, he stands relatively motionless next to the rack, leaning far enough forward that he can manipulate objects on the top of the rack.] 147:30:24 Irwin: Joe, I have the flag unpacked

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1472954csm.text: Yeah, just fine. It took us a little longer to lock up that time. [Pause.]

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1472954csm.text: Yeah. A couple of minutes, but it still wasn't bad. [Long pause.]

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1472954csm.text: That's...

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1472954csm.text: I may...

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1472954csm.text: ...exactly right, Jim. We want you now to proceed on out toward Dave, and be back with you in a minute.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1472954csm.text: And, Karl, on the waste water dump, I overshot 10 percent, just a little bit, but I'm reading - I'm reading about 10 percent now.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1472954csm.text: You want me to carry the staff and the flag out there, huh?

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1472954csm.text: Negative, negative, leave it near the LM. We'll pick it up a little later when we come back to the Falcon. Just leave it there in a convenient place.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1472954csm.text: How much was that?

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1472954csm.text: Oh. Okay. (Chuckles) I thought I was going to be able do the Station 8 with the flag waving in the background.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1472954csm.text: I'm reading 10 percent.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1472954csm.text: Roger. Reading 10 percent now. I copy that. [Long pause.]

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1472954csm.text: Okay, Joe. Now I've got the drill partially out. Do you want me to try and take the drill off the probe (means the stem)?

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1472954csm.text: Dave, we wonder if you can just hold it there. Begin it running, and ease it back down into the hole, but without a whole lot of force, down into the hole. 147:31:30 Scott: Okay! [Dave straightens up, hops to the drill, takes hold of the hand grips, and starts drilling.]

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1472954csm.text: Al, we'd like to have High Gain [Antenna], Narrow and Auto. [Long pause.]

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1472954csm.text: And, just let it run for a while. There's a lot of power in that battery.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1472954csm.text: Okay, I'm not...(Hears Joe) I'm not putting any force on it. I'm letting it do its own forcing.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1472954csm.text: Okay, let her run. We've got a lot of power to burn. [After about six inches of rapid penetration, progress slows dramatically. A good means of gauging progress is to compare the relative locations of the end of the grip in Dave's left hand and the tip of the rammer-jammer in the foreground.]

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1472954csm.text: Okay, Houston. You got it.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1472954csm.text: Very good. Thank you. [Pause.]

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1472954csm.text: (Chuckles) It's a great massage.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1472954csm.text: Hey! I want to come out and get some of that! (Long Pause) [Scott - "I could just feel it vibrating. I don't remember the frequency but, yeah, you know it's turning. It feels good. And you don't have to push on it. Just put your hands on a nice vibrator."] [Jones - "Was there enough torque that you had to put some lateral pressure on it?"] [Scott - "I don't think so. I think it was torqueless. Was it?"] [Jones - "Gene's experience was that he had to hold it pretty firmly because it felt like it was going to turn him. Now, I'll have to check whether that was the heat flow or the deep core."] [S

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1472954csm.text: And, one other thing, Karl. The attitude change from the gegenschein calibration attitude to plus-X forward SIM attitude was pretty squarely in the middle of the gimbal lock. And I had to do some maneuvering to get around it, using a little extra fuel. You might run that back through with the FAO.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1472954csm.text: Okay, Jim. When you get out to the ALSEP site, once again being very careful with your dust, and particularly the exposed SIDE experiment, we'd like for you to do a photo pan out there. And...Stand by. Let's see; stand by. (Pause) [Dave releases his grip and backs away from the drill to stand still and get a few seconds of rest. He stands leaning forward with his arms hanging down in front of him. He hasn't made any progress beyond the six inches of penetration he achieved initially.] [Jones - "It looks like you're resting your hands, which suggests you were having to grip a little bit."] [Sco

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1472954csm.text: Roger. We copy. [Long pause.]

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1472954csm.text: Al, still a little trouble on the High Gain. Let's go Wide Beam for a second or two and back to Narrow. [Long pause.]

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1472954csm.text: And, Dave, take a breather there.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1472954csm.text: Yeah; (chuckling) it's tightening up again, Joe, and I'm not putting any force on it all. It pulls itself down in; and then it starts to bind up.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1472954csm.text: Roger. Copy.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1472954csm.text: Dave, I hope we get a chance to pick that rock up before we go back.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1472954csm.text: Which one?

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1472954csm.text: Over here. That black glassy one.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1472954csm.text: Oh, is it a nice one?

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1472954csm.text: Endeavour, let's go back to Reacq.

a15_1472954csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1472954csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1473514csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1473514csm.text: Al, we'd like to go Pitch, minus 11, Yaw 12, without changing the mode switch.

a15_1473514csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1473514csm.text: Gee, Joe, I think I got through something. (Pause) It's easier.

a15_1473514csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1473514csm.text: Roger, Dave. And we're learning things. [Dave hops back to rest. During his next transmission, he waves his forearms from side to side.] 147:35:39 Scott: Whew! Yeah, I guess we are. Let me take a little break here. It just started easing up there and went down a little easier. Like (laughing) we might have got through a layer, huh?

a15_1473514csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1473514csm.text: Roger. (Joking) I hope we're not going to let the air out (of the Moon).

a15_1473514csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1473514csm.text: (Laughing) Yeah, and me. [In reality, on one of the occasions when Dave pulled up on the drill, he pulled one of the subsurface stem sections out of the one below it and, in this last stage of drilling, the upper section slid past the lower one. See the discussion at 147:45:53 .] 147:35:59 Irwin: Dave, I'm wondering, if we're really serious about Station 8, whether maybe we could get started on that, and I could be doing...

a15_1473514csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1473514csm.text: You ought to do that if you're really going to do Station 8.

a15_1473514csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1473514csm.text: That sounds good to us, Jim. And Dave, I think maybe you could put another section on that. Video Clip 2 min 33 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 23 Mb MPG )

a15_1473514csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1473514csm.text: Yes, sir, I could. Let's see if I can get the drill off. (Long Pause) [Dave takes a step forward to get going and then does a single long hop that puts him next to the drill. He blocks the stems with his right foot and turns the drill 360 degrees, watching closely as the stem turns in unison. Readers interested in a discussion of the release mechanism should consult section 14.4.1.2 of the Apollo 15 Mission Report . The heat flow drill-stem re-design for Apollo 16 eliminated the need for this particular release mechanism.]

a15_1473514csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1473514csm.text: Try the old vise. (Pause) [The vise is on the ground next to the drill stems. Dave takes hold of the left drill handle with his left hand and drops to his knees. He reaches out with his right hand to grabe the vise, which is on the ground on the far side of the drill. he gets back on both knees to get the zise ready for attachment.]

a15_1473514csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1473514csm.text: Joe, you had a question about the bubble on the Central Station? [At 128:58:00 , during post-EVA-1debriefing, Joe asked, " Jim, once again back to the Central Station. How accurately was the bubble level when you saw it?" Jim replied, "Oh, it was within, oh, one-eight to one-quarter of the center." Here, Jim is back at the ALSEP for the first time since then is taking the opportunity to check his memory, even though Joe had indicated they were happy with his report.]

a15_1473514csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1473514csm.text: Wide - Al, we need to go to Wide for a couple of seconds and then back to Narrow. [Long pause.]

a15_1473514csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1473514csm.text: Jim, we're happy with that; no problem.

a15_1473514csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1473514csm.text: Okay; because the outer edge of the bubble is at the outer edge of the black mark.

a15a1474032.speaker: Allen
a15a1474032.text: Okay, Dave, take heart. You've got just one minute of drilling left.

a15a1474032.speaker: Scott
a15a1474032.text: (Chuckling) Okay, Joe. The only things that give out are the hands. I'll tell you...You know, all this working with the gloves on, after a while...(Long Pause) [Dave turns to watch Jim taking pictures. He stands still flexing his fingers. After a few seconds, he hops back to the drill.] Video Clip 3 min 13 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 29 Mb MPG )

a15a1474032.speaker: Irwin
a15a1474032.text: Okay, Joe, this mag ran out. I'm going to go back and change.

a15a1474032.speaker: Allen
a15a1474032.text: Okay, Jim. (Pause) [Jim got two sunstruck photos of the Heat Flow Experiment, AS15-87- 11859 and 11860 .] [Dave pulls the drill up a few inches but makes no further progress in a few seconds of drilling before Joe calls.] 147:41:21 Allen: And, Dave, we're satisfied with this drill hole. Suggest you stop, pull the drill off, and emplace the heat flow probe. [Dave hops back from the drill.]

a15a1474032.speaker: Scott
a15a1474032.text: Okay. We made a little money, didn't we? 147:41:35 Allen: Hand over fist. (Long Pause) [Scott - "I didn't argue about that at all. Joe said 'that's enough for now' and I said 'Great!' Thank you, Dr. Allen."] [Dave hops to the drill and turns it briefly, just on the off chance that he won't have to use the wrench. The drill turns freely. In order to get down to the wrench, Dave rests his left hand on the top of the drill which, this time, is about a meter above the surface. He hops and puts his feet a bit behind him and spread apart, and bends his knees, leaning and reaching to his right. Once

a15a1474032.speaker: Allen
a15a1474032.text: ...Jim. That is to say, any mag that's empty.

a15a1474032.speaker: Allen
a15a1474032.text: That is, any mag that's still full and not exposed, and you can look at the frame number.

a15a1474032.speaker: Irwin
a15a1474032.text: Oh, I thought you'd be able to give me a quick reading. (Pause)

a15a1474032.speaker: Allen
a15a1474032.text: Try Oboe Oboe. 147:42:50 Irwin: I already have it. [Comm Break] Video Clip 1 min 46 sec ( 0.5 Mb RealVideo or 16 Mb MPG ) This clip starts at about 147:44:10. [While Jim and Joe were talking, Dave examined the drill and stem and turned the drill a small amount. He then grabbed the drill with both hands and shook it vigorously up and down. The drill came off. He then put the drill down and got the heat flow probe off the rack. During this comm break, he feeds the probe into the drill stem and gets the rammer; but, apparently, has trouble engaging the rammer on the wire.]

a15_1474246csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1474246csm.text: We're all squared away on the High Gain now, Al. Thank you.

a15_1474246csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1474246csm.text: Okay, Karl. Was there a problem associated with my gear, or with yours? [Pause.]

a15_1474246csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1474246csm.text: We sus - we suspect that there was some problem about the new attitude, and we were getting some sort of reflection off your skin up there.

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: Okay. Sorry I couldn't get it all the way in, because that sure isn't very far. (Reading a mark on the rammer where it goes into the top drill stem) Bravo 9.

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: Roger. (Long Pause) [Dave carefully removes the rammer so that he doesn't pull the probe up.]

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: And, Dave, could you give... [Once Dave disengages the rammer from the probe wire, he puts it along side the drill string and positions it so that the "Bravo 9" mark is at the top of the string. The location of the tip corresponds to the top of the probe in the drill string and, from the TV, it is about 6 inches above the surface.]

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: About like that.

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: ...us an outside reading.

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: An outside reading? What do you mean?

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: Never mind, we got it already off the TV. [Somebody in the Backroom realized that Dave had just given them the desired information, albeit non-verbally.]

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: Of just how high the pipe comes up above the surface. We'd like for you to make sure the dirt is solid against the outside of the pipe, and then ask you to police the area as best you can of foreign objects.

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: Okay. [Dave started to measure the length of pipe sticking out of the ground but, once he realized that Houston had the information they needed, he stopped and is now tamping the dirt around the drill string by planting his right foot and pressing firmly on the surface.]

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: And as you...

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: The other thing I'm going to do, Joe, is re-align the...(Stops to listen)

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: ...leave, we want you to make sure the cables are lying as flatly as possible on the surface.

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: Okay. And I'll also make sure that the box (meaning the Heat Flow Electronics package or HFE) is aligned. 147:51:38 Allen: Good idea. (Long Pause) [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "After the initial alignment and all the shuffling around there with the probes and all, and one point I tripped over one of the wires to the probe and I moved the electrical box from its alignment position. I think the ground called up and asked some question relative to the position of wires or Boyd bolts around the electrical box. Maybe they were trying to get data, and the thing wasn't properly aligned.

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: And I'll leave this here; maybe the next guy can fix it.

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: Roger. (Long Pause) [Fendell pulls back on the zoom and follows Dave. Dave puts the rack down, removes a Universal Handling Tool (UHT) and heads back to the HFE.]

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: And, Dave, you'll be interested to know that probe went in as far as it will go. That's as deep as the hole was.

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: Really?! You'd have fooled me.

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: Roger. [Scott - "I wonder if this is a correct statement. 'Cause it didn't look right."] [Jones - "It doesn't seem right to me, either. After all, there's another drill stem down there. Maybe what they mean is that the probe went to the same depth as the rammer jammer (about 100 cm below the surface.)."]

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: And, Dave, and while you are there at the box, could you check to see if the Boyd bolt cup - the sleeves - have been taken away from the box.

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: No they haven't, Joe. Well, there were a couple of red washers sitting on the connectors there. The sleeves were gone, yeah.

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: Okay, we copy. Thank you. (Pause) Video Clip 3 min 03 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 27 Mb MPG ) [Dave uses the UHT to try to improve the alignment and leveling of the HFE. Jim is at the Rover and briefly crosses the TV field-of-view.]

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: And, Jim, how are you doing? 147:53:19 Irwin: Oh, I picked up a pink rock and a black rock. And they're documented. [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "You picked up a couple of rocks back there (at the ALSEP site). You picked up your black one."] [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "What I referred to as pink."] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "Pink."] [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "Pink with light plagioclase in it."] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "Did it really? You got to pick up rocks while I had to drill. You have all the luck."] [Irwin, fro

a15a1475024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475024.text: I'm just resting up for Station 8.

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: Not a bad idea. [Jim's breathing is a bit labored, perhaps as a result of picking up the rocks. It returns to normal quickly.] 147:53:33 Irwin: (As) soon at the boss (meaning Dave) tells me where...Tell me where the boss wants it dug. [Jim's last transmission is very difficult to understand and was originally transcribed as "There's a possibility we're just (garbled)."] [Jim comes into view, headed for the Central Station. The trip takes him about 36 seconds. Figure 5-52 from the Preliminary Science Report indicates that the distance from the front of the Rover to the Central Station was, duri

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: Rog. You're lost without the gnomon.

a15a1475024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475024.text: (Chuckling) Yeah. (Long Pause) [During the mission review, Dave and I were unable to fathom Joe's meaning. In a 1996 letter, Dave noted "the gnomon is normally put down to mark the 'spot'" and that observation suggests that, in this instance, Joe is saying Dave is the gnomon. This is another example of Joe's extremely dry wit.]

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: Okay, Joe, (the HFE is) aligned and the number is...(The gnomon shadow is) just about down to the centerline on 2.

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: Okay, Dave, copy. And, Jim, what are you up to there?

a15a1475024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475024.text: Oh, I'm just checking the Central Station.

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: Roger. The alignment's beautiful. [Fendell zooms in on Jim at the Central Station. Because the Rover is parked almost due east of the Central Station and the landing site is at a longitude of only 3 degrees 39 minutes east, this view of the Central Station antenna gives us a good estimate of the elevation of Earth in the Hadley sky.]

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: And, Joe, if Jim took...(To Jim) Hey, don't touch it.

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: Hey, again, it's working perfectly.

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: Okay.

a15a1475024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475024.text: I won't touch it, Joe. (Playfully) I swear!

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: Hey, Joe, if Jim took a picture of the heat flow box, the one he took probably isn't representative of the proper alignment, which it now has. 147:55:01 Irwin: I'll come over and take another one.

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: Okay. Come on over.

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: Jim, just make sure you are well clear of the (Central Station) antenna, with your PLSS there, old friend. (Pause) [Jim backs away from the Central Station and then goes to join Dave at the HFE.] [Scott - "They're dying, back in Houston, watching Jim. 'Don't step on it! Don't move back! Don't move forward. Don't hit the antenna!' Maybe it's not good to have TV, right?. It gives 'em heart palpitations back in the Control Room."] [Jones - "Especially this first time they've had this much TV."]

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: (To himself) I don't...Okay. (Pause)

a15a1475024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475024.text: I need an antenna like that on my PLSS. (Long Pause)

a15a1475024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475024.text: I picked up that black, glassy rock, Dave.

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: Good.

a15a1475024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475024.text: And I picked up another pink one that looked like it had a lot of the plagioclase glass in it.

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: Good. Don't step on this (cable between the HFE and the east probe); I'm trying to get it stretched out flat. (Pause) There. (Pause) [After Dave finishes with the cable, he goes to the HFE to double-check the alignment, accidently dropping the wrench along the way. Jim takes AS15-92- 12416 . The Central Station is in the background and we can also see the RTG, the Solar Wind Spectrometer, the PSE, and assorted trash. Dave's shadow is in the foreground.]

a15_1475550csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1475550csm.text: Okay. While I'm trying to get a bite of lunch here, I thought I'd just tell you that after the dump, the same thing happened - the same kind of cloud, the same kind of particles that - that I described yesterday. And they've just about - they've just about dispersed now. Well, you know, Karl, the interesting thing, I guess I hadn't thought about it before, but when you're sitting up here looking at the surface through one window, it's just pitch black out the other windows. So you go from a very bright scene in one window to a black in the other.

a15_1475550csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475550csm.text: Okay, it's dandy. It's got some dirt on it, but that's all right. Return to the LM Apollo 15 Journal Index The Dreaded Station 8

a15a1475618.speaker: Scott
a15a1475618.text: Okay, Joe, what's next on the agenda?

a15a1475618.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475618.text: Station 8.

a15a1475618.speaker: Allen
a15a1475618.text: I copied your question, Dave, and stand by and take a breather. We're thinking about it here. [Dave resumes his effort to straighten the cable to the east heat flow probe. All through this sequence, it is obvious that Dave and Jim are conscious of the cables underfoot and we see them repeatedly stepping or hopping over them.]

a15a1475618.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475618.text: Dave, if you'd just pick a site, I could sure start digging.

a15a1475618.speaker: Henize
a15a1475618.text: Yes. So, actually out - out the dark window...

a15a1475618.speaker: Allen
a15a1475618.text: Dave, why don't you do that?

a15a1475618.speaker: Scott
a15a1475618.text: Okay, Jim.

a15a1475618.speaker: Worden
a15a1475618.text: [Garble.]

a15a1475618.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475618.text: I've been resting. (Pause) [Dave is using the UHT handle to pick up the wrench, which he dropped about a minute earlier.] ]

a15a1475618.speaker: Henize
a15a1475618.text: Out the dark window, you are still able to see particles?

a15a1475618.speaker: Worden
a15a1475618.text: Yes, I see particles; there's no cloud now.

a15a1475618.speaker: Scott
a15a1475618.text: Okay; (I'll) just go after it (meaning the wrench) here. 147:56:48 Irwin: I'll be over at the Rover, Dave.

a15a1475618.speaker: Henize
a15a1475618.text: You - you did see...

a15a1475618.speaker: Worden
a15a1475618.text: You could until just a few minutes ago, and the particles dissipated rather quickly; and now I don't see any particles out that window.

a15a1475618.speaker: Scott
a15a1475618.text: Be right there. (Long Pause) [Jim runs to the Rover, using the loping stride, and we get a good view of the motion of his backpack. He covers the 25-meter distance in about 24 seconds and his average speed is about 3.7 km/hr.] [Jones - "The backpack's going side-to-side, a little bit, relative to the suit. It's a pretty normal motion that I've seen on all the flights. It's a function of the side-to-side stride, I think."] [Scott - "Probably is. I don't remember. Did we ever say anything about that, about feeling it?"] [Jones - "No. Nobody did. Nobody was bothered by it."] [Scott - "That's inte

a15a1475618.speaker: Henize
a15a1475618.text: Roger. We copy.

a15a1475618.speaker: Allen
a15a1475618.text: Dave, we've got some instructions when you're ready.

a15a1475618.speaker: Scott
a15a1475618.text: Ready, go. (Pause)

a15a1475618.speaker: Allen
a15a1475618.text: Rog, get Jim started on the ditching experiment, if you would please; and then I've got another good one to lay on you here. Don't quite know how to explain it. We'd like for you to try to get the deep core for us with the drill.

a15a1475618.speaker: Scott
a15a1475618.text: (Jim laughs) Aw, Joe, you didn't even have to tell me, because I knew darn well that was coming with the stuff that we must be on top of here. Okay. [This comment suggests that, at this point, Dave believes that the troubles he has been having with the drilling are due to hard subsurface layers.]

a15a1475618.speaker: Allen
a15a1475618.text: Roger. Look at it like this...

a15a1475618.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475618.text: Shall we take Station 8 with the (garbled)?

a15a1475618.speaker: Allen
a15a1475618.text: ...Jim is going to be digging at the same time.

a15a1475618.speaker: Scott
a15a1475618.text: Rog.

a15a1475618.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475618.text: (Looking at his cuff checklist) Well, the thing is, do we want to do the whole Station 8 activity. The comprehensive sample? Video Clip 2 min 58 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 27 Mb MPG )

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1475841csm.text: Al, another bulletin from the lunar surface. The fellows have been back at the LM for some time and working again on the ALSEP. And the problems they had with the drill, they're trying to catch up with now. And yesterday they got in one of the heat sensors and then had trouble finding the time to get in the second one. But they did get the second one in today, and I guess now they're going to go after the core - the core drill sample.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Sure! I guess if they want to do Station 8, they want to do Station 8.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Okay. [The Station 8 proceedures and cuff checklists can be found on pages 117-123 from Apollo 15 Final Lunar Procedures . There are slight differences between the CDR and LMP checklists.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: (Laughing) I guess. Comprehensive sample first, I reckon. Okay, LRV is not parked in the right spot. They could get TV. [Cuff checklist page CDR-15 indicates that they had planned to do Station 8 with the Rover pointed south and the trench west of the LM. This configuration would give good lighting on the trench wall for both the TV and the 16-mm camera. As per CDR-16, they had planned to load a fresh film magazine in the 16-mm camera and film the Station 8 activities at 12 frames per second.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Hey, let's just turn it around. Lift it up an turn it. 147:59:03 Scott: No, they won't like that because the TV is all messed up then. Oh, boy! Listen. Let's just play it out here in front, right out over there (pointing west) and pretend like that is the side of the LRV, except the 16-millimeter won't be in the right spot. Oh, boy! Show biz. [This is one of the few times during Apollo when both members of a crew are standing around, basically doing nothing while a decision is being made. Indeed, since Jim finished the ALSEP pan at 147:38:40 , he has done very little other than change film mag

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: (Pointing) We could aim the 16(-mm camera) out this way; out to the west.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1475841csm.text: Sounds like they're pretty busy down there, Karl.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1475841csm.text: Yep, they are having a good time there, all right.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah, let me...Hey, Houston; what would you rather have? 16 millimeter movies of Station 8 or TV movies of Station 8?

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1475841csm.text: Well, good for them. I'm having a hard time keeping my lobster bisque in the bag up here.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1475841csm.text: Hey, that sounds like a tough life you've got there. [Long pause.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: Dave, we copy that question. Stand by.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: (Getting a little frustrated) You know, by the time we stand by, and you get to a decision (lost under Joe)...

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: Roger; and we'll take TV; that's plenty good enough.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: ...squared away. Jim, let's...(Hearing Joe) Oh, okay. [Dave's tone of voice indicates that he is very pleased with the quick decision.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: And, Jim, you just get...

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Fine.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: ...started with the trench there...

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: We could turn the Rover around and...(Stops to listen to Joe)

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: ...And, Dave, once you get him started, we can begin with the drill.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Okay.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Okay, I guess we want to really start the trench first, Dave.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah, let me get the gnomon. [Dave's level of frustration must not be very high because he playfully uses a hard, non-silent "g" when he says "gnomon".]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah, and I'll get the comprehensive later, if we have a chance.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Okay, Jim, and you...

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: That's affirmative, Jim.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: ...you better...Boy. I better have your camera, because...Let's go out here where it's fresh. [Dave takes the gnomon to a spot about 8 to 10 meters northeast of the TV. Jim goes to his seat so that he can put the scoop down while he takes his camera off.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Let me take the camera off. (Pause)

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Bring it to me.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1480647csm.text: Karl, Endeavour. Just for your information, at the present time I'm right over Timocharis, and Lambert's coming up on - on the - just to the south of me, with Lambert R a very subdued ring just to the - to the south of Lambert. And the photos I want to take are over around the area of Mount La Hire and La Hire Rilles, a little bit west of Lambert.

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1480647csm.text: (Laughing) You know, Jim, I got a checklist on the left arm for one thing that's going on now, and a checklist on the right arm for something else that's going on now. [The checklist on Dave's right arm is the EVA-1 checklist from the previous day, covering the drilling activities which should have been long-since finished; and the one on his left arm is the EVA-2 checklist which covers Station 8. At 138:52:18, before they started EVA-2 preparations, CapCom Gordon Fullerton tolad them, "we suggest that you each wear your EVA-1 cuff checklist on your right arm for use at the end of EVA-2. That'

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1480647csm.text: (Hearty laughter) Unreal. (Long Pause) [After a 15 second break, Jim starts extending the trench toward the south. He digs 14 scoopfuls in about 43 seconds.]

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1480647csm.text: And, as a matter of fact, I have - Mount La Hire seems to be in view now and looks like I'm heading right at it.

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1480647csm.text: Hey, as I look at the map here, it looks like about three - three hills with a crater in the top of each - look like volcanoes here although this map is lousy from that point of view. What do they look like to you?

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1480647csm.text: Okay. (Probably reading from the checklist) "Change 16". (Long Pause) Okay. It looks like the Echo magazine worked okay. [Members of some of the other crews tended to read aloud from their checklists. Dave and Jim hardly ever do. EVA-2 checklist page CDR-19 lists "LMP: change 16-mm mag".] [Jim takes about a 10-second break and then resumes digging.]

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1480647csm.text: Well, I can see a - the - the - they're a chain of hills - ridges, and I can't see much more than that from here right now.

a15_1480937csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1480937csm.text: Okay, Karl. If you're following on the map, I'm right south of the intersection of the La Hire Rilles and the wrinkle ridge [Dorsum Zirkel] that runs off to the northwest there, just by Mount La Hire. In fact, I'm directly over Mount La Hire now, and it looks like there's a volcano in - or not a volcano, but a crater, in the top of the western-most hill.

a15_1480937csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1480937csm.text: Do you think it's long enough? 148:09:39 Scott: Oh, yeah!! That's just super. (Pause) [Dave adjusts the focus and f-stop settings on the camera.]

a15_1480937csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1480937csm.text: I really do think I'm almost down to bedrock. It really is hard.

a15_1480937csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1480937csm.text: Yeah, we ought to have some good sample there from the bottom. (Long Pause) [Dave positions himself northeast of the trench.] Video Clip 3 min 24 sec ( 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 30 Mb MPG ) MP3 Audio Clip ( 13 min 21 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15_1480937csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1480937csm.text: And I'm starting to take some pictures to the west now.

a15a1481011.speaker: Scott
a15a1481011.text: It looks like it has a little color change down there, too. [Dave takes a stereopair, AS15-92- 12439 and 12440 . He then changes the camera settings.]

a15a1481011.speaker: Henize
a15a1481011.text: We copy.

a15a1481011.speaker: Irwin
a15a1481011.text: Yeah, maybe a slight...Seems to get a little darker...A little lighter, then a little darker. (Pause) [Dave gets into position to take down-Sun pictures of the trench.]

a15a1481011.speaker: Scott
a15a1481011.text: A shadow in the way here. (Pause) [Dave takes a half step to his right and takes a stereopair, AS15-92- 12441 and 12442 .]

a15a1481011.speaker: Scott
a15a1481011.text: I have the photos. [Dave has been carrying the SESC in his left hand and, while Jim talks to Houston, takes the top off.]

a15a1481011.text: Roger, Jim.

a15a1481011.text: Okay, Dave and Jim. Jim, we think you can collect the samples here pretty well. [During Joe's transmission, Jim positioned himself southeast of the trench and, with some difficulty, dug a scoopful of soil out of the bottom of the trench. a15a1481011.speaker: Scott
a15a1481011.text: Okay, he can't get the SESC very well by himself, I don't think, Joe. It's tough for two of us to get. (Pause) [Dave is standing north of the trench and holds the SESC out at about waist height.]

a15a1481011.speaker: Allen
a15a1481011.text: Okay. When you finish that, press on with the drill.

a15a1481011.speaker: Scott
a15a1481011.text: (To Jim) Okay, rotate it a little bit. (Pause) [Jim couldn't raise the scoop handle high enough to pour the dirt out of the end and, at Dave's suggestions, rotates it around a horizontal axis to pour the dirt out the side.]

a15a1481011.speaker: Scott
a15a1481011.text: Okay, I need another scoop.

a15a1481011.speaker: Irwin
a15a1481011.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1481011.speaker: Allen
a15a1481011.text: And while you're looking down in there, how deep do you think it is now? [Jim gets another scoopful and, after he gets the tip of the scoop balanced on the top of the can - spilling about half of the dirt in the process - he raises the handle with a rotation of his left shoulder. a15a1481011.speaker: Irwin
a15a1481011.text: Okay.

a15a1481011.speaker: Scott
a15a1481011.text: Yeah. The water flag's clear, Joe. (Going to higher cooling) Ohh, that feels so good! [The Sun is currently about 30 degrees above the horizon and, from Figure 9-9 in the Apollo 17 Preliminary Science Report , we can estimate that the current surface temperature is about 50 C or 120 F.]

a15a1481011.speaker: Irwin
a15a1481011.text: Okay, I'm going for the Rover tracks.

a15a1481011.speaker: Allen
a15a1481011.text: Roger. (Long Pause) [Jim moves up-Sun, going slow enough that Fendell has no trouble following. a15_1481159csm.text: (Answering Joe) Oh, I'd say it's 14 (to) 16 inches deep, Joe.

a15_1481159csm.text: Extraordinary. Thank you. (Pause) [Jim gets a third scoopful and, although his body hides most of the scoop, he seems to use a pouring technique more like the one he used for the first scoopful than the second.] Video Clip 3 min 1 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 27 Mb MPG )

a15_1481159csm.text: Okay, babe. Can you tilt it up? Got it. (Pause) White clast in there. A little bit more; keep coming. Good job.

a15_1481159csm.text: Think we got enough.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Yes, sir. We got 75 percent full.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Outstanding. [Dave removes the Teflon seal protector and drops it on the ground next to the trench. The tranch sample is 15014 , consisting of 333 grams of soil.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: (To Dave) Okay, you're going to leave me, and I'll sample it myself. I guess I'll fill the bags myself then. a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: Roger. I copy.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: I guess you'll have to.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay. [While Dave puts the top on the can, Jim walks to the Rover.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1481159csm.text: And there's nothing particularly significant that you can see on the map there. It's just that the La Hire Rilles seem to be associated with a lot of those flows, and the flows - there's so many of them, and they're so overlapping and intermingling that I just want to get some general pictures of those flows coming out of La Hire.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay. (Brief pause) Unless you want to go do the drill.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Not at all, brother! You got her. I'll do all the...(Pause) Why don't you loan me your checklist.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: LM Crew
a15_1481159csm.text: (Sustained, hearty laughter at the thought of Jim with three cuff checklists)

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Oh, yeah! (Jim continues laughing) Guess what!

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Yeah, I...(Stops to laugh) Oh, I think I can get...Joe'll talk me through it. [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "You did all the penetrometer yourself. That was an interesting departure from our pre-flight plan, because we had planned to do the Station 8 together. I had all the procedures in my checklist (see CDR-17 to 19), since (in the planned Station 8) I just walked you through them. Apparently, you made out all right without having all those detailed procedures."] [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I had just enough abbreviated details (see LMP-17 to 19) that I could follo

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: Roger. That sounds like a very interesting region, and I see over by Diophantus there, you've got some very prominent rilles at the present time that probably are just on the - on the terminator, aren't they?

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1481159csm.text: Yes, Karl. I'm - I'm beyond the terminator now.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: (Answering Dave) Any one's fine.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: ...for now so I can get going. (Hearing Joe) No; (you're) too late. [Jim is still standing at his seat and, off-camera, Dave may be trying to put the SESC in Jim's SCB.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Get up. Jim?

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Yeah?

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay. Nothing; press on. [Dave's transmission at 148:14:39 suggests that he has given up on the attempt to get the SESC in Jim's SCB.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay, Joe, I'm going to do a little (laughing) sampling of the trench.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: Next time you get the Flight Plan in hand, let me give you the T-start for the zodiacal light photography.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: I hear you. (Pause)

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: (If I can) just hang on to the (individual sample) bags. (Pause) [Jim has dropped the sample bag and, rather than waste time retrieving it, returns to the Rover to get another.] 148:14:11 Scott: (Garbled) A little unorthodox. I'm going to drill. Watch me.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay. 148:34:26 is the zodiacal light photo PAD.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: (To Houston) Probably won't be quite as much of a sample here, since I'm doing it myself, Joe. [Jim walks to the trench and, initially, kicks some dust ahead of him. a15_1481159csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1481159csm.text: Understand, 148:34:26.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: That's affirmative. [Long pause.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: That's fine. That's a perfect place; couldn't have suggested any better myself.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Good. [Jim extends the scoop into the trench with his right arm. He has virtually all of his weight on his right leg but has his left leg and his left arm back for balance. a15_1481159csm.text: And D(avid). R., as you probably know already, all we need from this EVA is really the hole in the ground. The drill (battery) will probably give out on us during your rest period. And, if need be, we can pull up whatever you get later on.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay, Joe. Fine.

a15_1481159csm.text: Say again, Endeavour.

a15_1481159csm.text: Shoot, no. Never! (Pause) [Jim got a second scoopful of soil from the bottom of the trench into the bag and, now, walks to the Rover.]

a15a1482253.text: Roger. (Pause) And, Dave and Jim...

a15a1482253.text: Okay, adjacent to the Rover tracks. (Pause) Pushing.

a15a1482253.text: (Grunting) Bottomed out. (Pause) We don't want to leave here before I get a chance to collapse my trench, Joe.

a15a1482253.text: (Chuckles) (Pause) Okay, I'm going for the plate.

a15a1482253.text: Roger. (Long Pause) [While Jim goes to the Rover, Fendell aims the TV at Dave, who is twisting the drill off the drill string. a15a1482253.text: Roger, Jim. [The plate is the small, rectangular object on the tip of the penetrometer shaft.]
