a15a1482253.text: Roger. (Pause)

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: It bottomed out.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Dave's breathing is intermittently audible. Dave is still having trouble getting the stems threaded.] [Jones - "The thing that amazes me is that the threads on those cores really had a big pitch. In shirtsleeves, it's trivial to get those things attached. I've tried it and it's easy. But standing there at the end of that lever arm, wearing those gloves with the huge fingers..."] [Scott - "Yeah. And you've got to move the suit. The suit's good, but you still have to move against it (and) overcome the pressure."] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I got all the sectio

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Indexing to seven. 148:27:01 Allen: Roger. (Long Pause) [Just before Jim's next transmission, Dave finally gets the drill stems threaded. At some point during his struggles, he knocks the drill over but, this time, has no trouble bobbing down to get it. He doesn't quite go to his knees.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay; I'm going to be collapsing the trench side. I hope. (Long Pause) [Dave threads the drill on the drill string and, as Fendell zooms in on the treadle, Dave steps on the treadle and starts to drill.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay. I'm about four inches out from the side of the trench. (Pause) And I'm pushing. (Pause) It's bottomed out. A slight amount of collapse.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: It won't collapse?

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: (Grunting) I'm continuing to push. Yup. It just collapsed.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Okay.

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: ...collapsed. I'll take a quick picture here so you can see the location of all of those. (Long Pause) [Jim passes in front of the TV on his way to the back of the Rover where he will remove the extension handle and stow the penetrometer.] Video Clip 3 min 13 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 29 Mb MPG )

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Dave, are you working on the last stem there?

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Yeah.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: You are one fast worker. (Pause) [Dave's breathing is can be heard again. After about 57 seconds of drilling, Dave comes close to finishing the last two sections. Probably following Houston's request to let the drill go in slowly, his average rate for this 80 cm was about 1.4 cm/s or 0.6 inches/s. Dave relaxes his grip and hops back to rest. When Fendell pulls back on the zoom, we see Dave leaning forward with his arms hanging down.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Okay, Dave. Take a breather. And I've got one last instruction for you here. Using the drill, we want you to break it loose (meaning "free the drill string in the hole") and then let the drill and the stem sit there in the surface and we'll pull it out later.

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Okay. Let me finish it off. (Long Pause) [Dave starts drilling again and completes the remaining 20 to 30 cm. When he steps back, the drill chuck is only a few centimeters off the ground.] 148:29:26 Allen: And just leave the drill on stem, handle away from the Sun, as long as flutes pull free. [Joe's "flutes" is difficult to understand. He may, in fact, have said "lutes".]

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: As long as what?

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Rog. As long as the threads pull free from the hole.

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Yeah. Well, we'll try that now. [Dave leans forward and grabs the drill handles. He pulls up sharply, raising the drill perhaps 20 cm.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: (Grunts) Ahh, we can get it! Okay, Joe; we're in good shape.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Okay, Dave. We want the handle away from the Sun. And we're ready for you to get back on the Rover.

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Wait a minute Joe. [Dave grabs the drill again, gets his feet on either side of the drill stem and twice uses his legs to pull up on the drill. He ends up with the chuck just below knee height.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: (Grunting) I'm not sure I'll ever get it out. (Pause) What bothers me, Joe, is...Okay. Handle away from the Sun. (Pause) (The battery) box is sort of dirty. [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "When I got the drill all the way in, I attempted to pull it out and, not surprisingly, it was very difficult to pull out. We expected that from our training. In certain cases during training, people observing in shirtsleeves couldn't get the drill out of the ground at the Cape. I wasn't at all surprised to find that, after having drilled through bedrock, I couldn't pull the drill out. I got maybe

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Get pictures of the drill will you, Jim? Take...Go...Hey, just south of the drill, I really need a (locator)...I already did a pan here. Get your trench (pictures) and get a couple of pictures of the drill to show its position.

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Okay, Jim. A few pictures and you can walk back and, Dave, we want you to start on the Rover, please.

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Yeah, Joe. I'm on the way. 148:31:11 Allen: Okay. (Long Pause) [Fendell stops his pan to look at the Central Station. Note how little of Hill 305 is visible beyond the local horizon. As with LM visibility near Station 4, the fact that relatively little of the mountain is visible is probably due to local terrain.] [Jim takes only one picture, AS15-92- 12443 , which is a down-Sun after of the collapsed trench.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay, Dave. I think everything...You're not going to drive too fast are you?

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Heck no. [Fendell resumes his pan.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay, I'll meet you back there.

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Yeah. (Pause) Much dust when you drive fast. [Jim is concerned about the possibility of getting sprayed with dust as Dave drives by him.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Keep it clean.

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Okay, Joe, you going back PM1/WB . (Long Pause; heavy static which continues until noted below) [TV off.] Heat Flow Reprise Apollo 15 Journal EVA-2 Closeout

a15a1483216.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483216.text: Okay, Joe, I'm back at the LM. (Pause)

a15a1483216.speaker: Allen
a15a1483216.text: (Making a rare mis-identification because of the static) Okay, Dave, copied you back at the LM, parking the Rover normally, and we're standing by for TV again.

a15a1483216.speaker: Allen
a15a1483216.text: Roger, Dave. While you're brushing the LRV BAT covers, you might as well give the whole area a good dusting and cleaning. The LCRU covers, the TCU, the television camera, please.

a15a1483216.speaker: Scott
a15a1483216.text: Be glad to, Joe. (Pause) Taking three up this time, Jim?

a15a1483216.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483216.text: Huh? 148: Scott: This go in that bag? 148: Irwin: Yeah. Just put all those rocks - I can get those, Dave.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1483228csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. The Rover boys have finished their tasks - most of their tasks with the ALSEP, and they are just now beginning ingress into the LM. Dave managed to get the core drill completely in; and, although he hasn't pulled it out yet, he'll pull it out on the next EVA. The time to set the mission timer, or to set your countdown for the zodiacal light photos is going to be about in one minute. And the word down here is that all of your systems are Go; everything's looking super.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1483228csm.text: No, that's Jim. Jim is back. I don't know, Dave might be close.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1483228csm.text: I'm getting on the Rover now Jim. I'm just parking your TV for you. (Long Pause)

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1483228csm.text: (Static fades) Hey, Dave, you do have some cores now to go in the SRC. Is that right?

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1483228csm.text: Roger, Karl. Thank you very much. See you on the other side. And, if you'll check my DSKY, you'll see I got the time count down there too.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1483228csm.text: No, Jim, I didn't get them out yet.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1483228csm.text: Okay. Well, I guess I'll go ahead and put the bag that I have here in SRC 2.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1483228csm.text: Jim, if you can get the SESC in there that would be great, and then go ahead and close out that rock box. (Pause) No problem on those drill stems, we'll get them later. (Long Pause) And, Dave, this is Houston. If there's dust on the LRV Batt(ery) covers, brush it off before you open them, please.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1483228csm.text: And I'm even managing to finish my lunch. Thank you.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1483228csm.text: That is a soft life up there, when you get a chance to finish your lunch.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1483228csm.text: You better believe it. Some times it's not so easy.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: And, Dave, this is Houston.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Go ahead.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Roger, Dave. While you're brushing the LRV BAT covers, you might as well give the whole area a good dusting and cleaning. The LCRU covers, the TCU, the television camera, please.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Be glad to, Joe. (Pause) Taking three up this time, Jim?

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Huh? 148: Scott: This go in that bag? 148: Irwin: Yeah. Just put all those rocks - I can get those, Dave.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, here's one for you. I'll set it right up by your camera. Okay?

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: And, Jim, are you packing the rock box yet?

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Yeah; I am.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Did you happen to get a number off the SESC?

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: No, I didn't. But, shoot, you ought to be able to track that one, Joe.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: We'll track it. No problem. (Long Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: And, Dave, we assume that you're dusting and cleaning now; and we'll be standing by for TV.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Well, okay, Joe. I'm not sure I'm going to take the time to give you the TV, unless you really need it.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Dave, we've got a lot of time. We're going to deploy the flag now and we need the TV please. (Jim laughs)

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, Joe.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: And, we're in good shape on the time. We're back at the LM; and we've got a lot of time to work with. So no problem.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, Joe. Why don't you just give us about five minutes with no comments and let us just cool it for a while. Okay? [Houston has handled this situation badly. At the very least, they should have taken a few minutes during the drive back to explain what was contemplated, rather than feed one revision at a time, keeping the crew in the dark about the schedule for the rest of the EVA. The disruption caused by the drilling problems has been frustrating enough and, having rushed to get things done in expectation of an immediate close out, to be told now that "we've got a lot of time", must have be

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Roger. (Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Cool it, Jim. Just take it easy. Take a break. That's enough.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Okay.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: We've got plenty of time. We're going to cool it right now.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Okay. (Pause) I'm having the same problem with that SRC today as I did yesterday. I had to pound on the handle to get it sealed. (Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, well just take your time.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Well, I'm not rushing.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Use these five minutes as part of our rest period tonight. (Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Dave and Jim, while you're taking a breather there, let me make a comment. We've got 37 minutes before repress. So we're in good shape on the time. And just for your own information - I know you're curious - your oxygen consumption has been considerably less today - considerably less - and we're running well over a seven-hour PLSS capability.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, Joe. Very good. Just give us five minutes with a nothing, will you? (Pause) Just (to) make sure we've got a good last twenty-seven minutes. [Having made his point, Dave relaxes quickly.]

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Yes, sir. (Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Dave, I going to get you to give me a hand with this.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Sure.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: It's almost a two-man operation. (Pause) Bring it over here.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Huh? Want to go to the MESA table? Let's go to the MESA table.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: No, its...Well...

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Yeah, it's easier to work with; it's higher. (Pause) Okay.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: If you can push down on it, I'll lock it. You might have to hit it down.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Oh, yeah. (Laughing) 148:39:34 Irwin: You can pound it. That's what I had to do. I had to pound it with my fist yesterday. [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "We found out subsequently that, apparently, part of the bag was caught in the rear hinge."] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "Subsequently being now. It looked to me like the lid was closed on the seal."] [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "In the front, yes; but we never looked at the back of it."] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I didn't either. I should have. It looked like the handle was just mismatc

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, let me hold your arm, and use your arm as (garbled). Okay?

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Okay.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Oh, my! Let me try it this way. (Pause) Even my total body weight won't do it, so I'm going to have to stick one arm under you...

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: I had to pound it yesterday to get it closed. (Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Well, it closes, but it doesn't lock.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Well, I'll have to push it locked.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Really?

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Yeah, it won't spring locked.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Try it again, Dave.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: It's that close?

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Yeah. (Dave grunts) (Pause) (Garbled) (Pause) You ought to have that seal pretty well made now.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Yeah. I'll try it again. (Pause) ... Jim, it's never going to lock. You know why? The lock isn't in the right place! Look at that. Look at where the handle is relative to the lock. You'll never get it over. I've got the handle all the way down!

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Yeah.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: That lock will never lock this way.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Okay, let's look at the right one and see if the right one is the same way.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: The right one's the same way, I don't know how I ever got the one locked yesterday.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: It can't lock, because the handle was bent up above the lock. There's no way!

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Yeah.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, let's take the stuff out of there and leave the SRC. Just leave it, take the stuff in without it.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: No, we'll take it that way.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: What do we want the SRC for? It's not closed. 148:41:33 Irwin: Well, I think we probably have a seal, if we keep these handles in this position, because the...

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Yeah. That's true.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: ...the seal is already made. If we could tape those handles down, we'd probably have a vacuum in there.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Wait. Be careful we don't release them.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, yeah. You're right. Okay, what else do you have to do here?

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: (That's) about it.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Well, let's take a look at things. [The closeout procedures are on LMP-21 and 22 and CDR-21 and 22.]

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Dust each other off. 148:42:02 Irwin: Hey, let's get those cover bags.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Oh, that's a good idea. [They will put the covers on the SCBs to help control dust in the cabin.]

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: I'll get them if you got something to do out there.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Yeah. Let me get the TV going here. (Long Pause) Okay. Got some more rocks on the seat pan, too, Jim.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, Joe, I want to put you on TV...(Brief static) See if I can't find the old Earth here.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Super, Dave, we're waiting and we still have a full half-hour remaining; good shape.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, I suggest we take it and go nice and slow and easy.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: That's exactly right.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Okay, I have the sample containment bags out here, Dave. I'll just leave them here on top.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay. [ Sample Containment Bags were flown on the J missions to help reduce the amount of dust in the cabin. The Sample Collection Bags were put inside the Containment Bags . Photos of containment bags in the National Air & Space collection courtesy Allan Needell.]

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: I'll come over and pick up those other rock samples. (Long Pause) Video Clip 3 min 01 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 27 Mb MPG )

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, Joe, the AGC says you ought to have a picture. [TV on.]

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: We've got a beautiful picture.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Of the streaks on the battery covers, huh?

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: You never know what you might like to look at. (Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Yeah. I can even see the Earth. You know, another problem (with use of the sighting scope) is, the Earth is getting smaller. [Earth is well past half phase. Apollo 15 was launched at 13:34 Greenwich Mean Time on July 26, 1971. We are now at 6 days 4 hours 44 minutes into the mission and it is now 18:18 GMT/UTC on August 1st. Because of the tilt of the Earth and of the Moon's orbit, at this moment the Moon is directly over the southern tip of Africa. It is just past sunset in Lagos, Nigeria, and the Earth is about 1/4 full. The Earth was half full at about 1000 GMT/UTC on the 30th.]

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Roger, Dave. That's one of Kepler's mission rules.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Right. [This is, of course, a reference to the German mathematician/astronomer Johannes Kepler (1571-1630) who was the first person to correctly describe the motions of objects in the Solar System.] [As we will learn at 148:45:18 , Fendell is unable to raise the TV camera. He pans right to the LCRU mirror, which Dave has dusted, but not completely.]

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, I got the LCRU (mirror and the) battery covers dusted off; and the console on the LRV isn't too bad, I dusted that off. It wasn't too bad anyway.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: And I guess the next order of business (pause) (is to) get the rocks all packed. [Fendell pans farther right and looks at the disturbed soil at the front of the Rover.]

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Okay, Dave, I've got all the rock samples.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay. Get the ETB and get all our film. (Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: The only task is getting all this stuff up.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Yeah. We'll use the old...(Pause) 148:45:18 Allen: Dave and Jim, once again our TV camera is stuck in the down position. I wonder if you could give us some help there. And we'd also like an amp-hours reading from the Rover, and a battery temp, please.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: I'll get that Dave. [Dave bounces around the front of the Rover from the direction of his seat and raises the TV. As he goes past the front of the Rover, we get a good look at the flat sheet of dust he kicks forward with his boots.]

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: The old TV's up.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Thank you.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: You're welcome.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: I'll get that other gear - stuff - while you pack.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Okay, amp-hour reading is 91 and 96. Battery temp is 100, on both.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Beautiful, Jim. Are we ever making the miles on that Rover. [At the start of the EVA-1 traverse at 120:33:49 , the initial battery charge readouts were 100 and 115 amp-hours. Thus far, they have driven about 22.8 km (10.3 during EVA-1 and 12.5 km during EVA-2) and have drawn about 38 amp-hours, giving an average of about 1.67 amp-hours/km. Readers should note that this figure includes LCRU usage and an unknown level of uncertainty. Of relevance here is the fact that the indicated use rate is much less than the pre-flight prediction of 3.67 amp-hours/km. See, also, the discussion at 167:35:58 .

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Yeah. Let's see, I should pull the circuit breakers on the Rover.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: I can get them easier over here.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: If you got fingers left for it. I appreciate it.

a15a1491150.text: Okay. (Hearing a warning tone) Must be my water. (Pause, while Dave looks at his RCU indicators). [The sensor system in Dave's EMU is telling him that there is no water flow to the sublimator. Clearly, the warning system is still working.]

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: No flags, (but) I've got a tone. (Still trying to get Jim's water valve) And I sure can't reach it from here.

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: How did we do it yesterday?

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Turn left. Can you come forward and turn left? Turn right. Just turn right the way you were, maybe all the way around. (Pause)

a15a1491150.text: (Can you see) what I'm hung up on.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Can't really see anything. Come forward. Oh, I know. Go up. Up. (Pause)

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: What is it?

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: It's the tool harness (that's caught) on your bar. (Pause) [Scott - "Wasn't there a bar in there that we hold on to. Isn't there a bar that you hold on to when you land?"] [Dave may be referring to the "crash bars" which ran along the lower window sills as shown in a Grumman cabin sketch and in Apollo 11 photo AS11-36- 5392 .] [Jones - "Wouldn't be surprised. And that would be sort of the right place, at the right-hand corner for him. And that would make sense with how you were telling him to move his PLSS."] [Scott, from a 1996 letter - "There were also vertical 'posts' adjacent to the handco

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Still stuck?

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: If you could go up and turn right, you'll unhook. Up and turn right. Yeah. No, you're not...You're going to have to get your water by yourself, I'm afraid, until we get depressed.

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Well, we can depress with the water on.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Yeah.

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: We'll just get a little water in the cabin.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: We'll have to, because I'm not (garbled)...Okay. [Reading] "Post-EVA. Water closed. Forward hatch closed and locked." Okay. Let's get that. (Pause)

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: I have to get unlocked here, though, to get around.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: I know it. (Pause) Okay. Let's see if I can tell. Closed and locked. I think. (Pause)

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Unless you can ...You can't reach around me to get the (cabin repress valve and circuit breaker)

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: You have to raise your right side up and go to your left. It would be the best thing you could do. (Pause) That's it. Keep coming. Up and left; up with the right and over to your left. That a boy! Good show. There you go.

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: (Garbled) Dave?

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Yeah, you're clear.

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Okay.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Now...Let me get the...(To Jim) Easy does it! Go easy.

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Yeah, I am. (Long Pause)

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Okay? (Pause)

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Okay. You can read to me.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Okay. Well, maybe I can get your water, if you go forward. Can you move into the corner?

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Yeah. I can rotate around to the right, Dave.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Okay. You've got to move.

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Move which way? In?

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Into the corner, because I can't get my arm up to your control there. (Pause) Now, we've got it. Okay. Prime feedwater is Off.

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Good.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: I think.

a15a1491150.speaker: Allen
a15a1491150.text: Good show. [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "We again had trouble getting hold of the water valves. That is probably because both our hands were hurting at the end of the EVA. It's just hard to feel with them."]

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Now, if you can come around and get the hatch (dump valve).

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: I got it. It's Auto.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Okay. Okay. "Both to Auto", and then " Cabin Repress (valve) to Auto".

a15a1491150.text: Cabin Repress, that was the first one?

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Yes, sir. "Cabin Repress to Auto". Okay. And, "CB(16): ECS Cabin Repress, closed". (Pause; then sound of repress starts)

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Cabin Repress, closed.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Okay. Coming up. 0.5 (psi) (Long Pause)

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: 2.0. (Long Pause)

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: 4.1. Okay. We're about there. (The sound of repress ends) " Press Reg A and B to Cabin ." (Pause) Get them?

a15a1491150.text: Yeah.

a15_1492757csm.text: Okay. (Pause) Eww. Mine's verified.

The only problem we had was our fingers were so sore."] [After I turned the tape recorder off, we started talking about differences in hand soreness and fatigue between zero-g and one-sixth g.] [Jones - "I thought part of the problem was that, for example, on the long Apollo 17 traverse out to Station 2, Jack's camera

a15_1492757csm.text: Dave and Jim, while you're enjoying that (freedom from wearing the gloves), stand by to copy a new EVA record: 7 hours plus 12 minutes plus 53 seconds. And I'll be prepared to sign your sporting certificates a little later.

a15_1492757csm.text: Oh, how about that! Thank you, Joe! They would put in one set of records on o

a15_1492757csm.text: Okay, gloves off. (Pause)

a15_1492757csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1492757csm.text: (Garbled)

a15_1492757csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1492757csm.text: Did you get them both off?

a15_1492757csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1492757csm.text: Whew! Oh, that feels good!

a15_1492757csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15_1492757csm.text: Okay. Let's get your (garbled). Let me get this up.

a15_1492757csm.text: Can you reach it? (Long Pause)

a15_1492757csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15_1492757csm.text: Okay.

a15_1492757csm.text: Safety's on the dump valve .

a15_1492757csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. How do you read? [Pause.]

a15_1492757csm.text: And Houston. Endeavour loud and clear, and I've got you locked up now.

a15_1492757csm.text: Roger. I thought you were trying to tell us something.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. First of all, we're going to cancel the VHF comm check at 149:37. Your buddies just got into the LM down there, and we don't think they'll be ready, and we won't push them at this time on that. [Pause.]

a15_1493403csm.text: It's in your way. Now turn around and I'll see if I can get...

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. (Pause) Probably should have dusted you off better. (Long Pause)

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. Understand.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: And the second one is, it looks like we'll be delaying your Mapping Camera business at 150:10 in the Flight Plan, and we'll get back to you later on exactly what we'll be doing and when on that. And now if you'll turn to 151 hours, we have a Mapping Camera photo PAD for you.

a15_1493403csm.text: Do you mean a Pan Camera photo PAD?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Negative. It says M - A - P.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: (It isn't) locked. Lock it again.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Huh?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: Push it in again.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. (Pause) You just got a magic touch. That was easy. How did you do it?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: Try it out. It was already unlocked. (It was) sliding, hard.

a15_1493403csm.text: Okay, Al, a little explanation. It's a photo PAD I'm due to read you at 150 and 10. So it's at the 151:10 - 150 and 10 that you'll find the little squares for it.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. Oh. Yeah.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: It helps. Having them back that far.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Did it? Yeah. Yeah, you didn't have any trouble getting it off today, did you? (Long Pause)

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. I'm with you. Yeah, when you call out a time like that, that's the time I go to the Flight Plan.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Roger. I thought that's what you should do - but I guess I was wrong. Okay. T-start, 151:09...

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay, 150 plus 10?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Roger. Okay. T-start, 151:09:22; T-stop, 152:09:01. And there's a little note that says at T-start...

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: I'll have to put them this way. (Long Pause)

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay; let's get a little suit flow.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Roger. Understand.

a15_1493403csm.text: Stow mine, I'll have you plug mine up. [Jim's use of the word "plug" suggests that he is having trouble installing a seal in the PLSS/OPS hoses.]

a15_1493403csm.text: [Garble.] [Pause.]

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. Yeah; I thought you had them. Sorry. (Pause) [Jim is having trouble getting his LM oxygen hoses connected.]

a15a1503140.text: Now, I know where you are in the checklist.

a15a1503140.text: We're trying to get to lunch time here. 150:32:15 Gordon: Well, the sooner you do it, the sooner you get to sleep, and we'll be very anxiously awaiting that. [Comm Break]

a15a1503140.speaker: Irwin
a15a1503140.text: Dick, I missed your comment when we lost comm there.

a15a1503140.speaker: Gordon
a15a1503140.text: Jim, I gave you a go-ahead on that battery; and, concerning your lunch, we're anxiously awaiting you to do all that so you can get to bed. We've got a time problem, as you might well recognize.

a15a1503140.speaker: Gordon
a15a1503140.text: And, we'll talk to you a little bit about that when you get a chance.

a15a1503140.speaker: Irwin
a15a1503140.text: That's a...I'm sorry, I got the wrong one, Dick.

a15a1503140.speaker: Gordon
a15a1503140.text: Okay, we didn't have you on high bit rate, but we'll get it as soon as you do.

a15a1503140.speaker: Gordon
a15a1503140.text: Okay, we are looking at your batteries now, they look great. (Long Pause)

a15a1503140.speaker: Gordon
a15a1503140.text: Okay, Jim, we're getting good high bit rate and we'll watch those batteries for a little while.

a15a1503140.speaker: Irwin
a15a1503140.text: Okay. (Long Pause) Houston, ED (Explosive Device) batteries both checked at 37.

a15_1503557csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1503557csm.text: And Endeavour, as you go around the hill, you're looking good. We'll look for you on the other side.

a15_1503557csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1503557csm.text: Okay, Houston. See you on the other side.

a15a15112xx.speaker: Gordon
a15a15112xx.text: Okay, Dave. I bet that feels good.

a15a15112xx.speaker: Gordon
a15a15112xx.text: Look, on that telemetry biomed, since we looked at you last night, you can leave that where it is in the "Right" (LMP) position, and we'll look at Jim tonight. 151:13:45 Scott: Okay, fine. And I'll tell you the secret to living up here is getting out of these suits. It really makes the difference.

a15a15112xx.speaker: Gordon
a15a15112xx.text: Yeah, I believe you're absolutely right. a15a15112xx.text: Okay, and I owe you a word on your PLSS recharge (on surface 8-6). When you have those things in that good vertical position, they want you to charge that descent water for 10 minutes instead of 5 you have on your checklist.

a15_1512611csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1512611csm.text: Roger, Al. And we got a couple of VHFs - we got a single VHF window for you if you want to try and get hold of the crew down below. AOS is 151:51:25 and 152:04:15 for LOS. Over. [Pause.]

a15_1512611csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1512611csm.text: Okay, I understand. AOS with LM is 151:51 and LOS is about 152:04.

a15_1512611csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1512611csm.text: Roger. And if you'll give us cue just a little bit ahead, we'll get them to go to Voice so they can pick you up.

a15_1512611csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1512611csm.text: Okay, will do.

a15_1512611csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1512611csm.text: Okay. And second item, Al, is we're not going to put the Mass Spec. boom out tonight because of the problems we've been having with deployment. [Pause.] We will delete the Experiment and Ion Source, On, and Standby, at 152:13. [Pause.] And we will delete the Multiplier, Discriminator, and Ion Source functions at 152:45. Over.

a15_1512611csm.speaker: Worden

a15_1532311csm.text: Okay. Two, was the barber pole indication a half or between a half and three quarters of full during retract? [Pause.]

a15_1532311csm.text: Okay. Understand. Did the talkback change state after approximately...
