a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Understand. 162:16; delete "Gamma-ray Gain Step, Shield, On."

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Roger. Over on 163:10, we add "Map Camera, Image Motion, Increase" with appropriate barber pole comment. Increase, and then leave it on. "Increase/On" would be a better way of reading that to you.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay; understand. At 163:10, you want the "Image Motion, Increase to barber pole and On."

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Roger. And at 163:40, we can add, "Mapping Camera, Image Motion, Increase/On." And also, "Gamma-ray Gain Step, Shield, Off."

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Understand. At 163:40, you want the Image Motion, Increase to Increase/On. Do you want that - How many steps past barber pole do you want it? [Pause.]

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay, Al. I - I missed a beat there. The one at 163:10 was "talkback barber pole plus 4 steps" at that time. And at 63:40, take it to "talkback barber pole" and leave it there. [Long pause.]

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Did that come through okay?

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay; understand. The one at 163:10 is "Image Motion, Increase to barber pole plus 4, and then On". And then at 163:40 is "Increase to barber pole On", and "Gamma-ray Gain Step, Shield, On."

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Roger. 163:40, that was Shield, Off; O-F-F. and at 163:50, the Gamma-ray Gain Step will go Shield, On; Shield O-N.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay. Understand 163:40, Shield is Off; and 163:50, the Shield goes On.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1615936csm.text: Houston, this is Hadley Base. Do you want to leave the Biomed on Left? And I'm going S-band voice to voice.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Roger. And that's the end of the Mapping Camera and the Flight Plan update.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1615936csm.text: Roger, Jim.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Rog.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: The computer is yours, Al. And I have [a] consumables update, if you'd like it.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1615936csm.text: And, are you ready for the battery management called out at 160(:15)?

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay; go ahead.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: GET [Ground Elapsed Time] is 162 hours, 0 minutes; RCS total 60 [percent full]; Quad A: 60, [B] 60, [C] 59, [D] 61; hydrogen tanks: [1] 65, [2] 64, [3] 46; oxygen tanks: [1] 71, [2] 74, [3] 58.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1615936csm.text: Stand by. Okay, Falcon. We're ready.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay, in work. (Pause) ED batteries both check at 37 (volts).

a15_1621351csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1621351csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. The latest information from Hadley Rille is that the crew is awake and about one hour from egress time. This EVA number 3 has been shortened in length somewhat to about 4½ hours in order to get our time line back on time for the nominal ascent. You can expect that you'll have some company later this afternoon.

a15_1621351csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1621351csm.text: Very good, Karl. And, let's see, I guess I can give you a crew status report if you want it.

a15_1621351csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1621351csm.text: Okay. I've got 7½ hours of sleep in one period. No medication. The PRD [Passive Radiation Dosimeter] is 23164.

a15_1621835csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1621835csm.text: Houston, Endeavour. If you're copying the DSKY, the gyro torquing angles are up [on it].

a15_1621835csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1621835csm.text: Roger. We've copied them, thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_1621835csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1621835csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. [A] couple of quick questions. First of all, the Surgeons see something of a difference in your heart rate between the two nights sleep, and just out of medical curiosity, they'd like to have your subjective evaluation. Did you sleep better last night than the night before, or vice versa?

a15_1621835csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1621835csm.text: Gee, I guess subjectively, I slept pretty well both nights.

a15_1621835csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1621835csm.text: Just about equal in other words? Okay, and...

a15_1621835csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1621835csm.text: Yes, I think so, or maybe I slept a little better last night.

a15_1621835csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1621835csm.text: Glad to hear that. You're con - confounding their theories. On... [Long pause.]

a15_1621835csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1621835csm.text: Hadley Base, this is Houston. We're still showing the Cabin Gas Return in Cabin. Could you reverify that it's in Egress, please. (Pause)

a15_1621835csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1621835csm.text: Al, we'd like to have you verify tape motion at LOS; and if it isn't, start the tape running for us.

a15_1621835csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1621835csm.text: And, on this P30 business; I see something of a - a long comment they made to you last night. Is everything on that clear? [Pause.]

a15_1621835csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1621835csm.text: Cabin Gas Return is presently in Auto. I think we pick it up at Egress a little later on in the procedure. (Pause)

a15_1621835csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1621835csm.text: Rog, Karl. I think so. I - I guess for the story there is we'll stay away from using the clock at P30 as much as possible, and when we do use it, especially when we're in deadband, we won't let it run more than 30 minutes.

a15_1621835csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1621835csm.text: Jim, Rog. Actually we should have picked that up on page 8-10 in your checklist. So we think it should be in the Egress position now.

a15a16241xx.speaker: Irwin
a15a16241xx.text: Okay. I'm going Egress. [Very Long Comm Break] MP3 Audio Clip ( 13 min 14 sec ) by David Shaffer [During the comm break, the Public Affairs commentator tells the press that cabin depressurization is expected at about 163:14. This estimate is remarkably close since depress will actually happen at 163:18.]

a15a16241xx.speaker: Henize
a15a16241xx.text: Okay. Everybody down here thinks that's a - a great philosophy. Good. [Long pause.]

a15a16241xx.speaker: Worden
a15a16241xx.text: And, Houston; Endeavour. There were a couple of questions on the Flight Plan. I guess I'm wondering what we're going to do about the Mass Spec[trometer] today. We've got some things in here. Of course, we didn't use it last night, so there are, I guess, a few steps that you're to delete.

a15a16241xx.speaker: Henize
a15a16241xx.text: Righto. We don't intend to use the Mass Spec. today so you can delete these particular steps about retracting, or about extending the boom, et cetera . We just are not - That was it. Delete any action on the Mass Spec.

a15_1622345csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1622345csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. As you go around the corner, all your systems look to be in good shape.

a15_1622345csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1622345csm.text: Roger, Houston. See you at the other side.

a15a1625947.speaker: Irwin
a15a1625947.text: Okay, we should drop that back as far as we possibly can. (Garbled) (Pause) [They may be getting the water hose out of the way.]

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: That's going to come out with the ETB. (Garbled) (Pause) Okay. "Descent Water Valve, Closed."

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Okay, "position the mikes". And "helmet and glove donning. PLSS Fan to On, to the right. And vent flags should clear." Mine clears.

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: "Don helmets and LEVAs , check the drink bag position." Okay, let me get yours here. (Pause) Is that aligned?

a15a1625947.speaker: Irwin
a15a1625947.text: Yeah. It's aligned. (Long Pause) [We can hear the locks close on Jim's helmet. A detail from training photo 71-HC-724 shows Jim's drink valve.]

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: There we go. Closed and locked. (Pause) Okay, LEVA's locked. (Pause) Front flap secure. Okay. You're locked. (Long Pause) [Next, Jim gets Dave into his helmet.]

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Okay. "Secure tool harness self-doff straps to LEVAs." Okay, let me get yours. (Pause) There's the right one. (Pause) Left one. Okay. (Long Pause) Okay.

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Yeah. Okay. Let's see if you can get back in your corner. (Pause)

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: "Disconnect the LM water hose. Connect the PLSS water hose." Okay, in work. (Long Pause)

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Okay. Mine's connected and locked. Says, "Connect PLSS ...Okay, stow LM hoses." (Long Pause) I'll have to wait until you turn around here. (Long Pause)

a15a1625947.speaker: Irwin
a15a1625947.text: Getting them back as far as you can?

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Okay, verify the following...Turn around, and we'll check all that stuff. (Pause) Okay.

a15a1625947.speaker: Irwin
a15a1625947.text: Okay, Dave. I'll read to you, okay?

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Okay, they're aligned and adjusted and locked.

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Okay. Locked. Yeah, and that one's locked and the bootie's on. That one's locked and the bootie's on.

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Vertical. (Pause) Okay, "helmet and visor, aligned and adjusted."

a15a1625947.speaker: Irwin
a15a1625947.text: They're locked. Let me get the bootie around...(Pause) Got booties on all those connectors.

a15a1625947.speaker: Irwin
a15a1625947.text: Okay, you're locked. And it's vertical.

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Okay, "verify EVA CB configuration." And then, okay, put on the gloves. (Long Pause) Here's your other glove over here on your left, Jim.

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Fell down. (Long Pause) [It is not clear what fell; but, whatever it was, it didn't slow them down. The glove-donning procedures are on Surface 9-6.]

a15a1625947.speaker: Irwin
a15a1625947.text: Okay, my circuit breakers are verified.

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: And mine are verified. [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I do not think we ever hit any circuit breakers during the operation."] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "Yes, that's right. I do not think we ever did. Every time we checked them, they were configured right."]

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Yeah. [Glove donning is probably the trickiest of all the EVA Preps, particularly getting the wristrings on the second glove locked. In listening to this, I thought that Jim might have been saying that this was a "final test" of their glove donning prowess.] [Scott, from a 1996 letter - "Not really. Jim is probably referring to our sore fingers and the final test on how they will feel and function. Glove donning took some effort, but was not really 'tricky'."] [Comm Break]

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: (Intent on his own gloves) Stand by. (Long Pause) And mine are locked.

a15a1625947.speaker: Allen
a15a1625947.text: Dave, this is Houston. How do those gloves feel today? 163:11:04 Scott: (Laughing) Gee, I don't know how to answer that, Joe. Sure be nice when I get through with the drill and I can take off the overgloves. [This statement indicates that Dave has been wearing a fingerless overglove - like a golf glove - to protect the palm of his EVA glove from excessive dust abrasion. Post-mission pictures of one of Gene Cernan's cover gloves show the great amount of wear than can occur in a relatively short amount of time. Dave is eager to get them off because they add bulk to his hands and restrict movemen

a15a1625947.speaker: Allen
a15a1625947.text: Roger. Wondered if you're going to shoot a little pool today with Colorado Fats, there.

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Joe, today's the day for a little pool.

a15a1625947.speaker: Allen
a15a1625947.text: I was thinking the same thing. [Joe is having fun in this reference to the Jackie Gleason/Paul Newman film The Hustler . See the discussion following 139:43:46 . "Colorado Fats" is, of course, Jim, who had taken up residence in Colorado Springs before joining the Astronaut Corps and who returned there after his retirement from NASA.]

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Okay, let's verify the locks and the gloves.

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Okay, yours are locked, and locked. Okay. Put the covers over. (Long Pause) Okay, "PLSS Diverter on Min, verify." (Pause) Your PLSS Diverter on MIN, Jim?

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: (Checking his own) Okay, verify. "PLSS Pump, On, to the right."

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: " Press Reg A and B to Egress ."

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: Okay. With the PLSS O2 On, we'll do a pressure integrity check. (If I can) find that little valve down there.

a15a1625947.speaker: Irwin
a15a1625947.text: And my O2 is coming on.

a15a1625947.speaker: Scott
a15a1625947.text: And my O2 is on. And "the press flag should clear 3.1 to 3.4. Cuff gauge should come up 3.7 to 4.0." (Pause) And I'm coming up. (Long Pause) Okay, I'm off the peg. (Pause)

a15_1631401csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1631401csm.text: Endeavour, we'd like to have Narrow Beam on the High Gain [Antenna]. [Long pause.]

a15_1631401csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1631401csm.text: Okay. I'm coming. Here we go 3.6, 7, 8. (Pause) Okay, I'm stabilized. My O2 flag is clear. If you can get a hold of that little valve again, let's turn them off and get an integrity check.

a15_1631401csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1631401csm.text: Very good, Al. You're coming through loud and clear. What's new up there?

a15_1631401csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1631401csm.text: Oh, I've just had a very nice breakfast and getting ready for today's activities.

a15_1631401csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1631401csm.text: And, Houston marks one minute, and you have got good pumps.

a15_1631401csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1631401csm.text: Okay, thank you, Joe. Give us a call after your minute. (Long Pause)

a15_1631401csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1631401csm.text: Our major business on this rev is to get squared away for [the] plane change [burn] and as soon as we have good comm, I want to review with you the changes we need in your SPS burn cue card. [Pause.]

a15_1631704csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1631704csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. I guess we can go ahead with the plane change data anytime you're ready to copy.

a15_1631704csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1631704csm.text: Okay. And then the "forward dump valve Open, then Auto at 3-1/2."

a15_1631704csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1631704csm.text: Okay, standby. (Pause) [Jim was facing aft as he changed the ECS controls and now has to turn to get the dump valve on the forward hatch.]

a15_1631704csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1631704csm.text: Let's start out with the cue - with the cue card, if that's okay with you. [Long pause.]

a15_1631704csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1631704csm.text: Okay, I've got my eyeball on the pressure gauge, go ahead.

a15_1631704csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1631704csm.text: Okay. "Verify cuff gauge doesn't drop below 4.6. I'm looking at 5.1".

a15_1631704csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1631704csm.text: "LM suit (circuit) pressure locked up at 4.5." Okay. Something about (starting) the watch . (Pause) And "overhead (or) forward dump valve to Open." 163:18:09 Irwin: Okay. I'm going Open. It's Open. [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I don't remember exactly what time it was (that they did the depress), but we were letting Houston keep track of the time. I think it would be good to have some sort of procedure for what time we could expect the various events to be occurring. We did the checklist on Houston time (actually, planned mission-elapsed-time) so we could have something to refer

a15_1631704csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1631704csm.text: Okey-doke. As you know, this burn is going to be [a] fairly normal burn on bank B only. The only really special thing to remember is to close that SPS Pilot Valve Main B [circuit breaker] at 2 minutes before the burn. To make sure that we've got all the verifications and everything else straight though, let's go back into the cue card and do some verifying right after you cycle the cryo fans and before you go into your Delta-V check. And at that point, we've got, first of all, EMS Function, Off. Verify that before you put in the EMS breakers. Second is the circuit breakers, EMS Main A and B, b

a15a1631811.speaker: Scott
a15a1631811.text: Okay. "Stand by for a tone and the water flag at 1.2 to 1.7." Cabin is down to about 2.2. (Long Pause) Are you coming back around?

a15a1631811.speaker: Irwin
a15a1631811.text: No. Don't think I will, not right now.

a15a1631811.speaker: Scott
a15a1631811.text: Yeah. Why don't you wait until we get this down a little bit. Cabin is still 1.0.

a15a1631811.speaker: Irwin
a15a1631811.text: Okay, I have a water flag. [Jim's sensor system is telling him that he hasn't turned on his PLSS feedwater.]

a15a1631811.speaker: Scott
a15a1631811.text: Okay. (Pause) 0.5 on the cabin. (Long Pause) Okay. If you can move forward, Jim, I can get back in here and...

a15a1631811.speaker: Worden (continued)
a15a1631811.text: ...I understand. Yeah. The SPS burn is going to be a nominal bank B burn - bank B only burn. But to get set up for it, we want to check - after cycle cryo fans, check that EMS is Off, get the two EMS circuit breakers in, check that the Group 5 circuit breakers are Closed, and check that the SPS Pilot Valves both are Open at that time. And then down where it says 'CB Stability Control, panel 8, and SPS 10 or 12', we'll make that a 10.

a15a1631811.speaker: Scott
a15a1631811.text: Good. I'll get in mine. (Long Pause) [Jim is wedged in the far right corner against the front of the ECS cabinet and Dave is at the far left. This configuration will give Dave the most room to lean down to get the handle on the hatch .]

a15a1631811.speaker: Henize
a15a1631811.text: Roger. And then over there on the back of the card - [pause] Would you give us High Gain, Auto, right now, Al?

a15a1631811.speaker: Irwin
a15a1631811.text: Make it? [Jim is asking if Dave can get the hatch open against the remaining pressure.]

a15a1631811.speaker: Scott
a15a1631811.text: Nope. Not yet. (Long Pause) Okay, I'm going to let the cabin go down some more. (Long Pause) Okay, I'm going to try it again here. (Pause) There we go.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay. (Pause) 163:22:27 Scott: Oh, wait a minute. You've got to leave it in Open. The card's all arranged different here.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: (Garbled)

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yeah. Sorry about that.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Houston confirms. Leave it open.

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Rog; understand. In the cleanup, about where CB SPS Pitch 1 and Yaw 1 are Open, we'll pull CB SPS Pilot Valve Main B, Open, and CB EMS, two, Open.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yeah, Rog. Okay, now, "PLSS Primary Water to Open".

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: That's correct. And that - assuming that your cue card was clean to start with, that should give you a - a good cue card, not only for the plane change but also for any rescue maneuvers and also for the shaping burn.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: (Grunting as he reaches back) That's in work.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Rog; understand.

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: I have - [pause] and, I have - the comments here on trimming your residuals, if you're ready to copy those.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay, mine's Open.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Mine's Open. Okay, "H2O flag should clear in 2 to 4 minutes." [Comm Break]

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Okay. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: Okay. LOPC [Lunar Orbit Plane Change] residuals. First of all, trim V GY to 0. - 0.2 feet per second. Next, and this is because our quad C RCS is low and we're trying to conserve it, in - in the trimming. If you have a negative V GY , roll 90 degrees counter-clockwise and use your minus-Z thrusters. If you have a positive V GY , roll 90 degrees clockwise, and use your minus-Z thrusters. And, one final comment here is during - during the burn, we would like to keep the Oxidizer Flow Valve in the Decrease - Decrease position. [Pause.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay, my water flag's clear.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Mine is too. (Long Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Understand you want the Oxidizer Flow Valve in the Decrease position.

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: Affirmative. [Pause.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay; "verify PGA 3.7 to 4.6"; and mine's at about 4.2.

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: And did everything come through on the trim.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay, mine's 4.1.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay, caution lamps (to be checked) are PREAMPS and ECS. (Pause) H2O Sep(arator) Component Light's on. "Lower EV visor." On we go. [They have now finished with the EVA Prep & Post Card and will start to use cuff checklist pages LMP-23 and CDR-24.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Roger, Karl. You - you wanted to add to - to the - trim rules that we already have established for the plane change. That if the residual is a plus V GY greater than two tenths of a foot per second, then we roll clockwise 90 degrees and use the minus-Z thrusters. Otherwise the same as printed in the Flight Plan.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: How's the PLSS look to you down there, Houston?

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: They both look good, Hadley Base. And, Dave, you can have your (PLSS feedwater) diverter valve.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Oh, thank you, Joe. Okay, Jim, I'm going to get over here and open the door.

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: That's affirmative, Al.

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: And also, you want the PUGS valve in decrease.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: That's affirmative. And the next - the next bit of information I have for you is the plane change PAD. [Long pause.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Can you see what I'm hung on, Jim?

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Just a minute.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: And, Jim, diverter valve is yours as well.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: We'll switch here. (Responding to Joe) Okay, standby. Let's see if I can turn around here, Dave.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Okay, go ahead.

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: Okay. Purpose, PC [Plane Change], SPS/G&N; 37202; plus 0.33, plus 1.07; 165:11:31.96; minus 0009.2, plus 0330.3, plus 0018.4; 0 roll, 0 pitch, 0 yaw; 064.4 - Say that again for H A . 0064.4, H P is plus 0053.3; 0330.9, 0:18, 0319.1; 36, 012.8, 39.2; the rest is NA. Set stars are Deneb and Vega; 189, 256, 330. Ullage, we would like two quads, B and D quads; 17 seconds, 17 seconds. And that's all.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Back behind me?

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Say again.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: If you can turn right, I'm turning left.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay. That's right. Doesn't matter. (Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: (Garbled) turn that way. Try the other way. (Pause) Am I pushing against you?

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yeah. You sure are. (Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: I'll have to turn the other way then.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: No, go back in your corner. Maybe I'm unhooked now. Are you back in your corner?

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Yeah. I'm back here as far as I can.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay. I'm clear. Open the door. Oop. Door won't open all the way.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Hitting my foot, I guess.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yeah. (Pause) It's hitting your PLSS!

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Stand up a little bit here.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: There, okay.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Before you go out though, let me turn around so I can watch you.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Jones - "Jim must be facing the bulkhead with his body in the corner between the outside bulkhead and the ECS and his PLSS out in cabin. Sort of like a kid who's been bad, standing in the corner. This is the only clear statement in Apollo as to whether an LMP 'standing in his corner' has his face to the wall or his PLSS to the wall."]

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: How are you doing?

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Oh, I'm okay. Where are you?

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Oh, I've just got my feet out.

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Okay, understand. This is plane change 1; SPS/G&N; 37202; plus 0.33, plus 1.07; 165:11:31.96; minus 0009.2, plus 0330.3, plus 0018.4; roll, pitch, and yaw are all zeros; 0064.4, plus 0053.3; 0330.9, 0:18, 0319.1; 36, 012.8, 39.2. Vega and Deneb are set stars. And 189, 256, 330. Ullage is two jet, 17 seconds, using quads B and D.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay, let me turn around then.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Well, I'm not sure you can. I'm going out. I'm all right. Then you can turn around easier when I get to where you get my (PLSS/OPS) antenna .

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Oh, okay. I'll just stay over here in the corner then.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: In fact, if you want, Dave...Shoot, I'll get your (PLSS/OPS) antenna when we get down to the surface.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yeah. (Chuckles) There. Okay; I'm out.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay, I'm going to turn around. (Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: That's all correct. [Long pause.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: You might...See the little cover on the outside hatch handle? You might cover that; it's open.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay. (Pause) Just stay there on the porch until I get all the gear out to you.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Oh, yeah.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Like the jett bag and...

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) How you doing? Go easy. (Pause) [Jim has probably closed the hatch partially so that he can get over to Dave's side of the cabin and open the hatch fully.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: Al, we'd like to verify that the Oxidizer Flow Valve was in the Decrease position at the end of the last burn and has been there since then.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Doggone comm cord of yours was hung up on me.

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Negative, Karl. It was in Normal at the end of the last burn, which was the circularization burn and it was - it's been in Normal since then. It's in Decrease now; I put it there after you called it out on the PAD.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Oh. (Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay, ... jett bag.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Jim, this is Houston. Could you verify for us, please, that one of the two dump valves is Open?

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: Thank you, Al. [Long pause.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Yeah, the forward one is Open, Joe.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Sounds good, Jim. Thank you. [Houston wants to make sure that, if the door were to fully close and gas of some sort were released into the cabin, the gas would be able to vent. In principle, the crew could operate the dump valve from outside; but this simple check reduces the chance virtually to zero of problems later on.] [Scott, from a 1996 letter - "Actually, the forward dump valve would not have been difficult to open from the outside on the porch. We probably tried it in the one-sixth-g airplane. It would have been much more difficult to open the top hatch dump valve from the outside!!"]

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay. Send her out.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Send that and then I'll get you the ETB.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: It's the world's biggest jett bag . (Long Pause) [Dave probably drops the jett bag over the right porch rail, the side away from the MESA.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: Just a reminder, Al. Since I've been reading a lot of things to you, about the Pan Camera Mode, Standby; Power, On.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Standing by with the ETB there, Dave?

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yeah, standing right by. 163:31:20 Allen: And, Dave, while you're waiting. A word about the polarimetric filter. We are going to ask you to pick that up from the MESA and put it on your camera from the very first. We've got a dandy spot for you to do some polarimetric photographs later on. [A series of photographs taken with and without the polarimetric filter had been planned for the end of EVA-1, as per CDR-26 and 27. Because of the drilling problems, those activities were dropped.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Rog. It's there now.

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: And I have a TEI-52 PAD anytime you're ready to copy. [Long pause.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: All righty. (Pause) Okay, I'm heading down, Jim.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: I don't see the LEC out there. Where is it; down on the surface?

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Okay, go ahead.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: No; it's over here on the right.

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: TEI-52, SPS/G&N; 36003; plus 0.60, plus 1.07; 180:31:51.88; plus 3030.0, minus 0893.9, minus 0231.0; 180, 088, 346; the rest is NA. We have two jets for 17 seconds with the B and D quads, Bravo and Delta quads. The Lambda at T IG is plus 177.77; and it is assumes LOPC; and ascent REFSMMAT.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay; listen, when you get down, Dave, remember that LCRU battery is in that footpad.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Rog!

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Good thinking, Jim.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: As soon as you get down, I'll come down, I'll getyour ( PLSS/OPS antenna ).

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Oh, it's in the checklist somewhere.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Sure. (Pause) Okay; if you're clear, I'll come down.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yep. Clear.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Ohh! It's nice to be outside where you can stretch a little bit. (Long Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Rog; understand. TEI-52, SPS/G&N; 36003; plus 0.60, plus 1.07; 180:31:51.88; plus 3030.0, minus 0893.9, minus 0231.0; 180, 088, 346; 2 jet, 17 seconds, using quads B and D. And Lambda T IG is plus 177.77; and the PAD assumes the plane change and asc - ascent REFSMMAT.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay, the hatch is closed, Joe.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Okay, Jim. Thank you. (Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: And, Joe, the LCRU Power is going to Internal now.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Okay, Dave. And could you check the LRV batt covers closed at the same time?

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: No, they're open and I will close them now.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Rog. Those automatic devices fail us every now and then.

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: Did you get the LCRU battery already, Dave?

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: No, I haven't. (Pause) You're supposed to get that (as per LMP-23).

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: Yeah. I know it. That's why I reminded you of it being down here.

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Reminded me of what?

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: It was in this ( plus-Z ) footpad instead of the plus-Y .

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Oh, okay. (Pause)

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: Might be a little dirty.

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Really? Brush it off. (Long Pause) [ Fendell pans left, raises the camera, and finds Dave at his seat emptying the ETB as per CDR-25. The "P.O. Package" mentioned in the checklist is the postage-stamp cancellation kit he will use at the end of the EVA. Jim is at the back of the Rover.]

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Okay, Houston. Into the CDR's footpan goes Mag Union. (Long Pause) And we got (only) a little bit on November, so we brought that along. (Pause) Get organized here. (Pause) The LMP's camera with Tango.

a15a1633446.speaker: Allen
a15a1633446.text: Roger. (Pause) [Dave reaches across and puts the LMP camera on Jim's seat.]

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: CDR's camera with Sierra. (Pause) Mag Romeo. (Pause) And Mag Whiskey, which I'll put on the 500. (Long Pause) [Comm Break] [Dave removes the dark slide from Mag Whiskey, gets the 500-mm camera out from under his seat, and installs the magazine.] [Scott - "The camera was one of the best geologic sampling tools we had. Learn more geology from one photo than almost any other one thing we got, except maybe a really good rock."] Video Clip 3 min 13 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPG )

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: And I'll check it out. (Long Pause) [Dave turns to the north and appears to take a picture with the 500. There is, however, no such picture in the Apollo collection. The usual procedure was to expose two frames after installing a magazine and these were, of course, badly sunstruck.]

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: And it's all right. (Long Pause) [Dave puts the lens cap on the 500 and puts the camera under his seat.]

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: Okay, Joe. I have a BSLSS bag out (as per LMP-24).

a15a1633446.speaker: Allen
a15a1633446.text: Okay, Jim. And, Dave and Jim, we'll lose comm here perhaps. However, we'll get it back when the battery's changed, so don't worry.

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Okay. Understand, Joe. And into the ETB go 16-millimeter Hotel, Juliett, and Golf. (Pause) [Dave has mis-spoken. He is actually taking the 16-mm mags out of the ETB and putting them under his seat.]

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: (Mag) Item. And we'll put Foxtrot on the camera. (Long Pause) [After Dave finishes with the 16-mm magazines, he puts what may be the stamp-cancellation kit on his seat and takes the EVA-3 maps out of the ETB.] 163:40:40 Irwin: Dave, I'm going to stand up on the Rover. Get the BSLSS (Buddy Secondary Life-Support System) bag locked. [Jim is attaching the BSLSS bag to the forward surface of the geopallet as per LMP-24. The BSLSS is a set of hoses and fittings that would allow Dave and Jim to share cooling water in the event that one of them had a cooling system failure.] [Scott - "All this work o

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Oh, here. Maybe I can reach it, Jim. Let me try it, Jim...

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: ...My arms are longer. Just a second.

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: (Garbled)

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: Okay. (Pause) Video Clip 2 min 29 sec ( 0.6 Mb RealVideo or 22 Mb MPG )

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: I'll give you your maps so you can put them on. (Pause) [Dave takes the ETB and the maps around the front of the Rover to Jim's seat. During the following, Dave and Jim are just off-camera to the left.]

a15a1633446.speaker: Allen
a15a1633446.text: Dave, a reminder to pick up the polarimetric filter when you're at the MESA. [At 163:31:20 , Joe told Dave that they wanted him to put the polarization filter on his camera. At 164:01:09 , Dave will report that the filter won't fit over the lens.]

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Thank you, Joe. (Pause) See if I can get...down a little bit.

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: It's hard to get into the lock, Dave. I think if you have any difficulty just let me stand up. I can lean over and get it. (Pause) Down. We have to swing that lock on the left side forward to lock it in there. (Pause)

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Oh, yeah. (Pause) I'm not sure you're going to get to that at all.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1634151csm.text: Endeavour, a reminder on the Gamma-ray Gain Step. We need the Shield, Off, at this point.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634151csm.text: I could get it if I could stand up and lean over. 163:42:00 Scott: You can try. Be careful. (Long Pause) [Journal Contributor John Pfannerstill notes that, at this point, Dave affixes the LRV commemorative sign to the righthand side of the console, smoothing it down several times with the back of his glove. Jim will take two photos of the sign at 163:58:27 . Dave leaves the field-of-view to the left, probably going to the MESA.] [Fendell pans right.]

a15a1634559.speaker: Scott
a15a1634559.text: Okay, Joe, I'm going to change the LCRU battery .

a15a1634559.speaker: Scott
a15a1634559.text: Okay, ( LCRU ) power's going (Off). [TV off.] [Motion picture film shot during training shows Dave installing a LCRU battery.]

a15a1634559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1634559.text: Joe, we have bag 7 on the left-hand side of the tool carrier and bag 2 on the right side.

a15a1634559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1634559.text: And I'm wondering whether we should leave...

a15a1634559.speaker: Allen
a15a1634559.text: ...if it's easy to do just keep bag 2 under the seat and follow your checklist normally. Bag 2 is just an extra bag for us. (Long Pause) [Cuff checklist page LMP-24 indicates that they had planned to have bags 7 and 8 on the back of the Rover.]

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1634637csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. We have one small change in our set-up for the plane change burn, and that is that we would like to leave the Oxidaze - Oxidizer Utilization Valve [means Oxidizer Flow Valve, on panel 3 of the Main Display Console and part of the Propellant Utilization Gauging System (PUGS)] on - in the Normal position. We'd like it Normal instead of Decrease as we previously told you. [Pause.]

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634637csm.text: We still have some tools in bag 2, Dave. I'll just leave that bag there and put our last collection bag under my seat.

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634637csm.text: Okay. Why don't you tell them when they come back up here.

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1634637csm.text: Dave and Jim, do you read Houston? (No answer)

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1634637csm.text: Okay, going Normal on the PUGS Valve.

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634637csm.text: Okay, LCRU (power) is on Internal. Blankets are 100 percent open. (Long Pause)

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1634637csm.text: Roger; and the boys on the surface have the TV tuned up for us now and we're getting some lovely landscape pictures - Hadley Delta, et cetera . Those hills there are just beautiful, round, bare hills, a lot like the ones you see around San Francisco. It's a beautiful sight. They're just about loading up the Rover and getting ready to head off toward the South Com[plex] - first of all, to the rille for a quick visit and then off to the South Complex.

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634637csm.text: Get new sample collection bags for us, Jim?

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634637csm.text: Yeah, I (garbled under Joe) Video Clip 2 min 50 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPG )

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1634637csm.text: . ...is Houston. We prefer bag 2 under your seat shelf and bag 7 on the Hand Tool Carrier, instead. [TV on. Jim is at his seat.]

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1634637csm.text: Rog, Karl; understand. Did you say they are going to cut it a little bit short today?

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634637csm.text: Well, bag 7 is Dave's bag. It's on the left side. It's just a question of which one you want on the right side. In other words, which one do you want on me? [Jim has gone to the back of the Rover.]

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1634637csm.text: Right. They're going to cut it between one and two hours short because they got in - they wanted to get their normal sleep today; and, I guess they won't do quite so much exploration in between, but they still expect to get to the South Complex. Pardon me, that's the North Complex.

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1634637csm.text: Jim, bag 8 on the right side, please. And that's a new bag.

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634637csm.text: Okay, and you want bag 2 under the seat?

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1634637csm.text: That's right, exactly. And then we can follow the checklist exactly from here on in.

a15_1635906csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1635906csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. It's time to turn off the Mapping Camera.

a15_1640205csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1640205csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. If you'll go P00 now, you'll have a shorter maneuver down in your maneuver to the P52 attitude. And, if you'll give us Accept, we'll send up state vector and other burn information.

a15_1640205csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640205csm.text: No, you couldn't. It's not going to help any, Jim. 164:02:07 Irwin: Dave, I've got the lens brush here, if you want me to clean your lens.

a15_1640205csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640205csm.text: Yeah. (Pause) [Dave turns to face Jim and presents his Hasselblad lens.]

a15_1640205csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1640205csm.text: Okay. (Pause) [Dave takes the brush and cleans Jim's lens.]

a15_1640205csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1640205csm.text: Okay, Karl. You've got it; P00 and Accept.

a15a1640355.speaker: Allen
a15a1640355.text: Dave, when you get out to the (ALSEP) site, if you'll park down-Sun, we'll give you (the) Nav alignment when you get ready to go. (Pause)

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: And we're rolling.

a15a1640355.speaker: Allen
a15a1640355.text: Roger. (Pause)

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: Everything's working today. [This is a reference to the fact that the front steering did not work during EVA-1.]

a15a1640355.speaker: Allen
a15a1640355.text: Beautiful, Dave. And did you copy "park down-Sun, give us the readings, and we'll align the Nav system when you press on towards Station 9."

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: Okay. I understand, Joe. (Long Pause) 164:05:02 Allen: Dave, while you're driving, there, we're going to want you to take apart our core stems. We'll have Jim pack them away in bag 2, which is under his seat, and then we'll do the Grand Prix photographs before we start driving off toward Station 9.

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: Okay. Understand. (Long Pause) Oop. (Pause) Wait a minute, Jimmy, let me...I'm going to back up a minute, Jim. Okay?

a15a1640355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1640355.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: Never saw that before, huh?

a15a1640355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1640355.text: Kind of bogged down, isn't it?

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: Sure is. I never saw it do that. (Pause) Oh, I know why. Nope. (Pause)

a15a1640355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1640355.text: Okay. You're moving forward.

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: Okay. Oop.

a15a1640355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1640355.text: Kind of dug in there!

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: Yeah, it sure did, didn't it? Never seen that happen. Trusty old Rover. [The Rover is light enough that, if it did get stuck, Dave and Jim could simply lift it out of trouble.]

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: Get us going down-Sun here, so I can get those Nav readings. (Pause) Still got to get in position, so I can do my tricks with the drill. (Long Pause) Okay, Joe. I'm push in the Nav circuit breaker. And the Sun-shadow device is reading about one-half to the left, pitch is reading about 2 down, and roll...Jim, let go back there a minute...Roll is reading 2 left. 164:07:35 Allen: Copy, Dave. (Pause)

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: Okay. I'm going to need you to help me get this treadle up to the front, Jim.

a15a1640355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1640355.text: Okay. [Jim is taking pieces of equipment out of SCB-2 at his seat.]

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: Bring the whole bag back here, so I can work it.

a15a1640355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1640355.text: Oh, okay.

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: Just bring the bag back here, and I'll just work it like I usually do. You can be doing something useful, instead of just standing.

a15a1640355.speaker: Allen
a15a1640355.text: Jim, we need pictures of your beautiful trench there and the collapsed wall. And we'd like, I guess, a photo pan around this remarkable core hole. [Jim takes the bag to the back of the Rover and takes up a position behind Dave's right shoulder.]

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: (To Jim) Here. Come on; bring it on over here, Jim. [Dave motions toward the other side the geopallet, behind the CDR seat.]

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: Jim, bring it on over here.

a15a1640355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1640355.text: Yeah. [Jim goes off-camera to our right.]

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: Joe, just stand by until we get this settled down, and then we'll come at you for what is the next task.

a15a1640355.speaker: Allen
a15a1640355.text: Okay.

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: (To Joe) You're going to have to just hold off on jumping ahead of us, because we always have to come back and ask you what you said anyway. (To Jim) Okay...

a15a1640355.speaker: Allen
a15a1640355.text: Read you loud and clear.

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: ...Jim, if I could get you to help me take the treadle off.

a15a1640355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1640355.text: Okay. [This public show of irritation is remarkable for Dave and indicates the level of frustration that he is feeling.] [Throughout the extraction, Joe made only a few short transmissions, undoubtedly to avoid disturbing Dave and Jim's concentration. His quick response to Dave suggestion at 164:18:55 that Jim find 'something useful" to do indicates that he had a list of proposed tasks waiting. However, when he realized Dave's level of frustration and that Dave still needed Jim's help, he backed off with an immediate 'Read you lound and clear'.] [After putting SCB-2 on the back of the Rover to

a15a1640355.speaker: Scott
a15a1640355.text: So, if you'll get on the other side, we can jiggle it and move it up towards the drill. QuickTime Clip (1 min 38 sec) by Peter Dayton

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1640738csm.text: Al, the computer is yours; you've got a state vector, a target, and a REFSMMAT.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640738csm.text: Okay. Now to the drill. (Pause) We last left our friend...

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1640738csm.text: Okay, Karl; thank you. [Pause.]

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1640738csm.text: Now it's "our" friend, huh?

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1640738csm.text: And, Houston; Endeavour. I've got the SIM bay powered down now, and turning back all the jets - turning on all the jets.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640738csm.text: Yes, it is. And if you could...(Let me) see, if I can...

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1640738csm.text: Okay. Check me out on it.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640738csm.text: Well...

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1640738csm.text: Roger, Al; we understand.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1640738csm.text: What should I do there? (Pause)

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640738csm.text: Ahh! The object is to pull it out of the ground. But I'm not sure we can do that without driving the drill.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1640738csm.text: I don't think so either. Why not just drive it a little bit to break it loose.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640738csm.text: It's broke loost (sic).

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1640738csm.text: Huh.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1640738csm.text: Dave and Jim, this is Houston...

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640738csm.text: (Lost under Joe) pulled it up yesterday.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1640738csm.text: Well, one of us get on one side...

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1640738csm.text: ...we're standing by for Rover powerdown and TV remote.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640738csm.text: Okay, Joe. I didn't know you wanted the TV out here, too. (Long Pause) Okay. TV. (Brief Static) Okay, down-Sun position is a bad one for the old Earth, but I'll do it on the AGC. [Dave has to stand in front of the Rover to use the sighting scope and, since the Rover is headed west, he is looking back into the Sun. Before his next transmission, he probably glances down at the meter.]

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640738csm.text: Oh; you ought to have it, Joe.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1640738csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. You can expect us to give you a No - Go/No Go for LOI [means LOPC or lunar orbit plane change] before LOS. No, that's - that's right; that's a Go/No Go for plane change - pardon me, I'm a little bit behind time here - before LOS, and since - since your burn is so close to AOS, we'd like to give you a procedure here, so that we can lock up without your having to go over there to throw - to throw any switches. Can you copy it now?

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1640738csm.text: Okay. Thank you, Dave. Appreciate that. And by watching, maybe we can give you a few words of advice on this drill. 164:09:26 Irwin: Dave, I'm thinking, maybe if you get on one side, I'll get on the other. And maybe the two of us, by hooking an arm under that, can lift it out.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640738csm.text: Okay. Let's try it. [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "Each of us had a handle of the drill under the crook out our elbow, and we got it up to the point where we could put our shoulders under it."] 164:09:36 Irwin: Okay. You say when. 1, 2...

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640738csm.text: When.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1640738csm.text: ...3. 1, 2, 3. (Grunting on "3") A little bit. Video Clip 3 min 13 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPG ) [TV on. The camera is pointing down and does not move.]

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1640738csm.text: Let me get down a little bit. I'd like to get down and get a...

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640738csm.text: But it's got a long way to go.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1640738csm.text: Rog, Karl; go ahead.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1640738csm.text: Yeah. I know it. But if we break it loose...1, 2, 3. Okay. 1, 2, 3.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1640738csm.text: Okay. After LOS, we'd like to have you put the High Gain [Antenna] Track to Manual, and dial in Pitch, minus 10; Yaw, 251. When the high gain angle - when the High Gain Antenna [angle] meters read Pitch, minus 10 and Yaw, 251, then go to Track and Reacq with Narrow Beam. Then, if your Squelch is Off, your High Gain Antenna acquisition will be indicated at AOS by a loss of noise.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640738csm.text: Okay. That's enough. Hold it. I suspected as much. Joe, do you think...Looks to me like the only answer is going to be to back it off with the drill.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1640738csm.text: Roger. Let's do that.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640738csm.text: Okay. (Pause) Except that treadle is going to go.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1640738csm.text: Yeah, watch the treadle.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1640738csm.text: I know it.

a15_1640738csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1640738csm.text: Don't want me to push it (meaning the treadle)? Can I push it down and stand on it? (Pause)

a15_1641231csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1641231csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. You're Go for plane change 1.

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: Okay. I'm going to need you to help me get this treadle up to the front, Jim.

a15a1641844.speaker: Irwin
a15a1641844.text: Okay. [Jim is taking pieces of equipment out of SCB-2 at his seat.]

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: Bring the whole bag back here, so I can work it.

a15a1641844.speaker: Irwin
a15a1641844.text: Oh, okay.

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: Just bring the bag back here, and I'll just work it like I usually do. You can be doing something useful, instead of just standing.

a15a1641844.speaker: Allen
a15a1641844.text: Jim, we need pictures of your beautiful trench there and the collapsed wall. And we'd like, I guess, a photo pan around this remarkable core hole. [Jim takes the bag to the back of the Rover and takes up a position behind Dave's right shoulder.]

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: (To Jim) Here. Come on; bring it on over here, Jim. [Dave motions toward the other side the geopallet, behind the CDR seat.]

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: Jim, bring it on over here.

a15a1641844.speaker: Irwin
a15a1641844.text: Yeah. [Jim goes off-camera to our right.]

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: Joe, just stand by until we get this settled down, and then we'll come at you for what is the next task.

a15a1641844.speaker: Allen
a15a1641844.text: Okay.

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: (To Joe) You're going to have to just hold off on jumping ahead of us, because we always have to come back and ask you what you said anyway. (To Jim) Okay...

a15a1641844.speaker: Allen
a15a1641844.text: Read you loud and clear.

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: ...Jim, if I could get you to help me take the treadle off.

a15a1641844.speaker: Irwin
a15a1641844.text: Okay. [This public show of irritation is remarkable for Dave and indicates the level of frustration that he is feeling.] [Throughout the extraction, Joe made only a few short transmissions, undoubtedly to avoid disturbing Dave and Jim's concentration. His quick response to Dave suggestion at 164:18:55 that Jim find 'something useful" to do indicates that he had a list of proposed tasks waiting. However, when he realized Dave's level of frustration and that Dave still needed Jim's help, he backed off with an immediate 'Read you lound and clear'.] [After putting SCB-2 on the back of the Rover to

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: So, if you'll get on the other side, we can jiggle it and move it up towards the drill. QuickTime Clip (1 min 38 sec) by Peter Dayton

a15a1641844.speaker: Irwin
a15a1641844.text: Okay. (Pause) [Jim comes around the drill and stands next to his seatback.]

a15a1641844.speaker: Irwin
a15a1641844.text: Okay. [Dave and Jim both take hold of the treadle and rotate it back and forth around the drill-stem axis, trying to work it up toward the chuck.]

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: You can't put any up or down on it. It's got to be sideways. (Not making any progress) Nah, that's...

a15a1641844.speaker: Irwin
a15a1641844.text: Let me try it. (Pause) It's locked on there, isn't it?

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: No, it shouldn't be. (Pause) (Frustrated) Boy.

a15a1641844.speaker: Irwin
a15a1641844.text: Uh...

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: Boy. (Pause) I tell you, we'll do it section by...If you could hold it up there, Jim. Hold it on the Hand Tool Carrier.

a15a1641844.speaker: Irwin
a15a1641844.text: Yeah. Let me get on the other end.

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: Let me hold it. You just twist the drill off.

a15a1641844.speaker: Irwin
a15a1641844.text: Okay. (Pause) [Dave moves to his right and holds the drill-string with both hands. Jim steps around to grab the drill handles in both hands.]

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: Okay, now. Just rotate the drill left. Atta boy. Just rotate it left. Easy does it. Easy does it. (Pause) Keep it straight if you can. There you go. One more. Just a little...Keep it straight. Ought to break in a little bit, here. (Pause) Hold it up. There. Now. (Pause) Ease it off. Easy does it. (Pause) [The drill comes loose and Jim takes it to his footpan.]

a15a1641844.speaker: Scott
a15a1641844.text: I got to take my camera off. Okay. Just hold (garbled) there [Dave takes his camera off to get it out of the way and takes it off-camera, around to his seat.]

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1642118csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. We're 2 minutes from LOS, and all of your systems look to be in excellent shape.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1642118csm.text: You want me to stand by here, Dave?

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Yeah. Just hold on while I...(Long Pause) [Dave returns to the back of the Rover.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Dave, how many more sections to come apart?

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: If you can get the wrench, I'll hold the treadle.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay. (To Joe, with clear annoyance) Oh, stand by, Joe. (Counting the remaining sections) We've got 1, 2, 3. 4.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Thank you. [Dave is probably annoyed because Houston should have been able to keep count.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Okay, I've got it there if you can...

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) (Grunting) Ahhh! (Pause) Nope, wrong way. (Long Pause) That doesn't look right either. Let's go the other way. Man, how did that treadle get like that? (Long Pause) [During the struggle to remove the treadle, Dave edges off-camera to the right.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: It's moving.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Yeah.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: It's broken.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: That's got it. (Pause) It's really jammed.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: See if I can get it out.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Work it out towards you, because of the cap. See what I mean?

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Yeah.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Take that...The end of your right hand should come through, while I work on the rest of them, here. (Pause) Okay. Foxtrot on the next section. Video Clip 3 min 07 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 27 Mb MPG )

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Roger. (Long Pause) [Dave is back in view and has put a cap on the top of the third section. He pulls the string out until the fourth section is seated in the vise. Dave starts turning the wrench but, without the treadle on the string, it is difficult to tell if he is getting any grip from the vise.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: If I had known (about) this, I would have left my cover gloves on, Dave.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Well, don't mess with it then. Don't mess your gloves up. I'll do it. [Evidently, Dave is still wearing his cover gloves.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Oh, they're okay. I'll take it.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: This vise just won't hold. There's something wrong with it. (Long Pause) The vise doesn't work, at all! (To Jim) I'll have to have you hold it, the...(Pause as Dave glances at the watch on his left wrist) How about that: an hour and 15 minutes into it (meaning the EVA) already. We're still fiddling with this thing. [Scott, from a 1996 letter - Ah ha! I did use the watch!! And I recall this.] [Dave arrived at the drill site at about 164:03:55 and, consequently, they have been working on the deep core for about 30 minutes.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Okay. The treadle's off.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Beautiful! (I'll) stick this (stem-section 2) in here (SCB-2). (Pause) Now, hold that section for me...

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Okay.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: ...(Like you) did before. (Pause) It's just not gripping. The...

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Dave and Jim, this is Houston.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Go ahead.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Roger, troops. What's your best guess?

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: (Under Joe) Try to bring that back that way, Dave?

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Do you think you can turn off the bottom-most drill section? [Dave takes the drill string off the back of the Rover and holds it up for Houston to see.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Joe, you can see on the TV. That's what we got. Now, the vise...(correcting himself) My hand wrench works okay. The one on the back of the Hand Tool Carrier doesn't seem to want to work for some reason. It may just be because of the threads on the stems. I just can't get them broken apart! And that's the main problem. The wrenches don't work. (Pause) [Dave puts the string back in the vise and resumes his efforts with the wrench.] 164:35:43 Allen: Dave and Jim, put that section on the ground, if you would, please. [Dave takes the drill string out of the vise without hesitation once he hears Hou

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: We'll pick it up on the way back. And we want you to continue on with the Grand Prix.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Good enough. Do that. [During the Grand Prix, Jim will stand facing northwest and take movie footage with the Data Acquisition Camera (DAC) while Dave drives through a pre-determined set of maneuvers. They had planned to do the Grand Prix at the end of EVA-2 and the relevant cuff checklist page is EVA-2/CDR-20 .]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Stick it in there, Dave. We might be able to return it (to Earth) just like that. Video Clip 1 min 00 sec ( 0.3 Mb RealVideo or 9 Mb MPG )

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Yeah, I think probably so. I don't know where we're going to put it in the Command Module. (Jim chuckles) I'll think of something. Let me see. (Looking around) Let me put it someplace where we don't ding it. There's no place to put it. I'll lay it right here on the treadle. (Pause) [Dave goes off-camera to the right. He is looking for a way to prop the string up so that he can see it easily when he arrives back at the site at the end of the traverse.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: I guess we ought to take it back (to Earth). There's more time invested in that than anything we've done. Okay. (To Jim) Get your (16-mm movie) camera. [Jim comes into view at the back of the Rover and goes to the LMP seat. Dave is at the back of the Rover.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Okay. Let's see. We don't want the drill on here. What do you want to do with the drill?

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Oh. Just leave it right here.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Put it on the surface here?

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) [Jim lifts the drill and merely turns so that he can put it down far enough out that Dave won't hit it when he starts driving. Jim then removes the 16-mm camera from the post next to his inboard handhold. He is going to use it for the Grand Prix.] [Jim is not wearing his Hasselblad. The DAC has a bracket mounted on the back which would allow Jim to mount the camera on his RCU. A high-resolution detail from 11471 ( 169k ) shows the bracket.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Got a good mag (on the 16-mm)? Why don't you check it out and see if it runs?

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: I did. I checked it out at 1 foot per second earlier.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: I'll give it a short burst here.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Good thinking, Jim. (Pause) Dave, while you're climbing on the Rover, we'll take...

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: High gain antenna is getting...

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: The meter readouts and your heading is 292. [TV off. At this time, Jim is still in view and is holding the DAC in his hands. We do not know if he filmed the Grand Prix while holding the DAC or with it mounted on his RCU.] 164:37:26. Scott: Okay. Joe, I never did any systems reset, but they were all sitting zero when I stopped here.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Good enough for me.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: PM1/WB . (Long Pause) Okay. Let's get our little handy...

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Okay. I have the (16-mm) camera set.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay. (Looking at EVA-2 CDR-20) The Sun should be over your right shoulder, so why don't you take a right turn there. You should be 45 degrees, looking up towards Schaber Hill over there. [ Schaber Hill is the high ground immediately north of Pluton Crater. In the Command Module view linked here, Schaber Hill and the North Complex are right of center. See the discussion following 146:49:02 .]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: You want to do a quick turn there so you don't get dust on my experiments.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Oh, sure. Watch out going backwards, Jim.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Ah, no sweat.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) [Dave hasn't started driving. Jim is probably walking backwards, which can be a good way to fall down.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: If you want, you can do a left turn there, Dave. And I'll move back a little more.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay. If I can get my seatbelt on. (Long Pause) Oh, my.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Dave, before you move out, you want to double-check your heading at 292.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay, Joe. (Long Pause) Torquing now. (Pause) Got a long way to go. (Pause) Make this torquing switch a set-and-hold switch, instead of spring loaded, would help! (Pause) Be with you in a minute, Jim. I've got to torque another 90 degrees or so.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: No rush.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Enjoy the scenery, Jimmy. (Pause)

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Yeah. I'm looking to find out where all the big rocks are.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Sounds good. And tell Dave once again that you don't want any dust on your experiments. (Jim laughs)

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Hey, Joe, you never did tell me that drill was that important. Just tell me that it's that important , and then I'll feel a lot better. (Pause)

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: It's that important, Dave.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay. Good. Because then I don't feel like I wasted so much time.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: No. Quite seriously, Dave and Jim, that's undoubtedly the deepest sample we'll have out of the Moon for perhaps as long as the Moon itself has been there. [Grant Heiken, who took the core apart almost grain by grain, has called it the most valuable sample returned from the Moon. It revealed 58 distinct layers of soil, a detailed record of a very complex sequence of local impact events that covered, overturned, and re-covered this particular section. A summary of results obtained from the deep core can be found in the discussion of samples 15001-006 in the Lunar Sample Compendium .]

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Well, that sounds good. a15a1654346.text: Oh, you're getting the bedrock here, huh?

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Yeah.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Okay. (Pause) I thought you were going to press on to the north.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Well, he said go get the bedrock, and I think we ought to try and get it if we can. Because this sure looks like a bedrock to me. I looked down the rille to the south, and it's just one great big massive layer of the same kind of fragmental debris on the order of meters (in size). Quite well-rounded.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Yeah, but the thing that bothers me, Dave, is look to the north there.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: (Turning to look) Yeah.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: And there's a flat area there, it looks like it might be the top of the bedrock.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Yeah.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: And those blocks seem to be slightly different.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Darker.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: They...

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: A little darker.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: ...almost have columnar jointing. (Pause) Look to the north there. [Jim may be describing an outcrop similar to the one on the west wall shown in AS15-89- 12115 and sketched in Figure 5-37 in the Apollo 15 Preliminary Science Report . The vertical fractures in the sketch are columnar joints.] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "The color (of the boulders) looked darker black. Those very large, almost rectangular, fractured rocks as you called them, looked a little bit like columnar jointing. Those big black ones down there were darker black than the ones we sampled."] [Irwin, from the 1

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Yeah, I see what you are talking about. Come on down here and let's get a frag off of one of these boulders and then we'll head on back to the Rover.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Okay. (Pause) [Dave moves to our right to find a boulder suitable for sampling.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Here's a good one. (Pause) Can you get the cross-Sun from over here, Jim?

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: On that side?

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Yeah. 165:46:17 Irwin: Okay. (Pause) [Jim's down-Sun is AS15-82- 11142 . He and Dave then trade places and, while Dave gets the hammer, Jim changes camera settings.] 165:46:28 Scott: Okay. (Pause) Don't rush with the pictures.

a15a1654346.speaker: Henize
a15a1654346.text: They say that looked like a real good stretch of exercise there, Al. Should stand you in good stead a couple of days from now.

a15a1654346.speaker: Worden
a15a1654346.text: Rog. I sure hope so, Karl; been keeping it up just for that reason.

a15a1654346.speaker: Henize
a15a1654346.text: Very good.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Yeah; stand by. [Dave moves around the north side of the boulder and scans the area farther from the Rover while he talks to Joe. In the meantime, Jim moves to his left and takes cross-Sun's from the north.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Worden
a15a1654346.text: And I think it makes a difference in - in your whole outlook and - the - restful way that you can do this flight, too. A little exercise and I get a good night's sleep also.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Hey, Joe, these rounded fragments down here - on the order of meters in size - expose some very large, oh, 2 (to) 3 centimeter vesicles rather than the finer stuff that Jim saw back there before. And I believe, when I take a chip out of this, we're going to find it's the same, kind-of-crystalline basalt. And they're all...Well, they're subangular; looks like they've been weathered (by tiny impacts). Fairly clean on the surface and all buried. And I can look down to the south, and it's just a whole mass of great big boulders along the terrace here. And there's another break-off down into the ri

a15a1654346.speaker: Henize
a15a1654346.text: Yep, you're probably right.

a15a1654346.speaker: Allen
a15a1654346.text: Amazing. [Dave turns toward the gnomon.] 165:47:24 Scott: You got the pictures yet?

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: I got the pictures.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Jim's cross-Sun stereopair is AS15-82- 11143 and 11144 . These excellent pictures have Hadley Rille in the background. Note the rounded corners and sizable vesicles on the boulders.] [Dave is standing on the rille side of the boulder and, while Jim gets a bag, Dave hits the rock five times at about waist height.] Video Clip 2 min 44 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 24 Mb MPG )

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Beautiful stuff. (Pause) [Dave delivers three deliberate, well-measured blows, apparently knocking off fragments. Rock sampling is an art and the fact that Dave doesn't have to hit boulder very often to dislodge samples indicates that he has learned where and how to hit. The flat, fist-sized sample he dislodged earlier in this stop is the mark of a skilled sampler. Only Jack Schmitt, a professional geologist, had an easier time with the hammer on very hard rocks like these.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Okay; I got them all located. Get a bag... [Dave gets his tongs.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Okay; 281.

a15a1654346.speaker: Allen
a15a1654346.text: Roger. [Dave puts the first fragment in the bag.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Okay. (Pause as Dave stares at the ground) Thought I had them located.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Right here, Dave. Right under my (scoop)...

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Yeah, that's right. Okay. (Long Pause) [Although it appears that Dave puts a second sample in the bag, he and Jim are about 55 meters from the Rover and it is difficult to make out exactly what they are doing. The fact that only two chips are listed in the Preliminary Science Report suggests that, here, he is adjusting the tongs. In either case, he decides to put the hammer on the rock so that he can examine the next fragment closely. He gets the fragment with the tongs, takes it in his left hand, plants the tongs, and then uses both hands to hold the sample while he examines it. The samples a

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Okay; this looks like a darker, fine-grained, black, vesicular basalt, with vesicles on the order of millimeters (which are) non-uniformly distributed. There are laths of plagioclase about 3 millimeters long, and it may be a half a millimeter wide, randomly-oriented throughout. And that's about the only other mineral I see. And that...Did you get the number on that, Jim?

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Yeah.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Okay.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: I gave it to them. [Journal Contributor Ron Rosano notes that, at this point, Dave raises his gold visor part way and leaves it up for about ten seconds. He is facing east, but has his head down and is not getting any direct Sun in his eyes.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: There's one other frag down here that fell - that I got. Let me get a couple of rounded ones here, too, that are just on the surface. Which I can't tell... [Dave picks up one of the rounded rocks and tries to knock some dust off.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: I can't tell what that is, but we'll put it in anyway, as representative of surface material; at least the fragmental surface. [Dave gets a second rounded rock and puts it directly in the bag. According the Bailey and Ulrich and the Preliminary Science Report , these samples are 15597 and 15598 , 146-gram and 136-gram pieces of olivine basalt.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Okay; why don't you zip that one? Here let me zip it, and you can take the "after" picture, Jim.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Okay. [Dave plants the tongs and Jim takes up a position north of the boulder.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Boy, it hurts not to have two cameras. Oh, well. (Pause) Ah; wait a minute. [Dave reaches for the hammer, which is still on the top of the boulder.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Cover up what I just did. 165:49:55 Irwin: Okay; I have it. [Jim's cross-Sun "afters" are AS15-82- 11145 and 11146 . In 11145 , Dave is reaching for the hammer. Note that Dave is not wearing a camera and that he is holding individual sample bag 281 in his left hand. We can see at least one rock fragment in the bag. In 11146 , Dave is picking up the hammer. We can see Jim's reflection in Dave's visor.] [In 11145, note that Dave has a cuff checklist on each arm. At 138:52:18 , before they started EVA-2 preps, CapCom Gordon Fullerton suggested that they each wear their EVA-1 cuff checklist on the

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Okay. (We) told them that was 281? Video Clip 3 min 10 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPG )

a15a1654346.speaker: Allen
a15a1654346.text: Roger; we copied. And, Dave, when you finish this, we'd like you to move back towards the Rover.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Yeah, I think we ought to do that. Need to stick the hammer on you. (Long Pause) [While Dave gets the hammer off the rock, Jim presents the left side of his PLSS.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Boy, what a rock.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: I just wonder if that rock to the north...

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Okay.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: ...up there is the same.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: I don't know but...

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Maybe we could stop there for the...

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Maybe you...

a15a1654346.text: ...stereo pan.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Yeah. [Dave grabs the gnomon and they head for the Rover.] [After they leave Station 9a, they will drive 400 meters north and take more photographs of the west wall of the rille from Station 10.
