a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Okay, let's head back to the Rover. QuickTime Clip (1 min 35 sec) by Peter Dayton

a15a1654346.speaker: Allen
a15a1654346.text: Right on, Dave...

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: And, Joe, I think...

a15a1654346.speaker: Allen
a15a1654346.text: ...and we want a rake sample near the Rover...

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: (To Jim) Did you take a location shot down to the south, Jim. [After five or ten meters, Dave stops and points south.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Allen
a15a1654346.text: ...and the soil sample with that... 165:50:49 Scott: Take a location shot down there...

a15a1654346.speaker: Allen
a15a1654346.text: ...and a double core, please.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: ...and then that way. Okay?

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Okay.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Yes. Get it at infinity; f/8 at infinity and maybe take another one up here, another 15 or 20 meters or so. Get a good stereo down to the south. (Long Pause) [Dave heads for the Rover while Jim takes AS15-82- 11147 . The group of rocks just to the right of center are at the upper left in 11146 . After about ten seconds, Jim is on his way, again moving much more slowly than Dave did. Evidently, he decided that he'd already gotten half of a stereopair in form of his cross-Sun pictures at the boulder.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: (To Houston) Hold until we get back to the Rover to talk about the rake sample, Joe. Because you'll just have to tell us again.

a15a1654346.speaker: Allen
a15a1654346.text: That's fine, Dave. Sure will. [Dave stops about halfway back to the Rover.] [In a 1996 letter, Dave was amused by the dialog covering the last few minutes.] [Scott, from a 1996 letter - "This section is a good example of the many opportunities we had at this location. a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Oooh! Oooh! You can see a boulder exposed to the surface here, which has got layering within it. It's been weathered away, apparently, and just the surface top is exposed; but the boulder must be, oh, about a meter long with 2- to 3-inch layers in it. [Dave starts uphill again but, after a couple of steps, stops and turns.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Would you get a picture of that where I stopped, Jim, just a quickie cross-Sun? See where that thing is exposed there? [Jim reaches the buried boulder. It took him about 55 seconds to climb up from the place where he took the picture toward the south. The same climb took Dave about 30 seconds.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Oh, yeah.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: See those little layers.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Beautiful.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Okay. I think a cross-Sun stereo would be neat right there.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Okay. 165:52:11 Scott: Here. As a matter of fact, I'll drop the gnomon; that'll tell them what it was. [Dave puts the gnomon down while Jim gets into position north of the buried boulder.] QuickTime Clip (1 min 24 sec) by Peter Dayton

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Just to get a real quick picture. Oh, you're kicking up white albedo.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Yeah. I know it.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: That's the only place I've seen it. (Pause) [Jim takes a cross-Sun, AS15-82- 11148 . Note that Dave did not get the color-gray scale gnomon leg pointed at the Sun.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Get a little closer, huh? (Pause) [This exchange and others previously suggest that, because Jim usually took the down-Sun pictures and Dave took the cross-Suns, he is out of practise in judging the proper distance for taking cross-Suns.] [Jim moves in about a meter and takes a stereopair, AS15-82- 11149 and 11150 , stepping to his left between frames.] 165:52:40 Irwin: Okay.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Good. [Dave grabs the gnomon and resumes the climb. Jim follows. They both use the loping stride, but Dave takes two steps for every one that Jim takes. Because Dave tends to cover ground about twice as fast as Jim does, it suggests that they are getting similar stride lengths.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Too bad we don't have time to pick some up, but we'll get probably pieces (in the rake sample). (Pause) Good footing. (Pause) [Dave reaches the Rover. He makes the trip from the buried rock in about 25 seconds. The same trip takes Jim about 40 seconds.] Video Clip 2 min 44 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 24 Mb MPG )

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Okay, Joe. Say again your rake requirements, if they're different from the others?

a15a1654346.speaker: Allen
a15a1654346.text: Negative. No different, Dave, just a few frags using the rake...

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Oh.

a15a1654346.speaker: Allen
a15a1654346.text: ...if you think it's reasonable. [Jim arrives at the Rover. Fendell pans left.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Yeah, I think there's probably good statistical samples to be had here. (Long Pause) Go, partner. Hey, why don't you hand me the camera? Oh, that's right.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Okay, yeah I will. And you can take the pictures...

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Yeah.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: ...while I'm...

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: While you're raking. (Pause) [Fendell finds Jim at the back of the Rover with the rake and the extension handle.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Take it off, it'd be faster. (Pause) [Jim may not have taken his camera off yet and, consequently, may be suggesting that Dave take it off so that they can get started without waiting for him to have a free hand.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Okay. Pick a spot. I'll rake.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Why don't we take a few steps down, Jim?

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Okay. [Dave bounds off-camera to the right with the gnomon and Hasselblad. Jim follows at a more sedate pace, walking slow enough that Fendell has no trouble following him.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: So we get where there's more frags down here, I think.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Just afraid they'll be too large down there.

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: No. Right here. A good spot. (Pause) 165:54:41 Scott: (If I don't) fall down the hill. (Pause) [Fendell finds Dave standing up-Sun of the gnomon.] 165:54:46 Irwin: I think I'll rake (standing) downhill. 165:54:48 Scott: Yeah. Make it easy on yourself. (Pause) Just a minute, let me get the down-Sun here. (Pause) [Before Jim arrived, Dave took a cross-Sun stereopair, AS15-82- 11151 and 11152 . Frame 11153 is the down-Sun. Note that Dave oriented the color/gray scale properly for these pictures.] QuickTime Clip (1 min 22 sec) by Peter Dayton

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Have at it, partner. And I'll pick us out a route to go when we leave here. Get up to North Twin, and there's a nice outcrop up there, too.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Okay. I need a bag. [Jim got several fragments with his first swath. Fendell gets a good close-up of the raking.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Yes, sir. Okay. 282. (Kicking dirt onto the rake site) Ooop, oh. Gee, I just walked right into your area. I'm sorry. [Jim pours the rocks into the bag Dave is holding low for him.] Video Clip 3 min 30 sec ( 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 31 Mb MPG )

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Oh, you're getting some. Looks like some laths, vesicular basalt, nonvesicular basalt. Do it again.

a15a1654346.speaker: Irwin
a15a1654346.text: Okay, I'll try to avoid that larger one there. [During Dave's next transmission, Jim gets a second swath and shakes the soil out of the rake.]

a15a1654346.speaker: Scott
a15a1654346.text: Yeah. And I think I kicked up some more light-colored albedo. I think, if we have some time when you get through, we ought to make a quick trench, here, maybe. It looks like maybe the upper couple of inches might be the dark gray and below it the very light gray albedo. (Pause as Jim pours) Okay; there's two swaths (each) about a meter long and one rake-width wide. [Jim starts a third swath.]

a15_1655557csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1655557csm.text: Al, I have a REFSMMAT zero time for you when you have time to copy.

a15_1655557csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1655557csm.text: Okay, Davy. And are those frags (as opposed to clods)?

a15_1655557csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1655557csm.text: Jim's getting down about, oh, I'd say...(Answering Joe) Yeah.

a15a1655706.speaker: Scott
a15a1655706.text: Yeah. (Pause) Yeah. It looks like you're getting a good 2 to 3 inches down, as you rake through there. [Jim drags the rake through the soil without extraordinary effort until it catches on something. He tugs on it several times until it rides up and over the buried obstacle.]

a15a1655706.speaker: Irwin
a15a1655706.text: Must be hung up on a large one here. (Pause) 165:57:25 Scott: Yeah, that's right. (Long Pause) [Fendell gets an excellent close-up view of Jim pouring the fragments into the bag, which Dave is holding very low because Jim is downhill of him. The person on the right with his back to us may be Deke Slayton.]

a15a1655706.speaker: Scott
a15a1655706.text: Okay.

a15a1655706.speaker: Irwin
a15a1655706.text: Alright 165:57:41 Scott: Take one more. We'll fill the bag. (Pause) Hey, Joe, how about a quick single core here. [Jim starts a fifth swath.]

a15a1655706.speaker: Allen
a15a1655706.text: Yes, sir! Or maybe even a double core. We think you can probably drive two of them.

a15a1655706.speaker: Scott
a15a1655706.text: Okay. I think we probably can, too. I was just giving you a little bait there.

a15a1655706.speaker: Allen
a15a1655706.text: Rog. A piece of cake compared to that drill. [Jim pours.]

a15a1655706.speaker: Scott
a15a1655706.text: (Laughing at Joe's joke) Okay...

a15a1655706.speaker: Irwin
a15a1655706.text: Even I can agree with that, Joe.

a15a1655706.speaker: Scott
a15a1655706.text: Good. Good, comprehensive sample. [Dave stands and we get a good view of him sealing the bag.]

a15a1655706.speaker: Scott

a15a1655706.speaker: Scott
a15a1655706.text: Okay. Get one more load. (Pause) [Jim gets a quick load and swings the rake over to the bag.]

a15a1655706.text: There's a big rock in there, huh? [Dave brushes the rock off the rake. The rock isn't big enough to be noticeable against the background of dirt falling out of the rake.] Video Clip 2 min 55 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 26 Mb MPG )

a15a1655706.speaker: Scott
a15a1655706.text: Okay, there you go. (Pause)

a15a1655706.speaker: Irwin
a15a1655706.text: Okay.

a15a1655706.speaker: Scott
a15a1655706.text: Okay, maybe one more. Let's get a whole bag full. (Pause) [Jim gets another quick rake full of dirt and pours it into the bag.]

a15a1655706.text: A comprehensive...

a15a1655706.text: (To Jim) That a boy.

a15a1655706.speaker: Allen
a15a1655706.text: ...to end all comprehensives.

a15a1655706.text: Yeah. I think this is a Number One kind, Joe. (To Jim) Hang on to that, or you can put it in my pack while I zip this.

a15a1655706.text: Okay. [Jim takes bag 282, which contains the rock-fragment collection. Dave presents the SCB on the left side of his PLSS.]

a15a1655706.speaker: Scott
a15a1655706.text: 283 for the soil.

a15a1655706.text: Did you give him the number for this one?

a15a1655706.text: Yeah. (Pause) [While Dave seals bag 283, Jim opens Dave's SCB and stows bag 282.]

a15a1655706.text: (Garbled) Got it?

a15a1655706.text: Close it up. (Pause)

a15a1655706.text: Wait a minute. Here, I'll hand you this one; the other one, too.

a15a1655706.speaker: Irwin
a15a1655706.text: Oh, okay. 165:59:56 Scott: (Changing his mind) No, I'll get yours (garbled). (Pause) [Dave and Jim both rotate 90 degrees counter-clockwise and wind up with Dave facing Jim's SCB. He stows bag 283.] 166:00:01 Scott: Okay, let me get the ("after") pictures. (Pause)

a15a1655706.text: Listen, I'll go up (to the Rover) and take the rake off.

In the meantime, I can report that the X-ray data is beginning to show very clear patterns from highlands to mare region. It looks as though we are going to - we - we are high in magnesium in the mare and high in aluminum in the highlands, which tends to confirm the anorthosite theory for the highlands. It gets rather exciting when the data starts adding up like that. And the Laser Altimeter has shown us that the back side of the Moon is indeed furthe

The crater is very uniform. It has debris on the order of, oh, a foot or so almost throughout. No accumulation of talus at the bottom; and it's got fines covering everything, nothing really sharply exposed. And it's about 60 meters across and maybe, oh, 10 meters deep, smooth sides, and a ver

a15_1661748csm.text: Sounds pretty good so far, Karl. [Pause.] And I'm getting the SIM bay ready to have another shot of that.

a15_1661748csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1661748csm.text: Okay; we've been watching your maneuvering there. Have a good go at it.

a15_1661748csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1661748csm.text: And the Rover boys at Hadley Rille have just had a tremendous session picking up all sorts of useful samples. The TV has been beautiful, the - All sorts of layering shows - in the - in the edge - in - in the - in the rille walls, and it's just very exciting.

a15_1661748csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1661748csm.text: And, as craters go around here, it's deep. (Long Pause)

a15a1662355.text: Getting ready to move out, Dave?

Certainly, we understand the Moon a whole lot bett

a15a1662355.text: Okay, hop on, and we'll get on with it here. (Pause) Get your ol' handy dandy seatbelt fixed up there because we'll be going all the way back. (Pause) [Fendell reaches the clockwise pan limit and finds Dave and the LMP seat waiting for Jim. Fendell then reverses direction and starts a counter-clockwise pan.]

a15a1662355.text: And TV camera'll be (pointed) aft and down.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Hey, Joe, are you planning a mare stop on the way back? 166:27:42 Allen: Dave, we're standing by for a mark when you're rolling. And we'd like for you to press on back towards the drill site. We've got a procedure for you to separate two sections of the deep stem from the other two sections, and we're going to carry the two halves into the LM that way.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Okay.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: And the mare site, Dave; we will do a good mare site, but fairly near the LM.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: All righty. (Pause) Whew! (Pause)

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Are you buckling up for safety?

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah, man. We always do that. Okay; switches coming on. (Pause)

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Okay, Joe. We're moving.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Okay.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Right to 093.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Okay. (Pause) [This is the bearing to the LM and, if they follow that heading, they should be aimed directly for the spacecraft.]

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Sounds about...

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: ... give it a turn and go by slow.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: ...right, and you might pick up your Rover tracks before long.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Oh, what a big mountain that Hadley is! Whew!

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah, it's beautiful. Might want to swing a little more to the right, here, Dave.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah. Let me go around to the right of this...Sure we can get between those two craters ahead of us there. Yeah, think I'll come this way.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yes, the mountains up here are truly beautiful.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen

a15a1662738.text: Okay, now come to the right. (Pause)

a15a1662738.text: 097, Dave.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Okay.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: That's a friendly shallow depression there at...

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah, we'll go south of that. (Long Pause)

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Jim, this is Houston.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Boy, it's just over hill and dale, isn't it? [Scott, from a 1996 letter - "Irwin's Dunes."]

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah. (To Houston) Go ahead, Joe.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Roger. If you can take your...

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Go ahead.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: ...eyes off the scenery and the road for a moment, I could explain the core-stem separation procedure, if you'd like it now.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Fire away.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Rog. Your choice. I can give you the procedure now or we can wait until we get past...Oh, okay. Sorry, didn't understand. We think you can put the four sections of the core stem in the vise. Jim, you move it horizontally, put horizontal torque on the stem and tighten it up in the vise, while, Dave, you use the wrench and try to separate it. [By "horizontal", Joe means that Jim should push one end of the string either fore or aft to force the vise to grip.]

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Well, we tried that, Joe, but we'll try it again. It's worth another go. That was just about what we tried the last time, by trying to put horizontal and vertical forces and everything else on the vise, and the vise just doesn't seem to grip like it should, not nearly as well as the wrench does. And I don't really know why. It might be a little loose.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Okay, Dave. Copy that. It may also be that it's quite dusty, and the brush might help you out there.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Okay. We'll try that. Didn't try that.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: And to set your minds at ease, we think that even if you can't separate it into two pieces, we can get the whole thing into the LM. So we'll bring it home anyway. We'd like it in two separate pieces, though.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Well, I guarantee you we're not going to leave it here now (laughing) after we got that much invested into it. Oop! (Pause)

a15a1662738.text: We're looking directly east now as we head back to the LM...Did you put your visor down?

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Boy, that Sun is really fierce. (Pause) [In this passage, Jim seems to be using 'directly east' to mean up-Sun. The Sun is actually about 20 degrees south of east at this time. a15a1662738.text: Roger, Jim. Copy...

a15a1662738.text: One about a quarter of the way up directly east from us...That was Big Rock Mountain.

a15a1662738.text: And the name of the mountain again, please.

a15a1662738.text: That was Big Rock Mountain.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: You know, Joe. Big Rock-o Candy Mountain.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin

He made the decision."] [Jones - "Were you involved in the site selection process?"] [Scott - "Sure."] [Jones - "Tell me about it."] [Scott - "We had, what, four sites? Rocco finally had a meeting in Washington and said, 'We're going to make a decision, and nobody leaves the room, even for lunch.' And the contest was between Hadley and Marius Hills. And the two oppo

a15a1662738.text: Can't see the LM today. (Pause)

a15a1662738.text: Really is.

a15a1662738.text: By golly, that's just super! It's, you know, unreal. (Pause)

a15a1662738.text: Really?

a15a1662738.text: Yeah. Just barely see the top of it.

a15a1662738.text: Okay, well, you look far-range, and I'll look near-range.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah. And there are our tracks.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah, we got our tracks. How about that?

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: I think we'd do better going straight ahead on, don't you?

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah. We just got that one depression over that next ridge. Might want to just drive through it, huh?

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah, let's see how we do it.

a15a1662738.text: Wasn't that the deep one, though, that had the crater in the lower part? [The crater in question is centered at about BS.7/71.5.]

a15a1662738.text: Yeah. It's saying (bearing) 093 and heading 08(0), so coming right's going to help us some. (Pause) No, we're okay.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Good shape.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah. This is a better route than we used coming out.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) Wish we could get that 16-millimeter camera to work.

a15a1662738.text: I'll change mags on it.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah.

a15a1662738.text: How about that for maneuvering, huh? (Pause)

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Slick! (Pause)

a15a1662738.text: Keep trying.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Up on the slope of...

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: It's appropriately named, don't you think?

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yes, it is. (Pause) It's the only one around here.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Dave and Jim, we think it will be just as easy for you to bring them (meaning the 16-mm magazines) back, and we'll troubleshoot them. 166:38:34 Scott: All right, we'll do that. (Long Pause) You know, so far in the past, our Nav system has always been biased pointing us to the right a little bit more than we should, so I'm going to bias it a tad left here. a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: In fact, I reckon we're making pretty good time.

a15a1663922.text: Going about 11 clicks there.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Yeah. (Pause)

a15a1663922.text: There's the LM, 12:30.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: How about that! By golly, we must have come just about straight back. And the bearing - yeah, it's great.- says 096, and I'm... 166:40:39 Irwin: Hey, let me take a picture right here.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Oh, yeah!

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Slow down a little bit...

a15a1663922.text: Okay.

a15a1663922.text: You're okay. Swing it.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1663922.text: Okay, there you go. 166:41:26 Irwin: Got it. [After Dave turned slightly to the right, Jim took AS15-82- 11193 and 11194 . Dave Byrne has combined these with 11192 in a mini-pan .]

a15a1663922.text: Okay. (Pause) Let's see. We'll go find the ALSEP site; I think we've been there before.

a15a1663922.text: And Dave and Jim...

a15a1663922.text: Boy, this ALSEP... (Laughs)

a15a1663922.text: ...I want you to notice how we planned the fourth stop...

a15a1663922.text: ...at the ALSEP site for you.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: Roger. It'll certainly...

a15a1663922.text: All the good places.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Jim, I'll go around the north here and avoid the dust on our trusty ALSEP. (Pause)

a15a1670255.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) [Dave goes around the north side of the spacecraft to find a patch of undisturbed soil. Jim goes to his seat and gets the scoop and the SESC, in that order, and then goes to join Dave. Dave's "I've got a bag" at 167:03:47 suggests that, in addition to an SESC sample, they will collect some soil from the same spot and put it in an ordinary sample bag. However, if they did collect such a sample, they did not give Houston a bag number. An alternate possibility is that they will put the SESC in a bag before putting it in Jim's SCB.]

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: We had to do so much work around the Rover, there's hardly a spot that's not messed up. (Pause) Okay. Video Clip 3 min 04 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 27 Mb MPG )

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: Got it? 167:04:41 Scott: Yeah. Let me get the pictures. (Long Pause) [Dave's "before" pictures of the SESC site are a cross-Sun stereopair, AS15-88- 11884 and 11885 , and a down-Sun, 11886 . While taking the down-Sun, Dave is standing next to the minus-Z (east) footpad. The bent, gold-foil covered landing probe is in the foreground.] [Dave and Jim are at the lower left of the TV image. Because of the troubles Fendell has been having with the TV, he seems reluctant to re-adjust the aim.]

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: (Holding the SESC at the ready) Okay.

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: Need to fill that little jewel.

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: Fill it! (Pause) [Finally, Fendell re-aims the TV to the left in small, cautious steps. This puts Dave and Jim and bottom center. Fendell then zooms in and, again in small steps, lowers his aim until we have a close-up of the two heads.]

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: Don't spill it, we want to get the top part. (Garbled) (Long Pause)

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: Want some more in there?

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: Try to scoop up the top layer there right next to the one you just scooped. Scoop up the top half inch or so. (Pause) [Dave puts his right hand on the LM and bends his knees to get the SESC low to the ground. Jim pours some soil into it.]

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: That looks good, Jim. Okay! I can take care of the rest. [Fendell makes one more vertical adjustment so that we can see Dave's hands as he closes the SESC.]

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: Take that (SESC) back (to the Rover). (Pause) Or you can just put it in my bag; that's where it's supposed to go.

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: Okay. Boy! The old hands are (garbled)! (Long Pause) [Dave removes and discards the Teflon seal protector.] [There is no doubt that Dave said something about his hands being sore.]

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: Save your DSKY finger.

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: (Laughing) Yeah. [During the launch back to lunar orbit, Dave will fly the LM by making entries into the Primary Guidance Computer via the DSKY keypad. Therefore, he needs a healthy forefinger.]

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: There we go. (Pause) [Dave puts the top on the SESC and locks it.]

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: Boy, they sure make them tight. Okay. In your bag. (Pause) [Dave puts the SESC in Jim's SCB. Dave's comment that 'they sure make them tight' is ironic in that the wire connecting the SESC top to the base got caught between the top and base. This undoubtedly made it difficult for Dave to secure the top and, more importantly, meant that the SESC wasn't actually vacuum tight. Figure 1 from the Lunar Sample Compendium report on sample 15013 shows the wire caught in the seal before being opened. In a detail from Apollo 12 photo AS12-49- 7278 , the wire is faintly visible to the right of the handle

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: Got it in? 167:07:16 Scott: Yeah. Okay. I'll take the...

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: I'll move off.

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: Jim, give me your scoop. While you're moving give me your scoop and I'll bring it over to you.

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: Okay, listen. You're gonna keep that camera for a while...

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: Yeah.

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: ...will you take a down-Sun of the Solar Wind, for me?

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: Yeah. Sure.

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: f/11 at 7 feet.

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: Okay. Video Clip 2 min 58 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 26 Mb MPG )

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: I'll collect it.

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Dave takes Jim's scoop and leans down to scoop up something. He follows Jim off-camera to the left. Fendell does not follow them and, after a short while, Dave and Jim cross the TV picture from left to right.]

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: Let's get going.

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: Go ahead. You've got to get there first (to take the down-Suns of the Solar Wind Collector).

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: I know. I'm just right behind you.

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: Oh. (Laughs) I was waiting for you to pass me. (Pause) [Fendell pulls back on the zoom and pans right to find Dave and Jim but, almost immediately, runs into the clockwise limit.]

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: I'll tell you, at the high Sun angle, it's warm isn't it?

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: It is. (Pause) You know, if we collect these large rocks, Dave, if we have time, you could almost use the Rover and drive out there.

a15a1670255.speaker: Scott
a15a1670255.text: No, I don't think we have time.

a15a1670255.speaker: Allen
a15a1670255.text: Jimmy, we've got plenty of rocks. 167:09:06 Scott: Okay, down-Sun. Okay. (Garbled) I got the picture.

a15a1670255.speaker: Irwin
a15a1670255.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Dave's down-Sun stereopair of the Solar Wind Collector is AS15-88- 11888 and 11889 .]

a15a1671036.speaker: Allen
a15a1671036.text: Dave, you might save one (16-mm magazine) for the drive-away (to the VIP site). Put the rest in the ETB, please.

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: Okay. Union (goes into the ETB). And I'll save Item; it would be a good item for the drive-away.

a15a1671036.speaker: Allen
a15a1671036.text: Okay.

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: Juliett and Hotel. (Pause) And Kilo and Foxtrot. (Pause) [Jim goes to the MESA, probably carrying the Solar Wind Collector. According to LMP-37, he is stowing the foil sheet in a bag which he will put in the ETB once Dave brings it back to the MESA.] [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I retrieved the Solar Wind. It really had so much of a set that it wouldn't roll up properly, and the bottom part of it ripped. It was just like in training."]

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: (Garbled) (Long Pause) The maps...

a15a1671036.speaker: Irwin
a15a1671036.text: I'm ready to get the tools off, Dave, any time you are.

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: Okay. That's a good time to do it. So am I.

a15a1671036.speaker: Irwin
a15a1671036.text: Okay, the Solar Wind is (on) the MESA table. (Long Pause) [Jim joins Dave at the back of the Rover. Only Jim's back and PLSS are visible.] 167:12:12 Scott: Okay. Heck, we don't have to do anything; let's just take them off. Take care of...Don't need 'em any more. (Pause) (Garbled) Okay. Turn around and I'll get your bag. [Dave's "take care of" was originally transcribed as "picture of" and, indeed, that's what the transmission sounds like. However, because there are no pictures pertinent to the tool harnesses, I believe the present transcription is correct.] [Jim starts to turn to his right.]

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: The other way. The other way. [Jim makes a 180-degree turn to his left.]

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: Okay; right there. Okay. (Garbled) Could you bend over, Jim? (Pause) [Jim bends forward about 15 to 20 degrees. Dave is probably releasing the retaining strap from the bottom of Jim's SCB.]

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: Okay. That's your bag.

a15a1671036.speaker: Irwin
a15a1671036.text: Got it off?

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: Yup. It's off; you're clear. [Jim makes another 180-degree turn to his left so that he winds up facing Dave, who is still off-camera to the right.]

a15a1671036.speaker: Irwin
a15a1671036.text: Hey, I guess we might be able to consolidate the contents of both those bags into one.

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: That probably would help.

a15a1671036.speaker: Irwin
a15a1671036.text: But we can do that inside.

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: Yeah. And, then, why don't you get mine? (Pause) [Jim steps just off-camera to the right as he gets Dave's SCB.] [Fendell raises his aim slightly.]

a15a1671036.speaker: Irwin
a15a1671036.text: Can you bend over a little? (Pause) Might as well doff the tool harnesses out here.

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: Yeah. That's a good idea. Why not? See if it works. [They are each wearing a tool harness, a loose web of straps and fasteners, on the PLSS. Each of the harnesses is equipped with a "self-doffing strap" and Dave is wondering if they will work or if they will have to help each other out of the harnesses. There is good video of Jack Schmitt getting out of his harness at the end of the third Apollo 17 EVA.]

a15a1671036.speaker: Irwin
a15a1671036.text: And you're clear.

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: Okay. [Fendell has started a counter-clockwise pan.]

a15a1671036.speaker: Irwin
a15a1671036.text: Did you put my bag in my seatpan?

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: Your bag? What bag?

a15a1671036.speaker: Irwin
a15a1671036.text: The collection bag off the side (of the PLSS). Where'd you put it? Right here in the seat...

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: No, here it is, right here.

a15a1671036.speaker: Irwin
a15a1671036.text: Oh, I see. Okay.

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: I put it on the Hand Tool Carrier. Give it to you and you can consolidate. I guess those undocumented ones we want to put in the BSLSS bag.

a15a1671036.speaker: Irwin
a15a1671036.text: Hey, let me deploy (means "remove") your (tool harness)...It didn't come off. Let me pull it off.

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: Okay; let's see. What else we have here? (Reading CDR-39) "Penetrometer drum; 70 mm; 500 mm; 16 mm (magazines); maps".

a15a1671036.speaker: Irwin
a15a1671036.text: I can get the maps, if you want. Okay, the solar wind is in there now, Joe. Solar wind (and) penetrometer drum. (In the) ETB. [Jim comes into view at the LMP seat as he gets the traverse maps. He runs around the back of the Rover.]

a15a1671036.speaker: Henize
a15a1671036.text: And, Al, you'll be fascinated to know that Galileo's theory of gravitation has been confirmed. Dave just dropped a hammer and a feather and they hit the ground simultaneously.

a15a1671036.speaker: Scott
a15a1671036.text: Nothing like a little science on the Moon, I always say. Video Clip 2 min 50 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPG )

a15a1671036.speaker: Allen
a15a1671036.text: Been saying it for years. (Long Pause) [Jim appears at the back of the Rover, lifts the triple core-stem string off the vise, takes it to the LM and lays it across the back of the MESA.]

a15a1671036.speaker: Worden
a15a1671036.text: Did you ask him what kind of a feather it was?

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1671359csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1671359csm.text: I didn't get the lanyard (meaning the self-doffing strap). It fell off my head.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1671359csm.text: Pull off the other side.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1671359csm.text: Okay.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1671359csm.text: Okay, it's off.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1671359csm.text: Good.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1671359csm.text: Why don't you get mine.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1671359csm.text: Yeah. (Pause) That's good. (Pause) Off. Video Clip 1 min 41 sec ( 0.4 Mb RealVideo or 15 Mb MPG )

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1671359csm.text: Good. (Long Pause) You didn't put any rocks in the BSLSS bag.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1671359csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1671359csm.text: No, I didn't, because they're on the floor there. I just never had a chance to get enough to put in there. [Fendell reaches the counter-clockwise pan limit and finds Dave at the CDR seat and Jim at the LMP seat.]

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1671359csm.text: Dave, rather than waste time out here, I'm just going...

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1671359csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1671359csm.text: ...to just leave these all like they are. I think we can stow them just as well that way.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1671359csm.text: I think you're right.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1671359csm.text: We ought to put them all over on the MESA table.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1671359csm.text: Okay. And I've got one little thing to take care of here next on my checklist. (Pause) [Dave heads for the MESA to do the stamp cancellations listed on CDR-39 as "P.O. Package".]

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1671359csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. How do you read? [Pause.]

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1671359csm.text: I'll get the penetrometer drum, so don't worry about that. [Jim has also gone to the MESA and we can see the top of his helmet over the back of the LMP seat. Note that retrieval of the penetrometer recording drum is listed on the printed version of CDR-39 but not on any of Jim's closeout pages, LMP-36, 37, and 38. It is possible that Jim has a handwritten note on his checklist although, in a 1996 letter, Dave thought that was unlikely given the nature of the "paper" the checklists were printed on.]

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1671359csm.text: Okay. I'm going to take care of that other little item here, which is now due.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1671359csm.text: Hello, Houston; Endeavour. Loud and clear.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1671359csm.text: Yep. (Pause) [Jim starts walking toward the back of the Rover and probably notices that the MESA is hidden from the view of the TV audience.]

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1671359csm.text: Roger. Hear you likewise, loud and clear.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1671359csm.text: Maybe you ought to lift up the front end of the Rover, so you're clearly visible.

a15_1671359csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1671359csm.text: That's a good idea. Let's just swing it around...Let me get this side here. [Dave runs out to the CDR seat while Jim goes to the LMP seat. As shown in AS15-82- 11201 , they each have a U-shaped handle on the outer edge of the chassis and, by gripping the handles can lift and re-position the Rover. The empty weight of the Rover is 462 terrestrial pounds (210 kg) and only 77 pounds (35 kg) on the Moon.]

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1672106csm.text: Endeavour, would you confirm that [the] X-ray [Spectrometer] is On, please. [Long pause.]

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1672106csm.text: (To Houston) There's something I think you'll find rather interesting. Which will only take a minute. (Pause)

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1672106csm.text: Endeavour, negative. It's - it's Off right now, Karl.

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1672106csm.text: Roger. We'd like to have it On, please. [Pause.]

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1672106csm.text: I'll put this penetrometer drum in the ETB, Dave.

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1672106csm.text: Okay.

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1672106csm.text: As well as the Solar Wind.

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1672106csm.text: Rog. Going On. And sorry about that, Karl. I switched it one position thinking I had it On, but it was really in Off.

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1672106csm.text: Jim, we copied both Solar Wind and penetrometer drum in the ETB.

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1672106csm.text: Righto. [Long pause.]

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1672106csm.text: Not quite yet. I haven't put the Solar Wind in yet; but I will, shortly. I want to watch this. [Dave has returned to the MESA and stands facing the TV with his hands at chest height.] 167:21:58 Scott: Joe, I hope you have a good picture there. I've got...

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1672106csm.text: Beautiful picture there, Dave. Movie Clip (50 sec; 0.8Mb) MPEG Clip (49 sec; 6.2Mb)

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1672106csm.text: Well, in my left hand, I have a feather; in my right hand, a hammer. And I guess one of the reasons we got here today was because of a gentleman named Galileo, a long time ago, who made a rather significant discovery about falling objects in gravity fields. And we thought where would be a better place to confirm his findings than on the Moon. [Fendell zooms in on the hammer and feather but then pulls back to watch the action.]

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1672106csm.text: Al, another bulletin from Hadley Rille. The crew is back at the LM and starting their closeout. Just a few minutes ago, I saw them perform the philatelic wonder of the century.

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1672106csm.text: And so we thought we'd try it here for you. The feather happens to be, appropriately, a falcon feather for our Falcon. And I'll drop the two of them here and, hopefully, they'll hit the ground at the same time. (Pause) [Dave is holding the feather and hammer between the thumb and forefinger of his left and right hands, respectively, and has his elbows up and out the side. He releases the hammer and feather simultaneously and pulls his hands out of the way. The hammer and feather fall side by side and hit the ground at virtually the same time. Journal contributor - and artist - Ed Hengeveld had

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1672106csm.text: So, it's all out now, huh?

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1672106csm.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1672106csm.text: How about that! (Applause in Houston)

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1672106csm.text: Which proves that Mr. Galileo was correct in his findings. (Pause)

a15_1672106csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1672106csm.text: Superb. [Jones - "That is a beautiful piece of theater. What can you tell me about the origins of the experiment?"] [Scott - "The basic idea was Joe Allen's. It was another thing from sitting in the crew quarters at night, trying to figure out interesting things to do - that were useful, too. And I guess we had a lot of ideas. But Joe came up with the hammer and feather idea, and we decided where to get a feather. I had a friend who was a professor at the Air Force Academy. Their mascot's the Falcon. And we had the (LM) Falcon. So that was indeed, a falcon feather from an Air Force Academy bir

a15a1672306.speaker: Scott
a15a1672306.text: Okay; let's see. What else we have here? (Reading CDR-39) "Penetrometer drum; 70 mm; 500 mm; 16 mm (magazines); maps".

a15a1672306.speaker: Irwin
a15a1672306.text: I can get the maps, if you want. Okay, the solar wind is in there now, Joe. Solar wind (and) penetrometer drum. (In the) ETB. [Jim comes into view at the LMP seat as he gets the traverse maps. He runs around the back of the Rover.]

a15a1672306.speaker: Henize
a15a1672306.text: And, Al, you'll be fascinated to know that Galileo's theory of gravitation has been confirmed. Dave just dropped a hammer and a feather and they hit the ground simultaneously.

a15a1672306.speaker: Scott
a15a1672306.text: Nothing like a little science on the Moon, I always say. Video Clip 2 min 50 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPG )

a15a1672306.speaker: Allen
a15a1672306.text: Been saying it for years. (Long Pause) [Jim appears at the back of the Rover, lifts the triple core-stem string off the vise, takes it to the LM and lays it across the back of the MESA.]

a15a1672306.speaker: Worden
a15a1672306.text: Did you ask him what kind of a feather it was?

a15a1672306.speaker: Henize
a15a1672306.text: A falcon feather; yes, indeed.

a15a1672306.speaker: Worden
a15a1672306.text: How about that.

a15a1672306.speaker: Scott
a15a1672306.text: Okay, Jim, we got it all in the ETB? I'll seal it up if Joe's happy...Joe, you happy with our ETB now?

a15a1672306.speaker: Allen
a15a1672306.text: Dave, (we'll) be happy if you'd police the area there under the seats and on the console.

a15a1672306.speaker: Scott
a15a1672306.text: Yes, I'll do that, Joe. For sure.

a15a1672306.speaker: Allen
a15a1672306.text: Okay, thank you. [Dave takes the ETB to the MESA. Jim passes him, headed to the Rover.]

a15a1672306.speaker: Scott
a15a1672306.text: (To himself) Matter of fact...

a15a1672306.speaker: Irwin
a15a1672306.text: I still want to get that BSLSS bag off. Don't know what we'll need it for. [Jim puts his left hand on the back of his seat and jumps onto it, landing on his right knee. He reaches far over to get the BSLSS bag off the forward surface of the geopallet, kicking the TV in the process. This lowers Fendell's aim and we get a view of what is probably the LMP camera sitting upside down in the footpan.]

a15a1672306.speaker: Allen
a15a1672306.text: And, in particular, Dave, we're looking for mags Tango and Romeo. [Tango (AS15-88) is the magazine that is still on the CDR camera and Romeo (AS15-95) is an unused, spare magazine that they will use during rendezvous with the Command Module.]

a15a1672306.speaker: Scott
a15a1672306.text: Oh, I'm pretty sure I got them in, Joe. I was reading all that stuff out to you. I hope (you) had a chance to copy it all. [Jim hops off the LMP seat, but without the BSLSS bag. He will release it with the tongs at about 167:26:58.] [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "In order to get it unlocked there, I ended up jumping up on my seat and reaching over to get it unlocked. I guess the vise was really in the way, to some extent. It didn't give."]

a15a1672306.speaker: Allen
a15a1672306.text: Okay, just check in the seats there and the console, and we're happy.

a15a1672306.speaker: Henize
a15a1672306.text: Al, we're up to the time to turn Pan Camera mode, Standby and Power, On.

a15a1672306.speaker: Scott
a15a1672306.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Jim goes to the back of the Rover, brushing against the rear fender on the way. In the background, Dave kicks the hammer and feather under the MESA so that he and Jim won't step on them. As Dave turns to go off-camera to the CDR seat, we see that he has the CDR camera, which he used to take a picture, AS15-88- 11890 , of the hammer and feather lying next to the MESA.] [Scott - "Also, with the feather up there, Jim left a four-leaf clover. He dropped it right by the feather. (Straight-faced) So we have flora and fauna."] [Fendell raises his aim, losing our view of the LMP ca

a15a1672306.speaker: Worden
a15a1672306.text: Okay, Karl. [Long pause.]

a15a1673931.text: Dave, we need some help bumping our camera up, please.

a15a1673931.text: Okay, Joe. (Pause) Poor camera! [Dave raises the camera, which promptly starts to drift up toward the zenith.]

a15a1673931.speaker: Allen
a15a1673931.text: Okay, thank you. And I guess our only other request...

a15a1673931.speaker: Scott
a15a1673931.text: (Garbled)

a15a1673931.speaker: Allen
a15a1673931.text: ...is to take the dustbrush with you back to the LM. However, we may have also... 167:48:59 Scott: Okay, I'm going to take one last pan here.

a15a1673931.speaker: Allen
a15a1673931.text: Rog. And we may have overshot on the camera. We might have to have some help getting it back towards the horizontal.

a15a1673931.speaker: Scott
a15a1673931.text: (Laughing) Okay. One last comment on the mountain that's south of Hadley. I can see some large outcrops on the upper slopes, on the upper 10 percent. And they really stand out and there's a talus downslope. As a matter of fact, it almost looks like we have some layering on the upper slopes, the upper 10 percent, apparently...

a15a1673931.speaker: Allen
a15a1673931.text: (Cutting Dave off) Okay, Dave, we copy that. We need the camera fixed. 167:49:38 Scott: ...exposes bedrock (lost under Joe) slope. (Hearing Joe) Yes sir. Going right there! [Dave's tone of voice - you can almost hear him snapping to attention and saluting - indicates that he understands he is being scolded and that it is time to obey orders.] [Scott - "I'll bet somebody jumped on Joe and said, 'Get 'em back to LM, tell 'em to get the TV fixed, tell 'em to stop talking about all that geology stuff! We're through with that.' See, they're all getting nervous now, getting almost to the end."] [Jon

a15a1673931.speaker: Allen
a15a1673931.text: Rog, and we're interested in...

a15a1673931.speaker: Scott
a15a1673931.text: (Lost under Joe) you're only up about five degrees. Ten degrees [Dave re-positions the TV. Apparently, the clutch will only hold now when the camera is perfectly level.]

a15a1673931.speaker: Allen
a15a1673931.text: Roger. We're interested in moving on back towards the LM. Carry the dustbrush with you.

a15a1673931.speaker: Scott
a15a1673931.text: Okay. How's the camera? Is that okay? (No answer; Long Pause) [Dave hops off-camera to the left. Fendell starts panning left past St. George.]

a15a1673931.speaker: Scott
a15a1673931.text: Back to LM. 167:50:22 Allen: Okay. [Dave crosses the field-of-view from left to right, headed for the LM. He is carrying the large dustbrush .]

a15a1673931.speaker: Scott
a15a1673931.text: The camera all right now? That last time you called, the tilt-up was only up about 10 degrees.

a15a1673931.speaker: Allen
a15a1673931.text: Rog, Dave. I think Ed (Fendell) must have lost control. [Fendell stops his counter-clockwise pan and reverses direction.]

a15a1673931.speaker: Scott
a15a1673931.text: Well, Ed's been doing pretty good.

a15a1673931.speaker: Allen
a15a1673931.text: You're right. He has.

a15a1673931.speaker: Scott
a15a1673931.text: He has a pretty high batting average. Video Clip 2 min 58 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 27 Mb MPG )

a15a1673931.speaker: Allen
a15a1673931.text: He surely does. (Long Pause) [Fendell stops his clockwise pan once he is aimed at the LM. Dave is not yet back at the spacecraft. At some point during the trip, he takes AS15-88- 11928 , which shows Jim at the MESA. Note the rock just below and to the left of the flag. A few moments later, Dave stops again and takes 11929 , which shows a partially-buried boulder. This is probably the rock noted in 11928. Note the relative position of the intersecting Rover tracks in the two pictures.] QuickTime Clip (1 min 37 sec)

a15a1673931.speaker: Allen
a15a1673931.text: Dave and Jim, we're ready for you to move the baggage up into Falcon and climb in. 167:51:17 Scott: Okay.

a15a1673931.speaker: Irwin
a15a1673931.text: Okay. [Fendell zooms in on the LM and we see Jim working at the MESA.] 167:51:20 Allen: As the space poet Rhysling (the blind poet in Robert Heinlein's The Green Hills of Earth ) would say, we're ready for you to "come back again to the homes of men on the cool green hills of Earth." [Scott - "That's from the Green Hills of Earth . That's one we talked about before the flight. Have you read that one?"] [Jones - "Oh, yeah! That was a favorite when I was a kid. Had you read it?"] [Scott - "Sure. (Quoting from memory) 'We pray for one last landing, on the globe that gave us birth. To rest our eye

a15a1673931.speaker: Scott
a15a1673931.text: Thank you, Joe. We're ready, too, but it's been great. Fabulous place up here. (Long Pause) [Jones - "On the way back from lunch, you said that you and Jim were feeling really comfortable about the launch back to orbit because you'd worked it so often in the effort to develop and sell the shortened rendezvous."] [Scott - "In having to present a short rendezvous to the experts, we had to learn a fair amount about it. So, when we got to this part of it, we were very comfortable that we knew what was going on. So it was a good learning experience for us."] [Fendell zooms in on the LM and in doing

a15a1673931.speaker: Irwin
a15a1673931.text: (At the MESA) Dave, I'm going to start getting in.

a15a1673931.speaker: Scott
a15a1673931.text: Good.

a15a1673931.speaker: Allen
a15a1673931.text: Roger, Jim.

a15a1673931.speaker: Scott
a15a1673931.text: Let me brush you off maybe a little, partner. I'm almost there. (Long Pause) [Dave appears at the lower right in the TV image. He is running easily. Fendell has the TV aimed so that the LM footpads are at the bottom of the image and, at launch, he will get as much of the flight as possible without moving the camera.]

a15a1673931.speaker: Irwin
a15a1673931.text: Get time? [The original transcription of Jim's transmission was "Good time?", but I have a feeling - and it is nothing more than that - that he was asking Dave if he was able to "get time" to deploy the memorial. However, I am not convinced that "Get time" is any more valid than the original transcription. In a 1996 letter, Dave agreed that Jim was asking about the memorial and that "get time?" is probably right.]

a15a1673931.speaker: Scott
a15a1673931.text: (At the MESA) Yeah. (Pause) [Dave left the Rover at about 167:50:22 and, therefore, made the trip - stop at the rock included - in 2 minutes 8 seconds.]

a15a1673931.speaker: Scott
a15a1673931.text: (Garbled) Brush you off. (Pause) Man, that stuff really accumulates, doesn't it?. (Pause) Getting it off your...(Pause) Okay; when you're ready, you can dust me off. (Pause) [Although Dave and Jim are in view while they dust each other, the TV is too far away to give us useful detail beyond the timing information that is already available from the audio.] Video Clip 2 min 52 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPG )

a15_1675406csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1675406csm.text: Al, we're ready to have Gamma-ray Gain Step back to center [Shield, On].

a15_1675406csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1675406csm.text: Man, I'm glad we got that core!

a15_1675406csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1675406csm.text: I'll tell you. [A summary of results obtained from the deep core can be found in the discussion of samples 15001-006 in the Lunar Sample Compendium .] 167:54:21 Irwin: Okay, Dave, I think that's as good as we're going to get you. [They turn to the MESA. At some point, Dave takes AS15-88- 11930 , which is a view through the struts toward the Rover at the VIP site. Note that, as planned, Dave parked the Rover facing slightly to the right of the LM. John Young and Gene Cernan parked their Rovers in similar orientations.] 167:54:26 Scott: Okay. Let's take that along and...Oh, here's another (16-mm

a15_1675406csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1675406csm.text: These two over here. (Going to the ladder) Want to use the LEC ?

a15_1675406csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1675406csm.text: I think...Oh, I think it'll be okay, Jim.

a15_1675406csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1675406csm.text: Yeah. (Long Pause, comm clears) [Dave is saying that he can carry the remaining bags up to the porch by hand.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 14 min 57 sec )

a15_1675406csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1675406csm.text: And it looks like you're going to have your fun this rev by having a good look at Aristarchus, huh?

a15_1675406csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1675406csm.text: Yeah, that's right, Karl. I've looked at Aristarchus a couple of times already in Earthshine, and I'll tell you even in Earthshine, that thing is spectacular. I can see Schröter's Valley; it shows up very white, and the crater Aristarchus with the rays extending to the west are all - they're all very, very visible.

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: Yeah. (Pause) I think with a little practice, Jim, I could jump all the way to the porch! (Pause)

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: And if you'll...(When you) come up, if you hand me that tool, it'll help. Video Clip 2 min 35 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 23 Mb MPG )

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: Oh, yeah, I will. Here's the ETB; let me get you the tool. (Pause) [Dave and I were unable to figure out what tool Jim is talking about. Perhaps the tongs or scoop to help him drag the gear in through the hatch.]

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: Okay. (I'll) go back down and get the others. (Long Pause, probably as Dave goes down the ladder and then back up) Right over on your right there, partner.

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: Got it. [Comm Break] [Fendell plays with the zoom but, eventually, returns to the original setting. By pulling back on the zoom in the second immediately following launch, he could get a bit more of the initial flight.]

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: Getting the last one right now, Joe.

a15a1675559.speaker: Allen
a15a1675559.text: Oh, boy. (Long Pause) Video Clip 3 min 06 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPG )

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: Dave, just a reminder on the stems there.

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: Yeah. Let me get you this bag.

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: Good. Those are good little holders, there.

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: Yep. [Again, Dave and I were unable to translate "little holders".] 168:00:0 Scott: Last thing will be the stems. (Garbled) (Pause) Go, partner! Get them?

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: Okay. Watch it. The caps are on not very tight; so be careful.

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: Lie it on the floor, here.

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: Why don't you put it back up in the...That's all right.

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: Well, I'm afraid it'll get bumped there, Dave.

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: Yeah. I guess we'll just have to be careful and not step on the thing. (Pause) Okay.

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: Okay, let me...Hold on, Dave, let me...

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: Oh, yeah. Move out of the way.

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: I'll get behind my...(Get behind) the hatch.

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Jim has to close the hatch so that he can get on his side of the cabin and then open the hatch again so that Dave can get in.]

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: Okay; LEC's over the side. [Dave has probably dropped the LEC to the ground over the side porch rail.]

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: Okay, I'll move. Go ahead, Joe.

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: Okay, Dave. I think you can get in now.

a15a1675559.speaker: Allen
a15a1675559.text: ...We're hoping you've got four collection bags and an ETB...

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: We've even got the core stems.

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: Hold it there, Dave. I'll get your (PLSS/OPS) antenna .

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: Okay. Video Clip 1 min 38 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPG )

a15a1675559.speaker: Allen
a15a1675559.text: And, Dave and Jim, I've noticed a very slight smile on the face of the Professor. I think you very well may have passed your final exam.

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: (Hearty Laugh) Okay. [Scott - "The Professor is Lee Silver . He's the kind of guy that you like to do this for. You would like to excel for Lee Silver. He makes you want to do that. That's one of the beauties of his teaching. So, a smile from Lee Silver is worth the whole thing. 'Cause the guy conveys it that way."] [Jones - "The frustrations of the core stem. All that other stuff."] [Scott - "Sure. 'Cause you like to do things for a Lee Silver. The guy made such a contribution to the program that, somehow, he should be recognized, someday."] [At the very least, Lee Silver's contribution is re

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: A little more to your left, if you can.

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: Straight ahead. (Pause) More to your left? Okay.

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: You're hung up a little on me. If you can shift to your right...

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay. Just don't let me get that cover (?). (Pause) Okay. Let's see; why don't we close the door?

a15a1675559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1675559.text: Now I'll get you to get mine, then.

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: If you can turn around...Okay, back into your corner. Let me get back into my corner. There. Now I think you can turn around. (Pause) Get any further left? Oh, wait. Just let me try it. (Pause) Tell you what. (Laughs)

a15a1675559.speaker: Scott
a15a1675559.text: (I'm) thinking maybe I could shift your PLSS some. Yes. There, I shifted your PLSS. Now you try it. Pull your shoulder back. (Pause) Get it? (Pause) That was off.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1680411csm.text: We see you moving over to the antisolar point to take some gegenschein photos. It's about time we solved that problem, Al. Take some good ones. That Nikon camera ought to do a good job for us.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1680411csm.text: Yeah, I know. I can't get down that low. Get down that low. Go ahead and repress with it (meaning the primary water valve) open.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1680411csm.text: Let me try it. (Long Pause) (Feeling the switches on the bottom, right-front corner of Jim's PLSS ) Cooling. Oxygen. PLSS water, right there. Okay, I got you. Okay, now...

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1680411csm.text: Well, we're all set up here, Karl; and, if the Nikon will do it, we'll get them.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1680411csm.text: Did you see the seven rilles of Aristarchus, Al? [Pause.]

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1680411csm.text: Okay. We're fixed. (To Houston) Yeah, Joe; it's off. (To Jim) Get back in your corner if you can. Look. You have to turn right so you can get the dump valve .

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1680411csm.text: Certainly did. Wouldn't miss 'em. [Pause.] Not much to relate at this time as far as Aristarchus - or descriptions - visual observations are concerned in Earthshine. As a matter of fact, it was so close to the terminator that I wasn't really dark-adapted enough to see much except the very light colored crater Aristarchus and its ejecta pattern and a very light-colored Schröter's Valley and - which kind of surprised me. Schröter's Valley has about the same lightness as the interior of Aristarchus itself.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1680411csm.text: I've already got it; (it's) in Auto.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1680411csm.text: Okay, just move back so I can get the door then. (Can you) go farther?

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1680411csm.text: Go back in my little corner?

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1680411csm.text: That a boy. Okay. Now we're cooking. (Long Pause) Man! (Pause) Closed and locked, babe.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1680411csm.text: Rog. Didn't see any red spots up there, huh?

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1680411csm.text: Okay, " dump valves both to Auto".

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1680411csm.text: Al, the time line on the surface is going very well now, and they're just about to repress.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1680411csm.text: Hey, as I look back over towards Tsio - Tsiolkovsky, I see your new orbit is taking you over the crater Alden. Do me a personal favor and sneak in a shot of it, if you can.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1680411csm.text: Well, we'll check it here on the repress.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: (Reading Surface 11-1) "Verify EVA circuit breaker configuration." If you can move forward, I can get in there and verify mine.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Stand by.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Are you trying to get your O2 off?

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Yeah. Okay; it's off.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Good. Okay. (Pause)

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Okay, my circuit breakers are okay except Fan 2 to Suit Fan Delta-P, which we'll pick up (in just a few seconds).

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Yeah. Check mine here. Okay. Mine are okay. Let's see. "CB(16) ECS: Suit Fan 2, close."

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Okay, closed.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: "Suit Fan Delta-P, close."

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Closed.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay; "doff the gloves and stow on the comm panel."

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Wait. I didn't depress. I'm going to have to use the purge valve.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Oh, you didn't, huh? Oh. Okay. Can you get it, okay?

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Yeah. Stand by. (Long Pause)

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: No, I can't, Dave. I'll turn around.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay. Let me get out of your way. (Pause) Okay, come on around.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: It (meaning the suit pressure)'s coming down, but very slowly.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay; come on around. (Pause) Okay; put you in high (purge valve) flow, here. There you go.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Okay.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay; let's take off your gloves. When you get down (in pressure). (Long Pause) I'll "verify the safety" (on the forward dump valve ), here. Auto. Safety's on the dump valve. Next thing is to remove purge valves, anyway. "Descent Water valve, Open", when you get to it, Jim.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Okay; in just a moment. Back up a little bit. (Pause) Okay, Descent Water is coming open.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: What's next?

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay; "pull the purge valve out". You did it. "Disconnect OPS O2 hose." (Pause)

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: In work. (Long Pause) Okay; mine's out.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay; and the next thing is "connect the LM O2 hoses; red to red and blue to blue".

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Red to red and blue to blue.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Yeah, we've got to do a dump.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) [Once they doff the PLSSs and check the OPSs, they will depressurize the cabin, open the hatch, and jettison the PLSSs and a jettison bag .]

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: We better make sure we got them (the LM hoses) under the OPS (hose)...(correcting himself) PLSS (hose). Okay. Okay; I go to Suit Flow. (Garbled) Phew! (Pause)

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Doesn't look like my prime water is off.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Say again?

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Doesn't feel like the prime water is off.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: I've got bare hands, now, when I get back here. (Garbled)

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Getting water in the suit.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: I know it. There, it's off. It was off, and you must have bumped it, maybe. (Pause) It was off, but you are getting water, all right.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: I feel it running down my leg.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Yeah. I can't understand that. It was off. I mean it wasn't off then, but I remember turning it off, and it went off.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Yeah, it's probably catching up on something, Dave, just like it did yesterday...

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Yeah.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: When I turn around. Okay. My O2 hose is disconnected, and going to Suit Flow.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay. Then " Suit Isolation (Valve to) Suit Flow; PLSS Pump, Off".

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: Okay. "Disconnect PLSS water from PGA and connect LM water to PGA."

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1681613csm.text: Okay. You ready for me to turn the Data Systems, Off? [Pause.]

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1681613csm.text: In work. (Long Pause) Okay; water's connected. How about a little (LM) LCG pump action?

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1681613csm.text: Roger, Al. If you've secured the SIM bay experiments, we're ready for the Datum [means Data] System, Off.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: Not yet. Let's press on down here.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: Your (LM oxygen) flow ought to cool you there; it's cooling me pretty good.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1681613csm.text: Yeah. [They have completed Surface 11-1 and are about to start 11-2.]

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: Okay. "PLSS Mode, both to O. Audio circuit-breaker, open, and connect to LM comm."

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1690607csm.text: Yeah, it's morning down here, Al. Al, we've got a couple of changes for you. We're going to delete the P22 because the LM crew needs a little extra time, and substitute a P24 from the Command Module for it. If you've already got your camera on the sextant, sorry about that. If not, delete it.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1690607csm.text: Okay. I've already got it on, but that's no problem.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1690607csm.text: Okay. We'll give you a P24 landmac - landmark track PAD whenever you're ready.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1690607csm.text: Okay. Your target's the LM. T-1, 169:34:08; T-2, 38:15; TCA, 40:38; T-3, 41:06; south 3 nautical miles; and your attitude will have to change a little, Al. We're using roll, pitch and yaw of 000, 350/231 and 000. Noun 89, latitude 26.107; longitude over 2, plus 01.828; altitude, minus 013.26; and, at 169:25 in your Flight Plan, change the R2 of Noun 78 to minus 080.00.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell

a15a1691556.text: Okay, Falcon. We observe the batteries coming on; and I have a lift-off time when you're ready.

a15a1691556.text: Stand by. (Pause) Okay, Ed. I'm ready to copy the LM ascent PAD (as per Surface 12-4).

a15a1691556.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1691556.text: Okay; I don't have an ascent PAD for you, but I have the lift-off time. It's 171:37:22.36.

a15a1691556.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1691556.text: I think I heard that. Let me read it back: 171:37:22.36. And I have some star changes for the P57.

a15a1691556.speaker: Irwin
a15a1691556.text: Okay; go ahead. [In Program 57, they re-align the inertial platform using star sightings made with the Alignment Optical Telescope (AOT). The P57 procedures are on Surface 12-2.]

a15a1691556.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1691556.text: Rog. For the P57 coming up right now, let's use star 5 (Polaris) and detent 3 and you should find it at a cursor of 182.2 and the spiral of 284.0.

a15a1691556.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1691556.text: And, Falcon, when you get around to it, how about an ED batt, check, please (as per Surface 12-1)?

a15a1691556.text: And, Ed, an E(rasable)-memory dump coming down (as per Surface 12-1).

a15a1691556.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1691556.text: Okay; we're ready. Let her come. (Pause)

a15a1691556.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1691556.text: Okay. Hadley Base, Houston. We got your E-mod. We're ready to give you an uplink (as per Surface 12-2) if we can have P00 (Program Zero-Zero) and Data. (Pause)

a15_1694137csm.speaker: Worden

a15_1730041.text: Okay, I guess we're not - Well, Al's talking to us.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Okay, what we're looking for is to see if anything is in the way of the lens of that sensor. [Pause.] If you're not familiar, I can give you a page number in your LM Data Systems Book to take a look at it. [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, stand by one.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: No, it's not - it's not on the lens, Dave. It's right alongside the lens on the body of the camera...

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: We've got a picture of it, Al.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: ...it tells us what speed to take the picture at.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, we'll get a picture of it.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay. I'll go ahead and do your pitcharound. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: And, give me - give me a call when you start.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Houston, what page is that on in the LM Systems book?

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Okay. It's page 43 in the LM's System's Bo - Data Book.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Okay. On the right-hand side, Dave, you see that one little line that says, "Mapping and Pan Cameras N 2 [nitrogen] Press[ure] Systems Assembly."

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: We haven't got it out yet. Stand by.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Yeah, I'll go the higher rate, Dave. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Okay, here we go.

a15_1730041.speaker: Irwin
a15_1730041.text: Go ahead. [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, looks good, you're going the right way. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Dave, while he's pitching, I'll tell you - should be about the middle of the SIM bay by the Mapping Camera. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Unknown speaker
a15_1730041.text: [Garble.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Unknown speaker
a15_1730041.text: [Garble.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: A very nice maneuver, Endeavour. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, Houston. We don't see it labeled in here. Where - is it labeled on the picture?

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Negative. As soon as you have the picture, I'll tell you where to look.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, we got the picture; tell us where to look.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Okay, way over on the right-hand side, where it says, "Mapping and Pan Cameras N 2 Press System Assembly." [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: It's on the right picture. [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Irwin
a15_1730041.text: The one with the covers open?

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: That's affirm. Between the end of that arrow and the lens, about halfway, is a little dot that represents the V-over-H assembly. Now, the camera lens will be covered - rather it will be folded up so you will not be able to see it; however, that is the item you're looking for, represented by the small circle about halfway in between the end of the arrow and the lens of the camera.

a15_1730041.speaker: Irwin
a15_1730041.text: Okay, I see a small circular object there just - just to the right of the handle, and I don't see anything covering it.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Are you talking about the diagram, or in the SIM bay?

a15_1730041.speaker: Irwin
a15_1730041.text: No, in the SIM bay.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Okay. That's what we wanted to know.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Yeah, it's a little round black...

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: That's it - that's it.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: ...holder type of affair, right?

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: If you can snap a picture of it, we'd appreciate it. [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, we'll get one, Ed. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, we've got the picture, Houston, and we'll proceed on with the docking.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Thank you, sir. [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Okay, I'll pitch back around now, Davy.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: And, Falcon; Houston. Do you have any comments on the SIM bay, anything look out of the ordinary?

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: No, it looks very clean. The doors are all covered, and all the booms are retracted; and it looks neat and tidy.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Thank you.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Okay, where'd you go?

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: We should be right where we were. Have you completed your maneuver?

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Rog.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, we're in the same inertial attitude, I'll come back around to you. Just stay there.

a15_1732724.speaker: Scott
a15_1732724.text: Okay, Endeavour. Would you handle station-keeping, we're going to pitch and yaw now.

a15_1732724.speaker: Worden
a15_1732724.text: Okay, Houston. Ready to get [garble, should be "Pyro"] Arm, On.

a15_1732724.speaker: Worden
a15_1732724.text: Roger. I'll [garble] turn on the [Sequential Events Controller] Logic when you're ready.

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: I got barberpole.

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: [Garble. May be "There, I got you."].

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Roger.

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: [Garble.] [Pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: Okay. You ready to come in?

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: All set. [Long pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: Hard dock.

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Roger. Roger. Copy hard dock. And, Falcon, if you'll give us 105 [degrees pitch] and 67 [degrees yaw, on the steerable S-band antenna], we should have your steerable [antenna].

a15_1733552.speaker: Irwin
a15_1733552.text: Roger. 105 and 67. [Pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: Good show, Endeavour. It's nice to be aboard again.

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: Welcome home.

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: Thank you. [Pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: And Falcon, Houston. Now that we have the steerable [antenna] back, when you get a moment, pull the ECS Auto Transfer, Open, and then the Glycol Pump 1, Open.

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: Roger. ECS Auto Transfer is Open - and I'll open the Glycol Pump 1 now.

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Roger. We want to get a little data down here.

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: Okay, do you want us to select 2, or just let it run?

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Negative. Just wait for 30 seconds.

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: Okay, we'll stand by for your call.

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Thank you.

a15_1733552.speaker: Irwin
a15_1733552.text: And, Houston; Falcon. Do you have an update for us for the LM weight/CSM weight?

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Roger. Stand by. LM weight, 5444 [pounds, 2,469 kg].

a15_1733552.speaker: Irwin
a15_1733552.text: Roger. LM weight 5444.

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
