a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Yes sir. [Long pause.]

a15_1924511.speaker: Scott
a15_1924511.text: Oh, as a matter of fact, Joe, we made a good thorough search of the LM before we let it go. We went from top to bottom to make sure we got everything, and I'm sure we got everything we brought up off the surface, and I'm pretty sure we did - did fairly well cleaning up the surface.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Okay, Dave. Good news; good news. Al, if you're ready, I'll start hitting you with a few things we're interested in knowing from you right away. And then, when we get those, I'll give you the general plan for the day. And I think, in some cases, we'll want to just talk you through some of the changes while you're making your front-side pass. There's no need to feed up all the data in detail to you at the beginning here. My first question: we need from you a configuration of panel 230 , particularly - in fact, only really the Mass Spec. switches, could you - call out the settings for the Mass S

a15_1924511.speaker: Scott
a15_1924511.text: Okay, Joe, I'm right there. Experiment is up and On. Ion Source is centered. The Discriminator is Low and the Multiplier is Low.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Okay, thank you. That's - that's what we'd guessed. And, Al, I - I guess the first thing we want - we're going to want you to do today is to start to get ready to go plus-X forward, P20 option 5. We're going to want you to retract the Mass Spec. boom and close the X-ray and Alpha Particle cover.

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Okay, Joe. We'll do all that. How about putting it on a - on a time basis for me so I can write it in the Flight Plan.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Okay, real fine. You can start that right now at - just put it in at 192:52, I guess. And also, right after that, list fuel cell purge, H 2 O dump and LiOH canister change. [Long pause.]

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Okay, Joe. Understand. You want us to go ahead into plus-X P20 SIM bay attitude, and pull in the Mass Spec. and the Gamma-ray booms, and, I guess, turn off the Mass - turn the Mass Spec. to stand by.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Al, let me hit you with that last statement again. We want you to retract the Mass Spectrometer boom, but not the Gamma-ray, and close the X-ray and Alpha Particle covers. Retract Mass Spec. boom and close two covers. Over.

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Okay, understand. You want us to pull in - to retract the Mass Spec. boom and close the X-ray [and] Alpha covers, then do the fuel cell purge, the water dump and a canister change.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: That's affirm.

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Okay, Joe. I'll get that in work. [Long pause.]

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: And one more item. You can start to charge Bat B at your convenience.

a15_1925634.speaker: Worden
a15_1925634.text: Okay, Joe. While we're maneuvered here to a plus-X forward, how about reading some news to us?

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: Okay. Sure will. Let me - let me begin with just a note on that water dump. It'll take about 15 minutes to run, and they're interested in your dumping it to close to 10 per cent onboard reading. Over.

a15_1925634.speaker: Worden
a15_1925634.text: Roger, understand. Probably the same as we've been doing before. We dump down to 10 per cent, but not below 10 per cent.

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: That's correct. And I've got several things to read to you here. I have the official morning Gold Bugle Zeitung report and - that comes from two rows behind me here. And I've also got a telegram for you, Jim. And I have some history - a little bit of history that's been researched for you by the people at Honeysuckle concerning a small problem with a leak on the Endeavour about 200 years ago. And I'll start with whatever you'd like to hear first. [Long pause.]

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: Okay, let me just start with the morning's news. The weather report in Houston-Galveston area calls for showers and thunder showers through Wednesday. Today's temperatures will be in the lower 70s and upper 80s.

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: The United States will support Communist China's admission to the United Nations this fall, Secretary of State, William Rogers announced. The U.S. will also fight against expelling the Nationalist Chinese Government on Taiwan. U.S. Steel, the industry pace setter, announced a price hike averaging 8 per cent on virtually all its products and several other companies followed suit, as an aftermath of a new 3-year labor contract. Trainmen won pay increases of nearly a dollar and a half an hour, spread over a 42 months, in a nationwide contract settlement, and called off their crippling strike agai

a15_1925634.speaker: Worden
a15_1925634.text: Roger, Joe. Copied all these off.

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: Roger. Okay. In the National League: Philadelphia 4, Atlanta 0; Cincinnati 4, New York 2; St. Louis 3, San Diego 1; and Los Angeles 5, San Francisco 4. And Lee Trevino added another thousand bills to his bank roll, Monday, by taking first place with the number - with a 7-under-par, 65, in the Colombus Invitational Pro-Am. Jack Nicklaus and Arnie Palmer teamed last weekend to close in on Trevino in professional golf's money-winning race, though. Nicklaus and Palmer won twenty thousand dollars each when they won the National Team Championship at - I guess Ligonier, Pennsylvania. Trevino leads fo

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: And, I'll go over now to - Jim, a special telegram for you which reads, essentially: Mother, Dad, and your brother Charles are proud of you. We were thinking of our trip together on top of Mount Whitney and we are with you in spirit on the Moon. Love, Mother, Dad, and your crew. And I might add, that there - An occasional piece of mail for - for all of you that's starting to - starting to come in to the Manned Spacecraft Center, here. In fact, I think a truck pulled up there yesterday to deliver some of the first.

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: I'm going to go on, if you're still listening, to read some history that was sent to us by the Honeysuckle people. And the subject is "A Leak on the Endeavour at 62 hundred GET." Following the above incident and the wonder from the Apollo 15 crew whether Captain Cook's Endeavour had ever sprung a leak, staff at Honeysuckle Creek Tracking Station has searched the records and come up with the following incident, which may be of interest. Information has been extracted from an old newspaper article and an entry in Captain Cook's log book. "It was 11 pm on June 11, 1770, a clear moonlit night, whe

a15_1925634.speaker: Scott
a15_1925634.text: That's quite an analogy, isn't it.

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: Quite an analogy, Dave. Certainly is.

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Houston, 15. I'm ready to copy the consumables, Joe.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Okay, Alfredo. GET 191 plus 25; RCS total, 47 [per cent]; quad A: 50, [B] 47, [C] 46, [D] 47; H 2 tank 1: 56, [2] 53, [3] 42; O 2 tank 1: 64, [2] 67, [3] 54.

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Rog, understand, Joe. At 191:25, RCS total, 47; quad A: 50, 47, 46, 47; H 2 is 56, 53, 42; O 2 is 64, 67, 54.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Copy, Al. And I'll be right back.

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Okay, Joe. [Long pause.]

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Endeavour, this is Houston again.

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Okay, Al. Let me lay some more words on you concerning your Flight Plan, when you're - you're ready to talk about that.

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Roger, Joe. Go ahead.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Okay. You'll be in the configuration plus-X forward, and will be taking Gamma-ray, X-ray and Alpha Particle data, data during rev 60. We want you to do, at 193 plus 45, a P52 option 3. And we're going to add a Map and Pan Camera pass sometime during rev 60. And I'll be coming at you with the necessary data for that. Also...

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Roger, Joe; understand.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Okay, Al. Now I guess a - a word about biomed configuration, today. In order to get some very interesting baseline data, medical data on you, Al - and, Jim, for your EVA coming up later - we're requesting that the two of you give us that biomed data today. I think, Dave, you were scheduled for it, but I guess we'd prefer Jim on the line with Al to get baseline data for later. Now, Al, let - let me run through in just some blocks here, [of] the next revs as we see them, and the approximate activities. And then I'll come up with specific data concerning those revs later on, perhaps actually duri

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Roger that.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Okay. On rev 61 will be UV photography of the lunar mare. We're coming up on, I guess, an hour of light flash experiments, and it's pretty much dealer's choice between Dave and Jim, who - whichever one of you would like to do that. Rev 62 will be a crew exercise period, science photos, and science visuals. And we'll be taking the Mapping Camera and Laser Altimeter data during rev 62. And it will end with terminator photos. On rev 63, more Mapping Camera, Laser Altimeter, and a burst of the Pan Camera. UV photos and terminator photos again. Rev 64 will be eat period, boom photos, LiOH canister

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Okay, Joe. Understand in the Flight Plan that the object is going to be to get us back to the - to the printed Flight Plan as much as possible.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: That's exactly right, Al. And you'll be coming on to it kind of as the day progresses. We're just going to pick up a few quick items that we've missed over the past 2 hours and mainly just lift - lift out other sections, as I understand it. But you'll be back on the Flight Plan shortly.

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Okay, Joe. Fine. Thank you.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Rog. And...

a15_1930736.speaker: Scott
a15_1930736.text: And, Joe, let me request that Jim be...

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Go ahead, Dave.

a15_1930736.speaker: Scott
a15_1930736.text: I'd like to say that I'd like to have Jim without his sensors on today. That 3 - 4 days in a row is pretty tough with those things on. I think probably, if we get him tonight, you could probably get your data, don't you think?

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Stand - stand by, Dave, and I'll - let me double check,

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Good ship Endeavour, this is Houston. [Pause.]

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Roger. On our downlink data, we see indications of High Gain Antenna yaw fluctuations. Wonder if you could glance over at your onboard indication and see if you see it there as well. And, also we're standing by for crew status reports, when you're ready to give it.

a15_1932051.speaker: Scott
a15_1932051.text: No, we - we see no oscillations up here, Joe.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Al, this is Houston. With a TEI-62 PAD, when you're ready for that. We also have a question. How did the Mass Spec. boom retraction go? And we've got a switch setting for your Mass Spec. when you're ready.

a15_1932051.speaker: Worden
a15_1932051.text: Okay. Jim will be ready to copy a TEI PAD here in a minute. And Mass Spec. boom retracted without a hitch this time, Joe. Sorry I didn't get the time on it, but it was very close to the nominal time, and apparently it didn't hung up this time.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Okay, fine, Al. Thank you. We'd like the - I guess the Mass Spec. placed on Standby, please. And that's the Experiment switch.

a15_1932051.speaker: Worden
a15_1932051.text: Okay. Mass Spec. on Standby. Yeah, that's verified on standby, Joe.

a15_1932051.speaker: Irwin
a15_1932051.text: And, Joe, I'm ready to copy that TEI PAD.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Okay, Jim, good morning. We need Accept, and we're going to uplink a new state vector to you.

a15_1932051.speaker: Irwin
a15_1932051.text: Okay, Joe. The readback on TEI-62. SPS/G&N; 36310; plus 0.61, plus 0.92; 200:10:34.64; plus 2928.4, plus 0190.3, minus 0043.5; 180, 106, 006; four jets, 12 seconds.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Okay, Jim. Readback correct. And how are you doing this morning?

a15_1932051.speaker: Irwin
a15_1932051.text: Fine, Joe. Had a good night's sleep.

a15_1933257.speaker: Allen
a15_1933257.text: Hello, Endeavour. This is Houston with a Map Camera photo PAD when you'kre ready.

a15_1933447.speaker: Worden
a15_1933447.text: Houston, 15. Go ahead with your Mapping and Pan Camera photo patchup.

a15_1933447.speaker: Allen
a15_1933447.text: Okay, Al. And I - I forgot to tell you when you're dumping water, you can also go ahead with the urine dump if you need to do that. I just forgot to mention that. The Map Camera photo PADs for rev...

a15_1933447.speaker: Allen
a15_1933447.text: Yeah. For rev 60. T-start, 194:35:05, T-stop, 195:34:50. Image motion setting at T-start: barber pole plus 4; At 195 plus 20 plus 00: barber pole. And a couple of notes on this. Be sure to retract the Gamma-ray boom prior to the start of the camera pass. And be sure to go to 5 degrees deadband in P20 - I'm sorry, Al; that's 5/10ths of a degree deadband in P20 prior to camera pass. And you want to extend the camera and start the Laser Altimeter per the system's checklist, page S/1-38. Over. [Pause.]

a15_1933447.speaker: Worden
a15_1933447.text: Roger, Joe. Understand. Mapping Camera photo PAD: T-start, 194:35:05; T-stop, 195:34:50. Now for the image motion, you want a T-start barber pole plus 4, and at 195:20:00, you want that increased to barber pole. And notes: Retract the Gamma-ray boom before taking the pictures; go to half-degree deadband; and extend the Mapping Camera; and start the Laser Altimeter as per system's checklist S/1-38.

a15_1934116.speaker: Allen
a15_1934116.text: Endeavour, this is Houston with the new O 2 heater configuration for you. [Pause.]

a15_1934116.speaker: Allen
a15_1934116.text: Rog, Al. We want O 2 Heater in tank 3 to Auto and tanks 1 and 2, Off. Over.

a15_1934116.speaker: Worden
a15_1934116.text: Understand, Joe. You want O 2 Heater in tank 3, Auto, and the other two, Off.

a15_1934116.speaker: Allen
a15_1934116.text: That's right, Al. And we want you to proceed with your O 2 fuel cell purge listed at 193 plus 58 in the Flightk Plan.

a15_1934116.speaker: Worden
a15_1934116.text: Roger, Joe. We'll get that in work here now.

a15_1934438.speaker: Allen
a15_1934438.text: Al, this is Houston. You can terminate the dump now. And turn the Alpha Particle experiment Off, please. [Long pause.]

a15_1934438.speaker: Allen
a15_1934438.text: Endeavour, Houston. Requesting Auto in the High Gain [Antenna]. And, troops, you may have to delay the P52 we've called out to you, and it's coming up shortly, until about 194 plus 20, to make sure most of the water's out of the way. Over. [Pause.]

a15_1934438.speaker: Worden
a15_1934438.text: Roger, Joe. I'll just go take a look here and see if I can pick up the star okay, I'll go ahead and do the P52.

a15_1934438.speaker: Allen
a15_1934438.text: Okay, Al. And you got the call about the Alpha Particle counter, I hope.

a15_1934438.speaker: Worden
a15_1934438.text: Right. Roger. We got it turned off.

a15_1935113.speaker: Worden
a15_1935113.text: Okay, Joe. I got the gyro torquing angles up, and I'll torque them out on the minute.

a15_1935339.speaker: Allen
a15_1935339.text: Al, we no - noted the termination of your fuel cell 3 purge. At your convenience, open the X-ray and the Alpha Particle experiment covers, please, and turn the Alpha Particle back on. Over.

a15_1935339.speaker: Worden
a15_1935339.text: Okay, Joe. We'll be about another 2 or 3 minutes finishing up all the dumps, and then we'll do that.

a15_1935339.speaker: Allen
a15_1935339.text: Okay. Fine. We do want you to wait until all the dumps are completed, and then open the doors and turn Alpha Particle on at your convenience, really.

a15_1935339.speaker: Worden
a15_1935339.text: Roger.

a15_1935339.speaker: Scott
a15_1935339.text: [Garble] this morning.

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: Yes, Myrtle. I didn't use - I didn't - hadn't used Myrtle this morning. I didn't use Myrtle this morning.

a15_1935339.speaker: Scott
a15_1935339.text: I think that checklist is [garble] 5 minutes and then closed.

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: Yes, it does.

a15_1935339.speaker: Scott
a15_1935339.text: Yes, that's [garble]. Yes. Yes. [Garble].

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: Yes. Yes. I didn't use that this morning.

a15_1935339.speaker: Scott
a15_1935339.text: [Garble] Al. [Garble].

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: That's true.

a15_1935339.speaker: Scott
a15_1935339.text: [Garble].

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: Yes. You were smart.

a15_1935339.speaker: Allen
a15_1935339.text: Good ship Endeavour, this is Houston. We'll see you on the other side.

a15_1935339.speaker: Worden
a15_1935339.text: Okay, Joe.

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: Okay, we got...

a15_1935339.speaker: Scott
a15_1935339.text: We stow this in that Jum [?] bag down there? When I took that [garble], Al? Okay.

a15_1935339.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1935339.text: This is Apollo Control at 193 hours, 56 minutes. We've had Loss Of Signal on this revolution. Endeavour and its crew performing orbital science throughout the day. We passed up an update to the Flight Plan for today. Crew reporting 9 hours of sleep last night and no medication. The briefing on the subsatellite will begin momentarily in the MSC News Center briefing room. We'll reacquire Endeavour again at 194 hours, 41 minutes, about 30 seconds on its 60th revolution. At 193 hours, 57 minutes; this is Mission Control, Houston.

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: How about this? Go Manual and Wide. Right, Al? That what you say? Then - then go to Reacq? Just leave it in Manual and Wide until we come around, right?

a15_1935339.speaker: Worden
a15_1935339.text: What?

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: Manual and Wide. How about the Squelch Enable?

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: I have the Squelch Enable on.

a15_1944309.speaker: Allen
a15_1944309.text: Hello, Endeavour. This is Houston. [No answer.]

a15_1944309.speaker: Worden
a15_1944309.text: Hello, Houston; Endeavour. Loud and clear.

a15_1944309.speaker: Allen
a15_1944309.text: Roger, Al. I wanted to tell you that, except for a couple of minor changes, you'll shortly be back on the nominal Flight Plan. I do have a Pan Camera photo PAD to be copied into your Flight Plan at 195 plus 00 when you're ready.

a15_1944309.speaker: Allen
a15_1944309.text: All righty. At 195 plus 00, Pan Camera Mode, Standby; Power, On; Stereo, Exposure, Normal. At 195:04:13, Pan Camera Mode, Operate. At 195:14:30, Pan Camera Mode, Standby. Pan Camera Mode, Mono. At 195:18:23, Pan Cam Self Test to Self Test. The talkback should be barber pole for 30 seconds and then gray. And after the talkback is gray, Pan Camera Self Test to Heater. At about 195 plus 21, Pan Camera Power, Off, on a cue from MSFN. At - at 195 plus 34 plus 50, Laser Altimeter, Off; Retract Map Camera; and Close Map Camera Cover, per steps 7 and 8, page S/1-39 in your checklist. Over.

a15_1944309.speaker: Worden
a15_1944309.text: Okay, Houston; understand. And I'll go through the whole thing here for you. At 195, Pan Camera Mode, Standby; Power, On; Stereo and Exposure, Normal. At 195:04:13, Mode to Operate. At 195:14:30, Mode, Standby, and Stereo to Mono. At 195:18:23, Self Test to Self Test, and barber pole for 30 seconds and then Self Test to Heaters. At 195:21:00, Pan Camera Power to Off on your cue. At 195:34:50, Laser Altimeter, Off; Retract the Mapping Camera, and close the covers per steps in checklist S/1-39.

a15_1944309.speaker: Allen
a15_1944309.text: Okay, Al. Right on. And could you verify for us, please, that the Alpha Particle Spectrometer's been turned On and that the X-ray and Alpha Particle covers are Open. Over. [Pause.]

a15_1944309.speaker: Worden
a15_1944309.text: Okay, Joe. The covers are open. X-ray is On, and Alpha Particle coming On now.

a15_1944309.speaker: Allen
a15_1944309.text: Okay, thank you. And, Endeavour; we need Narrow Beam on the High Gain [Antenna], please. [Pause.]

a15_1945122.speaker: Worden
a15_1945122.text: Joe, looking ahead a little bit in the Flight Plan, I see we've got gegenschein coming up on this rev. And I guess my question is do you want me to change the film in the - in the camera now? In other words, have we missed any picture taking with the - the - the Nikon that maybe we want to pick up with that mag before I offload that mag?

a15_1945122.speaker: Allen
a15_1945122.text: Al, I'll have an answer for you in just a minute on that. In the meantime, could you reverify that the covers on the X-ray and Alpha Particle are open, and we're getting some problems on that, and I guess the best thing to do would be - to just go to your checklist, page 1-33, and do that Cover, Open, couple of steps - which is listed "Number 1, Cover, Open"...

a15_1945122.speaker: Worden
a15_1945122.text: Okay, now, Joe. You're right. I don't know - I don't know where we got - got our wires crossed, but the covers were closed and they're now open.

a15_1945122.speaker: Allen
a15_1945122.text: Al, on your question on the gegenschein experiment, we want you to go ahead and change the mag to Victor, just per the Flight Plan.

a15_1945742.speaker: Allen
a15_1945742.text: Roger, babe. Requesting you - give us a Gainstep on the Gamma experiment up three clicks, please. And we're also wondering what mag you've taken off the Nikon to put mag Victor on. There's some confusion in our minds. I guess we thought Victor was already on there. Over.

a15_1945742.speaker: Worden
a15_1945742.text: Negative. Mag U was on there before, Joe, and I had just taken it off.

a15_1945742.speaker: Allen
a15_1945742.text: Okay, thank you, Al. That helps us. And once again, the Gainstep on the Gamma, up three clicks. And we're showing that now.

a15_1950211.speaker: Allen
a15_1950211.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. Requesting Auto on the High Gain, please.

a15_1950211.speaker: Allen
a15_1950211.text: Mark. 15 seconds to Pan Camera, Off - On, Pan Camera, On. Sorry.

a15_1951404.speaker: Allen
a15_1951404.text: Pan Camera to Standby in 30 seconds. [Pause.]

a15_1951404.speaker: Allen
a15_1951404.text: We copy, and thank you, Al. And I've got a UV photo PAD, a big one liner, when you're ready to copy that.

a15_1951404.speaker: Allen
a15_1951404.text: Rog. This is for your PAD located at 196 plus 50. And it is T-start, 196:56:19. [Pause.]

a15_1951404.speaker: Worden
a15_1951404.text: Understand, Joe. UV photo PAD. T-start, 196:56:19.

a15_1951404.speaker: Allen
a15_1951404.text: Right on, Al. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_1951404.speaker: Allen
a15_1951404.text: Al, I gave a bad call. I was 30 seconds premature on that. Stand by.

a15_1951404.speaker: Worden
a15_1951404.text: Okay. [Pause.] Looks like you'll get two Self Tests, Joe. [Long pause.]

a15_1951404.speaker: Allen
a15_1951404.text: Al, that's no problem. We'll take both of them, and I'll cue you for the next.

a15_1951404.speaker: Worden
a15_1951404.text: Okay. I'll give you a whole series of them if you want them. [Pause.]

a15_1951404.speaker: Worden
a15_1951404.text: Houston, 15. Pan Camera is in Heater Mode now.

a15_1951404.speaker: Allen
a15_1951404.text: Okay, Al, and on the Map Camera, Image Motion to barber pole, please.

a15_1952820.speaker: Allen
a15_1952820.text: Hello, Endeavour, this is Houston.

a15_1952820.speaker: Worden
a15_1952820.text: Houston, Endeavour. Go ahead. [Pause.]

a15_1952820.speaker: Allen
a15_1952820.text: Roger, Al. I've got what they tell me is the last change to your Flight Plan to put you back on the nominal.

a15_1952820.speaker: Worden
a15_1952820.text: Okay, Joe; stand by just one.

a15_1952820.speaker: Allen
a15_1952820.text: Okay. No hurry.

a15_1952820.speaker: Worden
a15_1952820.text: Okay; Houston; 15. Go ahead with the Flight Plan update. [Long pause.]

a15_1952820.speaker: Allen
a15_1952820.text: Okay, Al. The first change is at 195 plus 36 in your Flight Plan. And it is "Gamma-ray Boom, Deploy, talkback barber pole for about 2 minutes and 40 seconds, then gray, and then to Off. Center position." Over. [Pause.]

a15_1952820.speaker: Worden
a15_1952820.text: Roger, Joe. Understand. At 195:36:00, "Gamma-ray Beam - Boom, Deploy, talkback barber pole about 2 minutes, 40 seconds, then gray, and switch Off."

a15_1952820.speaker: Allen
a15_1952820.text: Okay, Al. That's good, and the next two items are deletes over at 196 plus 31. And that is, delete...

a15_1952820.speaker: Worden
a15_1952820.text: Okay, go ahead.

a15_1952820.speaker: Allen
a15_1952820.text: ...delete "Map Camera/Laser Experiment Covers," et cetera , and delete "Map Cam Track," et cetera , and at 196 plus 37, delete "Laser Altimeter, On." Over. [Pause.]

a15_1952820.speaker: Worden
a15_1952820.text: Roger; understand. At 196:30, delete the 2 lines dealing with the Mapping Camera, and at 196:37 delete the Laser Altimeter function. [Pause.]

a15_1952820.speaker: Allen
a15_1952820.text: Okay, Al, and you're now back on your Flight Plan except for the additional couple of Pan Camera bursts and a Map Camera pass, that you already have copied down. And while I've got you on the line here, I'd like for you to think back yesterday, and I've got a question to ask concerning your suit integrity check. We're trying to go through this and reconstruct exactly what had happened. And I guess what we need is a - a comment about your third suit integrity check. And, that one was the one you did just after the first LM jett had been scrubbed and you went around the back side and did a suit

a15_1952820.speaker: Worden
a15_1952820.text: Okay, understand you're concerned about the second suit integrity check we did. The third one was okay. The suits were - held integrity fine, and we had an O 2 flow of about .6 to .7. So, I guess you're talking about the second one, huh? [Pause.]

a15_1952820.speaker: Gordon
a15_1952820.text: Dave, we're talking about the one you did before the last one, whatever number you call that.

a15_1952820.speaker: Worden
a15_1952820.text: Yes, Dick, that - that was the one we recycled quickly onboard up here, and it was because we had one of the gloves that wasn't fastened on exactly right.

a15_1952820.speaker: Allen
a15_1952820.text: Roger, Al. Map Camera and Laser, Off, please. [Pause.]

a15_1952820.speaker: Worden
a15_1952820.text: Okay, Map Camera and Laser, Off. And, did you understand the comment on the suit integrity check?

a15_1952820.speaker: Allen
a15_1952820.text: Fine, Al. Thank you. That helps us a lot.

a15_1952820.speaker: Worden
a15_1952820.text: Okay.

a15_1952820.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1952820.text: This is Apollo Control at 195 hours, 36 minutes. That last bit of information was for the Environmental Control Systems officer [EECOM] on shift now, who wanted to reconstruct the events of the suit integrity checks yesterday. The - a bad glove on that - bad glove connector prevented a good check on the one they were discussing. They, since that time, did get a good suit integrity check.

a15_1952820.speaker: Allen
a15_1952820.text: And Pan Camera Power, Off, when convenient, please. [Pause.]

a15_1952820.speaker: Worden
a15_1952820.text: Okay, it's Off.

a15_1952820.speaker: Allen
a15_1952820.text: Roger.

a15_1955203.speaker: Allen
a15_1955203.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. You're coming up on LOS in about 2 minutes, and everything's looking just as slick as glass.

a15_1955203.speaker: Worden
a15_1955203.text: Okay, Joe; and, we're just sitting here in [the deep space] attitude, all set to dim the lights and do the gegenschein [photography].

a15_1955203.speaker: Allen
a15_1955203.text: Okay, Al; sounds like fun. Enjoy the back side, and see you in a few minutes. And if there's anything you need from us down here, just give a call. [Pause.]

a15_1955203.speaker: Worden
a15_1955203.text: [Laughter.]

a15_1955203.speaker: Worden
a15_1955203.text: Certainly, Joe.

a15_1955203.speaker: Worden
a15_1955203.text: [Laughter.]

a15_1955203.speaker: Allen
a15_1955203.text: Knew you would.

a15_1955203.speaker: Scott
a15_1955203.text: "Anything you need, give us a call."

a15_1955203.speaker: Worden
a15_1955203.text: [Laughter] Just like we're assigned right behind [garble].

a15_1955203.speaker: Worden
a15_1955203.text: Better check our camera time here.

a15_1955203.speaker: Scott
a15_1955203.text: 153 even is where the Flight Plan calls us.

a15_1955203.speaker: Worden
a15_1955203.text: Go ahead.

a15_1955203.speaker: Scott
a15_1955203.text: Okay, in one minute, Al.

a15_1955203.speaker: Worden
a15_1955203.text: Yes. What frame time?

a15_1955203.speaker: Irwin
a15_1955203.text: One frame, the whole minute.

a15_1955203.speaker: Worden
a15_1955203.text: Yes.

a15_1955203.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1955203.text: This is Apollo Control at 195 hours, 54 minutes. We've had Loss Of Signal on Endeavour . Photography of the lunar surface and orbital science being conducted throughout this revolution. Data from the science experiments coming in good. We'll acquire Endeavour on its 61st revolution at 196 hours, 39 minutes, 20 seconds. At 195 hours, 55 minutes; this is Mission Control, Houston.

a15_1955203.speaker: Scott
a15_1955203.text: Ten seconds.

a15_1955203.speaker: Worden
a15_1955203.text: One in each hand. [Garble] look all right? Okay?

a15_1955203.speaker: Scott
a15_1955203.text: Looks like we're 1 minute and 18 seconds down in the Flight Plan.

a15_1955203.speaker: Worden
a15_1955203.text: Bravo. I want to go get a star mark.

a15_1955203.speaker: Scott
a15_1955203.text: Okay.

a15_1955203.speaker: Worden
a15_1955203.text: Hey. Got coffee?

a15_1955203.speaker: Irwin
a15_1955203.text: Yes.

a15_1955203.speaker: Worden
a15_1955203.text: Yes. [Garble].

a15_1955203.speaker: Scott
a15_1955203.text: Okay, Jim, if you'll give us Free.

a15_1955203.speaker: Worden
a15_1955203.text: And turn the lights off down there.

a15_1955203.speaker: Scott
a15_1955203.text: Can't get used to it. We're getting free light out there.

a15_1964234.speaker: Allen
a15_1964234.text: Roger, Al. Copy. And I've got a TEI-64 PAD when you're ready.

a15_1964234.speaker: Worden
a15_1964234.text: Okay, go ahead with the PAD.

a15_1964234.speaker: Allen
a15_1964234.text: Rog, Alfredo. SPS/G&N for a TEI-64; 36310; plus 0.61, plus 0.92; 204:08:11.62, plus 3011.0, minus 0019.6, plus 0048.8; 180, 102, 002. All the rest NA. Ullage: 4 jet, 12 second. Over.

a15_1964234.speaker: Worden
a15_1964234.text: Roger, Joe. Understand TEI-64, SPS/G&N; 36310; plus 0.61, plus 0.92; 204:08:11.62; plus 3011.0, minus 0019.6, plus 0048.8; 180, 102, 002. The rest is NA. Four jet, 12 seconds.

a15_1965547.speaker: Allen
a15_1965547.text: Endeavour, Houston. [Pause.]

a15_1965547.speaker: Worden
a15_1965547.text: Hello, Houston; Endeavour. Go ahead.

a15_1965547.speaker: Allen
a15_1965547.text: Al, could you give us the Mass Spec. Discriminator switch to Low, please. [Pause.]

a15_1965547.speaker: Worden
a15_1965547.text: Mass Spec. Discriminator to Low.

a15_1965547.speaker: Worden
a15_1965547.text: Yes, I think we have a volunteer for you.

a15_1965547.speaker: Allen
a15_1965547.text: Okay.

a15_1965547.speaker: Irwin
a15_1965547.text: Your volunteer is checking in here, Joe.

a15_1965547.speaker: Allen
a15_1965547.text: Okay, Jim. A quick word on it. Everything per the Flight Plan. We are going to ask you to go ahead and give us your description real-time on the downlink and your choice if you want to push-to-talk or go on to VOX. And then, when you go around the corner you can put it on the DSE like you did before, in High Bit Rate.

a15_1965547.speaker: Worden
a15_1965547.text: Okay, we'll do that, Joe. Stand by. That ought to be good. [Long pause.]

a15_1965547.speaker: Allen
a15_1965547.text: And, Endeavour, you'll be interested to know that the impact of Falcon was picked up on three beautiful seismometers on the Moon. A really remarkable record.

a15_1965547.speaker: Scott
a15_1965547.text: Which ones were they, Joe?

a15_1965547.speaker: Allen
a15_1965547.text: Apparently, they were the ones from Apollos 12, Apollos 14, and Apollos 15. We haven't had reports from other seismometers yet. [Pause.]

a15_1965547.speaker: Scott
a15_1965547.text: That's very interesting.

a15_1965547.speaker: Scott
a15_1965547.text: Tell us, Joe, did they get the LM impact close to where they wanted it? [Pause.]

a15_1965547.speaker: Allen
a15_1965547.text: Roger. It went in to within about a degree and in fact, as you know, it doesn't - the exact point isn't all that important. It - it went in just about where we wanted it, though. [Pause.]

a15_1965547.speaker: Allen
a15_1965547.text: And Al, as soon as you have Noun 79 and you give us Accept, we'll give you a state vector. Over.

a15_1965547.speaker: Worden
a15_1965547.text: Okay, Joe. You have it.

a15_1965547.speaker: Allen
a15_1965547.text: Rog. We see it. Thank you.

a15_1965547.speaker: Irwin
a15_1965547.text: Okay, Joe, I'm ready to start the - experiment.

a15_1965547.speaker: Allen
a15_1965547.text: Okay, Jim, we're copying.

a15_1965547.speaker: Irwin
a15_1965547.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1965547.speaker: Allen
a15_1965547.text: Endeavour, Auto on High Gain, please. [Pause.]

a15_1965547.speaker: Irwin
a15_1965547.text: Rog. Auto.

a15_1965547.speaker: Allen
a15_1965547.text: Al, this is Houston. You can go back into Block. We still need a half a degree deadband. And you can delete two lines in your Flight Plan, one at 197:04 and one at 9 - 197:09, both the "Pan Camera" lines there. Delete them. Over.

a15_1965547.speaker: Worden
a15_1965547.text: Rog, Joe. Understand. Delete the "Pan Camera" lines at 197:04 and 197:09.

a15_1965547.speaker: Allen
a15_1965547.text: Roger. You can Block the computer but we need a half a degree deadband.

a15_1965547.speaker: Worden
a15_1965547.text: Roger, Joe. I've loaded it a couple of times. Let me check it again. [Long pause.]

a15_1965547.speaker: Worden
a15_1965547.text: Okay, Joe. I've got half a degree in. Guess I'm having a hard time counting today.

a15_1965547.speaker: Allen
a15_1965547.text: Thank you, Al. I'm not doing any better.

a15_1965547.speaker: Worden
a15_1965547.text: Rog.

a15_1970827.speaker: Irwin
a15_1970827.text: As long I'm lying here waiting for a flash, I might comment that Dave and I both observed the flashes while we were on the surface, while we were in the bunks down there. We observed the flashes with the - oh, about the same frequency as we observed in orbit. One night there was about a 5-, 10-minute period there where I was awake, and I ran a little experiment by just turning over in the bunk. It seemed like the frequency was much less when I was lying on my stomach as opposed to lying on my back. It's just a - anote of interest.

a15_1970827.speaker: Allen
a15_1970827.text: Okay, Jim. That's a most interesting comment. And as you know, with about 10 minutes to go during the experiment today, we'll ask for you to - to turn over and be oriented with your face away from the Moon, and we might very well get the same sort of information this time.

a15_1970827.speaker: Worden
a15_1970827.text: Okay, Joe. Go with the PAD.

a15_1970827.speaker: Allen
a15_1970827.text: Roger. Pan Camera PAD at 197 plus 16 plus 22. And you're to go to Operate per step 5 in your checklist, page S/1-38. And at 197 plus 18 plus 22, the Pan Camera to Standby. And at 197 plus 40, you can delete the P52 scheduled then. Over.

a15_1970827.speaker: Worden
a15_1970827.text: Roger, Joe. Understand. You want the Pan Camera to - to Operate at 197:16:22 as per the system's checklist 1-38 and to Standby at 197:18:22. And delete the P52 at 197:44 - or - 40.

a15_1970827.speaker: Allen
a15_1970827.text: Right on, Al. Thank you. And, Jim, we're standing by to copy your comments. [Pause.]

a15_1970827.speaker: Allen
a15_1970827.text: And, Jim, this is Houston. We'd like for you to transmit your description as well as the mark call, please.

a15_1970827.speaker: Irwin
a15_1970827.text: Mark. And it was at the left eye; 8 o'clock, and it was a streak, and it seemed to be moving from 8 o'clock to maybe the 1 o'clock position, about - it covered about 20 degrees of arc out to a position - periphery at 8 o'clock into midway on our sphere of reference. An intensity of three. And...

a15_1970827.speaker: Irwin
a15_1970827.text: Mark. I just had a flash at 1 o'clock, moving to the center - the center of - moving toward the 12 o'clock position. It was intensity 3. And that last one was the right eye.

a15_1971613.speaker: Irwin
a15_1971613.text: Mark. A flash at the 12 o'clock, intensity 4.

a15_1971613.speaker: Irwin
a15_1971613.text: That was right down the plus-X axis, Joe. [Pause.]

a15_1971613.speaker: Irwin
a15_1971613.text: Mark. A flash at the 8 o'clock, left eye, periphery, intensity 2. [Long pause.]

a15_1971613.speaker: Allen
a15_1971613.text: Al, Pan Camera Stereo switch to Stereo, please.

a15_1971613.speaker: Allen
a15_1971613.text: Okay, Al. Thank you. That might be a super picture.

a15_1972221.speaker: Allen
a15_1972221.text: Jim, this is Houston. How are the eye flashes coming?

a15_1972654.speaker: Irwin
a15_1972654.text: Mark. A first ray of flash, 10 o'clock, left eye, about three quarters of the way out to the periphery, intensity 5.

a15_1972654.speaker: Irwin
a15_1972654.text: Mark. A streak, at 1 o'clock, moving from the bottom to the top of the - our sphere. Moving - moving definitely vertically up, beginning at 1 o'clock, about three quarters of the way up - intensity 2.

a15_1972958.speaker: Allen
a15_1972958.text: Jim, this is Houston. And we're still listening to you. In the meantime, I've got a Map Camera PAD to give to Al when he's ready. Over.

a15_1972958.speaker: Irwin
a15_1972958.text: Okay, he'll be with you shortly.

a15_1972958.speaker: Worden
a15_1972958.text: Yeah. Hold on, Joe. We're going over the Harbinger Mountains and right over the Aristarchus Plateau right now. And Dave and I are looking like mad and taking pictures.

a15_1972958.speaker: Allen
a15_1972958.text: Fine, Alfredo. When you get back to me, I'll give you this other PAD. It's got to be within the next 15 minutes though.

a15_1972958.speaker: Worden
a15_1972958.text: Okay, Joe. No problem, we're about done. [Long pause.]

a15_1972958.speaker: Irwin
a15_1972958.text: Mark. Flash at, seems like it was in both eyes, at about the 7 o'clock position, one quarter of the way out the periphery, intensity 5.

a15_1972958.speaker: Worden
a15_1972958.text: Houston, 15. Ready to copy the PAD.

a15_1972958.speaker: Allen
a15_1972958.text: Roger, Al. At 198 plus 25, [pause] go to narrow deadband in P20; Verb 22, Noun 79, plus 000.50. Open Cover and Extend Map Camera, per steps 3 and 4 in your checklist. 198 plus 31, Map Camera Image Motion, On. 198 plus 32 plus 10, Map Camera, On; Image Motion, increase, barber pole plus 4 steps; Laser Altimeter, On. 199 plus 19, Image Motion, increase, talkback barber pole. 199 plus 31 plus 56, Map Camera, Off; Laser Altimeter, Off; wait 30 seconds then Map Camera, On - That - that should read, Map Camera, On, to Standby; and then Retract and Close Cover, per steps 7,8 - 7 and 8 in the checklis

a15_1972958.speaker: Worden
a15_1972958.text: Roger, Houston. Copy. At 198:15, go narrow deadband at P20. Open Mapping Camera Covers and Extend the Mapping Camera. At 198:31 plus 00, Mapping Camera, On. - Oh, I'm sorry, Image Motion, On. And 198 plus 32 plus 10, Mapping Camera, On; Image Motion to barber pole plus 4; and Laser Altimeter, On. At 199:19:00, Image Motion to barber pole. At 199:31:56, Mapping Camera, Off; Laser, Off; wait 30 seconds, Mapping Camera to Standby - No, that's Retract and Close Covers.

a15_1972958.speaker: Allen
a15_1972958.text: That's correct, Al; and you can delete those three lines at 199 plus 30. And - and there's a note that goes with this, that this particular pass will be taken with the Gamma[-ray] experiment and the Mass Spec. experiment booms extended. So don't worry about the fact they're out. One number you gave to me, the first one, should be 198 plus 25, go to narrow deadband. Over.

a15_1972958.speaker: Worden
a15_1972958.text: Roger. 198:25. That's what I had written. [I] read it wrong.

a15_1972958.speaker: Irwin
a15_1972958.text: Okay, Joe. During that conversation, I saw two - both at 8 o'clock. First one was three-quarters of the way out, intensity 2. The last one was at intensity 3, about halfway out, appeared to be at left eye.

a15_1974415.speaker: Irwin
a15_1974415.text: Mark. Flash at center, plus-X, intensity 2.

a15_1974633.speaker: Irwin
a15_1974633.text: Mark. Flash, left eye, 9 o'clock, on the periphery, intensity 5.

a15_1974633.speaker: Allen
a15_1974633.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_1974633.speaker: Scott
a15_1974633.text: Well, we ought to be able to tell in an hour.

a15_1974633.speaker: Irwin
a15_1974633.text: Okay.

a15_1974633.speaker: Scott
a15_1974633.text: The what? Oh, yes. Okay?

a15_1974633.speaker: Irwin
a15_1974633.text: Joe, how's the time going on my one hour?

a15_1974633.speaker: Allen
a15_1974633.text: Okay, Jim. My sand dial shows about 15 minutes remaining. You'll be going around the corner LOS shortly. We don't have any more instructions for you on the experiment or in fact on anything else going on. We would like your present - a description of your present position in the spacecraft. And, we'd like for you to remain in that position for the rest of the 15 minutes in the experiment. Over.

a15_1974633.speaker: Irwin
a15_1974633.text: [Garble].

a15_1974633.speaker: Scott
a15_1974633.text: We are, Jim. I got it hot for you. Don't worry, pal, we won't forget you.

a15_1974633.speaker: Irwin
a15_1974633.text: Okay, understand you don't want me to turn over.

a15_1974633.speaker: Irwin
a15_1974633.text: I'll bet you [garble].

a15_1974633.speaker: Scott
a15_1974633.text: No. I think he's right here.

a15_1974633.speaker: Scott
a15_1974633.text: Neuter? Okay, that spaghetti is mine. Hamburger wet pack. Pea soup, ham and salad, applesauce, cheese crackers. Brack!

a15_1974633.speaker: Scott
a15_1974633.text: Blach! Does it look like it, Jim?

a15_1974633.speaker: Irwin
a15_1974633.text: Yes.

a15_1974633.speaker: Scott
a15_1974633.text: You say it looks like it, Jim?

a15_1974633.speaker: Irwin
a15_1974633.text: No.

a15_1974633.speaker: Allen
a15_1974633.text: Okay, Jim, copied that and that's correct. Just - just stay in your present position, and we'll see you on the other side.

a15_1974633.speaker: Worden
a15_1974633.text: You got eyes, they're almost 20 - 20, so - (laughter) Okay, it's a...

a15_1974633.speaker: Irwin
a15_1974633.text: Okay.

a15_1974633.speaker: Scott
a15_1974633.text: I think it's time to raid you. I want to make sure they get it all down - down on the - on the file there.

a15_1975220.speaker: Irwin
a15_1975220.text: May be, David. The empty ones, you mean. Oh, that's what you're talking about. Empty one. Yes. Yes. A-2.

a15_1975220.speaker: Scott
a15_1975220.text: Okay, Jimmy, you got 8 minutes to go.

a15_1975220.speaker: Scott
a15_1975220.text: Hey, listen. You - you - you're bugging me a little bit. If you're going - if you're going to exercise, you ought to at least have the decency to put your biomed on (laughter). There's no sense wasting all that on us. Let the doc see it.

a15_1975220.speaker: Scott
a15_1975220.text: Ooh, applesauce. Their applesauce is good stuff.

a15_1984115.speaker: Allen
a15_1984115.text: Hello, Endeavour. This is Houston requesting Reacq and Narrow. [Long pause.]

a15_1984115.speaker: Allen
a15_1984115.text: Okay, Al, thank you very much. Some time during this pass, we're going to be requesting an ISA [Interim Stowage Assembly] weight which you have in your Lunar Surface Checklist, page 3-2. And we'll have a Map Camera and a Pan Camera PAD to send up to you. [Long pause.]

a15_1984115.speaker: Worden
a15_1984115.text: Okay, Joe. That all sounds very good. [Long pause.]

a15_1984115.speaker: Allen
a15_1984115.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. We're showing your Mapping Camera not on at this time and are requesting it on. It may be just to reverify from your 198 plus 32 plus 10 on the Flight Plan. Over.

a15_1990846.speaker: Allen
a15_1990846.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. We copy the Gamma-ray Gainstep, Shield, On. And Al, we have photo PADs to you when you're ready to copy. Over.

a15_1990846.speaker: Allen
a15_1990846.text: Okay. In your Flight Plan, at 199:20, you can strike PCM Cable, unless your relativistic speed has managed to lengthen that cable, I guess. At 199:25, you can strike the 3 lines "CMC Mode, Verb 22, and CMC Mode." And, then I have a PAD for you at 200 plus 20, when you're ready. [Pause.]

a15_1990846.speaker: Worden
a15_1990846.text: Rog. Go ahead with the PAD at 200:20.

a15_1990846.speaker: Allen
a15_1990846.text: Okay, Al. At this time, it's a camera configuration for terminator photos that we missed a little earlier. And the lines should read "CM4/EL/250/VHBW, IVL, f/5.6 at 1/125th, infinity, six frames, Mag Romeo." Over. [Pause.]

a15_1990846.speaker: Worden
a15_1990846.text: Rog, Joe. Understand. Terminator photo PAD at 200 plus 20 is CM4/EL/250/VHBW, and that's with the intervalometer, IVL, at f/5.6, 1/125th, infinity, six frames and Mag R.

a15_1990846.speaker: Allen
a15_1990846.text: Readback's correct, Al. And, the next entry is at - 200 plus 25, which is open the Map Camera covers and extend the camera per page S/1-39. And, at that time, Map Camera, Image Motion to On. And then, coming up to the time 200 plus 27 plus 56, EL On; and 200 plus 29 plus 36. EL Off. At the time 200 plus 30 plus 36, Map Camera, On; Image Motion, Increase; talkback to barber pole, plus 4 steps; Laser Altimeter to On; Pan Camera Mode to Standby, Power, On; Stereo, Exposure, Normal. Over. [Pause.]

a15_1990846.speaker: Worden
a15_1990846.text: Roger, Joe. At 200 plus 25, open Mapping Camera covers and extend the Mapping Camera. Turn the Image Motion, On. At 275 - 200:27:56, EL On, and at 29:36, EL Off. At 30:36 Mapping Camera, On; Image Motion to barber pole, plus four; and Laser, On. And then Pan Camera, Standby, Power, On; Stereo, Exposure, Normal.

a15_1990846.speaker: Allen
a15_1990846.text: That's correct, Al. And continuing on through a few more steps here, and I'll read them all, and then stand by for your readback. 200 plus 33 plus 29, Pan Camera, Mode to Operate. 200 plus 49 plus 32, Pan Camera to Mono. 200 plus 54 plus 27, Pan Camera, Stereo. 200 plus 59 plus 22, Pan Camera, Mode, Standby; Pan Camera, Power to Off on MSFN cue. And, moving right along, 201 plus 17 plus 00, Pan Camera, Image Motion, Increase. I'm sorry, Al. That was misread. That should be Map Camera, Image Motion to Increase; talkback barber pole. 201 plus 28 plus 21, EL On. 201 plus 30 plus 01, EL Off. 201 p

a15_1990846.speaker: Worden
a15_1990846.text: Roger, Joe. Understand at 201:17:00, Mapping Camera, Image Motion, Increase to barber pole; at 201:28:21, EL On; at 201:30:01, EL Off; 201:32:00, Off. No, back to 30:01, after EL Off, read Map Camera, Off; Laser, Off. And, at 201:32:00, retract and close the Mapping Camera covers.

a15_1990846.speaker: Allen
a15_1990846.text: Okay, Al. And read back to me 4 more lines, beginning with 200 plus 33 plus 29. You didn't go back quite far enough, and that - that one should read Pan Camera, Mode to Operate.

a15_1990846.speaker: Worden
a15_1990846.text: Roger. At - at 33 - at 200:33:29, Pan Camera to Operate. At 49:32, Pan Camera to Mono. At 54:27, Pan to Stereo. And, at 59:22 Pan to Standby; Power, Off, on MSFN cue. [Long pause.]

a15_1990846.speaker: Allen
a15_1990846.text: Okay, Al. Sounds real good. But double check for me one line, which I may have goofed. It's the 201 plus 30 plus 21, Map Camera, Off; Laser Altimeter, Off. [Pause.]

a15_1990846.speaker: Worden
a15_1990846.text: Roger, Joe. Understand. At 201:30:21, that's 20 seconds after EL Off, we get the Mapping Camera, Off and the Laser, Off.

a15_1990846.speaker: Allen
a15_1990846.text: Yes sir, that's affirmative. And, I guess - we're still waiting for an ISA weight. Other than that, we're doing real fine.

a15_1991910.speaker: Allen
a15_1991910.text: Go. [Pause.] Go ahead, Al. And, we're waiting for a Image Motion talkback to barber pole.

a15_1991910.speaker: Worden
a15_1991910.text: Okay. Dave's going to get the ISA weight out for you and call you.

a15_1991910.speaker: Allen
a15_1991910.text: Okay. If he's able to weigh it right there, I'd like to know how he's going to do it. I assume he's got it written down, though.

a15_1991910.speaker: Worden
a15_1991910.text: He's got it written down. He just has to get it out.

a15_1992247.speaker: Irwin
a15_1992247.text: Yes, Joe. I have weight information on the ISA. The ISA total was 64 pounds, which includes bags 4 and 6, and 8 pounds return items. And the ISA, by itself, without anything loaded in it, was 8 pounds. Over.

a15_1992247.speaker: Allen
a15_1992247.text: Okay, Jim, copied that. Sounds like there might be a stone or two in there. [Pause.]

a15_1992847.speaker: Parker
a15_1992847.text: Apollo 15. We'd like Gamma-ray Shield, On, please. [Pause.]

a15_1992847.speaker: Scott
a15_1992847.text: Roger, Dr. Parker. Shield, On. [Long pause.]

a15_1992847.speaker: Parker
a15_1992847.text: And, 15. Time to start the terminator [photography] now.

a15_1993427.speaker: Parker
a15_1993427.text: Apollo 15, Houston. If you have a chance, we'd like to talk to Dave and Jim about this LCG connector problem some time.

a15_1993427.speaker: Scott
a15_1993427.text: Okay, stand by.

a15_1993427.speaker: Parker
a15_1993427.text: And Auto on High Gain [Antenna], please.

a15_1993427.speaker: Scott
a15_1993427.text: Auto. [Long pause.]

a15_1993427.speaker: Scott
a15_1993427.text: Houston, 15. Go. [Pause.]

a15_1993427.speaker: Parker
a15_1993427.text: 15. Two questions we'd like to ask. First one's specific, and that is, if you noticed anything about the connector between the LCG and the suit when you took it out in order to put the plugs in yesterday afternoon. Was it already out? Was it loose? Was it not lock-locked? Or what? And secondly, a general question building up from this. Can you tell us anything - any insights you acquired in taking the suits off and looking at the connector or just, in general, about what this problem may have been caused by? [Pause.]

a15_1993427.speaker: Scott
a15_1993427.text: Well, I guess - I guess our first indication was lack of a good integrity check. As a matter of fact, we couldn't get much more than about a pound in the suit. And the first - In thinking it over, we - we thought the only thing it could be would be those connectors, because that was the on - only semi-open port, even though it shouldn't - shouldn't be leaking. And, everybody checked their helmet and gloves and they appeared to be locked, so we broke open the helmet and gloves and Jim reached in through my zipper and pulled out the LCG connector and stuck in the plug. And then we rezipped, or I

a15_1993427.speaker: Parker
a15_1993427.text: Roger. Did Jim notice when you - when Jim took out your connector there, to put the plug in, did he notice it as being loose, unattached, or not lock-locked? Did he have any - could he tell any of that just reaching in with his fingers? [Pause.]

a15_1993427.speaker: Irwin
a15_1993427.text: Bob, this is Jim. The lock-lock was engaged on that water connector on Dave's suit.

a15_1993427.speaker: Parker
a15_1993427.text: Okay, copy. And do we understand that Dave's suit was the only one that did not pass the integrity check that first time around?

a15_1993427.speaker: Scott
a15_1993427.text: No. You can't isolate it. The whole suit circuit is the integrity check. It's spacecraft plus three suits. So, there's no way to tell.

a15_1993427.speaker: Parker
a15_1993427.text: Roger. But on - what I mean is that you did not put - did you put plugs in Jim's suit, too, or just in Dave's suit?

a15_1993427.speaker: Scott
a15_1993427.text: No, only - only in one suit. But we did go through the operation of taking off helmets and gloves, which also may have been the problem.

a15_1993427.speaker: Parker
a15_1993427.text: Roger. Copy that.

a15_1993427.speaker: Scott
a15_1993427.text: In - in other words, there may have - even though we checked the lock-locks on the helmets and gloves, why, somebody could have had a cocked one and - and missed it. These - es - especially the - the surface equipment was - had an - an awful lot of lunar dust on it, and it's sort of hard to work. We're - we're going to get them cleaned up before the EVA, but after three runs down there, why, the connectors were getting pretty tough to work, even though we did lubricate them.

a15_1993427.speaker: Parker
a15_1993427.text: Roger. Copy. I don't think we have anything else, Dave. We noticed you did seem to have some trouble getting a suit integrity check the second time around, also. Is that right?

a15_1993427.speaker: Scott
a15_1993427.text: Yeah. There was a glove that wasn't locked.

a15_1993427.speaker: Parker
a15_1993427.text: Okay, guess I wasn't on the loop. Thanks. [Long pause.]

a15_1993427.speaker: Scott
a15_1993427.text: I think the suit circuit's tight. I think that just might have just been one of those things, because the last one we ran was real good. It - the flow dropped down to like 6 or 7 tenths, I guess, and it would have stayed there all day long. I think we've got a good suit loop, but - I'm not worried about that at all. Just a matter of getting all the connectors cleaned up so they all work well, and ensuring that everybody gets a good lock-lock.

a15_1993427.speaker: Parker
a15_1993427.text: Rog, Dave. We agree too. I - it seems to us that that sounds like it was just one of those situations we run a suit integrity check for.

a15_1993427.speaker: Scott
a15_1993427.text: Rog. That's exactly right.

a15_1994949.speaker: Parker
a15_1994949.text: And, 15; Houston. You're Go for LOS. [Pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Worden
a15_2004614.text: Hello, Houston; this is Endeavour.

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Rog. We got the usual Flight Plan updates, if you'll get a Flight Plan out and copy them in, please. [Pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Worden
a15_2004614.text: Okay; stand by one.

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Okay; and if someone could give us High Gain Antenna to Auto, we'd appreciate it. [Long pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Worden
a15_2004614.text: Go ahead with the update.

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Okay. First one is the UV photo plan at - PAD at 201:05 in the Flight Plan. The T-start for that will be 201:11:19. Over.

a15_2004614.speaker: Worden
a15_2004614.text: Understand. UV T-start 201:11:19.

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Roger. Next, at 201:20, we will delete "PCM cable." [Pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Worden
a15_2004614.text: Okay; got that.

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Roger. At 202:30, it's Discriminator, Low, in that line on the Mass Spec. [Pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Worden
a15_2004614.text: Okay. Discriminator, Low, at 202:30.

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Roger. At 203:21, we will delete "Laser Altimeter, Off." [Pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Worden
a15_2004614.text: Understand. Delete "Laser Altimeter, Off" at 203:21, and let's hold up on the rest for now. [Long pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: And 15, 30 seconds to Pan Camera, Mono. [Long pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Scott
a15_2004614.text: Hey, go with the rest of the updates, Bob.

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Okay. At 203:23, we'll delete the "Mapping Camera Track, Retract, talkback barber pole, 4 minutes, gray then Off, center;" that whole line. [Long pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Scott
a15_2004614.text: Okay; that's deleted. Next. [Pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: And we want Pan Camera, Mono, please. [Pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Scott
a15_2004614.text: It's there.

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Roger; sorry.

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Okay; 203:27, we'll delete "Mapping Camera/Laser Experiment, Covers, Closed, talkback barber pole, grey then Off, center;" et cetera . That whole line there. 203:27. [Pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Scott
a15_2004614.text: Okay. Next?

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Okay; now we have here a little test the guys down here would like to run with the Laser [Altimeter] to see if we can zap it a little bit and rejuvenate it, perhaps. The first step is back on 201:30. We will delete the "Laser Altimeter, Off" and "Mapping Cover/Laser Altimeter Cover, Close." At 201 plus 30. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Scott
a15_2004614.text: Are you making an update to the update?

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Stand by here. Stand by a minute.

a15_2004614.speaker: Scott
a15_2004614.text: Okay; I didn't exactly find that one.

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Yeah, stand by. I got to check with OSO.

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Okay, 15. We got a clarification on that. The "Laser Altimeter, Off" is at 201:30. The "Mapping Camera/Laser Altimeter Cover, Close" is called out at 201:32. And we want to delete both of those.

a15_2004614.speaker: Scott
a15_2004614.text: Stand by, Bob. We're taking pictures. We'll come back to you.

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: Yeah, give me a call. [Long pause.]

a15_2004614.speaker: Parker
a15_2004614.text: And 30 seconds to Pan Camera, Stereo.

a15_2005533.speaker: Worden
a15_2005533.text: Okay, Houston; 15. Go ahead with some updates, if you've got them.

a15_2005533.speaker: Parker
a15_2005533.text: Okay, Al. Did you copy? What we're doing is we're changing that update, deleting the Laser Altimeter, Off at 201:30. And then, we're also deleting at 201:32, the callout to "Close the Mapping Camera/Laser Altimeter Cover." Over. [Pause.]

a15_2005533.speaker: Worden
a15_2005533.text: Okay; I understand. At 201:30, you want the Laser Altimeter left On, and the Mapping Camera left out and the Covers, Open.

a15_2005533.speaker: Parker
a15_2005533.text: That's affirm. Okay; now after the Mapping...

a15_2005533.speaker: Parker
a15_2005533.text: That's affirm. And now, after the Mapping Camera is Off at 201:30, we want to cycle the Laser switch Off for 1 second, then On for 15 seconds, Off for 1 second, On for 15 seconds, et cetera , for 20 cycles. And after 20 cycles, we will leave the Laser Altimeter, On, for MSFN analysis. Over. [Long pause.]

a15_2005533.speaker: Worden
a15_2005533.text: Okay; understand. You want at 201:30 - you want to cycle the Laser Altimeter, Off for 1 second and On 15 seconds, for 20 seconds [correcting himself] for 20 cycles, and then leave it turned on.

a15_2005533.speaker: Parker
a15_2005533.text: That's a Roger, and we'll get back to you at that point. [Pause.]

a15_2005533.speaker: Parker
a15_2005533.text: And that's all we have for right now, Al. [Pause.]

a15_2005533.speaker: Parker
a15_2005533.text: And, Al, 30 seconds to Pan Camera, Standby, Power, Off.

a15_2010108.speaker: Parker
a15_2010108.text: And, 15, we verify the Pan Camera lens is stowed. When convenient, we'd like Battery B Charge - Battery Bravo Charge terminated.

a15_2010616.speaker: Parker
a15_2010616.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. One more request, please.

a15_2010616.speaker: Parker
a15_2010616.text: Rog. Since we don't have the PCM cable, we'd like to, for these UV photos, to have you give us a mark each time you press the shutter button, please, on the air-to-ground.

a15_2010616.speaker: Worden
a15_2010616.text: Okay, Bob. Would you like me to hook up the PCM cable to it?

a15_2010616.speaker: Parker
a15_2010616.text: Well, the word that I was given down here was that you couldn't reach with the PCM cable.

a15_2010616.speaker: Worden
a15_2010616.text: No, we're taking - we're taking the pictures out of window 5, and that's where the scientific instrument outlet is.

a15_2010616.speaker: Parker
a15_2010616.text: Stand by. [Pause.] 15, if you can do that, that's fine.

a15_2010616.speaker: Worden
a15_2010616.text: Okay; I'll tell you what, Bob. I'll go ahead and hook up the PCM cable, and - and you tell me if you're getting a signal down there after I start taking pictures.

a15_2010616.speaker: Worden
a15_2010616.text: And the word you got on it was - was correct. It looks like window 5's about the only window that can be used for the PCM cable.

a15_2010616.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2010616.text: The ultraviolet photography, which the crew is preparing to perform in about 2 minutes, is done with the Hasselblad electric camera, mounted on a special window bracket. The purpose of the experiment is to obtain ultraviolet photographs of the Earth and the Moon, and these will be used in a study of planetary atmospheres. They'll also be used for investigation of short wavelength radiation from the lunar surface.

a15_2010616.speaker: Parker
a15_2010616.text: And, Endeavour, we won't be able to see that PCM real time, but we'll just assume that it's coming down if you've got the PCM cable hooked up.

a15_2010616.speaker: Worden
a15_2010616.text: Okay, Bob. I got it hooked up. [Long pause.]

a15_2011811.speaker: Worden
a15_2011811.text: Houston, 15.

a15_2011811.speaker: Parker
a15_2011811.text: Go ahead, 15.

a15_2011811.speaker: Worden
a15_2011811.text: Okay, Bob. When we took the - the shade out of window 5, window 5 still appears very clean.

a15_2011811.speaker: Parker
a15_2011811.text: Copy. [Long pause.]

a15_2011811.speaker: Parker
a15_2011811.text: And, Endeavour, two questions if you've got a chance, between now and the terminator photos.

a15_2011811.speaker: Worden
a15_2011811.text: Say again on the terminator photos, Bob.

a15_2011811.speaker: Parker
a15_2011811.text: Rog. Do you have time for a couple of questions, between now and the start of the terminator photos.

a15_2011811.speaker: Worden
a15_2011811.text: Yes, sure. Go ahead.

a15_2011811.speaker: Parker
a15_2011811.text: Roger. First, any comments on the Mass Spec. boom retraction you did a half hour ago.

a15_2011811.speaker: Worden
a15_2011811.text: No, no comments on it. And - I guess we're back to the position we were in before, that the thing is sort of half barber pole. And when I go back out with it - fiddle with it a little bit, the barber pole goes full up and then comes down about halfway again.

a15_2011811.speaker: Parker
a15_2011811.text: Okay; we copy.

a15_2011811.speaker: Worden
a15_2011811.text: And that's where it stands right now.

a15_2011811.speaker: Parker
a15_2011811.text: Okay. Second question...

a15_2011811.speaker: Worden
a15_2011811.text: I played with it for a while, and then got busy in other things. But I'll continue - I'll continue working on it.

a15_2011811.speaker: Parker
a15_2011811.text: Copy, Al. Second question, do you want me to continue giving the - you these real time marks on air - air-to-ground, just before and after various camera passes? [Pause.]

a15_2011811.speaker: Worden
a15_2011811.text: Yeah, I like the reminder, Bob.

a15_2011811.speaker: Parker
a15_2011811.text: Okay; 30 seconds...

a15_2011811.speaker: Worden
a15_2011811.text: Don't expect an answer, I'll probably be busy doing it.

a15_2011811.speaker: Parker
a15_2011811.text: Hopefully. 30 seconds a good time?

a15_2011811.speaker: Worden
a15_2011811.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_2011811.speaker: Worden
a15_2011811.text: And, Houston; 15.

a15_2011811.speaker: Parker
a15_2011811.text: Go ahead. [Pause.] 15, go ahead.

a15_2011811.speaker: Worden
a15_2011811.text: Okay; for your info, the Mass Spec. took about - oh, maybe 7 or 8 cycles this time, before it came all the way in. And the same operation as before.

a15_2011811.speaker: Parker
a15_2011811.text: Roger; copy. It took you 7 or 8 cycles to get it all the way in.

a15_2013003.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2013003.text: This is Apollo Control. The crew has now completed the photography of the terminator using the electric Hasselblad camera and also the Mapping Camera in the Scientific Instrument Module bay. We're standing by now for them to begin a procedure which we hope will possibly solve the problem with the Laser Altimeter. About 35 or 40 minutes ago, we asked the crew to...

a15_2013216.speaker: Parker
a15_2013216.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. Be advised, we like an accurate 15 seconds, On; 1 second, Off. No more than 16 or 17 seconds, On.

a15_2013216.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2013216.text: What Al Worden is doing is cycling the switch on the Laser Altimeter on and then off. And it'll do this 20 times. The hope is that in cycling the switch it will cause a particular circuit in the laser altimeter to fail. This circuit is used to discharge high voltage from some of the components and in discharging the voltage, it's thought that perhaps we're introducing some noise into the altimeter which is in turn causing the intermittent flow of data from that particular instrument.

a15_2013814.speaker: Parker
a15_2013814.text: And, 15. Roger; thank you. Unfortunately, like everything else, the Laser didn't do much good. We'd like now, Mapping Camera to Standby; Laser Altimeter, Off. Then we'll do the Retract and Door Close. Over.

a15_2013814.speaker: Worden
a15_2013814.text: Okay, Bob. We'll go Mapping Camera, Off and Laser, Off.

a15_2013814.speaker: Parker
a15_2013814.text: We need Mapping Camera, Standby, please.

a15_2013814.speaker: Worden
a15_2013814.text: Roger; Standby, and Image Motion, Off, and Laser Altimeter, Off. And retracting the - retracting the camera now.

a15_2014705.speaker: Parker
a15_2014705.text: Roger, Al. If you could get us a film budget status on the backside to give us when you come around, we'd appreciate it. And except for that, you're Go for LOS.

a15_2014705.speaker: Worden
a15_2014705.text: All righty. Thank you, sir. And we'll see if we can conjure one up for you.

a15_2014705.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2014705.text: This is Apollo Control. We're now about 1 minute, 15 seconds from losing radio contact with Endeavour. On the next revolution, the crew will be eating and then we plan to put them to bed.

a15_2024000.speaker: Parker
a15_2024000.text: Roger, if you - Roger, if you guys give us an Accept, we'll send you up a state vector and time uplink. [Pause.]

a15_2024000.speaker: Parker
a15_2024000.text: Copy. [Pause.] And if you fellows will give me a call in the middle of your eating there, when you got time, we'll do some talking at you.

a15_2024000.speaker: Scott
a15_2024000.text: Okay, give us about five minutes here.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: And 15, its your computer. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Houston, Endeavour. We're ready to chitty-chat, if you like.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Okay. While you guys are eating your supper there, it might be a good time to get a report on your food so far. How's it been going?

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Oh, I think we have consumed every meal as planned and we've made a pretty good cut into the pantry.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: You've made a pretty good cut into the pantry, you say?

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Rog. That extra little box over there with extra little goodies.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Okay, and can you guys give us any estimates on the water that you and Jim consumed on the surface, say in the LM and on the EVA, and any differences between this and what Al's been consuming? [Pause.]

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Not without sitting down and doing some thinking about it. We'd be glad to do that, if you like.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Roger. If that's not too much trouble, I guess we could start out by some estimate as to how much you guys were drinking in the LM and on the EVA. Was the drink bag adequate, or what?

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Oh, I think that's probably a good discussion for the debriefing after the flight. [Pause.]

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Okay. Sounds like you are at least eating and drinking a lot so far. We are anxious for you all to continue eating and drinking well, because of the EVA yet to come.

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Oh, okay. Well if that's your - your interest, yes, we - we consumed quite a bit of water on the surface, and we were quite satisfied with what we had. We had plenty. And we've been eating and drinking a lot up here. I think everybody is in fine shape and ready to take care of what's on - on the Flight Plan the rest of the way.

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: No, there's been no medication taken by anybody on the flight.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Okay. However, I - we down here would like to recommend for all three of you to take one tonight just to make sure we get another good night's sleep.

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: I think that's unnecessary.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Well, that's our recommendation anyway. And can you tell us who plans to sensor up tonight, Dave.

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Okay. Rog. I guess as per our agreement this morning, why - you'll get CMP and a LMP tonight.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Roger; understand. And then we'll press on with the normal Flight Plan tomorrow. [Pause.] And, Al, we'd like to have you - you wear the lightweight headset tonight, because then, we'd like to wake just Al up on schedule so he can do us a P20 to - give us some plus-X time on the Mass Spec. And so we'd like to - arrange it that way, if its convenient with you guys.

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: No, I don't think that's practical, Bob. You can't have one person awake in here and the other two sleeping. It - just can't do it.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Okay; understand. And to avoid what we had last night with all those last minute calls again and again and again, why don't you guys give us a final call just before you're ready to go to sleep. We'll get a final status down here, and then we won't - we won't have to keep calling back tonight.

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Oh, that's a good idea. All right. We'll do that.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: It got a little embarrassing down here after a while. [Pause.]

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Oh, that's okay. Yesterday was a long day.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Roger that. And we got a TEI-69 PAD down here, when Jim's ready to copy. And we're also ready to copy some torquing angles from that P52, if you got them. And we'd like you to leave your High Gain Antenna at plus 25 and 185 on Yaw and in Narrow and Reacquire as you go around the corner this time.

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Oh, okay. You want Narrow, Reacquire and plus 25 and 185. We'll do that. If you're ready to copy, I've got the P52.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Roger. I'll copy that now.

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Okay. Noun 05 was .01; Noun 93 was plus .07, minus .47, minus .05. They were torqued out at 202:00:30.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Roger. Copy .01, plus .07, minus .47, minus .05, and 202:00:30.

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Rog. That's cricket. [Pause.]

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: And, Dave, we'd like Optic, Zero, at this time, please.

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Oh, yes, Optic, Zero. Hey, by the way, I - I should have said .007. Pardon me. I had my decimal point in the wrong spot.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Understand .007. And was the...

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Just - just put a zero in front of all - the three torquing numbers. The - the platform is too good and the numbers are so small we - we're not even thinking in three digits anymore.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Okay. We've got 007, 047, and 005. Understand.

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: That's correct. [Long pause.]

a15_2024317.speaker: Irwin
a15_2024317.text: Okay, Bob. I'm ready to copy the PAD.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Okay, Jim. It's TEI-69, SPS/G&N; plus 36245; plus 0.61, plus 0.92; 213:51:51.04; plus 2803.1, minus 0465.4, minus 0099.6; 179, 132, 353. The rest of the PAD is NA. Ullage; 4 jets, 12 seconds. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2024317.speaker: Irwin
a15_2024317.text: Okay. Readback for TEI is SPS/G&N...

a15_2024317.speaker: Irwin
a15_2024317.text: You read me better? Bob, are you reading me okay?

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: You've got a loud squeal there, Jim, but I can probably read you. [Pause.]

a15_2024317.speaker: Irwin
a15_2024317.text: Okay, Bob. Here's the readback. SPS/G&N; 36245; plus 0.61, plus 0.92; 213:51:51.04; plus 2803.1, minus 0465.4, minus 0099.6; 179, 132, 353; 4 jets for 12 seconds. Over.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Roger, Jim; copy. Good readback. [Pause.] And, Endeavour, that's all we've got for you right now, until you give us a presleep call, except for standing by for a film budget report from Al. [Long pause.]

a15_2024317.speaker: Worden
a15_2024317.text: Houston, 15.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Go. Go, 15.

a15_2024317.speaker: Worden
a15_2024317.text: Okay, Bob. I've got that film thing compiled for you, if you want to copy.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Copying.

a15_2024317.speaker: Worden
a15_2024317.text: Okay. I will read you frames expended. Magazine Nectar 76, Oscar 58, Romeo 55, Victor 12. And I haven't used anything out of S, and L is running right now on the Mass Spec.

a15_2024317.speaker: Parker
a15_2024317.text: Roger; copy. 76, 58, 55 and 12. [Pause.] Thank you guys. Give us a call when you're ready for sleep and we'll tuck you in.

a15_2024317.speaker: Scott
a15_2024317.text: Okay, Bobby. Love to have you do that.

a15_2030558.speaker: Parker
a15_2030558.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. We'd like Pan Camera, Standby. [Pause.]

a15_2030558.speaker: Worden
a15_2030558.text: Okay, Bob. Roger on the Standby. [Long pause.]

a15_2030558.speaker: Scott
a15_2030558.text: Houston, the Pan Camera was on Standby.

a15_2030558.speaker: Scott
a15_2030558.text: I say - the Pan Camera already was in Standby.

a15_2030558.speaker: Parker
a15_2030558.text: Okay. We'll have them check again. [Long pause.]

a15_2030558.speaker: Parker
a15_2030558.text: Okay, Dave. What we'd like is Power, On, also Pan Camera Power, On, for 5 minutes.

a15_2031147.speaker: Parker
a15_2031147.text: And, Endeavour; this is Houston. We can go Pan Camera Power, Off, now.

a15_2032003.speaker: Scott
a15_2032003.text: Houston, Endeavour. Did you get the E-Mod dump?

a15_2032731.speaker: Parker
a15_2032731.text: Endeavour, Houston. It's not clear that we got it the first time. Why don't you give us another E-Mod dump again, please? [Pause.]

a15_2033959.speaker: Parker
a15_2033959.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. We [garble] at the LOS in about 2 minutes. Everything looks in configuration for sleep. We'd like to verify the Oxygen Heaters are Auto, Auto, Off. Except for that, you are Go for sleep and Go for LOS.

a15_2033959.speaker: Scott
a15_2033959.text: Okay; understand. And we're fixing to give you the presleep checklist, there. And we have a little unscheduled maintenance on our friendly water valve again. So we'll be about 10 more minutes, but it's under control. Same - same problem we had before.

a15_2033959.speaker: Parker
a15_2033959.text: Rog. And understand it's under control.

a15_2033959.speaker: Scott
a15_2033959.text: Yeah, it's just - just the same thing worked loose again, and we're cinching it down.

a15_2033959.speaker: Parker
a15_2033959.text: Roger. We copy. You guys didn't strike a coral reef there, did you?

a15_2033959.speaker: Scott
a15_2033959.text: [Laughter] No, I don't think so. [Long pause.]

a15_2033959.speaker: Scott
a15_2033959.text: Okay. O 2 hea - O 2 - O 2 heaters are going to Auto, Auto, Off.

a15_2111600.speaker: Henize
a15_2111600.text: Apollo 15. [No answer.]

a15_2111600.speaker: Henize
a15_2111600.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston. Good morning. Apollo 15, this is Houston with a message from Richard Strauss, Arthur C. Clarke and Stanley Kubrick.

a15_2111600.speaker: Henize
a15_2111600.text: Good morning, fellows. We have only about 10 minutes of comm left and we'd like to start out the morning with an Accept so we can send you up a state vector. Are you up there? [No answer.]

a15_2111600.speaker: Henize
a15_2111600.text: And after giving us Accept we'd like to have you manually roll clockwise 40 degrees. And then we'd like to get the sharp end forward. I'll give you the P20 when you're ready to copy. [Long pause.]

a15_2111600.speaker: Worden
a15_2111600.text: Hello, Houston, 15.

a15_2111600.speaker: Henize
a15_2111600.text: Good morning, Al. How're you doing?

a15_2111600.speaker: Worden
a15_2111600.text: Good morning, Karl. I'm doing just fine.

a15_2111600.speaker: Henize
a15_2111600.text: Righto. If you didn't hear what I said before, I'd like to repeat that we'd like to have Accept, and we'll send you up a state vector. And then we need to manually roll clockwise...

a15_2111600.speaker: Worden
a15_2111600.text: Roger. You've got Accept.

a15_2111600.speaker: Henize
a15_2111600.text: ...Righto. Then we need to manually roll clockwise 40 degrees, and I have here P20 data for you to get the sharp end forward. [Pause.]

a15_2111600.speaker: Worden
a15_2111600.text: Okay; we're rolling, and stand by one until I get a pen. [Pause.]

a15_2111600.speaker: Worden
a15_2111600.text: Okay, go ahead with the P20.

a15_2111600.speaker: Henize
a15_2111600.text: Roger; P20, option 5; plus-X forward, SIM attitude. The time is 211 plus 40. Verb 23, Noun 78, plus 180.00. The attitude is 141, 000/177, 000. [Pause.]

a15_2111600.speaker: Worden
a15_2111600.text: Roger, Karl. Understand. You want that P20 turnaround done at 211 plus 40, instead of 212:00. [Long pause.]

a15_2111600.speaker: Henize
a15_2111600.text: Al, we'd like to have you start the maneuver as soon as we finish the uplink, and that time is the time we should be completing the maneuver.

a15_2111600.speaker: Worden
a15_2111600.text: Okay. Fine, Karl. I'll just move that whole thing up. We're doing the roll maneuver now.

a15_2111600.speaker: Henize
