a15_2111600.text: Roger. And while you've got the Flight Plan there, the only update that concerns us for the next hour and a half - is to - Over there at 21:54 [means 211:54], delete Manual - "Manually roll clockwise". You got that one? [Pause.]

a15_2111600.speaker: Worden
a15_2111600.text: Yeah. Roger.

a15_2111600.speaker: Henize
a15_2111600.text: And everything after that, all the way down to 212 plus 20. And then we'll be in contact with you again for further updates. [Pause.]

a15_2111600.speaker: Worden
a15_2111600.text: Okay. Understand. That block between 21:54 - or 211 plus 54 and 212 plus 20, that - that all goes as - as scheduled.

a15_2111600.speaker: Henize
a15_2111600.text: Entire thing deleted. Roger. [Pause.]

a15_2111600.speaker: Worden
a15_2111600.text: Roger. Then we'll be in P20 attitude and standing by for your word when we get contact again then. [Long pause.]

a15_2111600.speaker: Henize
a15_2111600.text: Okay, Al. The computer's yours. [Pause.]

a15_2111600.speaker: Worden
a15_2111600.text: Roger. Understand. [Pause.]

a15_2113449.speaker: Henize
a15_2113449.text: Al, we need the - the TLM [Telemetry] switch in Block, please. [Pause.]

a15_2113449.speaker: Henize
a15_2113449.text: 15, if you'd like a quick consumables update, I can give it to you now or I can wait until the next rev. [Pause.]

a15_2113449.speaker: Worden
a15_2113449.text: Go ahead, Karl. If there's time, I'll copy it now.

a15_2113449.speaker: Henize
a15_2113449.text: Roger. The time is 211 plus 00; RCS [Reaction Control System] total 46; Quads: Alpha, 48; Baker, 45; Charlie, 44; Delta, 46; hydrogen tanks: 49, 47, 39; oxygen tanks: 61, 64, 48.

a15_2113449.speaker: Henize
a15_2113449.text: 15, this is Houston. Are you still reading?

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston. How do you read? [Pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Hi, Houston; 15. Loud and clear. How us?

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: Hi, Dave. You're coming through loud and clear. How did our consumables update get to you. Okay? [Pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Yes, we got normal ...

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Okay. We got everything but the oxygen.

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: Okay. Want me to read those three up? [Pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Okay. Go ahead. [Pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: Roger. Oxygen tanks at that same time that I gave you originally were 61, 64, 48. [Long pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Okay. 61, 64 and 48. And I have a P52 for you and a crew status report.

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: Fire away with them. [Pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Okay. The P52: Noun 05 was .01, Noun 93 was plus .029, minus .025, plus .018. [The platform] was torqued out at 211:52:00.

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: And if you still have your pencil handy, why, the sleep came out to 7, 7¼, 7. And the PRD's: 25026, 23182 and 08033. And go ahead with your updates.

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: Roger. [Pause.] Okay. Flight Plan updates for the coming rev and - There's several of them here. And just to keep you feeling a little bit more optimistic, on the following revs, there are very few updates. Okay. At 212:40, we want to delete "Map Camera Image Motion, Increase." [Pause.] At 2...

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Roger. Got the deletion at 212:40. Go.

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: Roger. At 213 plus 24, we want to delete the "Gamma-ray Boom Deploy". [Pause.] And at that - there are 3...

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: 213:24 [I] have the deletion.

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: Roger. And just below that, the "MSFN verify lens tuck in" and also the "Pan Camera, Power, Off", delete both of those.

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Roger. Copy the next two deletions also. Go.

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: At 214 plus 02, we want to change that camera configuration to the 250-millimeter lens, 250. The f-stop should be 5.6; the exposure time should be 1 over 125. [Pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Rog. 214:02. Camera configuration: 250-millimeter lens, f/5.6 at 1/125. Go.

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: Correct. At 214 plus 06, add "Mass Spectrometer, Ion Source, Off. Experiment, Standby". And at the same time, add "Logic Power, 2, Deploy/Retract". [Long pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Rog. At 214:06, "Mass Spec. Ion, Off. Experiment, Standby. Logic Power, 2, Deploy/Retract". Go.

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: Roger. At 214 plus 11, "If Ion source, Off, 5 minutes, Mass Spectrometer Boom, Retract." [Long pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: 15, we'd like High Gain [Antenna], Auto.

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Okay. At 214:11, "If Ion, Off for 5 minutes, Mass Spec. Boom, Retract." Go.

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: At 214 plus 12, we add "Mapping Camera/Laser Experiment Covers, Open; Mapping Camera Track, Extend; Mapping Camera Image Motion, On." [Long pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Okay. 214:12. "Map/Laser Experiment, Open; Map Track, Extend," and "Image Motion, On."

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: Roger. At 214 plus 16, we change the "EL, On to T-stop minus 1:40" to "T-start 1:40." Simply change stop to start.

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Rog. Stop to start. Go.

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: And at 214 plus 17, again change stop to start. And at that time also, add "Laser Altimeter, On." [Long pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Okay. 214:17, stop to start and "Laser Altimeter, On." Go.

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: And at 214 plus 18, change "Mapping Camera On, Off" to "Mapping Camera On, On". In another words, change Off to On. Add parenthesis T-start. Delete the next line, "Mapping Camera," - delete "Mapping Camera On, to Standby". And the third line, change "Mapping Camera, Image Motion, Off", to "Mapping Camera, Image Motion, Increase; barber pole plus four steps/On." [Long pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Okay. 214:18. "Map Camera, Image Motion, Increase; barber pole plus four steps/On." [Pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: Roger. And did you get the "Mapping Camera" - "Mapping Camera, On" on T-start? [Pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Oh, Rog. "Map Camera, On", on T-start, and scratch the "Map Camera, On, to Standby".

a15_2122805.speaker: Henize
a15_2122805.text: Roger. That takes care of all the - all the updates required for the next rev. [Pause.]

a15_2122805.speaker: Scott
a15_2122805.text: Rog. Understand. Thank you.

a15_2123926.speaker: Henize
a15_2123926.text: 15, this is Houston. A couple of comments, and then a - one change in your G&C checklist. The comments are as follows. As you will note from the consumables update, we now have single-tank capability at the 40-amp level.

a15_2123926.speaker: Scott
a15_2123926.text: Okay. I understand. Just retract it for 4 minutes and leave it there. Okay?

a15_2123926.speaker: Henize
a15_2123926.text: That's right. And has somebody got a G&C checklist there on page 9-4?

a15_2123926.speaker: Scott
a15_2123926.text: Okay. Stand by. We'll pull it out. [Long pause.]

a15_2123926.speaker: Scott
a15_2123926.text: All right. I've got page 9-4. Go ahead.

a15_2123926.speaker: Henize
a15_2123926.text: All right. We'd like to correct one of the short burn constants, and it's in column D, row 5. The number should be changed from 1 - 01605 - it should be changed to 01614. [Pause.]

a15_2123926.speaker: Scott
a15_2123926.text: Okay. I've got it now. I'm sorry. I thought you said B, Bravo. How about reading the number again, please.

a15_2123926.speaker: Henize
a15_2123926.text: And whenever somebody tells me he's ready to stop breakfast and copy a PAD, I have TEI-71 and also a Mapping Camera photo PAD.

a15_2123926.speaker: Scott
a15_2123926.text: All right. Stand by one, please. Probably be a couple of minutes.

a15_2124404.speaker: Irwin
a15_2124404.text: Okay, Karl. I'm ready to copy the TEI PAD. [Pause.]

a15_2124404.speaker: Henize
a15_2124404.text: Roger, Jim. Good morning. TEI-71, SPS/G&N. The weight is not applicable. P trim: Noun 48 is plus 0.64, plus 0.98; 217:49:18.04; plus 2838.6, minus 0581.0, minus 0027.7; 178, 129, 351; the rest is N/A. Four jet ullage for 12 seconds. And that's all. [Pause.]

a15_2124404.speaker: Irwin
a15_2124404.text: Okay. TEI-71 readback. SPS/G&N. Weight is N/A; plus 0.64, plus 0.98; 217:49:18.04; plus 2838.6, minus 0581.0, minus 0027.7; 178, 129, 351; four jet for 12 seconds. Over.

a15_2124404.speaker: Henize
a15_2124404.text: Roger, J - Roger, Jim. And would you repeat the - the yaw trim.

a15_2124404.speaker: Henize
a15_2124404.text: That's all correct. Thank you. [Pause.] And the last bit of information I have down here is a Mapping Camera photo PAD. At 214 plus...

a15_2124404.speaker: Henize
a15_2124404.text: Roger. It's at 214 plus 20 in your Flight Plan and there is no slot for it. You'll just have to stick it in. Mapping Camera, Start, 214:20:03; Stop, 215:19:49.

a15_2124829.speaker: Henize
a15_2124829.text: 15, this is Houston with just a passing comment to Dave. We have Lee Silvers and Jim Head in the backroom,r available for any questions or comments concerning the lunar surface activities that you'd like to make. Is there anything on your mind you'd like to discuss with them? [Pause.]

a15_2124829.speaker: Scott
a15_2124829.text: Well, it shouldn't take more than about a couple of weeks, I guess, if we started now. I guess we got a lot to discuss with them. We've talked it over a little bit. We've come to some conclusions about rilles and mountains and those sort of things. And I - I guess, rather than get into the details now, we probably ought to wait until the debriefing. If they have any questions for us, we'd be happy to answer.

a15_2124829.speaker: Henize
a15_2124829.text: Okay. It's my understanding that they didn't - you - you gave them so much data they didn't really have any questions left but stand by. I'll see if they - if they come up with some after you've invited them to - Joe says, hey, they just might have...

a15_2124829.speaker: Scott
a15_2124829.text: Yeah, that's right. I've never seen the day yet when those two didn't have some questions.

a15_2124829.speaker: Henize
a15_2124829.text: You opened yourself up there, Dave.

a15_2125335.speaker: Henize
a15_2125335.text: Lee and Jim are sitting right beside me here; and their comment is they - they don't really want to ask very many questions and perturb the debriefing a week from now. But they do just have a couple. And the first one - the first one concerns a unique crater close to Scarp that you described as having about a 40-meter diameter, with a very soft rim. And the texture of the material in it was - instead of being fine angular fragments, was more in the form of clods. They'd like to know a little bit more, if - if possible, about it's location relative to Scarp, and any other comments you can make

a15_2125335.speaker: Scott
a15_2125335.text: Okay, Houston. I guess our answer to that is that we had interpreted that particular crater as being Scarp. Perhaps it wasn't. Perhaps we were near Scarp and that was a somewhat smaller crater. But, I guess, as we remember it, that was the one we had called Scarp, and it was, I believe, the only crater we really sampled as we approached Rim Crater in the terrace there. And that particular crater had very soft rims - extremely soft, and all the fragments - the apparent fragments were very frangible. They just fell apart like dirt clods. And we did sample some, and we had a discussion, I think,

a15_2125335.speaker: Henize
a15_2125335.text: Dave, this particular crater sounds more and more interesting to the people down here. And I guess the next question is what - Was there anything about the crater, it's shape or anything else, that would lead you to think it had a different origin than most of the other impact craters? [Pause.]

a15_2125335.speaker: Scott
a15_2125335.text: No. It - it's depth-to-diameter ratio was about par for the - for the course up there. And it had a slightly raised rim, and the rim may have been somewhat higher than - than others. But I wouldn't be able to distinguish that specifically. It - it was a rather standard-appearing crater, until we walked up onto the rim, and it was extremely soft. And, of course, we only sampled one edge of the rim there. We didn't get any circumferential sampling on it, so it might have been a - a unique part. But it looked pretty uniform all the way around.

a15_2125335.speaker: Scott
a15_2125335.text: And, we did get the appropriate photographs plus a pan at that site, which, I think, when we go over during the debriefing - perhaps we can extract some more of what we saw. As you remember, at that particular time, we were pretty well hustling, and we didn't have a chance to do much looking at the maps as we got there.

a15_2125335.speaker: Henize
a15_2125335.text: They say that's great. Thanks a lot.

a15_2125335.speaker: Scott
a15_2125335.text: Well, that's because I happened to have had a very good professor.

a15_2125335.speaker: Scott
a15_2125335.text: That's right. As a matter of fact, so many of them, it's just hard to - hard to remember it all. But we sure appreciate all you all did for us in getting us ready for this thing. And I'll tell you, I think Jim and I both felt quite comfortable when we got there, about looking around and - and seeing things. I just wish we had had more time, because, believe me, there's an awful lot to be seen and done up there.

a15_2125335.speaker: Scott
a15_2125335.text: Well, as we go around in lunar orbit here, I can look down - and I could just spend weeks and weeks looking. And I can pick out any number of superb sites down there which would take you several weeks to analyze on the surface. There is just so much here. To coin a phrase, it's mindboggling.

a15_2125335.speaker: Scott
a15_2125335.text: Yes, sir. And I hope someday we can get you all up here too. I - I think we really need to have some good professional geologists up here. As a matter of fact, good professional scientists of all disciplines, not only in lunar orbit, but right on the surface, because you all would just really have a field day, where - with your backgrounds and what you know. There's just so much to be gained up here. [Pause.]

a15_2133033.speaker: Henize
a15_2133033.text: 15, this is Houston. Just a point of curiosity. Are you guys seeing Aristarchus and Schröter's valley in daylight yet? [No answer.]

a15_2133431.speaker: Henize
a15_2133431.text: 15, this is Houston; 3 minutes to LOS, and all your systems are Go. [Long pause.]

a15_2133431.speaker: Henize
a15_2133431.text: 15, this is Houston. How do you read?

a15_2133431.speaker: Henize
a15_2133431.text: 15, this is Houston. Could you give us a comm check, please.

a15_2142202.speaker: Henize
a15_2142202.text: 15, this is Houston. How do you read? [Pause.]

a15_2142202.speaker: Henize
a15_2142202.text: Roger, 15. We're reading you loud and clear. We have Flight Plan updates available any time you're interested in copying it.

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Okay, Houston. Go ahead with your updates. [Pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: Roger, Dave. We'd like to have you start the battery A charge first.

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Roger. We're just doing it right now.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: Okay. Flight Plan updates; 214 plus 41. [Pause.] The - we delete the Pan...

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Go ahead.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: ...we delete several lines there. "Pan Camera Mode, Standby; Power, On; Stereo; Exposure, Normal;" and "Pan Camera Mode to Operate", all deleted. [Pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Rog; understand. Three lines deleted. Deleted at 214:41. Go.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: Rog. At 214 plus 50, we delete "Pan Camera Mode, Standby" and "MSFN veri; verify lens tuck in". [Pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Roger; 214:50; delete 2 lines. Go ahead.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: Roger. At 214:53, delete "Pan Camera Power, Off", and at 55 delete "Gamma-ray Boom, Deploy". [Pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Rog. At 53 and 55, delete one line each. Go.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: At 215:17, we add "Map Camera, On, switch Off, parenthesis T-stop; Laser Altimeter, Off; Map Camera, On, Standby, T-stop plus 30 seconds. Map Camera, Image Motion, Off".

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Stop - break - break, Karl. Try it again - a little slower so I can write it.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: Roger; 215 plus 17. First line, "Map Camera, On, Off, parenthesis T-stop". [Pause.] Second line, "Laser Altimeter, Off". [Pause.] Third line, "Mapping Camera, On to Standby, T-stop plus 30 - 30 seconds". [Pause.] Fourth line, "Mapping Camera, Image Motion, Off". [Long pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Okay. Copy. At 215:17, "Map Camera, On to Off, T-stop; Laser Altimeter, Off; Map Camera, On to Standby at T-stop plus 30 seconds" and "Map Camera, Image Motion to Off".

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: Roger. At 215 plus 19, add "Gamma-ray Boom, Deploy". [Long pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Okay. 215:19; "Gamma-ray Boom, Deploy". Go.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: 215 plus 25, delete "Laser Altimeter, Off". [Pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Rog. 215:15 [sic], delete "Laser Altimeter, Off". Go.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: Over at 216:01, "Laser Altimeter, On", is moved down to 216 plus 15. [Long pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Okay. 216:01 "Laser Altimeter, On", deleted; at 216:15 "Laser Altimeter, On" added. Go ahead.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: Correct. 217 plus 14, add "Laser Altimeter to Off". [Pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Okay. 217:14, "Laser Altimeter, Off". Go.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: At 217 plus 20, we delete - three lines. "Mapping Camera, Image Motion", "Mapping Camera, On", and "Mapping Camera, Image Motion" - steps, all three. [Pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Okay; 217:21 delete three lines. Got 'em. Go ahead.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: Right. And, in that place at 217:20, put the line down below at 217:25 "Gamma-ray Boom, Deploy". [Long pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Okay. At 217:20, we should have "Gamma-ray Boom, Deploy" vice 217:25.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: Roger. At 218:02, we change the camera configuration there. We're going to use window 5, CM-5. We need the 80-millimeter lens - 80-millimeter lens, and the setting should be stop 2.8, exposure time 1 over 250. [Pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Okay. 218:02, use CM-5/EL/80-millimeter, 2.8, 1/250th. Go.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: And the note there is - use the Lex - use the Lexan shield on CM-5; in other words, leave it on the window.

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Okay. Lexan shield. Got it.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: At 218:10, delete "Mapping Camera, Image Motion, Increase". [Pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Okay. One line deleted at 218:10. Go.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: At 218 plus 14, we add "Laser Altimeter, On". We have four lines here. "Mapping Camera, Image Motion, On; Mapping Camera, On to On at T-start; Mapping Camera, Image Motion, Increase; talkback barberpole plus 4/On". [Long pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Okay. 218:14 "Laser Altimeter, On; Mapping Camera, Image Motion to On; Mapping Camera, On to On at T-start; and Mapping Camera, Image Motion, Increase; and talkback barber pole plus 4 seconds/On".

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: Roger. At 220 plus 07, we add "Pan Camera Mode, Standby; Power On". [Pause.] And that will be "Mono and Exposure, Normal". [Long pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Okay. 220:07 "Pan Camera to Standby; Power, On; Mono; Exposure, Normal". Go.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: At 220 plus 13, we add "Pan Camera Mode, Operate at T-start". [Pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: 220:13, "Pan Camera to Operate at T-start".

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: Roger. And about 220:18, expect the talkback showing you film depletion - the film finished. At that time, go Mode, Standby; and wait for a MSFN cue to go Power, Off. [Long pause.]

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: And 15, we'd like to have High Gain [Antenna], Auto.

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Okay. 220:18, Pan Camera [pause] - 220:18, we should have film depletion; Pan Camera to barber pole, then go Standby and wait for MSFN cue for Power, Off. Go.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: And that's the end of the update.

a15_2142801.speaker: Scott
a15_2142801.text: Okay. I guess when you run out of film, you run out of updates.

a15_2142801.speaker: Henize
a15_2142801.text: That's about the size of the situation.

a15_2144709.speaker: Henize
a15_2144709.text: 15, Houston. If you are willing to listen, I have about a 3-minute update on the morning news. [Pause.]

a15_2145317.speaker: Worden
a15_2145317.text: Okay, Houston; 15. We're ready for the news.

a15_2145317.speaker: Henize
a15_2145317.text: Roger, 15. The flight of Apollo 15 is still front page news around the world. Even yesterday's relatively quiet activities were noted by most news media. The rail strike with the United Transportation Union has ended, and ten railroads that were out of operation for 18 days are back on the tracks. Growers in California were hardest hit by the strike, losing an estimated 45 million dollars in sales and related industries. [Pause.] President Nixon has asked Congress not to allow the use of federal funds to pay for bussing school children. The administration also announced that it is appealing a

a15_2145317.speaker: Worden
a15_2145317.text: Oh, yeah; but we sure got nice sunny weather up here.

a15_2145317.speaker: Henize
a15_2145317.text: No clouds up there, huh? That's amazing.

a15_2145317.speaker: Worden
a15_2145317.text: No. It's just as clear as crystal. [Pause.]

a15_2145317.speaker: Henize
a15_2145317.text: Thinking about all that sunshine up there reminds me that we're in a bind down here about your exposure to UV, and we recommend that, on the several times on the next couple of orbits when you're requested to take the - the Lexan cover off of window 5, that you alternate handling that photography to keep under the legal doses. [Pause.]

a15_2145317.speaker: Worden
a15_2145317.text: All right; we'll do that. [Long pause.]

a15_2145317.speaker: Henize
a15_2145317.text: 15, Houston. The doctors down here with their - with their electrocardiograms see that the CMP - or at least they think the CMP - is on the - the biomed apparatus; and, according to Flight Plan, they'd like to have the LMP on. [Pause.]

a15_2145317.speaker: Worden
a15_2145317.text: Okay. We thought we'd give you both since you were sort of interested in that yesterday.

a15_2145858.speaker: Henize
a15_2145858.text: 15, Houston. We have a couple of camera PADs when you have time to copy. [Pause.]

a15_2145858.speaker: Worden
a15_2145858.text: Okay; stand by a couple of minutes, will you please, Karl?

a15_2145858.speaker: Irwin
a15_2145858.text: Okay, Karl. I'll copy those PADs for you.

a15_2145858.speaker: Henize
a15_2145858.text: Roger. They're in the Flight Plan at 216. The first one is the Solar Corona photo PAD. T-start is 216:03:55. Down below, the Mapping Camera photo PAD: Start 216:18:30, Stop 217:18:15. [Pause.]

a15_2151329.speaker: Henize
a15_2151329.text: 15, Houston. If you'll give us Accept, we'll send up a new state vector.

a15_2151910.speaker: Henize
a15_2151910.text: Hey Al. I've sort of got an itch to hear what the Aristarchus region looks like in daylight. You got any comments? [Pause.]

a15_2151910.speaker: Worden
a15_2151910.text: Well, I'll tell you, Karl; we've all been sitting here kind of looking at Aristarchus a little bit in awe. It looks like probably the most volcanic area that I've seen anywhere on the surface. And certainly it's just very covered with rilles, very - quite deep rilles, too, some of them. Schröter's Valley, for instance, is a magnificent big rille which looks like it's worked - been worked twice; of course, the large rille and then a smaller rille inside.

a15_2151910.speaker: Henize
a15_2151910.text: What about the source of Schröter's Valley?

a15_2151910.speaker: Henize
a15_2151910.text: What about the source of Schröter's Valley. Does it look volcanic? [Pause.]

a15_2151910.speaker: Worden
a15_2151910.text: Well, that whole area in there looks volcanic, yeah. And that certainly comes from - from up on the plateau there. I would guess that the Cobra Head is the source for Schröter's Valley. The elevation is - is a little subtle from this - from this vantage point, but I - I guess that would be my guess. And as far as where the - think we've found something interesting anyway about the - the ends of the rilles, particularly around the Schröter's Valley area, it looks quite distinctly like the rilles - the - the mouths of the rilles - or the delta's have been covered with rising maria - ma

a15_2152323.speaker: Henize
a15_2152323.text: 15, this is Houston. I'm turning you over to Joe now. I'll see you on the way home tomorrow.

a15_2152323.speaker: Worden
a15_2152323.text: Okay, Karl. Talk to you tomorrow. Thanks for coming out so early for us.

a15_2152323.speaker: Henize
a15_2152323.text: It was a pleasure, believe me.

a15_2152443.speaker: Allen
a15_2152443.text: Good morning, Yankee Clipper; this is Houston. [No answer. Long pause.]

a15_2152443.speaker: Allen
a15_2152443.text: Good morning, Endeavour; this is Houston.

a15_2152443.speaker: Scott
a15_2152443.text: Good morning, Houston; this is Endeavour. How are you today?

a15_2152443.speaker: Allen
a15_2152443.text: The devil in the backup commander made me do the other. [Pause.]

a15_2152443.speaker: Scott
a15_2152443.text: Seems like that other fellow is hung up on that other flight [Apollo 12] for some reason or another.

a15_2153138.speaker: Allen
a15_2153138.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. We're about 4 minutes from LOS. You look to be in good shape to go around the corner. [Pause.]

a15_2163700.speaker: Allen
a15_2163700.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. We'd like Auto on the High Gain [Antenna], please, and we show your optics in the CMC Mode. We'd like that zeroed at your convenience, please. [Pause.]

a15_2164912.speaker: Allen
a15_2164912.text: Endeavour, Pan Camera Power, Off, please. [Pause.]

a15_2165129.speaker: Allen
a15_2165129.text: Hello, Endeavour. This is Houston with photography PADs and a TEI-73 PAD, when you're ready. [Pause.]

a15_2165129.speaker: Irwin
a15_2165129.text: Okay, Joe. I'm ready to copy the photo PADs. [Pause.]

a15_2165129.speaker: Allen
a15_2165129.text: Okay, Jim. I've got a Map Camera photo PAD, a Pan Camera PAD, and a Terminator photo PAD for you. And before I start, just a word of explanation. Because of your change of trajectory from what we considered a nominal one, we've got some details to add to the PAD that involve image-motion setting changes and exposure changes. And I'll read those in detail, in a moment. I just wanted to give you a word of explanation on it. The first PAD is the Map Camera photo PAD copied at 217 plus 10. [Pause.] And at 217 plus 10 it is T-start: 218 plus 16 plus 59, T-stop: 219 plus 16 plus 44. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2165129.speaker: Allen
a15_2165129.text: That's correct, Jim. And if you'll turn the page now, I want you to delete two lines, one at 218 plus 35 and that is "Map Camera, Image Motion, Increase, talkback barber pole, On". Delete that, and delete the line at 218 plus 55 which reads, "Map Camera, Image Motion, Increase, talkback barber pole plus four steps" et cetera . And, instead, put in the instructions: At T-start, [pause] it should be barber pole plus four. At 218 plus 39 plus 00, barber pole plus three; and at 218:49 plus 00, barber pole plus four. Readback, please. [Pause.]

a15_2165129.speaker: Irwin
a15_2165129.text: Okay, the instructions are that at T-start, it should be barber pole plus four; at 218 plus 39 plus 00, barber pole plus three; at 218 plus 49 plus 00, barber pole plus four. [Pause.]

a15_2165129.speaker: Allen
a15_2165129.text: That's correct, Jim. And those are your image-motion settings, and you're to delete the other two image-motion instructions in the Flight Plan. One at 218:35 and the other at 218:55, and - and I know you got that. The second...

a15_2165129.speaker: Irwin
a15_2165129.text: Yes, I made those two deletions.

a15_2165129.speaker: Allen
a15_2165129.text: Okay, the second is the terminator photo PAD to copy at 218 plus 07. And it is T-start: 218 plus 15 plus 19. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2165129.speaker: Allen
a15_2165129.text: Roger. And finally, the Pan Camera photo PAD. Copy at 218 plus 39. T-start: 218 plus 52 plus 55. T-stop: 219 plus 16 plus 44. And delete the two Pan Camera exposure lines. The first one at 218 plus 57. Delete that. And the second one at 219 plus 03. Delete that. And instead, use these exposure instructions. [Pause.] At 219 plus 00 plus 13, decrease. At 219 plus 00 plus 50, normal. At 219 plus 06 plus 35, decrease. At 219 plus 07 plus 28, normal. Readback please. [Pause.]

a15_2165129.speaker: Irwin
a15_2165129.text: Okay, I understand the instructions on the Pan Camera. Exposure at 219 plus 00 plus 13, it's decrease; 219 plus 00 plus 50, it's normal; 219 plus 06 plus 35, it's decrease; 219 plus 07 plus 28, it goes back to normal.

a15_2165129.speaker: Allen
a15_2165129.text: That's right, Jim. And give me the T-start and T-stop times, please. [Pause.]

a15_2165129.speaker: Allen
a15_2165129.text: Sounds fine, and I'm holding TEI-73 PAD when you're ready for that. [Pause.]

a15_2165129.speaker: Irwin
a15_2165129.text: Okay, Joe. I'm ready here for the TEI PAD.

a15_2165129.speaker: Allen
a15_2165129.text: Roger, Jim. It's TEI-73, SPS/G&N: 36188; plus 0.63, plus 0.98; 221:47:42.81; plus 2883.3, minus 0661.3, minus 0195.5; 179, 128, 350. All the rest is NA. Ullage, four jet, 12 seconds. Other: the PAD assumes no shape maneuver, and it assumes the lift-off REFSMMAT. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2165129.speaker: Irwin
a15_2165129.text: Okay, Joe. TEI-73, PAD readback. SPS/G&N; 36188; plus 0.63, plus 0.98; 221:47:42.81; plus 2883.3, minus 0661.3, minus 0195.5; 179, 128, 350. Four-jet, 12 seconds; PAD assumes no shape burn, and lift-off REFSMMAT. Over.

a15_2165129.speaker: Allen
a15_2165129.text: Okay, Jim. Right on. Thank you.

a15_2170409.speaker: Allen
a15_2170409.text: Roger, Jim. Just for your own thinking, we'd like to advise you that we have reviewed the cue card F-K1 for the plane change burn that Al copied, and it's update is still valid for your shape burn later on. And we're in the process of going over your SPS thrusting procedures on G5-1 in the checklist, and we see very - only very minor changes that we'll be coming up to you with regarding your burn later on today, so I think things are pretty well in hand down here. Over.

a15_2170409.speaker: Scott
a15_2170409.text: Okay, we copy. Thank you, Joe.

a15_2170409.speaker: Allen
a15_2170409.text: Another item regarding that, the FAO wants me to urge you again just to follow the Flight Plan items regarding SIM bay operation before and after these burns coming up, and we'll get no - we'll get into no problems at all. Over.

a15_2172853.speaker: Allen
a15_2172853.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. We have no problems at all as you come up on 5 minutes before LOS. Al, we do have a question for you, if this is a good time to ask it. Over.

a15_2172853.speaker: Worden
a15_2172853.text: Yeah; go ahead, Joe.

a15_2172853.speaker: Allen
a15_2172853.text: Rog, Alfredo. We're sitting down here wondering if, perhaps, at sometime over the past few days you've gotten a visual on the Mass Spectrometer boom and unit, and if so, has it been possible at all to determine which direction the Mass Spec. might be twisting as you move through the orbit over the Moon? Over. [Pause.]

a15_2172853.speaker: Worden
a15_2172853.text: Yeah. I have seen that, Joe, and I've - haven't watched a great deal of twisting and, as a matter of fact, I was rather surprised that there wasn't more twist than what I observed. I may not have picked up the maximum deflection, but I only observed about a - maybe a 5- or 10-degree rotation on the end on the boom, and, as I recall, as I was looking at it from inside the spacecraft, the rotation was counter-clockwise.

a15_2172853.speaker: Allen
a15_2172853.text: Okay, Al. That's interesting information. We don't necessarily expect it to have rotated more, but just wondering if you had some good visual data for us, and that's excellent. Another comment, and it's more in the way of a reminder; during your EVA, we're going to ask you to look very closely at the V over H sensor, and the symptoms we've had concerning that sensor down here, is as though it has a small crack in the lens or perhaps there's foreign contamination of some kind down in the barrel. And we're going to ask you to look particularly for either a crack, or contamination in the barrel d

a15_2172853.speaker: Worden
a15_2172853.text: Roger, Joe. I understand that one. [Long pause.]

a15_2172853.speaker: Allen
a15_2172853.text: Endeavour, we'd like a Pro on the P20 now, please. [Pause.]

a15_2172853.speaker: Irwin
a15_2172853.text: Okay, that's in work, Joe.

a15_2172853.speaker: Allen
a15_2172853.text: Roger; Jim. Thanks. [Pause.]

a15_2172853.speaker: Worden
a15_2172853.text: Yeah.

a15_2172853.speaker: Allen
a15_2172853.text: And, Endeavour, requesting you configure DSE now, please.

a15_2172853.speaker: Worden
a15_2172853.text: Okay.

a15_2172853.speaker: Scott
a15_2172853.text: Back to normal now.

a15_2172853.speaker: Worden
a15_2172853.text: Okay. [Garble].

a15_2172853.speaker: Scott
a15_2172853.text: Okay.

a15_2172853.speaker: Scott
a15_2172853.text: [Garble]?

a15_2172853.speaker: Worden
a15_2172853.text: No, [garble] 15.

a15_2172853.speaker: Allen
a15_2172853.text: Endeavour. Recall the 50 18 and get the attitude, please.

a15_2172853.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2172853.text: This is Apollo Control at 217 hours, 34 minutes. Endeavour 's gone behind the Moon on the 71st revolution and we've had Loss Of Signal. And a Lunar Surface Science briefing is beginning now in the main MSC auditorium.

a15_2172853.speaker: Irwin
a15_2172853.text: Well, I can do it. But...

a15_2172853.speaker: Irwin
a15_2172853.text: But my needles are not close to center. The needles are not very close to center.

a15_2172853.speaker: Scott
a15_2172853.text: I can't hear you.

a15_2172853.speaker: Irwin
a15_2172853.text: You can't hear me?

a15_2172853.speaker: Scott
a15_2172853.text: No.

a15_2172853.speaker: Irwin
a15_2172853.text: Well, you're not on comm. Yes.

a15_2172853.speaker: Irwin
a15_2172853.text: We're off about - 20 degrees in pitch.

a15_2182506.speaker: Allen
a15_2182506.text: Roger, Dave. Looking downstream a little bit here, I know you'll be interested to know that both the shape burn and the satellite jett[ison] will be coming up very close to the nominal times in your Flight Plan. And we've got the photo PADs here when you're ready to copy, and there are only a few lines. Over.

a15_2182506.speaker: Allen
a15_2182506.text: Roger. The first is a terminator photo PAD to go in at 220 plus 05; and it reads T-start, 220 plus 13 plus 45. Over.

a15_2182506.speaker: Allen
a15_2182506.text: Thank you, Jim. And I've got a milestone for you to add here - a Pan Camera photo PAD, with a T-start of 220 plus 15 plus 25. And the instructions on that are: "Run the Pan Camera to film depletion." And your indication is talkback barber pole. That's a lot of feet of film. And finally an entry at 221 plus 59 - it's an addition which reads "circuit breaker O 2 Tank 100W Heaters, three, Main B, Closed". Over.

a15_2182506.speaker: Irwin
a15_2182506.text: Okay; on the last one, it was 221:59, "circuit breaker O 2 Heaters - 100 watt Heaters, three, Main B, Closed". And then going back to the entry for a - a T-start time of the Pan Camera of 220:15:25, and run the camera to film depletion, and it'll be talkback barber pole.

a15_2183912.speaker: Allen
a15_2183912.text: Endeavour, this is Houston requesting [Mapping Camera] Image Motion to talkback plus 3.

a15_2183912.speaker: Irwin
a15_2183912.text: That's in work right now, Joe.

a15_2183912.speaker: Allen
a15_2183912.text: Okay; thank you. And if you give us Accept, we'll update a REFSMMAT to you. [Long pause.]

a15_2183912.speaker: Allen
a15_2183912.text: And, Endeavour; Houston again with a couple more items.

a15_2183912.speaker: Allen
a15_2183912.text: Rog, Jim. Coming up on our TEC partial Gamma-ray [boom] extension, and looking downstream towards that, we are requesting that you time the Gamma-ray boom extension, which you're going to do at 219 plus 19 - and we'll be standing by for that time. And also requesting - that you get on the biomed via the Flight Plan, please.

a15_2190236.speaker: Allen
a15_2190236.text: Endeavour, please terminate battery Bravo charge.

a15_2190236.speaker: Scott
a15_2190236.text: Except we were charging battery Alpha. [Long pause.]

a15_2191256.speaker: Allen
a15_2191256.text: Endeavour, Houston. Turn the Map Camera back On, please. [Pause.] And it's not necessary to extend it.

a15_2191721.speaker: Allen
a15_2191721.text: Rog, troops. We'd like to tag up with you on the recommended TEI procedures. And, Al, I guess maybe you'll be doing this. And we - we're interested in reverifying the entries which you've made in your P40 SPS Thrusting Checklist, pages G5-1 through to the end. And we've got, I guess, two new entries to put in, but we want to reverify the entries that you've already got in there. Your choice, if you want to read those entries to us, or if you'd like to have us to read them to you. Over.

a15_2191721.speaker: Scott
a15_2191721.text: Okay. Let's get Al up on the headsets. Stand by one, please.

a15_2191721.speaker: Allen
a15_2191721.text: Endeavour, Houston. Requesting Pan Camera Power, Off, please.

a15_2191721.speaker: Scott
a15_2191721.text: Rog. We're doing it right now. [Long pause.]

a15_2191721.speaker: Worden
a15_2191721.text: Okay, Houston. We had a continuous barber pole on the Pan Camera there. [Pause.]

a15_2191721.speaker: Allen
a15_2191721.text: Roger. Copy that. That's a lot of film across those rollers.

a15_2192313.speaker: Allen
a15_2192313.text: Roger. A question on your Pan Camera. When you turned the power off, was it already barber pole or was it gray and then went to barber pole as you threw the switch? Over.

a15_2192313.speaker: Allen
a15_2192313.text: Okay, thank you. And we're standing by for Al on the headset.

a15_2192313.speaker: Scott
a15_2192313.text: Okay; let's - let us get all this SIM bay stuff cleaned up first.

a15_2192313.speaker: Allen
a15_2192313.text: And, Endeavour; this is Houston. You're coming up on 8 minutes to LOS. And we'll just go over the TEI procedures on the next rev. No hurry on that at all. [Pause.]

a15_2192313.speaker: Scott
a15_2192313.text: Okay, that sounds like a good idea. [Long pause.]

a15_2192313.speaker: Scott
a15_2192313.text: And, Houston. Gamma-ray Boom Deploy was 2 plus 33.

a15_2192313.speaker: Allen
a15_2192313.text: And, Endeavour; this is Houston with instructions on the Pan Camera. You can start the Pan Camera power using the normal procedures at T-start. And if you get an incorrect indication, namely continuous barber pole, just leave it in the normal configuration until AOS. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2192313.speaker: Scott
a15_2192313.text: Roger. Understand. Start it normally at T-start, and if it is in barber pole, just leave it till AOS.

a15_2192313.speaker: Allen
a15_2192313.text: And we have the torquing angles. Thank you.

a15_2193117.speaker: Allen
a15_2193117.text: Endeavour, you're looking good at LOS minus 60 seconds. Configure the DSE for us, please. And we see you've done that. Thank you.

a15_2193117.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2193117.text: This is Apollo Control at 219 hours, 32 minutes. We've had Loss Of Signal on the 72nd revolution. A briefing on orbital science is scheduled for 1 pm today in the MSC Auditorium. This briefing will not be carried on the Public Affairs release line. To repeat, the 1 pm briefing on orbital science will not be carried on the Public Affairs release line. At 219 hours, 32 minutes; this is Mission Control, Houston.

a15_2193117.speaker: Worden
a15_2193117.text: Boy, that puts that star smack in the middle. Beautiful. Okay. Are we in P20, Jim?

a15_2193117.speaker: Worden
a15_2193117.text: We were in it before, weren't we?

a15_2193117.speaker: Worden
a15_2193117.text: Okay. Okay, we got it for TEI ascent. No, wait a minute.

a15_2193117.speaker: Irwin
a15_2193117.text: Okay. It calls for GDC Align. Yes, you went back in P20; I'll go CMC Mode, Auto, huh?

a15_2193117.speaker: Worden
a15_2193117.text: That has to be done from your couch there.

a15_2193117.speaker: Irwin
a15_2193117.text: I can do one. I'll - probably use the checklist. It's been a long time since I've gone through one.

a15_2193117.speaker: Scott
a15_2193117.text: [Garble] burn, Al? Get all your [garble] all set? No, you're [garble] open.

a15_2193117.speaker: Irwin
a15_2193117.text: Well, we might as well get in our regular couches then, huh?

a15_2193117.speaker: Irwin
a15_2193117.text: Do you want me to switch around to regular couches there?

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Endeavour. This is Houston. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Worden
a15_2202206.text: Go ahead, Houston. Endeavour.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Roger. Could you tell us, please, the status of the Pan Camera switch? [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Worden
a15_2202206.text: Roger. Right now, it's in Standby and Power and it's been barber pole.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Okay, we copy that, Endeavour. You can go ahead and power it down. We've run through to the last of the Pan Camera film.

a15_2202206.speaker: Worden
a15_2202206.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: And, 15. We've powered up the drugstore to receive the film when you get home.

a15_2202206.speaker: Worden
a15_2202206.text: Roger. Better get a couple. [Long pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Endeavour, a last request on that Pan Camera. Requesting Power, On and Operate, please.

a15_2202206.speaker: Worden
a15_2202206.text: Roger. Power, On and Operate. [Long pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Endeavour, requesting Accept for your new state vector and a shaping target load.

a15_2202206.speaker: Worden
a15_2202206.text: Rog. You've got it.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. We've reverified that your Pan Camera is out of film, and you can power it down for us, please, for the final - final time. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Irwin
a15_2202206.text: Joe, you'll have to give us that transmission again. We were off [garble] temporarily.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Roger, Jim. Just said that we've reverified that the Pan Camera is out of film and you can power it down for the final time at your convenience.

a15_2202206.speaker: Irwin
a15_2202206.text: Understand.[Long pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Endeavour, we have a preliminary TEI-74 PAD, if you're ready to copy. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Irwin
a15_2202206.text: Stand by one, Joe.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Roger, Jim. No hurry. [Long pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Irwin
a15_2202206.text: Okay, Joe. Ready to copy.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Roger. TEI-74 preliminary, SPS/G&N; 35852; plus 0.62, plus 0.96; 223:48:43.63; plus 2945.0, minus 0769.6, minus 0152.8; 000, 000, 000; NA, plus 0022.3; 3047.7, 2:22, 3029.4; 37, 224.3, 30.5; NA, NA, NA; plus 26.12, minus 157.98; 1083.8, 36179; 294:58:40. GDC Align, Vega and Deneb; Roll align, 102; 178; 028. Ullage: 4 jet, 12 seconds. Standing by for readback. Over. And the computer's yours, Endeavour. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Irwin
a15_2202206.text: Roger, Joe. Would you start with Delta-V T , again? I missed that.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Rog. Delta-V T is 3047.7; B T , 2:22; and Delta-V C , 3029.4. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Irwin
a15_2202206.text: Roger. Read on down the rest of that PAD, from there on down.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Oh, okay; coming at you, Jim. The sextant is 37, 224.3, 30.5; NA, NA, NA; latitude, plus 26.12; longitude, minus 157.98; 1083.8, 36179; and GET 294:58:40. Vega and Deneb; 102; 178; 028; 4 jet, 12 seconds. Over.

a15_2202206.speaker: Irwin
a15_2202206.text: Okay, Joe. Readback for TEI-74 preliminary. SPS/G&N; 35852; plus 0.62, plus 0.96; 223:48:43.63; plus 2945.0, minus 0769.6, minus 0152.8; zero for roll, pitch and yaw; Delta-V T 3047.7, 2:22, 3029.4, 37, 224.3, 30.5; latitude, plus 26.12, minus 157.98; 1083.8, 36179; 294:58:40. Vega and Deneb; 102; 178; 028; 4 jet for 12 seconds. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: That's correct, Jim, and your Noun 44 is NA and plus 0022.3 and readback's correct.

a15_2202206.speaker: Irwin
a15_2202206.text: Roger; copied. H P is plus 0022.3. [Long pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: And Jim; this is Houston. Could you adjust your S-band volume for us, please? You have a side tone squeal when you transmit and the - the volume is - is fairly weak for us. Give us a count before you do it and after you do it. And, would you reverify the Delta-V Y for us? Over. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Irwin
a15_2202206.text: Okay, Delta-V Y was minus 0769.6. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Okay, Jim. Thank you. And the volume is better. Thank you. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: And, Houston; Endeavour. We're just finishing up final stowage right now, and we'll be with you in a couple of minutes on the procedures.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Okay, we're standing by. [Long pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Endeavour, at your convenience, Gain Step switch to center, please. And I have the shape SPS/G&N PAD, when you're ready for that. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Irwin
a15_2202206.text: Okay, Joe. Gain Step is center, and I'm ready on the shape PAD.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Roger, Jim. Shape, SPS/G&N; weight, 36171; plus 0.63, plus 0.98; 221:20:47.23; plus 0017.0; minus all zips, minus 0064.2; 355, 198, 010; 0076.1, plus 0054.3; and, Jim, why don't you readback from there, and I'll pick up again. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Right on, Jim. Delta-V T is 0066.4, 0:03, 0054.8; [pause] sextant, 13, 164.3, 12.6; 001, down 09.1, left 4.6. The rest is NA. GDC Align, Vega and Deneb; roll align, 102; 178; 028. Four jet, 12 seconds. Other is subsat launch, GET 222 plus 39 plus 27; roll, 266; pitch, 141; yaw, 038. High Gain [Antenna angle]: pitch, minus 70; yaw, plus 113. Standing by for readback starting with Delta-V T . Over.

a15_2202206.speaker: Irwin
a15_2202206.text: Okay, Joe. 0066.4, 0:03, 0054.8; 13, 164.3, 12.6; 001, down 09.1, left 4.6; Vega and Deneb; 102; 178; 028. Four jet for 12 seconds; subsatellite launch, GET 222:39:27; roll, 266; pitch, 141; yaw, 038. High Gain is pitch, minus 70; yaw, plus 113. Over.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Right on the money. Thank you, sir. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: And, Jim, I guess those High Gain angles are to be applied to the shaping maneuver, not the subsat launch. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Irwin
a15_2202206.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: And, Houston, we're ready to talk over the procedures any time you are now.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Okay, Endeavour, I guess we're ready to start. I want to put one final note on the subsat launch. We'd like for you to reverify for us the talkbacks on the RCS after the launch. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: Okay. Understand. Check the RCS talkbacks after the launch. We'll do that.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Okay, Dave; and I guess you might cast an eye up at the - the few - fuel cell - talkbacks as well. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. Ready to tag up with you on the TEI procedures. And, Dave, I guess we're standing by for your recommendation. Do you want to read through the additions you now have in your P40 SPS Thrusting Checklist, or do you want us to go through the changes we want you to have there? It looks pretty much exactly like your TLI maneuver. There are just two changes; there are two difference from that, I guess. Over.

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: Okay, why don't you give us the two differences, and then we'll read it all back to you to make sure we've got it straight.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Okay, Dave. That sounds like a good way. Turn to page G5-4. And right down at the bottom of the page...

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Roger. Right at the bottom of the page after the two lines, "SPS Fuel/Oxidize Pressure" and "PUGS balanced", add the step "Cut-off minus 10 seconds, circuit breaker SPS Pilot Valve, Main A to Open." [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: Okay: bottom line on page 5-4. Cut-off minus 10 seconds, "Circuit Breaker SPS Pilot Valve, Main A, Open."

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: That's correct. And turning over a page to 5-5, you have an addition underneath the normal step which reads, "Circuit Breaker SPS Pitch 1 and yaw 1 to Open". Your addition reads, "Circuit Breaker SPS Pilot Valve, Main B, Open." And we have still another step to add in there, which is, "Circuit Breaker EMS, two of them, Main A and Main B, to Open." And, also, we would like to delete, one step below that, the three lines, "Map Camera, On, to Off," "Pan Camera Power to Off," and "SM/AC Power to Off." Over.

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: Okay; on page 5-5, beneath the addition of "CB/SP - S - SPS Pilot Valve, Main B, Open," add "CB EMS, two, Open," and them delete the three lines on Map Camera, Pan Camera, and SM/AC power below that.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: That's correct, Dave, and we're standing by for the other additions you've made, now.

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: Okay, we'll go back to the beginning, here. [Pause.] Okay; our initial configuration has the addition of both Pilot Valve Circuit Breakers Open, and to verify that both EPS Group 5 circuit breakers are Closed, and also on page 5-1, beneath the caution/warning test, EMS Function, Off, to verify, and the CB EMS A&B both Closed. That's what we have on 5-1.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Okay; that's good. Turn the page.

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: Okay, on 5-2, under "TVC Check and Prep", second line, "CB SPS (10), closed". That's all on 5-2.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Roger.

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: Page 5-3, at minus 2 minutes, "CB SPS Pilot Valve, Main B, Closed", instead of Delta-3 - "Delta-V Thrust A and B, Normal".

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: That is correct.

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: Okay. And on page 5-4, at 5 minutes prior to ignition when we get - 5 seconds prior to ignition when we get the flashing 99, we Delta-V Thrust A and B to Normal after the Pro. And then, on down at ignition, if we have a flashing 97, the SPS thrust fail, "CB SPS Pilot Valve A, Closed". And, if everything goes according to Hoyle, why, at 5 seconds, we'll close the C - CB SPS Pilot Valve Mi - Main A. And then, of course, the step you just answered - just added - at the bottom of the page, at cut-off minus 10 seconds, to close the Pilot Valve - or to open the Pilot Valve Main A.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Okay, Dave. That's right on the money.

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: Okay. And then on 5-5, we just discussed those two, which were a "CB SPS Pilot Valve, Main B, Open", and the "EMS circuit breakers, Open".

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Roger, Dave. That sounds good to us.

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: Okay; and I think we've practised one of those once before. I think we'll be able to handle that. [Long pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Dave, just out of curiosity, we know you or Al...

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: Yes.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: ...marked up the cue card for the plane change maneuver, and we wonder if you're going to use that marked-up card for the shape burn. Over.

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: No, no. We'll use the checklist straight through on the rest of the burns. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Okay, Dave. That's fine with us as we know you're aware it's a single bank B burn, which has been marked correctly onto that cue card. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: Rog. Yeah, I guess all - all our burns in orbit are just a straight single bank B.

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Right on. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Scott
a15_2202206.text: And, coming out, we'll have all the ball valves open and all the eyeballs watching. [Pause.]

a15_2202206.speaker: Allen
a15_2202206.text: Sounds like a good idea.

a15_2205148.speaker: Scott
a15_2205148.text: We were just getting the hoses set up here for the burn and noticed that there's a little bit of water coming out of the - the blue hose in the suit loop. Thought you might be interested. [Long pause.]

a15_2205148.speaker: Allen
a15_2205148.text: Okay, Dave. We copy that. Thank you.

a15_2205148.speaker: Scott
a15_2205148.text: Not much. It's just, if you put your hand around the nozzle there, why, you can get some water on it.

a15_2205148.speaker: Allen
a15_2205148.text: Okay; we copy that. We think it's probably normal, but we'll look into it real closely. Sounds to me like the Endeavour has a few plumbers aboard as well as experts in other things.

a15_2205148.speaker: Scott
a15_2205148.text: Well, by the time this is over, I guess we will be plumbers.

a15_2211547.speaker: Allen
a15_2211547.text: Endeavour, you're looking good. You are Go for the shaping burn.

a15_2212152.speaker: Scott
a15_2212152.text: Okay, Houston. Endeavour with a burn status report.

a15_2212152.speaker: Scott
a15_2212152.text: Okay. Burn was on time, and it was a 3-second burn. We had about 1.0 or 1.1 residual, and that was trimmed to 0.1, minus 0.2, minus 0.2. Delta-V C was minus 11.0; fuel, 26.40; oxidizer, 26.25. [Pause.]

a15_2212152.speaker: Scott
a15_2212152.text: And it has us in an orbit, 76.0 by 54.3 [nautical miles, 140.8 by 100.6 km].

a15_2212152.speaker: Allen
a15_2212152.text: Okay, Dave. Great. And you just gained about 240 more days for our subsatellite, something like that.

a15_2212537.speaker: Allen
a15_2212537.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. You're looking good at LOS minus 5. And I have a reminder on your water dump. We'd like you to monitor it down to 10 percent. And we'll see you on the other side. Over.

a15_2212804.speaker: Allen
a15_2212804.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. And we've copied your torquing angles.

a15_2221542.speaker: Irwin
a15_2221542.text: Clear.

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: Oh, my. Look at this. That's a good picture.

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Hello, Endeavour. This is Houston. [Pause.]

a15_2221542.speaker: Scott
a15_2221542.text: Houston, Endeavour. Go.

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Roger, Endeavour. We're requesting you verify your systems - Data Systems, On, and the S-band Aux switch to Science, please. [Long pause.]

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: Yes.

a15_2221542.speaker: Scott
a15_2221542.text: Right here it is.

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: Huh!

a15_2221542.speaker: Scott
a15_2221542.text: Yes. That's verified, isn't it?

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: No, Data Systems isn't On.

a15_2221542.speaker: Scott
a15_2221542.text: Well, it wasn't in here then.

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: It sure was and I missed it. I'm sorry.

a15_2221542.speaker: Scott
a15_2221542.text: Okay; that's verified now, the data systems are on now.

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: Shoot!

a15_2221542.speaker: Scott
a15_2221542.text: They're easy to overlook, aren't they?

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Okay, Dave; we copy that. I've got a map update, rev 75, when you're ready to copy. And I have a message for Al from the King [Farouk El-Baz], when he's ready to copy. [Pause.]

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: Go ahead, Joe.

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Roger, Al. The message to you is to stand by to copy your final exam grade in orbital science and observation. It's an alpha-plus, with a subnote of "Well done." Over. [Pause.]

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: Tell the King, thank you very much, Joe.

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Rog, Al. And I've got the map update...

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: And I expect to see him back in Houston soon.

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Oh! Oh, no - no problem there.

a15_2221542.speaker: Irwin
a15_2221542.text: Go ahead, Joe.

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Rog. The map update, rev 75. Copy at 223 plus 20. [Pause.] And it is: LOS, 223 plus 29 plus 45; 180, 223 plus 52 plus 57; AOS with TEI, 224 plus 03 plus 03; AOS without TEI, 224 plus 15 plus 30. Over.

a15_2221542.speaker: Irwin
a15_2221542.text: Okay, the map update readback for rev 75: 223:29:45, 223:52:57, 224:03:03 and 224:15:30.

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Readback's correct, Jim; thank you.

a15_2223128.speaker: Allen
a15_2223128.text: Endeavour. We verify your SIM pyro bus...

a15_2223128.speaker: Scott
a15_2223128.text: This is Endeavour. Can you verify the...

a15_2223128.speaker: Allen
a15_2223128.text: ...arm, and - your rates look good to us down here. Over.

a15_2223128.speaker: Scott
a15_2223128.text: Okay. You had us all figured out. We'll go Free.

a15_2223128.speaker: Allen
a15_2223128.text: And we know one of you will be watching out the window. We're particularly interested if the spin of the satellite is sweeping out a cone or if it seems to be a fairly flat spin as it comes out. Over.

a15_2223355.speaker: Allen
a15_2223355.text: Endeavour, we're requesting you go back to Auto and do another Verb 49, please. We see you've drifted off about a degree.

a15_2223355.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2223355.text: We're 5 minutes away from subsatellite jettison.

a15_2223355.speaker: Allen
a15_2223355.text: Okay, Endeavour. We're recommending that you go back to Free at launch minus one minute.

a15_2223355.speaker: Irwin
a15_2223355.text: Okay; Free at launch minus one minute.

a15_2223355.speaker: Allen
a15_2223355.text: Endeavour, we've got a new update to the last instructions. Go Free at launch, please. [Pause.]

a15_2223355.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2223355.text: Spacecraft rates look good at one minute.

a15_2223355.speaker: Allen
a15_2223355.text: Okay, Dave; copied that. Sounds great. [Pause.]

a15_2223355.speaker: Scott
a15_2223355.text: Oh, looks like it might be oscillating maybe 10 degrees at the most. [Long pause.]

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: And, Endeavour, when you're ready, I've got a coming-home PAD to read to you. [Pause.]

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Stand by one, Joe.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Okay, Jim. And we would like Accept, please, on the computer. [Pause.]

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Stand by one.

a15_2224102.speaker: Scott
a15_2224102.text: A very pretty satellite out there. We get about two flashes per rev off each boom, and it seems to be rotating quite well. Very stable.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Very good, Dave. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: And, Joe, I'm ready to copy that coming-home PAD.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Okay, Jim. I'm ready to read it to you. It's TEI-74, SPS/G&N. The weight, 35768; plus 0.57, plus 0.88; 223:48:45.05; plus 2945.2, minus 0761.3, minus 0171.4; all zips on roll, pitch and yaw; [Pause.] Noun 44 is NA, and plus 0022.1; 3046.8, 2:21, 3028.5; 37; 224.3, 30.5; 053, down 10.3, right 3.1; plus 26.11, minus 157.97; 1084.1, 36179; and the GET, 294:58:34. GDC Align, Vega and Deneb; 102; 178; 028. Four jets, 12-second ullage. And, we'd like Accept, please. And I'm standing by for the readback. Over.

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Okay; you have Accept, and here's the readback, Joe. TEI-74, SPS/G&N; 35768; plus 0.57, plus 0.88; 223:48:45.05; plus 2945.2, minus 0761.3, minus 0171.4; all zips for roll, pitch and yaw; H P , plus 0022.1; 3046.8, 2:21, 3028.5; 37, 224.3, 30.5; 053, down 10.3, right 3.1; plus 26.11, minus 157.97; 1084.1, 36179; 294:58:34. Vega and Deneb; 102; 178; 028. Four jet for 12 seconds.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Okay, Jim. The readback is right on. I've got a TEI-75 preliminary PAD and a Flight Plan update PAD, when your ready. [Pause.]

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Okay, I'll take TEI-75.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Okay. SPS/G&N, TEI-75; 35768; plus 0.57, plus 0.88; 225:48:44.08; plus 2981.4, minus 0807.2, minus 0145.1; 000, 002, 001; all the rest, NA. Ullage, four jet, 12 seconds. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Roger. TEI-75, SPS/G&N; 35768; plus 0.57, plus 0.88; 225:48:44.08; plus 2981.4, minus 0807.2, minus 0145.1; 000, 002, 001. Four jets for 12 seconds.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Sounds good, Jim. Thank you. And I'm standing by for your call for the Flight Plan update.

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Go ahead, Joe; I'll take that.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Okay, Jim. And it's your computer [i.e. the upload of a state vector and target have been completed and the crew can take control of the computer again]. The Flight Plan update begins at 223 plus 51. And change the "Verb 49 maneuver" from the numbers listed to the numbers "127, 270, 030." Over. [Pause.]

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Read you. For the Verb 49 that occurs at 223:51, change the numbers to "127, 270 and 030."

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: That's correct. And the next entry is at 224 plus 00. Change the line "Omni Delta" to read "Omni Charlie."

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Okay, Joe. Going back to 224:00, that'll be "Omni Charlie" instead of "Omni Dog." Then, on that Map Camera photo PAD, its 224:03:00 and stop on MSFN cue. Then down to 224:15, on the "Map Camera, Image Motion" will - it'll be "barber pole plus two" instead of "three". At 224:21, we'll delete the "Verb 49 maneuver." At 224:23, we'll delete the "Map Camera track." At 224:27, delete "Map Camera/Laser Experiment Covers, Closed." And at 224:40, do a "Verb 49 maneuver to 127, 295, 030; High Gain, pitch, 23; yaw, 229."

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Right on, Jim. Thank you.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Good ship, Endeavour, be advised that our tracking stations have acquired the satellite.

a15_2224102.speaker: Scott
a15_2224102.text: Oh, very good.

a15_2230102.speaker: Allen
a15_2230102.text: Roger. Jim, this is a comment for you. When I was reading the Flight Plan update to you, we noticed that you might be coming up on something not too clear in the Flight Plan and it involves the long list of steps between 224 plus 00 and 224 plus about 15. And there are a number of steps in there that have to be accomplished before the T-start time on the Map Camera photo PAD. It may be, you - be you'll want to start on a few of them, I guess, a little early. Over.

a15_2230102.speaker: Allen
a15_2230102.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. We'll be requesting Omni Delta when you lose the uplink.

a15_2230102.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2230102.text: And Endeavour is maneuvering to the burn attitude now.

a15_2231653.speaker: Allen
a15_2231653.text: Roger, Endeavour. I have three requests for you. The first, the Optics is in the CMC Mode, and we've noticed it's drifting off. We'd like you to drive it manually back to a value less than 10 degrees in Trunnion and then zero it. We're also waiting for a DAP load and a P40. And I have a guaranteed last correction to your Flight Plan, when you're ready.

a15_2231653.speaker: Scott
a15_2231653.text: Okay, number 1, we've still got to make the star check. We'll take care of that, and I hope - I hope you've already seen the DAP load and the P40, but we'll take a look at it again for you. [Long pause.]

a15_2231653.speaker: Irwin
a15_2231653.text: Okay, Joe. We - I'm ready to take that last change to the Flight Plan.

a15_2231653.speaker: Allen
a15_2231653.text: Okay, Jim; stand by one. [Long pause.]

a15_2231653.speaker: Allen
a15_2231653.text: Okay, Jimmy, this is an easy one. At 224 plus 14, we want you to delete the line that reads "Map Camera, Image Motion to On, talkback barber pole in three to five seconds, then gray." Delete that line, please. Over.

a15_2231653.speaker: Irwin
a15_2231653.text: Okay, that's an easy one. I'll delete that line that says "Map Camera, Image Motion, On, talkback barber pole in three to five seconds, then gray."

a15_2232305.speaker: Allen
a15_2232305.text: Roger. Dave, Al and Jim, be advised you are Go for Trans-Earth Injection. Set your sails for home. We're predicting good weather, a strong tail wind, and we'll be waiting on the docks. Over.

a15_2232305.speaker: Scott
a15_2232305.text: Okay. Thank you very much, Houston. We'll see you around the corner.

a15_2240105.speaker: Scott
a15_2240105.text: Hello, Houston. Endeavour's on the way home with a burn status report for you.

a15_2240105.speaker: Scott
a15_2240105.text: Roger. Ignition was on time. Burn time was 2 plus 21. No trim. Our residuals were minus 0.2, plus 0.6, and plus 0.2. Delta-V C was minus 16.7; fuel, 2.35; oxidizer, 2.2; the unbalance was about minus 25. And what a smooth burn that one was.

a15_2240105.speaker: Parker
a15_2240105.text: Roger. Sounds very good to us, Dave. [Pause.]

a15_2240105.speaker: Scott
a15_2240105.text: Just can't beat these rocket engines for traveling.

a15_2240105.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2240105.text: That was Dave Scott passing the burn report back to CapCom Bob Parker and Scott reporting the burn almost precisely as planned. Burn time; 2 minutes, 21 seconds and other residuals so low that he did not even have to trim them.

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: Houston, 15. Go.

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: Roger. Two questions. One, we notice you have A/C roll jets selected. I guess we aren't sure whether you have B - A/C roll jets selected on DAP, we aren't sure whether you have A/C or B/D selected on the panel. [Pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Worden
a15_2242010.text: Okay. Al's checking them over now. [Long pause.] Okay, A/C, you're selected.

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: Okay, and could we pry out of you guys any comments on the Moon as you leave?

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: Well, we're almost speechless looking at this thing. It's amazing. Looks like we're going straight up; and we're leaving, there's no doubt about that. And we're right on the terminator. It shows very distinctly all the topography - all the topographic highs and lows. And we can see some major rilles. And we noticed one large lava filling within a depression, with domes very prominent within the lava fill. [Pause.] Oh, it's just really pretty spectacular. We have one crater almost below us that has a flat floor with radial rilles and circumferential rilles extending from the central peaks. I th

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: Roger; copy. Sounds beautiful.

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: It's really spectacular. The elevation - the topography on the ridge line is quite clear, and, of course, all the features near the terminator stand out quite well because of the shadows. And we're busily taking pictures so maybe we can bring some of it back for you to see.

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: Be looking for it in three or four days.

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: Rog. It's really spectacular though, and there's no question that we're leaving. As a matter of fact, the first glimpse we got, it was quite obvious that we're on the way. [Pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Gordon
a15_2242010.text: That's a pretty good view after all those days of going around and around, isn't it Dave?

a15_2242010.speaker: Worden
a15_2242010.text: Yeah, boy.

a15_2242010.speaker: Worden
a15_2242010.text: Looks like you're going straight out, Dick.

a15_2242010.speaker: Gordon
a15_2242010.text: Yep. Reminiscing for me. Thank you.

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: Although, I'll tell you, we never got to see half of what we passed over, I'm sure. There's just so much up there. [Pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Gordon
a15_2242010.text: Well, I'll tell you, Dave, I'm not so sure you guys didn't get at least your share, or maybe a little more. Spectacular.

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2242010.text: That was Dick Gordon reminiscing with Dave Scott there. Gordon was backup commander for Apollo 15 and also was..."

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: Well, I guess our orbital geologist up here just figured out which way we were. I guess we were sort of momentarily disoriented there, because south is up, and we're looking right up and down the terminator. So I guess we're upside down looking at new territory that we haven't seen during the flight. [Long pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: Jim just said "Gee, maybe I ought to look out my window." and, by golly, on his window he's looking up - he's looking up to the north. As a matter of fact, out window number 5 now, you can get a full half - half Moon view. [Pause.] And you can see it all in one big gulp, and boy, what a gulp. [Long pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: We'll look at Tycho, now, before too long. [Pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: That's a good point; we can't see it yet. [Long pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Worden
a15_2242010.text: Houston, 15.

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: Go ahead, 15.

a15_2242010.speaker: Worden
a15_2242010.text: Okay, Bob, I'm looking from Humboldt straight south now, and, in fact, you can draw a line between Humboldt and the - and a great ditch or scarp to the south [Vallis Schrödinger]. And there's quite a change in the - in the light level or the intensity of the albedo in - between those two areas. And it looks like there's some - you know - fairly smooth fresh lava flows throughout that area. And, in fact, we noticed that while we were in orbit also, that in several of those areas around Humboldt there, and to the north of Humboldt, and to the east of Humboldt, that the flows in some of the

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: Copy Al. Very interesting.

a15_2243047.speaker: Scott
a15_2243047.text: And, Houston; 15. As we leave and look back, why, I guess we still have the impression the Moon is mostly gray. However, when you're up-Sun, as we were just prior to TEI - when you're looking up-Sun, it does definitely take on a chocolate brown color. We came around prior to TPI on the day side - or TEI on the day side, looking backwards into the Sun across Schröter's Valley, and that was a pretty spectacular sight. And it did start turning a chocolate brown, but now everything is a variation of gray, very light to a gun-metal gray near the terminator.

a15_2243047.speaker: Parker
a15_2243047.text: Well, is that a unanimous vote in the spacecraft, Dave? [Pause.]

a15_2243047.speaker: Scott
a15_2243047.text: Rog. I got three ayes on that one.

a15_2243047.speaker: Parker
a15_2243047.text: Rog. We'll add that, and continue to keep the score. [Pause.]

a15_2243047.speaker: Scott
a15_2243047.text: Hey, Bob, we don't report to you the other kind.

a15_2243047.speaker: Parker
a15_2243047.text: Some day I'll get up there and make my report.

a15_2243047.speaker: Scott
a15_2243047.text: We can see a point on the terminator now where we mentioned we saw a lava filling and some domes in a depression which is not the circular crater-like depression; it's a big cavity. And now, I guess, as the Sun angle has changed some, we can see where the lava has apparently spilled over a scarp into a deeper cavity, which is in - in shadow. And it's very clearly a filling of the cavity with two levels.

a15_2243047.speaker: Parker
a15_2243047.text: Roger, Dave. We call that a polye, don't we? [Pause.]

a15_2243047.speaker: Scott
a15_2243047.text: Well, I guess if we were in Hawaii.

a15_2243047.speaker: Parker
a15_2243047.text: You guys don't see any motion of that stuff, do you?

a15_2243047.speaker: Scott
a15_2243047.text: And, Houston; 15. We got another unanimous vote up here. That was really a great trip.

a15_2243047.speaker: Parker
a15_2243047.text: Roger. I think that's unanimous on everyone, isn't it?

a15_2243910.speaker: Parker
a15_2243910.text: And, 15, if you'll give us Accept, we'll uplink a REFSMMAT for desired orientation PTC.

a15_2244111.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2244111.text: This is Apollo Control. Most of that vivid description of the lunar surface came from Dave Scott. Al Worden also interjected some comments about what appeared to be distinct fresh lava flows near the crater Humboldt. During the description, the spacecraft was at an altitude that began at about 1,200 [nautical] miles [2,200 km] from the Moon and when most of the description was finished, they were about 1,700 [nautical] miles [3,150 km] from the Moon. Our change of shift press briefing is ready to begin at this time in the MSC News Center Briefing Room. During the briefing, we'll record any con

a15_2244447.speaker: Parker
a15_2244447.text: And, Apollo 15; Houston. We'd like that Verb 49 maneuver, so we can pick up [the] High Gain [Antenna], please.

a15_2244447.speaker: Worden
a15_2244447.text: Roger. We just did it, Bob.

a15_2244500-cospb.speaker: Scott
a15_2244500-cospb.text: Hey, Houston. Take a look at the DSKY. I think those are the numbers you gave us.

a15_2244500-cospb.speaker: Parker
a15_2244500-cospb.text: Roger, 15. Those are the numbers. Looks good, thank you.

a15_2244500-cospb.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2244500-cospb.text: This is Apollo Control at 224 hours, 53 minutes. Apollo 15 now about 27 hundred [nautical] miles [5,000 km] from the Moon, and during the change of shift press briefing, we had one or two very brief exchanges with Dave Scott aboard the spacecraft. We'll play that for you now.

a15_2245729.speaker: Parker
a15_2245729.text: And, 15; Houston. We'd like Gamma-ray Gain Step, On, up, three clicks. Over.

a15_2245729.speaker: Scott
a15_2245729.text: Okay. Gain Step, On, up, three clicks.

a15_2250407.speaker: Parker
a15_2250407.text: Roger. We'd like to move that "Verb 49 maneuver to lunar surface photo attitude" that you'll find at 225:30 in the Flight Plan. We'd like to move that up to 225:24. Over.

a15_2250407.speaker: Worden
a15_2250407.text: Roger. Understand; move the "Verb 49 maneuver" to 225:24.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Apollo 15, Houston.

a15_2252526.speaker: Worden
a15_2252526.text: Houston, 15. Go.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Ah, Rog. Be advised we'll be monitoring your maneuver here in case you get in your gimbal lock. And the High Gain [Antenna] angles [you should use] in case you lose antenna lock in the new attitude will be pitch of minus 45 and yaw of 024. Over.

a15_2252526.speaker: Worden
a15_2252526.text: Roger. Understand pitch minus 45 and yaw 024, if we lose it.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Roger.

a15_2252526.speaker: Worden
a15_2252526.text: And thanks for watching it for us, Bobby. [Long pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: And, 15, if one of you has time, I have a few more Flight Plan updates for you. [Pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Worden
a15_2252526.text: Okay, Houston. Stand by one. [Pause.] Go ahead, Bob.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Okay. The pitch and yaw angles for the P20 - P52 attitude at 226:00 is: pitch of minus 37; yaw of 322. [Pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Irwin
a15_2252526.text: Understand at the P52 attitude, it's pitch minus 37, yaw 322.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Roger. At 226:15, we're changing that Verb 49 maneuver attitude to the following coordinates, 327, 143, 055. [Pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Irwin
a15_2252526.text: Roger. Copy the change to the Verb 49 maneuver that occurs at 226:15 to 327, 143 and 055.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Roger; and the High Gain angles will be pitch 13, yaw 212. [Pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Irwin
a15_2252526.text: Roger. Pitch 13, yaw 212.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Roger. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: And, 15, we're observing yaw of 61 degrees right now. [Long pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: 15, Houston. We have 65 degrees yaw.

a15_2252526.speaker: Worden
a15_2252526.text: Rog, Bob. We're watching.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Okay, three more Flight Plan updates, Jim, if you're ready. [Long pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Worden
a15_2252526.text: Go ahead, Bob.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Okay, at 226:22, on - it'll be a line above the line that says "X-ray, On." The new line that will be added will be "X-ray, Off, for 1 second; then". Over. [Long pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Irwin
a15_2252526.text: Understand. The new line added above "X-ray, On", and it'll read "X-ray, Off, 1 second; then".

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
