a15_2443413.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15_2443413.speaker: Henize
a15_2443413.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15_2443941.speaker: Scott
a15_2443941.text: Houston, Apollo 15. We'll start to charge on battery B now, if you're ready.

a15_2443941.speaker: Henize
a15_2443941.text: Roger, 15. We're ready for the battery charge; and, while we're about it, the experimenters are getting a little fidgety about the waste water dump because that will impact their Mass Spectrograph work, so we would like to get the dump and the O 2 fuel cell purge started also.

a15_2443941.speaker: Scott
a15_2443941.text: Rog. We'll get on it right away. [Long pause.]

a15_2443941.speaker: Henize
a15_2443941.text: And, 15, whenever Al has a couple of minutes, we have a few questions about the SIM bay that we'd like to debrief on. [Pause.]

a15_2443941.speaker: Scott
a15_2443941.text: Okay, give - give him another 15 to 20 minutes here.

a15_2450419.speaker: Henize
a15_2450419.text: We need to make a small change in the Flight Plan, because there's a need now to turn the X-ray experiment on. If you'll go down to that group of steps at 245:30, we'd like to do four of them. We'd like to get the "Data Systems - On - switch to On." We'd like to "Disable the jets." We'd like to get "S-band Aux, TV to Science."

a15_2450419.speaker: Henize
a15_2450419.text: Roger. Four of those steps down to 245:30 we want to do right away, if possible. We want to get the "S-band Aux, TV to Science." We want the "Data System On switch to On." We want to "Disable all jets except -" and we want "X-ray Experiment, On." [Pause.]

a15_2450419.speaker: Worden
a15_2450419.text: Okay. Understand at 45:30 - 245:30, you want "S-band Aux, TV to Science, Data Systems On to On, disable all jets, and X-ray Experiment, On" immediately.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: [Garble].

a15_2451649.speaker: Henize
a15_2451649.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston. We're having some ground problems in communications networks, and we'd like to have a comm check. [Long pause.]

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: Oh! Did you notice anything loose?

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Well, I thought I saw - Well, I saw a...

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: Hey, do you guys [garble] get some orange juice? [Garble]. Let's enjoy it - let's enjoy it while we can.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: [Garble].

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: Except for bad stuff, we can always put up with it for 1 more day.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Yes, that's right. Well - Hey, let's - [garble] will be our last meal. We have three meals below and breakfast [garble] 1 day.

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: And a long way to go.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Oh, hush.

a15_2451649.speaker: Henize
a15_2451649.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston. How do you read? [Pause.]

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Hello, Houston; this is 15. Loud and clear, and I got your first message, Karl. I'm sorry.

a15_2451649.speaker: Henize
a15_2451649.text: Hi, Al. Yeah, we've got some sort of problem on ground circuits here. Just wanted to make sure we were in contact with you.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: No, we're here.

a15_2451649.speaker: Henize
a15_2451649.text: Roger; very good. [Long pause.]

a15_2451649.speaker: SC
a15_2451649.text: [Cough.]

a15_2451649.speaker: Henize
a15_2451649.text: Al, we have some questions for you on the SIM bay experiments, whenever you have some time to answer them.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Oh, yes. That's right. That's great.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Okay, Karl. Tell you what, I'll give you a call back in about 10 minutes when I'm ready.

a15_2451649.speaker: Henize
a15_2451649.text: Very good.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: No, he's got some questions on the SIM bay.

a15_2453050.speaker: Scott
a15_2453050.text: Six-foot waves in the recovery area, huh?

a15_2453050.speaker: Worden
a15_2453050.text: Yes, if we can dodge and land, that's great.

a15_2453323.speaker: Henize
a15_2453323.text: Roger. Just sending up a reminder about the X-ray pointing attitude, which is due very soon now, and the activation of the SIM bay experiments.

a15_2453323.speaker: Worden
a15_2453323.text: Okay, Houston. Boy, oh, boy, I used to think it was a good thing to get on a flight and then they could only talk at you one at a time. Whew, boy! Now, I think it's a good thing to get back so you - you don't have to listen to that goddam radio all the time.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Apollo 15, we'd like to have Omni Alpha. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Rog; Omni Alpha. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Houston, 15.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Go ahead, 15.

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay, Karl. I'm ready to talk SIM bay; but first, a couple of questions.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Fire away. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay. What attitude do you want us to do the UV photo - photography at. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger, Al. The information on - on UV photos is to follow the procedures - Okay - you want the attitude - the procedures are on page 3-352, and the attitude to be used is 210, 242, 322.

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Say the attitude again, please.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: 210, 242, 322. Also, note use of magazine P, and also the time - the time that we start the maneu - the time that we finish the maneuver is 247 plus 45. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: And let me clarify that magazine. That is the magazine for the UV color photographs. That is magazine P instead of magazine M. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay. Understand. Use the procedures on page 3-352 , except change the attitude to 210, 242, and 322, and this whole thing is to be done at 247:45.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. That's the time for completing the maneuver. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Well, what time would you like us to maneuver to that attitude then? [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. The time to start the maneuver is 24 - 247 plus 36.

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: I understand. 247 plus 36. Rog. Thank you, Karl. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay, Al. Are you ready for the SIM bay questions? [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Rog, Karl. Sure am.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay. First of all, the guys down here would like send up their warmest congratulations on such an ex - successful EVA. You sure made it look easy up there. And the questions. The questions we got are about the Mapping Camera, and they're directed at the general problem of is there - was there anything you could see which might indicate why it jammed? And there are three - three particular items that you might have looked at. First of all, it was the main camera cover at the bottom of the camera. Was it touching or scraping the camera in any way that you noticed?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: The answer to that is negative. In fact. I checked it. I checked the Mapping Camera cover, Laser Altimeter cover quite carefully to make sure, because I do know that there have been some interference problems with that before, particularly with the Pan Camera, so I was looking at that in particular to see that it was maybe adjusted too close or - or interfering along the side of the Pan Camera, and it was not. There was about half an inch clearance between the upper edge of the cover and the body of the Mapping Camera, so that I - I don't see that that was responsible for the thing jamming.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. I think you've very clearly put that suspicion to rest. There are also two covers to the solar camera in the upper left side of the Mapping Camera. And did you notice any - any distortion or any scraping in - in these covers? There's one possibility. The one that stuck out to the left - it - it might have jammed and the screwjack that controls it might have twisted it or distorted it. Was there anything you noticed like that?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Negative, Karl. I noticed nothing out of place with the Mapping Camera, nothing interfering. I checked all the way around it, down into the cavity, nothing interfering. I saw no evidence of anything interfering, and it looked clean underneath, so I don't think there was anything blocking it from underneath. I don't know. My distinct impression after surveying the Mapping Camera and looking around the cavity where the Mapping Camera fits was that there is a problem with the drive.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. You didn't see anything inhibiting its motion, not even the electrical cables up on the top, huh?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Negative, and I guess I can ask a question along that line. Has anyone noticed any high current when we've gone to Retract on the Mapping Camera to indicate that it was hanging up?

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: We didn't see any, Al, although there had been a long controversy down here about the long amount of time required to extend and retract. It was, even though it was about the 4 minutes predicted several months ago, it was somewhat longer than what we'd observed at the Cape. People had been worrying about that for some time.

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Yeah, I realize that. And I also, as I re - as I go back to what we saw at the Cape, there was some problems with that thing hanging up in drive itself at the Cape.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. Okay, a couple of questions on the Mass Spectrometer. You gave us some good information there, but when you said the Mass Spectrometer cover wasn't completely closed, could you give us some idea at - as - to - to what degree it had closed, to what angle, and was there any poss - any cocking, any - any twisting in - in that cover.

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Well, I couldn't tell whether there was any warpage in the cover or not, particularly because that kind of a cover is a little - looks like its warped anyway. It looked to me, I could - I pulled the cover out of the way enough to look at the Mass Spec. inside, and I could see the guide pin and along the sides of the carriage coming through the holes all the way up, so that they were plainly visible from the outside which - which meant to me that the - the Mass Spec. was either very close to being seated on the carriage or it was seated. I - I guess I don't really know how far those guide pins

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger, Al. We copy that. And would you open the X-ray and Alpha Covers right now, please?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay, X-ray/Alpha Covers coming open.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay. I guess you've answered most of our questions on the Mass Spec., and you've approached one that we might get a little more out of, and that is those guide rails sticking through the guides. There is a tapered portion, and when it's completely seated, you actually see the - the - the cylindrical portion beyond the tapered portion. Did you actually see the cylindrical portion, or was it all tapered area that you looked at on the guide rail?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay, that's good scoop. All I saw was the tapered area.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. You probably - If it was fully seated, you would have seen about a half inch of - of the cylinder there, and this is a good indication that it was not all the way seated even though it was close. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Here's a couple of other questions. Give me a second to look at them.

a15_2453822.speaker: Scott
a15_2453822.text: Why don't you get the [garble]?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay, Al. Mostly questions here about the contamination status and things in the SIM bay. First of all, how about the - the - the door eder - the door edges? Did they blow off smoothly and cleanly?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Yes, very cleanly. I saw no rough edges at all. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Stand by a moment, Al.

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Don't forget to [garble].

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Ion - Ion Source to Standby.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Al, we're anxious to bring up the High Gain Antenna. I've got a couple of angles here if they'll help.

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Minus 76 and 117. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay. Minus 76 and 117. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay. We copied your comment on the SIM bay door jettison, and further questions go as follows. The white coatings in the SIM bay were - Did you notice that any of them why - were obviously discolored or - or coated from contamination or overheating? [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: I saw no evidence of heating in the SIM bay. I saw no evidence of discoloration of the white surfaces. There were - [cough] - as - as best I could tell, no particulate matter that had come to rest on any of the surfaces in the SIM bay. It looked very, very clean. And - even across the top of the Mapping Camera where there was a - such a heating problem expected, I saw no indications of heating whatsoever, particularly on things like the cover over the Mapping Camera cassette, which was supposedly a very hot spot, and it was just as clean as a whistle. There wasn't - there wasn't any evidence o

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. And, on the insulation and foils, I guess there's a question here - Were any of them burned or discolored? You probably already told us that. Were any of them torn or were there any attachment failures? [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: No, I couldn't see any evidence of - of any burning or tearing or anything else back there, Karl. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay, we got one more general question there. And our Flight Dynamics Officer, who is vitally concerned about our reentry weight, would like to know whether or not we jettisoned more or less than a nominal 32 pounds; and, if so, by how much?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay. Stand by one.

a15_2453822.speaker: Scott
a15_2453822.text: Say, Houston, we've talked it over, and I guess we'd say it was pretty close to a nominal - as far as weight. We have no idea of - of determining exactly what the weight was, but we're going to try and work our reentry stowage over this afternoon and tomorrow morning, and we hope to give you a - a plan by - somewhere around noon tomorrow, of where all the rocks are stowed and where everything is stowed and what we have on board. So you can start - so Mr. FIDO can work up his entry plan.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. And, if somebody has the time to copy it, I've got a small Flight Plan update available now.

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay, Karl. I'll take that.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Hi, Jim. How're you doing?

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Just fine.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay. 246 hours and 20 minutes; we have High Gain [Antenna] angles of pitch, 00; yaw, 240. [Pause.] At...

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. And at 246 plus 46, we want to add "Change discriminator to low." [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Understand. Scratch "Discriminator, High," and make it "Discriminator, Low."

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: That's correct. And, on 247 plus 28, delete that DAP load. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay. We already have that change.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Sorry about that. On 247 plus 30, we'd like to have the "Alpha/X-ray Covers, Closed; then Off", and delete the note on the Cover Open/Close. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay, understand. At 247:30, you'd like "Alpha/X-ray Doors, Closed," and just delete the note here. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. And stand by one second. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: 247 plus 30. Also, we would like to add "Mass Spectrometer Multiplier, High; Discriminator, Low." [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Understand. At 247:30, you want to add "Mass Spec. Multiplier, High, and Discriminator, Low."

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Rog. And, at 247 plus 32, we'd like to have "Mass Spec. Multiplier, High; Discriminator, High." [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay, 247:32, "Mass Spec. Multiplier, High, and Discriminator, High."

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. And I guess you need to save room, if there's any left there, because at 34 and at 36, we want to change these two switches again. At 34, we want "Mass Spec. Multiplier, Low; Discriminator, High." [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Understand. At 34 you want "Multiplier, Low; and Discriminator, High."

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Affirmative and at 36, we want "Multiplier, Low; Discriminator, Low." [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay. At 247:36, it's "Multiplier, Low; and Discriminator, Low."

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Affirmative. Also at 247:36 is "Add the UV photos," and we've already sent up the changes required for that; the changes over and above what's on page 3-352 . And there's one reminder there, and that is to verify that when you use filter 2, that you take one frame for 20 seconds and one frame for 2 seconds.

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Roger. We remember that.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay. The next step is 247 plus 45, "X-ray to Standby." [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay. At 247:45, "X-ray to Standby."

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: And, at 247 plus 50, we want to move the PTC initiation steps from 247:30 to 247:50. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay. Understand. The initiation of PTC to be delayed from 247:30 to 247:50.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: That's affirmative. At 248 hours and 0 minutes, we'd like the following: we'd like the Mass Spectrometer boom retraction sequence. Each retraction step will last 20 minutes, instead of 12. [Pause.] And terminate this test at 249 plus 30. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Go back to 248, Karl, on that Mass Spectrometer boom retraction sequence.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. I...

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: I have that in there.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: I - I guess all - all we're doing there is changing - The - the retraction step will be 20 minutes instead of 12 minutes. Down at the end of the writing there, it says "Each sample period will last 12 minutes." We'd like to have that at 20 minutes. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay. I'll change the note there then. It occurs about 248:20; this 12 will be 20.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: That's correct. At 249:05, we'd like to move the Mass Spec. boom deploy from 05 to 30 - from 249:05 to 249:30. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Understand. Move the Mass Spec. boom deploy from 249:05 to 249:30. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. And one final one at 251:48, which you may already have, is delete the DAP load there.

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: I do; we have that one, Karl.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay. That completes the update. Thank you.

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: 15, Houston. We'd like to have Gamma-ray Gain Step up 4 clicks. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay. That's Gamma-ray Gain Step up 4 clicks.

a15_2463658.speaker: Henize
a15_2463658.text: 15, this is Houston. We trust you'll be pleased to hear the news that the high voltage has been turned on to the subsatellite, and that they find that all systems are operational.

a15_2463658.speaker: Scott
a15_2463658.text: Oh, that's very good. Glad to hear it.

a15_2470446.speaker: Henize
a15_2470446.text: 15, Houston. We have a couple of more comments on the UV photo procedures, if somebody can copy.

a15_2470446.speaker: Henize
a15_2470446.text: Roger. We overlooked the fact that you are taking these photos in the midst of SIM bay operation, so a couple of little things change. Going back to page 3-352 , you can first of all delete, below the damp rates notation, in - you can delete "Inhibit all jets, except" the jets that are there, and just keep the jet configuration you got right now. [Long pause.]

a15_2470446.speaker: Irwin
a15_2470446.text: Okay. I copy that. Do you have any other comments?

a15_2470446.speaker: Henize
a15_2470446.text: Roger. Under "Remove the CM5 window," put in there "CMC, Free," and likewise, about four lines up from the bottom, just above "note", put in "CMC, Auto". And the final comment, "Enable all jets"; you can delete that. [Pause.] And that's all.

a15_2470446.speaker: Irwin
a15_2470446.text: Okay; understand. Just below "Remove CM5 window cover" put "CMC, Free," and then down at the - the bottom there, just above the note, put "CMC, Auto," and scratch "enable all jets."

a15_2473529.speaker: Worden
a15_2473529.text: Dr. Parker, I presume. Listen, Bob, we got to pull the Gamma-ray [boom] to 15 feet at 50, and wonder if you've got an updated retraction time for us.

a15_2473529.speaker: Parker
a15_2473529.text: That's affirm, Al. We have a retract time of 247 plus 50, for 72 seconds. Over.

a15_2473529.speaker: Parker
a15_2473529.text: That's affirm. And, 15, if you got your Flight Plan out, we can update a couple more times in that same general vicinity for you. [Pause.]

a15_2473529.speaker: Worden
a15_2473529.text: Okay, the Flight Plan is out and the door is open.

a15_2473529.speaker: Parker
a15_2473529.text: Okay. At 248:02, the Mass Spec. boom retract time - that should be 33 seconds. And that time will apply to the first retraction. The second, third, fourth, and fifth retractions will be 32 seconds. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2473529.speaker: Irwin
a15_2473529.text: Okay, Bob. Understand that the first retraction is 33 seconds and the succeeding retractions will be 32 seconds. Is that 4 or 5?

a15_2473529.speaker: Parker
a15_2473529.text: Apollo 15, Houston. That will be 32 seconds for all succeeding ones, and we are going to do that up to 249:30. And so all succeeding ones you get will be at 32 seconds. And we will finish that test at 249:30, no matter where we are. And I believe I see that Karl has sent up comment that the sample period would be 20 minutes instead of 12. Is that right?

a15_2473529.speaker: Parker
a15_2473529.text: Okay. And another change: at 249:36, the Gamma-ray deploy. That time will be 63 seconds. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2473529.speaker: Parker
a15_2473529.text: Okay. That's all we have for right now.

a15_2474313.speaker: Parker
a15_2474313.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Request Omni Delta, please.

a15_2474313.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2474313.text: This is Apollo Control at 247 hours, 59 minutes. During our change of shift briefing, we had no conversations with the crew. It's been quiet in Mission Control. And we're standing by live at this time.

a15_2474313-cospb.speaker: Parker
a15_2474313-cospb.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Request Omni Delta, please.

a15_2474313-cospb.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2474313-cospb.text: This is Apollo Control at 247 hours, 59 minutes. During our change of shift briefing, we had no conversations with the crew. It's been quiet in Mission Control. And we're standing by live at this time.

a15_2475913.speaker: Parker
a15_2475913.text: Roger, 15. If you guys will give us a hack when you start the first Mass Spec. retraction, we'll keep an eye on those 20-minute periods for you.

a15_2475913.speaker: Irwin
a15_2475913.text: Bob, we just completed one retraction for 33 seconds.

a15_2480627.speaker: Parker
a15_2480627.text: Roger, 15. We'd like to get a pitch of minus 4.0 and yaw of 90 for the High Gain Antenna. And then, if you'd change your antenna switch to High Gain without hitting the Command Reset switch, we'll maintain comm that way, please.

a15_2480828.speaker: Parker
a15_2480828.text: Negative. You did the right thing without us calling you. Thank you. [Pause.]

a15_2480828.speaker: Irwin
a15_2480828.text: Are we going to press on with the High Gain?

a15_2481417.speaker: Parker
a15_2481417.text: And 15, Houston, your rates look good to us for spinup.

a15_2482139.speaker: Parker
a15_2482139.text: And, 15, time for the next cycle on the Mass Spec.: 32 seconds. [Pause.]

a15_2482139.speaker: Worden
a15_2482139.text: Okay. We were a little ahead of you that time.

a15_2482413.speaker: Parker
a15_2482413.text: Roger. If you guys are - have a moment free, we'll pass up three comments to you preparatory to some stuff you want to do later on. [Pause.]

a15_2482413.speaker: Parker
a15_2482413.text: Okay, first is a reminder that we're counting on using the OPS to pump up the cabin for sleep tonight - another way of bleeding off the OPS. Guess we'll remind you now so you don't stow it away down underneath something where it's inconvenient. And we'd like a read-out on the OPS after you finish pumping up the cabin tonight. Second comment is a reminder that we'd like a cue on the vacuum cleaner, if you intend to use it for this contamination control period coming up in a half hour or so. And third one is that as far as the medics are concerned, it's dealer's choice on who wears the biomed to

a15_2482932.speaker: Parker
a15_2482932.text: Roger. We'd like to confirm Auto, Auto, Off on the O 2 heaters. It looks like we've gone beyond the point where they should have come on. [Pause.]

a15_2482932.speaker: Worden
a15_2482932.text: They're all Off right now, Bob.

a15_2482932.speaker: Parker
a15_2482932.text: Roger. That explains what we are seeing. Roger: we'd like Auto, Auto, Off, please.

a15_2482932.speaker: Worden
a15_2482932.text: Okay, just wanted to clear up the O 2 heaters with you. Are you aware that the last instruction that we had in the Flight Plan was at 243:30 that said "O 2 Heaters, three, Off"?

a15_2482932.speaker: Parker
a15_2482932.text: Stand by. That wasn't on my shift. [Pause.]

a15_2482932.speaker: Worden
a15_2482932.text: You're not the regular crew chief, huh? [Pause.]

a15_2482932.speaker: Parker
a15_2482932.text: 15 - Apollo 15, Houston. That callout at 243:30 is the O 2 heaters for tank 3, only. [Long pause.]

a15_2482932.speaker: Worden
a15_2482932.text: Okay, Robert, I stand corrected. [Long pause.]

a15_2482932.speaker: Irwin
a15_2482932.text: I think this package of mags goes into A-8.

a15_2490103.speaker: Parker
a15_2490103.text: And, Apollo 15; Houston. It's time to retract again.

a15_2490103.speaker: Parker
a15_2490103.text: And, 15, be advised that this is the last retract we'll do. We will not do the fifth retract in order to ensure that we don't damage the filament by getting it in too close. We'll sit in this retracted position for 30 minutes, and then deploy the Mass Spec. boom as per the Flight Plan at 249:30. Over.

a15_2492642.speaker: Irwin
a15_2492642.text: No, you have it on two different pages.

a15_2492642.speaker: Irwin
a15_2492642.text: Hey, what was this one for?

a15_2492642.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2492642.text: This is Apollo Control at 249 hours, 27 minutes. Apollo 15 is now 157,700 nautical miles [292,060 km] from the Earth, traveling at a speed of 3,322 feet per second [1,013 m/s]. The crew, at this time, should be about to get something to eat. Following the eat period they'll be aligning their platform, the guidance system stable platform used in attitude reference. And [they] will also be taking some star sightings using program 23 for midcourse navigation. During the rest period, which is scheduled to begin at 252 hours, 30 minutes, or about 3 hours from now, the Gamma-ray, Alpha Particle and

a15_2492642.speaker: Worden
a15_2492642.text: [Garble] time to figure it out - figured out [garble].

a15_2492642.speaker: Worden
a15_2492642.text: Yes, you got to reckon with him yet.

a15_2492642.speaker: Worden
a15_2492642.text: You're going to have to reckon with him yet on those ...

a15_2492642.speaker: Scott
a15_2492642.text: Yes. [Garble] make sure to recommend that he [garble].

a15_2492642.speaker: Parker
a15_2492642.text: Apollo 15, Houston. About 2 minutes to Mass Spec. boom deploy. And we'd like a Delta-T on the length of time it takes to deploy it, please.

a15_2493343.speaker: Irwin
a15_2493343.text: Bob, the deploy time on the Mass Spec. was 3 and 25.

a15_2495647.speaker: Parker
a15_2495647.text: Apollo 15, Houston. While you're eating your supper there, I thought you might be interested in knowing how the vectors are going. Your vector and the ground's vector are extremely close, and - at least at the moment - we'll see what happens when we take the next P23. Right now we're looking at no midcourse 6 and about 1.8 foot per second for midcourse 7. [Long pause.]

a15_2495647.speaker: Worden
a15_2495647.text: Houston, 15. That sounds pretty good, and it looks like we'll see what happens on the P23s. One - You say 1.7 on midcourse 7 is what it looks like right now.

a15_2495647.speaker: Parker
a15_2495647.text: Roger; 1.8. The vectors, I guess right now, about 4,000 feet apart and about a couple of feet per second in velocity and no more.

a15_2503522.speaker: Worden
a15_2503522.text: I'm so damn happy; nobody could give me any better service.

a15_2503522.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2503522.text: This is Apollo Control. We've still got about 5 or 10 minutes left in the crew eat period. They'll be finishing up their evening meal before completing the last activities, prior to their sleep period. That'll be a platform alignment, and some midcourse navigation. A little while ago, spacecraft communicator, Bob Parker, told the crew that it did not appear, at this time, that we would have to do a midcourse correction at the midcourse correction 6 opportunity, which is in about 22 hours; at 272 hours, 58 minutes. Possibly a small midcourse correction will be required just prior to entry at 29

a15_2504504.speaker: Parker
a15_2504504.text: Apollo 15, Houston. We can terminate battery Bravo charge now. [Pause.]

a15_2504504.speaker: Parker
a15_2504504.text: And 15, Houston. A reminder that when we exit PTC in about 15 minutes, we'd like to do it using the SIM bay RCS configuration. [Long pause.]

a15_2510122.speaker: Parker
a15_2510122.text: And, 15, this is Houston. We have your torquing angles. That's some platform, isn't it?

a15_2510122.speaker: Worden
a15_2510122.text: Yes, sir, Bob. You bet you; it sure is beautiful.

a15_2510122.speaker: Scott
a15_2510122.text: You say that sure has been planned for me?

a15_2511737.speaker: Parker
a15_2511737.text: Roger. Mister Lightning Fingers, we'd appreciate it if you'd keep your Noun 49 on for about 5 seconds on this P23, so we get a nice chance to look at it here on the ground. [Laughter.]

a15_2511737.speaker: Worden
a15_2511737.text: I will do my best, sir.

a15_2514253.speaker: Parker
a15_2514253.text: Super marks, Al. You can do my P23s any day. [Pause.]

a15_2514253.speaker: Worden
a15_2514253.text: They looking okay down there, Bob?

a15_2514253.speaker: Parker
a15_2514253.text: Rog. We caught all of them. Hey, when you go back into PTC now, we'd like to change Noun 79, the rate one anyway, to a minus .42. Over.

a15_2514253.speaker: Worden
a15_2514253.text: Going to try a little higher one, now? Okay, minus .42.

a15_2514253.speaker: Parker
a15_2514253.text: And, 15; Houston. If you've got a minute, we've got a couple more comments for you.

a15_2514253.speaker: Worden
a15_2514253.text: Okay. Anything I need to write down?

a15_2514253.speaker: Parker
a15_2514253.text: ...number one, we'd like to know the film status of magazine Victor. And number two, if you're planning on being the loop tonight, Al, for the biomed, your harness needs some attention. The heart rate that we're getting down is getting a little noisy. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2514253.speaker: Worden
a15_2514253.text: Well, in the first place, my heart rate is always noisy; and, in the second place, I guess Jim's going to be on tonight.

a15_2514253.speaker: Worden
a15_2514253.text: Okay, Bob. Mag Victor is 12 frames expended.

a15_2515726.speaker: Parker
a15_2515726.text: 15, Houston. We suggest that you go ahead with your Gamma-ray deployment while you're doing your rate damping. [Pause.]

a15_2515919.speaker: Parker
a15_2515919.text: And, 15; Houston. If you feel like it, we can take your E-mod now.

a15_2515919.speaker: Parker
a15_2515919.text: And, 15, we have your E-memory dump.

a15_2520437.speaker: Parker
a15_2520437.text: 15, Houston. We're Go for spinup for PTC.

a15_2521941.speaker: Scott
a15_2521941.text: Hi, Bob; got a presleep checklist for you.

a15_2521941.speaker: Parker
a15_2521941.text: Shoot; we're ready. Dave, hold on. We got a...

a15_2521941.speaker: Parker
a15_2521941.text: Okay, 15, we're back with you. We just had a site changeover.

a15_2521941.speaker: Scott
a15_2521941.text: Okay. Crew status is all good, no medication. And I've got the onboard read-outs if you've got a pencil.

a15_2521941.speaker: Scott
a15_2521941.text: All righty. Starting with Bat C, 37.0, 37.0, 37.0; RCS A is 56, B is 50, 48, and 52. And I guess everything else has been done, and I guess you got your E-memory dump. We pressurized the cabin with the OPS, and, when we got to about 5.7 or 5.8, the OPS was down to 800. And I reckon that's the size of it.

a15_2521941.speaker: Parker
a15_2521941.text: Roger, Dave. That sounds like the size of it to us. We copy all that, and there will be no vector update. Ground says your vector is just as good as theirs right now.

a15_2521941.speaker: Scott
a15_2521941.text: How about that? Oh, that's pretty good. We got a good navigator.

a15_2521941.speaker: Parker
a15_2521941.text: And, 15, let's hold a couple of minutes while we check some data on SIM bay and while we go around the MOCR one more time. And we'll be back with you in final status, I hope.

a15_2521941.speaker: Scott
a15_2521941.text: [Laughter.] Okay, we got - we got time. We're not quite ready to go to bed yet.

a15_2522515.speaker: Parker
a15_2522515.text: Apollo 15, Houston, the only thing we show lacking at the moment is Gamma-ray Gain Step, Shield, On. Other than that, you're Go for sleep.

a15_2522515.speaker: Scott
a15_2522515.text: Okay, understand. Gain Step, Shield, On.

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: Good morning, Endeavour. This is Houston. [Long pause.]

a15_2612900.speaker: Worden
a15_2612900.text: Hello, you guys.

a15_2612900.speaker: Scott
a15_2612900.text: Good morning.

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: Good morning, Dave. A little something special for your LMP from your lunar lift-off Flight Director with young Ed Fendell on the cymbal.

a15_2612900.speaker: Worden
a15_2612900.text: Oh, man; he's standing at attention right now. [Pause.]

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: Roger. We copy that. [Long pause.]

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: Endeavour, this is Houston, with our first request of the day. We'd like the X-ray Spectrometer, On, please.

a15_2612900.speaker: Scott
a15_2612900.text: Rog. Coming on.

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: Okay, Dave. And I've got High Gain Antenna angles for you when you exit PTC. [Pause.]

a15_2612900.speaker: Worden
a15_2612900.text: Okay. Stand by one, Joe. [Long pause.]

a15_2612900.speaker: Scott
a15_2612900.text: Okay. Go with your High Gain angles.

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: Roger. High Gain pitch, plus 24; yaw, 264. And, Dave, I've got CSM consumables if you're interested in copying those. [Pause.]

a15_2612900.speaker: Scott
a15_2612900.text: Okay. Go, Joe.

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: Roger. GET 261 plus 00. RCS total, 38. Quad A, 42; 39, 32, 38. H 2 tank: 34, 32, 33. O 2 tank: 49, 50, 40. And there's a note on that which reads, "Fat City." Over. [Pause.]

a15_2612900.speaker: Scott
a15_2612900.text: Yeah, man. I guess so. That's pretty even, isn't it?

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: Yes, sir. [Pause.] And, Dave, a comment...

a15_2612900.speaker: Scott
a15_2612900.text: What a machine.

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: Roger. A comment: you're being served now by the MOCR shift that witnessed a new endurance record for Apollo flights, being set during the night. [Pause.]

a15_2612900.speaker: Scott
a15_2612900.text: Ohh, that's interesting. We'd forgotten about that. [Long pause.]

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: And, Endeavour, I'll be standing by for when you're ready to copy down the few changes in your Flight Plan for today. I can bring you up to date over the next 7 hours or so and get all that out of the way. I'm also curious to know if you've had time to listen to any sea shanties from the HMS Endeavour up there. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2612900.speaker: Scott
a15_2612900.text: No. We haven't had a chance to, Joe. Stand by and I'll get my trusty pen out, after we get through with this - coming out of PTC, and we'll do the Flight Plan.

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: Okay, fine. You should ask your trusty record librarian, Al, where the sea shanties are, if you have time today.

a15_2612900.speaker: Scott
a15_2612900.text: Okay. We were talking about that last night, and came to the realization that we brought all these neat things along, and we hadn't had time to listen to a single one of them.

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: Not at all surprised to hear it.

a15_2612900.speaker: Scott
a15_2612900.text: I'll tell you, yesterday, we finally got to catch our breath. [Pause.]

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: You always said the hours are long. [Pause.]

a15_2612900.speaker: Scott
a15_2612900.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_2612900.speaker: Scott
a15_2612900.text: The hours are long but the accommodations are palatial.

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: Was that the way it went, Dave? [Pause.]

a15_2612900.speaker: Scott
a15_2612900.text: Sounds like you've recovered from all that - the other - couple of last few days, too.

a15_2612900.speaker: Allen
a15_2612900.text: Very nearly.

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Houston, this is 15. Standing by to copy Flight Plan update.

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: Roger, Jim. Good morning. The first...

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Good morning, Joe.

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: ...entry should be at 261:42. [Pause.] And it is a - a change in the first register of the DAP load - the time column. We want that to read, 11101. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Give me the time again on that, Joe.

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: Roger. 261 plus 42. [Long pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Okay. At 261:42, I don't see any DAP information. I see one on 261:35.

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: I may have done it again, Jim. Let me see. [Long pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: Stand by on that. Let's - let's continue on with some of the easier steps. At 262...

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Roger. [Laughter.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: ...plus 05, it should - that - that - that's 262 plus 05 add "Gamma-ray Gain Step, two steps." [Long pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Understand. At 262:05, Gamma-ray, two steps.

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: Roger. And at 263:55, under the line "Noun 70," et cetera , add "X-ray to Standby." And at 263:59 delete the Verb 48 line and the DAP load over in the time column. [Long pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Okay; at 263:55, we'll add a step there after the Noun 70, X-ray to Standby; and then, at 263:59, we'll delete the Verb 48 and also delete the DAP load that's in the time column.

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: Roger. Turning the page to 264:02, the DAP [pause] load in the time column should read, 11101. And at 265...

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Okay; understand.

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: ...the DAP load status in the notes column should read, 11101, X1111, and this continues through for 2 hours. Over. [Long pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Okay. Understand that 264:00, in time column, changed the DAP load there from all ones to 11101; and then, at 265, the DAP load will be changed the same way to continue for 2 hours. [Pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: That's correct, Jim. And moving on to 266:30, delete the "Gamma-ray Gain Step to Shield, On" line. [Pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Okay. 266:30, to - eliminate the Gamma-ray Gain Step.

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: Roger. Moving to 267 plus 20, add the two steps: "Gamma-ray boom, Retract, talkback barber pole for about 2½ minutes, then gray, and then Off." And the second step, "Gamma-ray Gain Step to Shield, On." [Long pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Okay. Understand, there are two steps there. The first one is Gamma-ray Retract, barber pole for about 2½ minutes, then gray, and then turn it Off. Second one is Gamma-ray Gain Step to Shield, On.

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: That's correct. Moving to 267 plus 42, change the DAP load in the time column to read 11101, X1111. Over.

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Understand, from all ones to 11101.

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: That's correct. Turning the page to 268:02, the DAP load in the time column, the same change. [Pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Okay. I copy. [Long pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: Okay. On the same page, 268:30, Gamma-ray Gain Step, five steps. [Long pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Understand, Gamma-ray Gain Step to five steps. [Pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: That's correct, Jim. Now looking at page 3-378 , the "UV photos - Trans-Earth Coast," A couple of changes there. About halfway down the page where it reads "two frames, filter 2, exposure time 20 seconds,". [Pause.] Delete that line, and add the line - the two lines, "one frame, filter 2, exposure time 20 seconds; one frame, filter 2, exposure time 2 seconds." [Pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Okay. I have that. Joe. It's kind of our standard change in the UV procedures.

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: That's correct, Jim. And the mag Metro under the "configure camera" section should be changed to read mag Papa. [Pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Okay. Understand mag Papa.

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: Okay, Jim. And the last one for you, a biggie, turning over four pages to the "Sextant Photo Test", strike the line "PCM Cable". [Pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Okay. Eliminate PCM cable on - on the Sextant Photo Test.

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Can we go back now to the very first one? [Pause.]

a15_2614900.speaker: Allen
a15_2614900.text: Jim, I knew you were going to ask that. The first one, I guess, was a small typographical error, and there's no change required there. And, please don't tell Dave about it. He's keeping score against me.

a15_2614900.speaker: Irwin
a15_2614900.text: Okay [chuckle].

a15_2620521.speaker: Allen
a15_2620521.text: Endeavour, this is Houston with a forecast weather report for your landing area. They're calling for a high scattered - 2,000 [feet altitude] scattered, 10 miles vis[ibility], winds about 15 knots out of the east-northeast, waves going to 4 feet, and we're predicting no midcourse 6 correction for trajectory reasons. From the weather report none is required for weather reasons. Over.

a15_2620521.speaker: Scott
a15_2620521.text: Gee, that sounds pretty good, Joe. Except we saw a movie about that weather stuff once. [Long pause.]

a15_2620521.speaker: Allen
a15_2620521.text: Rog. We copy that. And, Dave, we do have one question. Is it true that nothing can stop the Army Air Corps? [Pause.]

a15_2620521.speaker: Scott
a15_2620521.text: Well, that means you're just about qualified. [Pause.]

a15_2620521.speaker: Allen
a15_2620521.text: I'm glad you still have reservations, though. Your Gamma, by the way, is right on 6.5 as close we can tell right now. [Pause.]

a15_2620521.speaker: Scott
a15_2620521.text: Well, that's pretty good. Must be compensating errors along the way somewhere.

a15_2620933.speaker: Scott
a15_2620933.text: Say, Houston; 15.

a15_2620933.speaker: Allen
a15_2620933.text: Go ahead.

a15_2620933.speaker: Scott
a15_2620933.text: We reviewed our entry stowage last night. We're going to do the stowing this morning. And in the process, why, we came up with one extra little bag up here, which we're labeling LM return items, which is essentially the same thing as 14 brought back. And I wonder if you might check with our good FIDO and see if he wants the details of that, or whether maybe Ed Mitchell can give you the general kind of items, and that would be acceptable. But we have one - one bag, which I'm sure you're aware of, and we'll stow it and tell him exactly where we stowed it. And if he wants the details, well, we'll

a15_2620933.speaker: Allen
a15_2620933.text: Okay, fine, Dave. We copy that, and pass that information along. I have the morning news report if you're interested in listening.

a15_2620933.speaker: Scott
a15_2620933.text: Rog. Everybody's hooked up and listening. Go.

a15_2620933.speaker: Allen
a15_2620933.text: Roger. This is the news for 6 August, 1971. In the first round in the American Classic at Firestone Country Club, Akron, Ohio, the leaders are Jerry Heard and Mike Hill, both with 3 under par 67s. Arnie Palmer shot a 70 and Nicklaus a 73. The U.S. built its gold medal total to 50 in the Pan Am Games, and they're entering their second week now. Cuba is a distant second with 17 gold medals, but a Cuban set a world record yesterday in the hop, skip, and jump. The record was 57 feet, 1 inch. We're coming up on the first full weekend of national football exhibition games, and New Orleans Saints pla

a15_2620933.speaker: Allen
a15_2620933.text: We want to interrupt here. If we could have Accept, please, we'll provide you with a new state vector.

a15_2620933.speaker: Scott
a15_2620933.text: Oh, that's very good news, Joe. Thank you. We hadn't heard about the LR cubed, but we were hoping it was super-clean. [Pause.]

a15_2620933.speaker: Allen
a15_2620933.text: Roger; and it's your computer.

a15_2620933.speaker: Scott
a15_2620933.text: Rog.

a15_2620933.speaker: Allen
a15_2620933.text: And, an added a note for Al. Alfredo, I'm not sure if you got a report on your bistatic radar experiment. Taylor Howard got very, very clean echoes on both the S-band and the VHF frequencies, and he's busy analysing that data right now.

a15_2620933.speaker: Worden
a15_2620933.text: Very good, Joe. [Long pause.]

a15_2620933.speaker: Allen
a15_2620933.text: Endeavour, this is Houston with a final update concerning the trusty LCRU on the lunar surface. We turned it on yesterday, and it worked beautifully for about 13 minutes. We w - we were panning around, zooming in and out, got a few more good pictures of the - the surrounding mountains, and suddenly we lost the TM [telemetry] downlink. In fact, we lost everything in a very short time, about 1/60th of a second, almost as though someone had turned it off. We tried - we waited awhile and tried to reactivate it, and did such things as send signals back to it to pan around, while we looked carefully

a15_2620933.speaker: Allen
a15_2620933.text: Endeavour, this is Houston with a final update concerning the trusty LCRU on the lunar surface. We turned it on yesterday, and it worked beautifully for about 13 minutes. We w...we were panning around, zooming in and out, got a few more good pictures of the - the surrounding mountains, and suddenly we lost the TM (telemetry) downlink. In fact, we lost everything in a very short time, about 1/60th of a second, almost as though someone had turned it off. We tried - we waited awhile and tried to reactivate it, and did such things as send signals back to it to pan around, while we looked carefully

a15_2620933.speaker: Scott
a15_2620933.text: Gee, that's interesting, Joe. It's - you sh - I guess it completely went off, and just didn't get hung up somewhere.

a15_2620933.speaker: Scott
a15_2620933.text: Gee, that's interesting, Joe. I guess it completely went off, and just didn't get hung up somewhere.

a15_2620933.speaker: Allen
a15_2620933.text: That's right, Dave. It wasn't a mechanical problem. We most likely popped a circuit breaker or something like that. It's a little difficult to sort out.

a15_2620933.speaker: Scott
a15_2620933.text: Would you like us to go back up and check it for you?

a15_2620933.speaker: Allen
a15_2620933.text: Knew you were going to ask. Stand - stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_2620933.speaker: Allen
a15_2620933.text: Knew you were going to ask. [The following is a part of an extended discussion that Dave and I had just prior to the start of our Apollo 15 mission review. I had sent Dave an Apollo 15 summary, which Apollo 17 crew member Jack Schmitt had read previously. The draft that Dave read included a number of Jack's comments, many of which drew comments from Dave.] [Scott - "What was created in this exercise (meaning the Apollo Program) was a methodology by which humans decided how to go exploring another planet; which, as we all learned is quite different from exploring this planet (Earth), because th

a15_2620933.speaker: Scott
a15_2620933.text: Joe, I'm - I'm in - I'm interested in hearing you say that the temperatures were normal. One of the things that - Of course, we'll debrief them on when we get back, but Jim and I both noticed that each successive day was warmer than the preceding day. And, on the last day, if you left your hand or something in one position for any period of time, it would really - the suit would really heat up on that particular surface. And I'm surprised that the system ran this long with that temperature up there, because I suspect it really got pretty hot. [Pause.]

a15_2620933.speaker: Allen
a15_2620933.text: Dave, that's interesting comment. By normal, I guess I mean within limits. It apparently was about 90 degrees [Fahrenheit, 32°C] on the LCRU and about 90 de - 92 degrees [F, 33°C] on the camera when it gave up the ghost. However, that's well within its limits, and we don't think that circuit breakers, or whatever, let go because of the temperature. The one thing we did not have sensored, as I understand it, were the - the batt[ery] temperatures of the Rover that was - that was feeding the power into the TV, however. [Pause.]

a15_2620933.speaker: Scott
a15_2620933.text: Gee, 92 sounds pretty cool to us. I - I would have guessed much - much hotter than that. That's a pretty good thermal system on it, if it kept the temperatures down that low.

a15_2620933.speaker: Allen
a15_2620933.text: That's correct. [Pause.]

a15_2620933.speaker: Scott
a15_2620933.text: Or maybe [laughter] Jim mentioned maybe that's centigrade, huh? [Pause.]

a15_2620933.speaker: Allen
a15_2620933.text: Negative on the centigrade, Dave. However, when we turned the camera off at the end of EVA 3, the temperature was up around 122 degrees [F, 50°C]. [Pause.]

a15_2620933.speaker: Scott
a15_2620933.text: Yeah, I'd believe that, easily.

a15_2622602.speaker: Allen
a15_2622602.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. The Surgeon reports that we have good respiratory data from your biomed volunteer, but we have evidence that one of the three EKG leads is open-circuited, either not attached or broken somewhere. And, sometime over the next few hours, we'd like - we'd like you to troubleshoot this for us, please; and, if need be, there is an extra biomed harness in the medicine kit. Over.

a15_2622602.speaker: Scott
a15_2622602.text: Roger. Okay. We'll check into that.

a15_2630539.speaker: Allen
a15_2630539.text: Good Ship Endeavour, this is Houston. We'd like a crew status report at your convenience, please.

a15_2630827.speaker: Irwin
a15_2630827.text: Okay, Joe, I have the crew status. We all got 8 hours sleep. PRD readings were: Al was 25031, and mine was 08042. Consumables at 261:00; RCS total, 38. Quads: 42, 32, 39 and 38. H 2 : 34, 32 and 33. O 2 : 49, 50 and 40. Over.

a15_2632524.speaker: Worden
a15_2632524.text: Roger. I've resensored the EKG and appreciate a checkout from the docs down there.

a15_2632524.speaker: Henize
a15_2632524.text: Good morning, Al. How are you doing?

a15_2632524.speaker: Henize
a15_2632524.text: Says the EKG looks good down here. Hold one.

a15_2632927.speaker: Henize
a15_2632927.text: Al, your new CapCom is just coming up to speed this morning. I understand that there has been a problem with the biomed harness, and they want to know if the one you have on right now is the one that gave trouble shortly before.

a15_2632927.speaker: Worden
a15_2632927.text: That's affirmative. And I did find the loose one.

a15_2632927.speaker: Henize
a15_2632927.text: Okay; we're getting a good signal on you, and I guess that information makes everybody happy down here. Thank you.

a15_2635843.speaker: Henize
a15_2635843.text: 15, this is Houston. We still have a concern about your OPS pressure and would appreciate it, if it's at all accessible, to have a reading at the present time. [Pause.]

a15_2635843.speaker: Scott
a15_2635843.text: Okay; it's - it's pretty well buried right now, Karl. What's your concern on it?

a15_2635843.speaker: Henize
a15_2635843.text: Well, first of all, they're anxious that the OPS pressure be down close to zero at - at entry, and they'd like to figure out how much they're going to use tonight and how much tomorrow night in order to bring that down. I guess we don't have it tomorrow night. They're - they're anxious to know whether or not it's - we're going to be able to bring down it's pressure in using it tonight. [Pause.]

a15_2635843.speaker: Scott
a15_2635843.text: Okay. I guess it came down to 800 [psi, 5,500 kPa] from 2,000 [psi, 13,800 kPa] last night, but probably came back up. As soon as we get a chance to do some shuffling around here, why, we'll check it and give you a call.

a15_2635843.speaker: Scott
a15_2635843.text: Rog. It's sort of down in the bottom of the pile right now; and we're getting ready to start reentry stowage, so we'll be able to - to get to it in a little while.

a15_2640248.speaker: Henize
a15_2640248.text: Al, the way people talk down here, they're going to give you a medal for good sightings up - up there. They say that the - the gamma [this is the re-entry angle] from this last series of sightings was 6.55 [degrees], whereas the value we have down here is 6.50.

a15_2640433.speaker: Scott
a15_2640433.text: Houston, 15. You may have seen an - an excursion there as we started the Verb 49 maneuver to PTC, and we're trying to figure it out, too.

a15_2640433.speaker: Henize
a15_2640433.text: We copy.

a15_2640433.speaker: Voice in Mission Control
a15_2640433.text: What was that?

a15_2640433.speaker: Henize
a15_2640433.text: 15, Houston. We didn't see any obvious glitches down here, but we're going to go back and look at the data.

a15_2640433.speaker: Scott
a15_2640433.text: Okay. What happened was, we were loading Noun 22 to the Verb 49; and, apparently on the - the last entry, on the third register, we got about a 1-degree-per-second pitchdown pitch rate, and went to SCS, and then back to ch - to CMC, and tried it again, and it worked just fine.

a15_2640433.speaker: Henize
a15_2640433.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_2640433.speaker: Scott
a15_2640433.text: Houston, it looks like we might have got that old 22 degree glitch in the CDU. [Pause.]

a15_2640433.speaker: Henize
a15_2640433.text: We copy. [Long pause.]

a15_2640433.speaker: Scott
a15_2640433.text: And, Houston, right now, we're reading about: 93, 93 and 334 on the ball. [Long pause.]

a15_2640433.speaker: Henize
a15_2640433.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_2640433.speaker: Henize
a15_2640433.text: 15, this is Houston. We feel that we can get rid of that discrepancy if you'll do a Verb 40, Noun 20.

a15_2640433.speaker: Scott
a15_2640433.text: Okay, we'll do one of those. [Long pause.]

a15_2640433.speaker: Scott
a15_2640433.text: Yep. Looks like that's what it was.

a15_2640433.speaker: Henize
a15_2640433.text: Dave, we suspect the cause of that glitch back there was possibly due to the fact that you might have loaded a Noun 20 instead of a Noun 22. Is that possible? [Pause.]

a15_2640433.speaker: Scott
a15_2640433.text: We're thinking. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_2640433.speaker: Scott
a15_2640433.text: Karl, I guess it's a possibility, but we were both looking at it, and I guess we don't think so, but that's a distinct possibility. [Long pause.]

a15_2640433.speaker: Henize
a15_2640433.text: 15, Houston. About all we can say is that everything's looking fine at the moment, and we'll go back and look over the data. We haven't had a chance to do that yet.

a15_2640433.speaker: Scott
a15_2640433.text: Okay. Yes. Roger. Understand. It - it looks fine up here and that - that could have been the problem.

a15_2640433.speaker: Scott
a15_2640433.text: Houston, 15. Talking it over, I guess that must have been a - a Noun 20 load because, I guess as I remember it, the CDU glitches occur in increments of 11. And 11 plus 11 doesn't equal 26, I don't think.

a15_2640433.speaker: Henize
a15_2640433.text: Okay; we copy.

a15_2640433.speaker: Scott
a15_2640433.text: And, Houston, in our present attitude, a yaw CDU change would be converted to a pitch rate, so that sort of all adds up.

a15_2640433.speaker: Henize
a15_2640433.text: Very good.

a15_2641804.speaker: Henize
a15_2641804.text: 15, Houston. When you have some time to listen, I have a couple of sentences of comments on the procedure for the - the light flash experiment.

a15_2641804.speaker: Scott
a15_2641804.text: Okay. Why don't you stand by 'til we get our trusty crew all lined up and ready to go.

a15_2641804.speaker: Henize
a15_2641804.text: Incidentally, Dave, as we line them up, one of the changes is that we'd like to keep the cabin lights bright this time.

a15_2641804.speaker: Scott
a15_2641804.text: Oh, you like the lights bright? Okay.

a15_2642104.speaker: Henize
a15_2642104.text: 15, Houston. We see indications that the optics aren't zeroed, and we'd recommend that you zero them, with the reminder, of course, to bring the angles down to 10 degrees - less than 10 degrees before you zero them.

a15_2642104.speaker: Scott
a15_2642104.text: Okay; that's - that's standard procedure. We'll get it. Thank you. [Pause.] It's even been written up on the panel for about 8 days now, or so.

a15_2642611.speaker: Scott
a15_2642611.text: Okay, Houston. Go ahead with your procedures on the light flash.

a15_2642611.speaker: Scott
a15_2642611.text: Okay. Understand the - open the eyes, and - Stand by one. [Pause.]

a15_2642611.speaker: Scott
a15_2642611.text: And, Houston, we talked over the - the downlink bit, and it's just impractical if we're all going to try and keep up with the comments on where and what we see. It would just be too confusing for you. And I think - if - if you cannot get your data from the tape, we'll do that; but, I think it is much more practical to go ahead and put it on the tape and just inform you of when we get the marks.

a15_2642611.speaker: Henize
a15_2642611.text: Okay, we've had - we've had - we've had some trouble with the tape in the last couple of times around, is the reason the people are sort of saying "Hey, if we could possibly get it down in real time we'd feel happier." [Pause.]

a15_2642611.speaker: Scott
a15_2642611.text: Oh, you - you mean you - you cannot get the data off the tape, huh? [Long pause.]

a15_2642611.speaker: Henize
a15_2642611.text: I guess we've been having trouble with the voice quality on the DSE [Data Storage Equipment], and Gerry just now says, "Hey, let's check it right now. See how it's doing." And we'll let you know in the next few minutes as to what's pref - preferable.

a15_2642611.speaker: Scott
a15_2642611.text: Okay. That's a good idea. [Long pause.]

a15_2642611.speaker: Henize
a15_2642611.text: 15, this is Houston. It looks as though the DSE voice downlink is acceptable, now; and we'll do it your way. [Pause.]

a15_2642611.speaker: Scott
a15_2642611.text: Okay. Let us get squared away here and make sure we get all the shades up and all. [Long pause.]

a15_2642611.speaker: Henize
a15_2642611.text: 15, one more comment on that DSE voice problem. This is, to some extent, dependent on how well your mikes are adjusted. So make sure that they're in a good position.

a15_2642611.speaker: Scott
a15_2642611.text: Rog. I guess a downlink would probably be the same problem. We'll get them all squared away.

a15_2642611.speaker: Scott
a15_2642611.text: How do the rates look for PTC now?

a15_2642611.speaker: Henize
a15_2642611.text: Just got the word that they look good for spin-up.

a15_2642611.speaker: Henize
a15_2642611.text: I think that's another great example of ESP at work.

a15_2643450.speaker: Worden
a15_2643450.text: Okay, Houston; 15. We're experimenting [for light flashes]. [Pause.]

a15_2643450.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2643450.text: Distance is 124,934 nautical miles [231,377 km]. Velocity; 4,272 feet per second [1,302 metres/second].

a15_2644619.speaker: Scott
a15_2644619.text: Houston, 15. We're still here; it just looks like a quiet morning.

a15_2644619.speaker: Henize
a15_2644619.text: Roger. Glad to know that you're still awake. Keep on looking for the cosmic rays.

a15_2644619.speaker: Scott
a15_2644619.text: Looking as hard as we can.

a15_2645244.speaker: Scott
a15_2645244.text: Yes, down on the left eye at about 7 o'clock; intensity about 2. Point source of light.

a15_2650133.speaker: Irwin
a15_2650133.text: Flash at 8 o'clock on the periphery; intensity 2.

a15_2650133.speaker: Scott
a15_2650133.text: It was in the left eye at 6 o'clock at about a third of the way from the center out; intensity 3; point source of light.

a15_2650133.speaker: Worden
a15_2650133.text: You two guys must be shielding me.

a15_2650133.speaker: Scott
a15_2650133.text: It was in the left eye about 2 o'clock; a quarter of the way in; intensity 1; point source. Yes, we're taking it all for you, Al.

a15_2650133.speaker: Irwin
a15_2650133.text: I think Dave's imagining all these.

a15_2650133.speaker: Scott
a15_2650133.text: Got to do something for the [garble].

a15_2650133.speaker: Worden
a15_2650133.text: [Garble] he's gotten to the point where he's conjuring them up on me.

a15_2650133.speaker: Worden
a15_2650133.text: Right. Protecting all those who go after you.

a15_2650133.speaker: Scott
a15_2650133.text: Wait until you see how many I'm going to see in the last minute [laughter].

a15_2650133.speaker: Worden
a15_2650133.text: Left eye; dead center; intensity 2; point source. Only ones I can see are the ones that hit me right between the eyes like a ...

a15_2650802.speaker: Worden
a15_2650802.text: Right eye; about 1 o'clock; 2/3rds of the way out; intensity 2; and a little streaking - some towards the center of the eye - about another third of the way down.

a15_2650802.speaker: Irwin
a15_2650802.text: Do you have your eyelids closed?

a15_2650802.speaker: Worden
a15_2650802.text: Two flashes: one at 9 o'clock in the left eye and one at 6 o'clock in the left eye; both intensity 3. Yes, my eyes are closed, Jim.

a15_2650802.speaker: Worden
a15_2650802.text: Your eyelids aren't going to stop anything.

a15_2650802.speaker: Irwin
a15_2650802.text: Don't think so. Just want to get consistent data.

a15_2650802.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2650802.text: This is Apollo Control at 265 hours, 10 minutes. The Apollo 15 crew has about another 10 minutes left in the light-flash experiment. They're recording this data on the onboard tape recorder. Although obviously every once in a while the Command Module Pilot keys the air to ground when he takes a mark; you can hear that. Apollo 15 now 123,490 nautical miles [228,703 km] from Earth. Velocity: 4,320 feet per second [1,317 m/s]. We're 30 hours away from landing.

a15_2650802.speaker: Irwin
a15_2650802.text: Mark LMP. Flash. One at 4 o'clock, halfway out. Another one at 2 o'clock on the periphery. Intensity 3. [Long pause.]

a15_2650802.speaker: Worden
a15_2650802.text: Two o'clock; almost on the periphery; and intensity between 3 and 4. Bright one.

a15_2650802.speaker: Worden
a15_2650802.text: Two o'clock; streak from right to left; centered about the 2 o'clock radial; about halfway out; intensity 2.

a15_2652030.speaker: Irwin
a15_2652030.text: We could look at the Flight Plan when we get through. The distances are in there.

a15_2652030.speaker: Worden
a15_2652030.text: Mm-hmm. Yes. We could always figure it out.

a15_2652030.speaker: Irwin
a15_2652030.text: It was a streak; left eye; top to bottom; intensity 2; it was right at the periphery.

a15_2652030.speaker: Irwin
a15_2652030.text: Again it was a streak; it was - appeared to be in both eyes; moving from 1 o'clock toward the center; intensity 3.

a15_2652030.speaker: Worden
a15_2652030.text: Right eye; 11 o'clock; about halfway out; point source; intensity 3.

a15_2652851.speaker: Irwin
a15_2652851.text: Flash; position 2 on the periphery; right eye; intensity 2.

a15_2652851.speaker: Henize
a15_2652851.text: 15, Houston. Be advised the DSE just ran out tape. If there's anything significant to be said from here on in, say it on the air to ground, please.

a15_2652851.speaker: Irwin
a15_2652851.text: Mark LMP. Flash. Four o'clock, about a quarter of the way out. Intensity 3. [Long pause.]

a15_2652851.speaker: Scott
a15_2652851.text: Mark CDR. Right eye; a streak about 3 o'clock to 6 o'clock. Intensity 2. [Long pause.]

a15_2652851.speaker: Scott
a15_2652851.text: Mark CDR. Point source; right eye, 12 o'clock, halfway out. Intensity 2. [Long pause.]

a15_2652851.speaker: Scott
a15_2652851.text: Mark CDR. Right eye; point source; 7 o'clock about half way out; intensity 2.

a15_2653648.speaker: Henize
a15_2653648.text: 15, this is Houston. We find an hour's passed now, and we thank you very much for the data, and there's a general question. Since the counting rate was less than previously, is there - is there any impression that you have that the intensity may have been less than previously. Also, the intensity of the individual flashes. [Pause.]

a15_2653648.speaker: Scott
a15_2653648.text: Rog. I think that'd be a general comment that all three of us experienced. [Long pause.]

a15_2653648.speaker: Scott
a15_2653648.text: And, Houston, also, you might note that we all saw flashes last night when we went to sleep - just before we went to sleep, and I guess - we feel like there's a surprising decrease in numbers and intensity today.

a15_2653648.speaker: Henize
a15_2653648.text: Roger. We copy that you feel today's frequency is less than last night's and also that the intensity is less today. [Pause.]

a15_2653648.speaker: Henize
a15_2653648.text: Thank you very much for the free information. [Pause.]

a15_2654046.speaker: Irwin
a15_2654046.text: Looking back at 264:16, there's a callout there to close the Mapping Camera cover. We did not do that because [of] the extension of the Mapping Camera. [Pause.]

a15_2654046.speaker: Henize
a15_2654046.text: Roger. We concur with you that that was the right action; the one that you took. [Pause.]

a15_2655536.speaker: Henize
a15_2655536.text: 15, this is Houston. We'd like to set your mind at ease about that attitude glitch [at 264:04:33]. It was indeed due to loading a Noun 20 in place of a Noun 22.

a15_2660413.speaker: Scott
a15_2660413.text: Houston, Apollo 15. The OPS pressure is 1,000 [psi, 6,900 kPa].

a15_2660413.speaker: Henize
a15_2660413.text: Roger, 15. We copy 1,000 on the OPS pressure. And we have a suggestion down here that may make the OPS - simpler to handle. We'd like to put the hose over its connector there and simply turn the OPS on to bleed down gradually and simply replenish the cabin pressure and then you don't have to bother with you - operating it tonight.

a15_2660413.speaker: Scott
a15_2660413.text: Rog. That's sounds like a pretty good idea. Okay; we'll do that.

a15_2660413.speaker: Henize
a15_2660413.text: Rog. And then everybody will be completely satisfied that it's bled out by the time you reenter.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: 15, this is Houston with a couple of comments about the SIM bay experiments, if you're willing to listen. [Pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Rog, Houston. Go ahead.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: First of all, on the Gamma-ray experiment, Dr. Arnold reports that Al Worden probably performed the first recorded repair of a scientific instrument in space, because earlier in that day he'd began to experience some problem with excess noise in the Gamma-ray experiment. And when Al went out in the EVA - we don't know what happened there - but at the end of the EVA, the Gamma-ray cleared up and has been doing beautifully ever since. You must have given it a pretty good kick there, Al.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Well, not - not only is he a plumber, he's an electrician as well.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Roger. On the X-ray Spectrometer, the work you've been doing on the galactic sources of X-radiation has - is already showing considerable interest. And, in particular, the Scorpius X-ray 1 data gives us a longer continuous observation of this source than we've ever had before and shows a fairly long period variation, whi - which - I with - I should put in a word of caution - which still might be instrumental, but looks real, and was previously unrecorded and has the - has Dr. Adler rather excited. And I'm sure the other as - astronomers will be much interested also. Indeed, we may go back to t

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Rog. That sounds interesting.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: And otherwise, I guess - that - that's about the most exciting news from the SIM bay.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Okay. Very good. We're ready to talk about entry stowage, if you'll get out your - your map and your little legend there...

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Okay.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: ...on where things go and we'll run down the line here.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Okay. We've - incidentally - one more comment, the Mass Spectrometer, on the retraction sequence yesterday, showed us no increase in contamination, which was something of a surprise. And it's probable that we might try that once more today to make sure that that wasn't some sort of instrumental difficulty there. Maybe we just have a cleaner spacecraft atmosphere than we thought, though.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Yes, from what Al said when he was looking around out there, it sounded to me like things were pretty clean.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Okay, 15. If you will turn off your squelch it will help, because we may occasionally have periods in - when comm is rather weak. And, otherwise, go ahead.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Okay. What - what we use as a reference is the Entry Stowage Map, spacecraft 112, 26 July 1971, which is in the front of our Flight Plan. And, if you have that in front of you, why, I'll just go through that and give you the additions, deletions, and changes, of which there are very few. [Pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Okay. We're [pause] - Stand by one moment.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Okay. Go ahead. [Pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Okay. A-1 is stowed as prescribed there. Top of A-1 has a bag - a decontam bag in which we have sample container number 2, for 23 pounds, and the LM return items. [Pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Roger.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: A-2 is as you have listed. [Long pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Roger.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: And, on top of A-2, we have the ISA decontam bag, for 64 pounds.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: We copy.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Okay. A-3, A-4, A-5 and A-6 are as you have on your list right now.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: We copy.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: A-7 is as you have on your list, with the addition of the LM DAC and the LM - 70 millimeter camera that failed on the surface, which we thought you might like to take a look at.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Right. Both of those are - are added items, I take it.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: That's correct. [Pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: We copy.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Side of A-7 is the EVA umbilical and bag, as per - prescribed.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Rog.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Top of A-7 is a sample collection bag - Oh, stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Okay. Let me - let me go back and make a correction here, Karl. Look over in the left-hand column where it says top of A-1, and scratch "Sample collection bag number 2."

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Okay.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: And then go back to your right-hand column there. On top of A-7, we have a decontam bag with sample collection bag number 2 and the BSLSS bag, for a total of 48 pounds. [Pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: We copy. [Pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: The 35-millimeter bracket in the bag, we're going to put that in the...

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Okay.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Could I clarify that - both of those bags together were 48 pounds, or do I also put over the 20 - the 23 pounds we had on A-1?

a15_2670833.speaker: Irwin
a15_2670833.text: That's going to go in there.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: No, the total of collection bag number 2 plus the BSLSS is 48 pounds.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: I understand.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: And you can scratch the collection bag number 2 for 23 off of A-1.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Okay. And then in A-8, it's stowed as prescribed [radio noise] with the exception of one less lightweight headset, which is some - somewhere on the Moon.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Okay. On the side of the next page in the left column, on the side of A-8 in the bag, as you have there, with the addition of the core tube pole. [Pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Say again.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Okay. I - I figured that would be a strange one. On the side of A-8 in bag, there are four items there, and one additional item has been added. The drill core-stem, which we just labelled as a core tube pole, because it looks like a pole.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Roger. That's the three-foot core stem.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: That's correct. [Pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Okay.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: And A-9 is collection bag number 3, for 30 pounds.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: We copy.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: B-1, B-2 and B-3 are as you have them listed.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Okay.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: B-5 is rock box number 1, for 36 pounds; and B-6 is rock box number 2, for 40 pounds.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Okay. We copy.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: And then B-5 and 6, B-8, L-2 and L-3 are as you have them listed.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Okay.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: And R-1 is the Flight Data File and the LM PPK. [Pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: We copy.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: And then, on the next column, they're all as you have listed. From the top; R-2, R-3, and in R-3 we have the entire LM data file. And we've taken R-12 out of R-3 and put it in another spot.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Okay.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: R - far - R-4 is as you have it, as is R-5, R-6, R-8, R-11, R-13.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: We copy.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Okay. U-1 will only have one temporary stowage bag in it.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: We copy.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: U-2 will have the items listed, plus the accessory bag, in which we have - the contaminated gloves. And I'll read you a list of those items, if you're ready to copy.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Have one set of EV gloves and one set of IV gloves, the tethers - the - the waist tethers, paper towels. And I guess that's about it.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Roger.

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: U-3 is as you have prescribed there.

a15_2670833.speaker: Henize
a15_2670833.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
a15_2670833.text: Stand by one, Karl. [Long pause.]

a15_2670833.speaker: Scott
